@@ -0,0 +1,271 @@
+---
+title: Configure optional group SID claims for Microsoft Entra Kerberos tickets (Preview)
+description: Learn how to select the group SID categories and group membership scope included in Microsoft Entra Kerberos service tickets.
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 10/22/2026
+ms.reviewer: Vimala
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+# Customer intent: As an application administrator, I want to control which group SIDs Microsoft Entra ID includes in Kerberos service tickets.
+---
+
+# Configure optional group SID claims for Microsoft Entra Kerberos tickets (Preview)
+
+Microsoft Entra Kerberos service tickets can include group security identifiers (SIDs) in the Privilege Attribute Certificate (PAC). Resources can use these SIDs to authorize access to files, applications, and other Kerberos-protected resources.
+
+Kerberos tickets support a maximum of 1,010 group SIDs. If a user's effective group membership exceeds this limit, Microsoft Entra ID can't issue the service ticket. Configure optional group SID claims to include only the SID categories and group memberships that the resource requires.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> The `kerberosTicket` optional claim applies only to Kerberos tickets. However, `groupMembershipClaims` is an application-wide setting and can affect group claims in ID, access, and SAML tokens. Review existing token consumers before changing this setting.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+To configure optional group SID claims, you need:
+
+- A Microsoft Entra tenant with Microsoft Entra Kerberos enabled for the workload.
+- An application registration that represents the Kerberos-protected resource.
+- A role that can update the application registration, such as Cloud Application Administrator or Application Administrator. An application owner can also update an application when the administration model and Microsoft Graph permissions allow it.
+- Groups assigned or available to the application, based on the `groupMembershipClaims` value that you select.
+
+During preview, the Microsoft Entra admin center experience and Microsoft Graph schema might become available at different times. If the **Kerberos** section isn't displayed in **Token configuration**, use the Microsoft Graph beta endpoint.
+
+## How group SID selection works
+
+The configuration has two parts:
+
+- `groupMembershipClaims` controls which group memberships are eligible for the optional Kerberos group SID categories.
+- `optionalClaims.kerberosTicket` selects which SID representations Microsoft Entra ID adds to the PAC.
+
+The SID category and its PAC location are separate concepts. Microsoft Entra ID determines the PAC location based on the user's identity type and SID authority. Applications select SID categories; they don't select PAC fields directly.
+
+### Select the group membership scope
+
+Use `groupMembershipClaims` to control the group memberships considered for the optional SID categories.
+
+| Value | Optional group memberships considered |
+| --- | --- |
+| `None` | No optional group memberships. |
+| `SecurityGroup` | Security-enabled groups. |
+| `All` | Security groups, directory roles, and distribution lists. |
+| `ApplicationGroup` | Only groups assigned to the application. |
+| `DirectoryRole` | No optional group SIDs when used by itself. |
+
+Use `ApplicationGroup` when possible. This value limits the memberships considered for the application and helps reduce the likelihood of exceeding the 1,010-group SID limit. For more information, see [Manage users and groups assignment to an application](../enterprise-apps/assign-user-or-group-access-portal.md?pivots=portal).
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> For hybrid users, the user's base on-premises group SIDs remain part of the normal Kerberos PAC behavior. The `kerberosTicket` optional claim and `groupMembershipClaims` scope the optional SID categories; they don't remove the hybrid user's base on-premises group memberships.
+
+If both the client application and resource application configure Kerberos group SID claims, Microsoft Entra ID combines the selected categories and eligible groups from both applications.
+
+### Select the group SID categories
+
+Add a `groups` claim to `optionalClaims.kerberosTicket`, and use one or more of the following exact, case-sensitive values in `additionalProperties`.
+
+| Selector | Group SID selected | PAC behavior |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `hybrid_group_onpremises_sids` | The original on-premises SID (`S-1-5-21-...`) of a group that is synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID. | For a cloud-only user, the SID is added to `ExtraSids`. For a hybrid user, original on-premises group SIDs are already included through the normal PAC group processing. |
+| `hybrid_group_cloud_sids` | The Microsoft Entra cloud SID (`S-1-12-1-...`) of a synchronized group that also has an on-premises SID. | The SID is added to `ExtraSids`. For a hybrid user, the user's cloud SID is also added first in `ExtraSids`. |
+| `cloud_only_group_sids` | The Microsoft Entra cloud SID (`S-1-12-1-...`) of a group that doesn't have an on-premises SID. | The SID is added to `ExtraSids`. For a hybrid user, the user's cloud SID is also added first in `ExtraSids`. |
+
+For a cloud-only user, the user's cloud SID is required and remains the first entry in `ExtraSids`. The selected group SID categories follow it.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> Use only the canonical selector names in the preceding table. The pre-release names `hybrid_group_sids` and `onpremises_group_sids` aren't supported.
+
+## Configure the application
+
+# [Microsoft Entra admin center](#tab/entra-admin-center)
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as an administrator who can update the application.
+1. Browse to **Entra ID** > **App registrations**.
+1. Select the application registration for the Kerberos-protected resource.
+1. Under **Manage**, select **Token configuration**.
+1. Select **Add groups claim**, or edit the existing `groups` claim.
+1. Select the group membership scope:
+
+    - **Security groups**
+    - **All groups**
+    - **Groups assigned to the application**
+
+1. Expand **Kerberos**, and select one or more SID categories:
+
+    - **Hybrid group on-premises SIDs**
+    - **Hybrid group cloud SIDs**
+    - **Cloud-only group SIDs**
+
+1. Select **Save**.
+
+:::image type="content" source="media/configure-optional-group-claims-kerberos/select-kerberos-group-sids.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Edit groups claim pane with Kerberos group SID category options." lightbox="media/configure-optional-group-claims-kerberos/select-kerberos-group-sids.png":::
+
+After you save the configuration, the `groups` claim appears with the **Kerberos** token type.
+
+:::image type="content" source="media/configure-optional-group-claims-kerberos/kerberos-groups-claim.png" alt-text="Screenshot of Token configuration showing a groups claim for the Kerberos token type." lightbox="media/configure-optional-group-claims-kerberos/kerberos-groups-claim.png":::
+
+# [Microsoft Graph](#tab/microsoft-graph)
+
+During preview, use the Microsoft Graph beta endpoint.
+
+1. Read the current application configuration. Replace `{applicationObjectId}` with the object ID of the application registration, not its application (client) ID.
+
+    ```http
+    GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/applications/{applicationObjectId}?$select=id,appId,displayName,groupMembershipClaims,optionalClaims
+    ```
+
+1. Preserve the existing `idToken`, `accessToken`, and `saml2Token` optional-claim collections. Updating the `optionalClaims` complex property can replace the collections supplied in the request.
+1. Submit a `PATCH` request. The following example limits optional group SID evaluation to groups assigned to the application and requests all three supported SID categories:
+
+    ```http
+    PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/applications/{applicationObjectId}
+    Content-Type: application/json
+
+    {
+      "groupMembershipClaims": "ApplicationGroup",
+      "optionalClaims": {
+        "idToken": [],
+        "accessToken": [],
+        "saml2Token": [],
+        "kerberosTicket": [
+          {
+            "name": "groups",
+            "source": null,
+            "essential": false,
+            "additionalProperties": [
+              "hybrid_group_onpremises_sids",
+              "hybrid_group_cloud_sids",
+              "cloud_only_group_sids"
+            ]
+          }
+        ]
+      }
+    }
+    ```
+
+    Replace the empty token collections with the existing values returned by the `GET` request when the application already has optional claims.
+
+1. A successful update returns `204 No Content`. Read the application again to confirm that the configuration was saved:
+
+    ```http
+    GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/applications/{applicationObjectId}?$select=id,appId,displayName,groupMembershipClaims,optionalClaims
+    ```
+
+---
+
+## Configuration examples
+
+The following examples show only the `kerberosTicket` collection. Preserve the application's other optional-claim collections when you update the complete `optionalClaims` property.
+
+### Include cloud SIDs for cloud-only groups
+
+```json
+"kerberosTicket": [
+  {
+    "name": "groups",
+    "source": null,
+    "essential": false,
+    "additionalProperties": [
+      "cloud_only_group_sids"
+    ]
+  }
+]
+```
+
+### Include both SID representations for synchronized groups
+
+```json
+"kerberosTicket": [
+  {
+    "name": "groups",
+    "source": null,
+    "essential": false,
+    "additionalProperties": [
+      "hybrid_group_onpremises_sids",
+      "hybrid_group_cloud_sids"
+    ]
+  }
+]
+```
+
+### Include all supported optional group SID categories
+
+```json
+"kerberosTicket": [
+  {
+    "name": "groups",
+    "source": null,
+    "essential": false,
+    "additionalProperties": [
+      "hybrid_group_onpremises_sids",
+      "hybrid_group_cloud_sids",
+      "cloud_only_group_sids"
+    ]
+  }
+]
+```
+
+## Assign groups to the application
+
+If you set `groupMembershipClaims` to `ApplicationGroup`, assign each required group to the enterprise application:
+
+1. In the Microsoft Entra admin center, browse to **Entra ID** > **Enterprise applications**.
+1. Select the enterprise application that corresponds to the application registration.
+1. Under **Manage**, select **Users and groups**.
+1. Select **Add user/group**, select the required groups, and then select **Assign**.
+
+Only assigned groups that the user is a member of are eligible for the optional Kerberos group SID categories.
+
+## Verify the configuration
+
+1. Read the application object and confirm that `optionalClaims.kerberosTicket` contains a claim whose `name` is `groups`.
+1. Confirm that each `additionalProperties` value uses the exact supported spelling and casing.
+1. Confirm that `groupMembershipClaims` matches the intended scope.
+1. If you use `ApplicationGroup`, confirm that the required groups are assigned to the enterprise application.
+1. Clear cached tickets when appropriate for your test environment, and request a new Kerberos service ticket for the resource.
+1. Validate that access succeeds and that the expected SIDs are present in the ticket or resource-side authorization evaluation.
+1. Test each identity topology that the application supports, such as hybrid users, cloud-only users, synchronized groups, and cloud-only groups.
+1. Review the Microsoft Entra sign-in logs and resource-side Kerberos events if ticket issuance or access fails.
+
+## Migrate from a legacy application tag
+
+Some preview applications use the `kdc_enable_cloud_group_sids` application tag to opt in to cloud group SIDs. The `kerberosTicket` optional claim replaces this tag with an explicit per-application group scope and SID category selection.
+
+To migrate:
+
+1. Keep the legacy tag while you add the equivalent `kerberosTicket` optional claim.
+1. Read the application configuration to verify that the optional claim was saved.
+1. Test service-ticket issuance and resource authorization with representative users and groups.
+1. Remove the legacy tag only after the optional-claim configuration is deployed and validated end to end.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> Don't remove a working legacy configuration until the optional claim has been saved, read back, and validated in the target environment.
+
+## Troubleshoot
+
+| Symptom | Cause or action |
+| --- | --- |
+| The **Kerberos** section isn't displayed in **Token configuration**. | The preview admin center experience isn't available for the tenant. Use the Microsoft Graph beta endpoint. |
+| `kerberosTicket` is reported as an invalid property, or the saved collection is empty. | The Microsoft Graph or application-manifest schema used by the administration surface doesn't support the preview property in that environment. Use the supported beta endpoint and verify feature availability. |
+| The `groups` claim is ignored. | Confirm that it is inside `optionalClaims.kerberosTicket`. Kerberos group SID selectors aren't honored in `idToken`, `accessToken`, or `saml2Token`. |
+| A selector is ignored. | Use the exact canonical values: `hybrid_group_onpremises_sids`, `hybrid_group_cloud_sids`, and `cloud_only_group_sids`. |
+| No optional group SIDs are included. | Check `groupMembershipClaims`, group assignment, user membership, and the selected SID categories. The `name` value must be `groups`. |
+| Assigned groups are missing. | When `groupMembershipClaims` is `ApplicationGroup`, confirm that the groups are assigned to the enterprise application. |
+| Hybrid on-premises group SIDs are still present when a narrow optional scope is configured. | Hybrid users retain their base on-premises PAC group memberships. The optional claim scopes additional SID categories and doesn't remove the base group projection. |
+| Ticket issuance fails for a user with many group memberships. | Kerberos tickets support a maximum of 1,010 group SIDs. Reduce the scope, preferably by using `ApplicationGroup`, and assign only the groups required by the resource. |
+| Sign-in logs show error `140011` (`KerberosUsersGroupNumberExceeded`). | The effective PAC group SID count exceeded 1,010. Microsoft Entra ID returns a Kerberos field-too-long error and doesn't issue the service ticket. |
+| Sign-in succeeds but resource access fails. | Kerberos service-ticket issuance occurs when the user accesses the resource. Review the sign-in log entry for the TGS request and the resource's Kerberos and authorization logs. |
+
+## Security and operational guidance
+
+- Request only the SID categories that the resource requires. Additional authorization data increases ticket size.
+- Prefer `ApplicationGroup` to create a predictable, least-privileged group scope.
+- Assign only the groups required by the resource.
+- Treat group SIDs as authorization inputs only after the resource validates the Kerberos ticket and its intended service identity.
+- Monitor sign-in logs and resource-side Kerberos events during deployment and migration.
+- Validate cloud-only and hybrid identity topologies separately.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Introduction to Microsoft Entra Kerberos](kerberos.md)
+- [Configure and manage optional claims in ID tokens, access tokens, and SAML tokens](../../identity-platform/optional-claims.md)
+- [Configure group claims for applications by using Microsoft Entra ID](../hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-fed-group-claims.md)
+- [Manage users and groups assignment to an application](../enterprise-apps/assign-user-or-group-access-portal.md?pivots=portal)
+- [optionalClaims resource type](/graph/api/resources/optionalclaims)
+- [Update application](/graph/api/application-update)

englishSummary.summary: The guide explains how to control group memberships and SID categories in Kerberos ticket PACs using `groupMembershipClaims` and `optionalClaims.kerberosTicket`. It covers prerequisites, the 1,010-SID limit, and Microsoft Graph beta configuration when the portal option is unavailable.

@@ -0,0 +1,423 @@
+---
+title: Troubleshoot Microsoft Entra Kerberos
+description: Learn how to diagnose Microsoft Entra Kerberos ticket acquisition, key synchronization, and resource access issues.
+ms.topic: troubleshooting
+ms.date: 11/06/2026
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+# Customer intent: As an identity administrator, I want to diagnose Microsoft Entra Kerberos ticket acquisition, key synchronization, and resource access issues.
+---
+
+# Troubleshoot Microsoft Entra Kerberos
+
+Microsoft Entra Kerberos allows Microsoft Entra ID to act as a cloud-based Key Distribution Center (KDC). Depending on the scenario, Windows can receive a Cloud Ticket Granting Ticket (Cloud TGT) to request service tickets from Microsoft Entra ID or a partial TGT that an on-premises Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain controller exchanges for a full AD DS TGT.
+
+This article focuses on Kerberos authentication and ticket acquisition. Obtaining a service ticket doesn't by itself confirm that the resource can validate the ticket or that the identity is authorized. If ticket issuance succeeds but resource access fails, check server-side ticket validation, network connectivity, and resource authorization separately.
+
+## Before you begin
+
+Identify the ticket flow that your resource uses:
+
+- Resources configured to use Microsoft Entra Kerberos use the Cloud TGT to request a service ticket from Microsoft Entra ID. This includes supported cloud services and on-premises resources configured for the cloud-only identity preview.
+- Resources that use traditional AD DS Kerberos require an AD DS TGT. For supported hybrid identities, Windows exchanges the partial TGT with an on-premises domain controller before requesting the service ticket. This flow requires connectivity to AD DS and isn't available to a cloud-only identity that has no AD DS account.
+
+For more information, see [How the Kerberos ticket flow is selected](kerberos.md#how-the-kerberos-ticket-flow-is-selected). Check the supported device, Windows version, and sign-in requirements for your workload before you test.
+
+Run the client commands in the affected user's Windows session. Don't use a different administrator account to inspect the user's sign-in state or ticket cache. For an agent user, first establish a session through the supported agent user authentication flow. For prerequisites, see [Agent user support](configure-cloud-only-identities-on-premises-access-kerberos.md#agent-user-support).
+
+## Step 1: Verify the device and sign-in state
+
+On the affected Windows device, open a command prompt in the user's session and run:
+
+```console
+dsregcmd /status
+```
+
+Review **Device State** and **SSO State**. For a Microsoft Entra joined or Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device, verify that `AzureAdJoined` is `YES`. Also verify that `AzureAdPrt` is `YES`.
+
+The following shortened example shows the expected values for a Microsoft Entra joined client that has a Cloud TGT:
+
+```output
+AzureAdJoined : YES
+AzureAdPrt    : YES
+CloudTgt      : YES
+```
+
+The Kerberos fields describe different ticket states:
+
+| Field | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| `CloudTgt : YES` | A Cloud Kerberos ticket for cloud-resource access is present for the signed-in user. |
+| `OnPremTgt : YES` | A Cloud Kerberos ticket for on-premises resource access is present for the signed-in user. This value doesn't confirm that the partial TGT was exchanged for a full AD DS TGT. |
+
+Don't require `OnPremTgt` for a cloud-only identity that uses the Cloud TGT flow. Use the field names in the **SSO State** section; diagnostic fields can differ by Windows version and output section.
+
+If `AzureAdPrt` is `NO`, troubleshoot device registration and the Primary Refresh Token (PRT) before continuing. If the expected `CloudTgt` is `NO`, continue to step 2 and verify the client configuration and supported sign-in method.
+
+For field definitions and PRT diagnostics, see [Troubleshoot devices by using the dsregcmd command](../devices/troubleshoot-device-dsregcmd.md#sso-state).
+
+## Step 2: Verify the Cloud TGT
+
+In the same Windows session, run:
+
+```console
+klist cloud_debug
+```
+
+Review whether Cloud Kerberos is enabled and whether the client has the expected Cloud TGT. For background, see [Cloud TGT issuance](kerberos.md#cloud-tgt-issuance).
+
+If the output includes the following value, check whether the ticket retrieval policy was applied:
+
+```output
+Cloud Kerberos enabled by policy: 0
+```
+
+Enable the [CloudKerberosTicketRetrievalEnabled policy](/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-kerberos#cloudkerberosticketretrievalenabled) with a value of `1` through Microsoft Intune, or enable **Allow retrieving the Azure AD Kerberos Ticket Granting Ticket during logon** under **Computer Configuration** > **Administrative Templates** > **System** > **Kerberos** in Group Policy.
+
+Apply the policy and restart the device as described in the [client configuration guidance](configure-cloud-only-identities-on-premises-access-kerberos.md#enable-cloud-kerberos-ticket-retrieval). Establish a new session by using the supported sign-in flow, and check the ticket state again. Enabling ticket retrieval doesn't replace the workload's identity and authentication prerequisites.
+
+If a partial TGT is missing in a hybrid AD DS scenario, verify the Microsoft Entra Kerberos server object and configuration in AD DS. For instructions, see [View and verify the Microsoft Entra Kerberos server](howto-authentication-passwordless-security-key-on-premises.md#view-and-verify-the-microsoft-entra-kerberos-server). Don't create or change a Trusted Domain Object (TDO) unless the scenario requires one.
+
+## Step 3: Request a service ticket
+
+After you verify the required TGT state, test whether Windows can obtain a service ticket for the resource. For a Server Message Block (SMB) resource, use its Common Internet File System (CIFS) service principal name (SPN):
+
+```console
+klist get cifs/<server-fqdn>
+```
+
+Replace `<server-fqdn>` with the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) that the application or SMB client uses. For another service, use its service class and resource SPN.
+
+Inspect the ticket cache:
+
+```console
+klist
+```
+
+Verify that a ticket for the expected resource SPN appears. Test with the same host name that the application uses, including any alias. A ticket requested for a different host name doesn't validate the application's Kerberos configuration.
+
+For command syntax, see [klist](/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/klist).
+
+## Step 4: Check the configuration if no service ticket is issued
+
+If the required TGT is available but the service-ticket request fails, check the realm mapping, resource name, and configuration for the selected ticket flow.
+
+### Verify the host-to-realm mapping
+
+Windows uses host-to-realm mappings to determine which Kerberos realm handles a resource. You can configure mappings through:
+
+- Group Policy: **Computer Configuration** > **Administrative Templates** > **System** > **Kerberos** > **Define host name-to-Kerberos realm mappings**.
+- Microsoft Intune: The [ADMX_Kerberos/HostToRealm policy CSP](/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-admx-kerberos#hosttorealm).
+
+For a resource configured to use Microsoft Entra Kerberos, the expected realm is:
+
+```text
+KERBEROS.MICROSOFTONLINE.COM
+```
+
+Verify that the resource host name is mapped to this realm. Don't redirect resources that require traditional AD DS Kerberos to the Microsoft Entra Kerberos realm. Prefer a specific host mapping over a domain-wide mapping that could affect unrelated services.
+
+For more information, see [Realm mapping](kerberos.md#realm-mapping).
+
+### Verify the resource name and SPN
+
+Confirm that the host name used by the client matches the name in the Kerberos configuration. For SMB, the requested SPN is `cifs/<server-fqdn>`.
+
+Verify that the SPN is registered on the account that runs the target service and isn't duplicated on another account. For instructions, see [How to configure SPNs](/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/manage/how-to-configure-spn).
+
+### Verify the configuration for the selected flow
+
+For an on-premises resource configured for the cloud-only identity preview, confirm that the resource application, SPN association, tenant-specific KDC proxy mapping, and synchronized service key are configured. Use [Configure on-premises resource access for cloud-only identities](configure-cloud-only-identities-on-premises-access-kerberos.md).
+
+For a hybrid identity accessing a resource in an AD DS realm, verify connectivity to an on-premises domain controller and the partial-TGT exchange prerequisites. Use [Enable passwordless security key sign-in to on-premises resources](howto-authentication-passwordless-security-key-on-premises.md).
+
+For cloud services, follow the target workload's Microsoft Entra Kerberos requirements and troubleshooting guidance.
+
+## Step 5: Identify the next troubleshooting area
+
+Use the results to choose where to investigate next.
+
+| Result | Next step |
+| --- | --- |
+| Device registration or PRT state isn't established. | Troubleshoot device registration and Microsoft Entra sign-in. |
+| The expected Cloud TGT isn't available. | Verify the client policy, supported sign-in flow, and workload prerequisites. |
+| A TGT is available, but the service ticket can't be obtained. | Verify realm mapping, the resource name, SPN, and configuration for the selected Kerberos flow. |
+| A service ticket is issued, but the server can't validate it. | Check the target service's Kerberos logs, service account, encryption requirements, and current service key. For synchronized keys, check provisioning logs. For SMB error 1396, see [Service ticket is issued, but SMB access fails with error 1396](#service-ticket-is-issued-but-smb-access-fails-with-error-1396). Ticket issuance doesn't prove that server-side authentication succeeded. |
+| A service ticket is issued, but the client can't connect to the resource. | Troubleshoot DNS, required ports, and the network path. If you use Microsoft Entra Private Access, see [Troubleshoot application access](~/global-secure-access/troubleshoot-app-access.md). |
+| Required on-premises group SIDs are missing for the cloud-only identity preview. | Verify the application configuration in [Configure optional group SID claims for Microsoft Entra Kerberos tickets](configure-optional-group-claims-kerberos.md). Check the SID category, group assignment, membership, and membership scope. |
+| The server accepts the ticket, but SMB access is denied. | Verify the authorization group's SID in the server's logon session and check both share and NTFS permissions. A valid ticket doesn't grant permissions that the resource hasn't assigned. |
+
+Ticket acquisition, server-side authentication, and resource authorization are separate operations. In the traditional hybrid AD DS flow, the domain controller issues the full AD DS TGT with the authorization data used to request resource tickets. In the cloud-only identity preview, the resource uses the SIDs in the Microsoft Entra Kerberos service ticket instead.
+
+## Service ticket is issued, but SMB access fails with error 1396
+
+Use this section when a client obtains a Cloud Ticket Granting Ticket (Cloud TGT) and a CIFS service ticket from Microsoft Entra Kerberos, but can't access an on-premises SMB share.
+
+### Symptoms
+
+Connecting to the share fails with the following error:
+
+```output
+System error 1396 has occurred.
+The target account name is incorrect.
+```
+
+The client's ticket cache contains a service ticket for the expected `cifs/<server-fqdn>` service principal name (SPN), but access to the share fails.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> Obtaining a service ticket confirms ticket issuance. It doesn't confirm that the resource server can decrypt and validate the ticket or that the identity has permission to access the resource.
+
+### Possible causes
+
+If Kerberos events or a trace confirm `KRB_AP_ERR_MODIFIED`, investigate whether the target server can decrypt the ticket with the key for the account that runs the service. Possible causes include:
+
+- The SPN is associated with an incorrect AD DS account or is duplicated.
+- The client connects by using a host name or alias that doesn't match the intended service configuration.
+- The synchronized Kerberos key in Microsoft Entra ID no longer matches the current key of the AD DS account that owns the resource SPN.
+
+For synchronized resource keys, a failed synchronization match can prevent key updates after the AD DS account password changes.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> Windows error 1396 alone doesn't establish that a stale key caused the failure. Confirm the Kerberos error and review SPN configuration and provisioning history before determining the cause.
+
+### Diagnose the failure
+
+Follow these steps to distinguish ticket validation failures from authorization failures.
+
+#### 1. Confirm the requested resource and service ticket
+
+In the affected user's Windows session, run:
+
+```console
+klist get cifs/<server-fqdn>
+klist
+```
+
+Replace `<server-fqdn>` with the host name used in the failing UNC path, such as `\\<server-fqdn>\<share-name>`. If the application uses an alias, test that alias.
+
+Record the requested SPN, ticket timestamps, and KDC information.
+
+#### 2. Check the resource server
+
+Review Kerberos events on the client and resource server for the same access attempt.
+
+On the resource server, also check Security events for the affected identity:
+
+- **4624**: Successful logon.
+- **4625**: Failed logon.
+- **4627**: Group membership information.
+
+Missing Security events alone don't prove that the server rejected the ticket before logon. Confirm that the relevant audit policies are enabled. See [Verify group membership on the resource server](#verify-group-membership-on-the-resource-server).
+
+If ticket decryption fails, resolve that failure before troubleshooting group claims or share permissions.
+
+#### 3. Verify SPN ownership
+
+Confirm that the requested SPN resolves to the AD DS account whose key the target service uses. Check for incorrect or duplicate SPN registrations and verify any host name aliases.
+
+For configuration guidance, see [How to configure SPNs](/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/manage/how-to-configure-spn).
+
+#### 4. Check the resource's synchronization mapping
+
+Inspect the enterprise application that represents the resource. Verify the effective SPN associations and `tags` collection on its service principal, not only the application registration manifest.
+
+The resource service principal must contain the matching tag:
+
+```text
+KerberosSync:cifs/<server-fqdn>
+```
+
+The current synchronization implementation excludes a service principal from matching if it contains another distinct `KerberosSync:` tag. For example, adding a separate `KerberosSync:MSSQLSvc/...` tag to the same service principal can prevent key updates.
+
+Use separate resource applications and corresponding service principals for separate key-sync mappings.
+
+For this configuration's symptoms and recovery guidance, see [Kerberos key synchronization fails when multiple SPNs are configured](#kerberos-key-synchronization-fails-when-multiple-spns-are-configured).
+
+#### 5. Verify the last successful key export
+
+Review the synchronization job status and provisioning logs for the affected resource.
+
+- Look for failed or skipped matching operations, including `JoinNotFound`.
+- Identify the last successful key export for this resource.
+- Compare the export history with the AD DS account's password-change time and `msDS-KeyVersionNumber`.
+- Inspect the synchronized Kerberos credential on the resource service principal.
+
+A running provisioning agent or a started job doesn't confirm that this resource's key was updated. An old credential timestamp or an increased AD DS key version is a diagnostic clue, not definitive proof of a mismatch.
+
+See [Verify key synchronization](configure-cloud-only-identities-on-premises-access-kerberos.md#verify-key-synchronization).
+
+### Resolve and verify
+
+1. Correct any SPN ownership or synchronization-mapping errors. Preserve unrelated tags and credentials.
+1. Resolve provisioning errors and allow the next synchronization cycle to complete. If necessary, follow the supported procedure to restart the job with a full synchronization.
+1. Confirm a successful key export and an updated synchronized Kerberos credential for the affected resource.
+1. Follow [Clear cached tickets and test again](#clear-cached-tickets-and-test-again) to request fresh tickets in the affected test session.
+1. Retry access to the same UNC path.
+1. Confirm that the resource server accepts the authentication and that the intended file or folder access succeeds.
+
+> [!CAUTION]
+> Don't clear the entire `keyCredentials` collection as a routine recovery step. Normal key synchronization replaces the previous synchronized Kerberos credential while preserving non-Kerberos credentials. Clearing the collection can remove credentials used for other purposes.
+
+If the server accepts the ticket but access is denied, investigate authorization separately. Verify the required group SIDs and both SMB share permissions and NTFS permissions.
+
+### Clear cached tickets and test again
+
+After a configuration change, use a test session to request fresh tickets.
+
+> [!CAUTION]
+> Purging the cache removes the current session's cached Kerberos tickets and can interrupt authenticated connections. Use this command only when you can safely repeat the authentication attempt.
+
+In the affected test session, run:
+
+```console
+klist purge
+```
+
+Reproduce the authentication attempt, and run `klist` again to inspect the newly acquired tickets.
+
+## Kerberos key synchronization fails when multiple SPNs are configured
+
+Microsoft Entra Kerberos key synchronization supports one `KerberosSync:<SPN>` mapping per resource service principal. If multiple distinct `KerberosSync:<SPN>` tags are configured on the same enterprise application, Kerberos key synchronization might not update the key as expected. This limitation is specific to the key synchronization mapping. Kerberos itself supports multiple SPNs.
+
+### Symptoms
+
+You might experience one or more of the following symptoms:
+
+- Kerberos authentication initially works after you configure the resource.
+- The client can obtain a Microsoft Entra Kerberos TGT and a service ticket for the on-premises resource.
+- Access to the resource later fails after the on-premises resource account password or Kerberos key is rotated.
+- The resource's key credential in Microsoft Entra ID isn't updated after the on-premises key changes.
+- The on-premises resource can't decrypt a service ticket issued by Microsoft Entra ID because the ticket was encrypted with an older key. This can result in errors such as `SEC_E_WRONG_PRINCIPAL` for SMB scenarios.
+
+An SMB error alone doesn't confirm a key mismatch. Review the Kerberos error, SPN configuration, and provisioning history as described in [Service ticket is issued, but SMB access fails with error 1396](#service-ticket-is-issued-but-smb-access-fails-with-error-1396).
+
+### Cause
+
+This issue can occur when a single Microsoft Entra resource service principal contains more than one distinct `KerberosSync:<SPN>` tag.
+
+For example, don't configure a resource service principal with both of the following mappings:
+
+```text
+KerberosSync:cifs/fileserver.contoso.com
+KerberosSync:MSSQLSvc/sqlserver.contoso.com:1433
+```
+
+The Kerberos key synchronization process uses the `KerberosSync:<SPN>` mapping to identify the Microsoft Entra service principal that corresponds to an on-premises Kerberos principal. The current synchronization model expects a single Kerberos key mapping for the resource service principal.
+
+If multiple distinct `KerberosSync:<SPN>` mappings are configured, synchronization matching can fail and the existing key in Microsoft Entra ID can remain unchanged.
+
+This condition might not be immediately apparent. For example, if Microsoft Entra ID and the on-premises resource initially have the same key, access can continue to work. The problem can become visible after the resource account password changes and a new Kerberos key is generated. If synchronization doesn't publish the new key, Microsoft Entra ID retains the previous key and tickets issued with that key can't be decrypted by the resource.
+
+### Resolution
+
+Configure one Kerberos key synchronization mapping per Microsoft Entra resource enterprise application.
+
+For a file server resource application, use:
+
+```text
+KerberosSync:cifs/fileserver.contoso.com
+```
+
+For a SQL Server resource application, use:
+
+```text
+KerberosSync:MSSQLSvc/sqlserver.contoso.com:1433
+```
+
+If the CIFS and MSSQLSvc SPNs require separate key-sync mappings, configure them as separate Microsoft Entra enterprise applications instead of adding both `KerberosSync` tags to the same resource application.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> This restriction doesn't mean that Kerberos doesn't support multiple SPNs. The restriction applies to the current Microsoft Entra Kerberos key synchronization mapping, where the synchronized Kerberos credential is associated with the resource service principal rather than an individual SPN.
+
+### Verify the configuration
+
+Check the resource service principal and make sure that it contains only one distinct `KerberosSync:<SPN>` tag associated with the Kerberos key synchronization configuration.
+
+For example, for an SMB file server:
+
+```text
+KerberosSync:cifs/fileserver.contoso.com
+```
+
+Also verify that the SPN in the tag exactly matches the SPN associated with the on-premises Kerberos principal being synchronized. The key-sync design joins the on-premises resource to its Microsoft Entra service principal by using both the resource SPN and the corresponding `KerberosSync:<SPN>` mapping.
+
+Check the effective `tags` collection on the resource service principal, including tags from the associated application registration. For setup instructions, see [Create the resource application](configure-cloud-only-identities-on-premises-access-kerberos.md#create-the-resource-application).
+
+### Verify key synchronization
+
+After correcting the resource configuration, allow the Kerberos synchronization process to run again and verify that the resource service principal contains the synchronized Kerberos key credential.
+
+For example, with Microsoft Graph PowerShell:
+
+```powershell
+Connect-MgGraph -Scopes "Application.Read.All"
+
+(Get-MgServicePrincipal `
+    -ServicePrincipalId "<resource-service-principal-object-id>" `
+    -Property Id,DisplayName,KeyCredentials).KeyCredentials |
+    Select-Object DisplayName,Type,Usage,StartDateTime,EndDateTime
+```
+
+A missing Kerberos key credential can indicate that the resource isn't in synchronization scope or that the SPN-to-resource-application mapping didn't succeed. Other credentials can appear in this collection, so a nonempty collection alone doesn't confirm that the Kerberos key was updated. Review the provisioning logs and the last successful key export. For instructions, see [Verify key synchronization](configure-cloud-only-identities-on-premises-access-kerberos.md#verify-key-synchronization).
+
+Also verify that the Microsoft Entra provisioning agent is healthy under **Entra ID** > **Entra Connect** > **Cloud sync** in the Microsoft Entra admin center. For agent health checks, see [Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync troubleshooting](../hybrid/cloud-sync/how-to-troubleshoot.md#agent-problems). A healthy agent doesn't by itself confirm that this resource's key was synchronized.
+
+### Why the issue can appear after password rotation
+
+Under normal operation, when the password or Kerberos key of the on-premises resource changes, the synchronization process updates the corresponding Kerberos credential in Microsoft Entra ID.
+
+With an invalid multiple-`KerberosSync` configuration, the sequence can instead be:
+
+1. The on-premises resource and Microsoft Entra ID initially have matching Kerberos keys.
+1. Access works successfully.
+1. The resource password changes and the on-premises Kerberos key changes.
+1. Kerberos key synchronization can't correctly match the resource application.
+1. The new key isn't written to the Microsoft Entra service principal.
+1. Microsoft Entra ID continues issuing service tickets by using the previously synchronized key.
+1. The on-premises resource can no longer decrypt those tickets and access fails.
+
+### Recommended configuration
+
+For resources that require different Kerberos key mappings, use separate Microsoft Entra resource applications:
+
+| On-premises resource SPN | Microsoft Entra resource application |
+| --- | --- |
+| `cifs/fileserver.contoso.com` | File Server application |
+| `MSSQLSvc/sqlserver.contoso.com:1433` | SQL Server application |
+
+Configure each resource application with only the `KerberosSync:<SPN>` mapping for the Kerberos principal whose key is synchronized to that application.
+
+## Logging
+
+Use the resource server's Security log to verify logon group memberships and enable the required auditing when events aren't generated.
+
+### Verify group membership on the resource server
+
+For a network logon, such as access to an SMB share, Windows records logon events on the server that hosts the resource. With auditing enabled, Security event 4627 shows the group memberships associated with that logon session. It isn't a complete dump of the ticket's Privilege Attribute Certificate (PAC).
+
+You need permission to read the server's Security log. Administrative permissions are required to change its audit policy.
+
+On the resource server:
+
+1. Open **Event Viewer**.
+1. Browse to **Windows Logs** > **Security**.
+1. Select **Filter Current Log**, enter `4627` in **Event IDs**, and select **OK**.
+1. Find the event for the affected identity and access attempt. Review **New Logon** to identify the account and its **Logon ID**. Correlate that ID with the corresponding event 4624.
+1. Review **Group Membership** for the required group SIDs. If membership data spans multiple events, review all events for that logon.
+1. Compare the authorization group SIDs with the resource's permissions. For SMB, check both share permissions and NTFS ACLs.
+
+For field definitions, see [Event 4627: Group membership information](/windows/security/threat-protection/auditing/event-4627).
+
+### Enable auditing if event 4627 isn't generated
+
+Enable **Success** auditing for both **Audit Group Membership** and **Audit Logon** on the resource server, and then reproduce the access attempt.
+
+In Local Security Policy, browse to **Advanced Audit Policy Configuration** > **System Audit Policies** > **Logon/Logoff**. For a Group Policy-managed server, configure the same subcategories under **Computer Configuration** > **Policies** > **Windows Settings** > **Security Settings** > **Advanced Audit Policy Configuration** > **Audit Policies** > **Logon/Logoff**.
+
+Follow your organization's audit policy and log-retention requirements. For more information, see [Audit Group Membership](/windows/security/threat-protection/auditing/audit-group-membership) and [Advanced Audit Policy Configuration](/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/plan/security-best-practices/advanced-audit-policy-configuration).
+
+## Related content
+

+---
+title: Create a Device Access profile - Microsoft Entra Private Access

+author: johanogh

+# Customer intent: As an IT administrator, I want to create and assign a Device Access profile so that Windows devices can reach private resources before a user signs in.
+---
+
+# Create a Device Access profile for Microsoft Entra Private Access (preview)
+
+Create a Device Access traffic forwarding profile for Microsoft Entra Private Access in Microsoft Global Secure Access. Windows devices use the profile to connect to private resources before a user signs in.
+
+Use the profile to reach domain controllers, Network Time Protocol (NTP) services, Microsoft Configuration Manager, and Windows Server Update Services (WSUS). Devices can reach these resources during startup and from the Windows sign-in screen.
+
+This guide helps IT administrators enable applications, create and assign a profile, and verify connectivity. Review the client, device, and role prerequisites before you begin. Device Access is in preview and supports Windows and Private Access traffic only.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A Microsoft Entra tenant onboarded to Global Secure Access.
+- A Windows device that's Microsoft Entra joined or Microsoft Entra hybrid joined.
+- The Device Access-compatible [Global Secure Access client](https://aka.ms/GlobalSecureAccess-DeviceAccessClient) installed on the device. You can deploy the client by using Microsoft Intune or another mobile device management (MDM) solution. A user doesn't need to be signed in during installation.
+- [Private network connectors](how-to-configure-connectors.md) deployed for the private network that hosts your resources.
+- Application segments defined for each private application that the device needs to reach.
+- The [Global Secure Access Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#global-secure-access-administrator) and [Application Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#application-administrator) roles, or equivalent permissions, to manage traffic forwarding profiles and private applications.
+
+Device Access doesn't support domain join scenarios. The device needs to be Microsoft Entra joined or Microsoft Entra hybrid joined before you begin.
+
+For Active Directory Domain Services scenarios, also configure the following items:
+
+- Enable Private DNS and add the DNS suffix for the on-premises Active Directory domain. Windows uses the suffix to locate domain controllers.
+- Publish domain controllers as a separate private application. For related configuration guidance, see [Configure Kerberos single sign-on for Private Access](how-to-configure-kerberos-sso.md).
+- If your Private DNS definitions are part of Quick Access, enable Device Access on the Quick Access application and include Quick Access in the Device Access profile. In this configuration, Quick Access provides the Private DNS definitions but doesn't publish other resources to the device tunnel.
+
+## Enable private applications for Device Access
+
+Private applications don't allow Device Access by default. Enable the setting on each application that a device needs to reach before a user signs in.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) with the required roles.
+1. Browse to **Global Secure Access** > **Applications** > **Enterprise applications**.
+1. Select the private application.
+1. Open the application's network access properties.
+1. Select **Enable Device Access with Global Secure Access**, and then save the change.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/how-to-create-device-access-profile/enable-device-access.png" alt-text="Screenshot of network access properties with Enable Device Access with Global Secure Access selected." border="true":::
+
+1. Repeat these steps for each required application, such as domain controllers, Configuration Manager, WSUS, and on-premises identity services.
+
+Enable only the private applications that devices require without a signed-in user. Limiting the applications reduces the resources available through the device tunnel.
+
+## Create a Device Access profile
+
+Device Access forwarding profiles are separate from user-context traffic forwarding profiles. Their assignments are based on devices instead of users.
+
+1. In the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com), browse to **Global Secure Access** > **Connect** > **Traffic forwarding**.
+1. Select the **Device Access profiles** tab.
+1. Select **Create Device Access profile** > **Private Device Access profile**.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/how-to-create-device-access-profile/create-device-access-profile.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Device Access profiles tab with the Create Device Access profile menu." border="true":::
+
+1. On the **Basics** tab, configure the following settings:
+
+    | Setting | Description |
+    | --- | --- |
+    | **Profile name** | Enter a descriptive name for the profile. |
+    | **Description** | Optionally describe the devices and resources covered by the profile. |
+    | **Priority** | Set the evaluation priority. Device Access profiles have priorities that are independent of user-context profiles. |
+    | **Status** | Select **Enabled**, or select **Disabled** to stage the profile without applying it. |
+
+    The traffic forwarding type is set to **Private access** and can't be changed.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/how-to-create-device-access-profile/device-access-profile-basics.png" alt-text="Screenshot of Device Access profile basics with name, description, priority, and status settings." border="true":::
+
+1. Select **Next**, review the settings, and then select **Create**.
+
+## Add acquisition rules
+
+Acquisition rules determine which private applications a device can reach through the Device Access tunnel.
+
+1. Open the Device Access forwarding profile.
+1. Select **Acquisition rules**.
+1. If your configuration uses Quick Access for Private DNS definitions, ensure that Device Access is enabled on the Quick Access application, and then turn on **Include Private DNS**.
+
+    Only the Private DNS definitions from Quick Access are used. Application segments configured in Quick Access aren't added to Device Access.
+
+1. Select **Add applications**.
+1. Select the private applications that the profile should cover, and then save the rule.
+
+    The application picker shows only private applications that have Device Access enabled.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/how-to-create-device-access-profile/configure-acquisition-rules.png" alt-text="Screenshot of acquisition rules with Quick Access enabled and a domain controllers application selected." border="true":::
+
+## Assign the profile to devices
+
+A Device Access forwarding profile needs both a device assignment and a Windows platform assignment.
+
+1. In the Device Access forwarding profile, select **Assignments**.
+1. Next to **Device assignments**, select **View**.
+1. Choose one of the following assignment scopes:
+
+    - **No devices**: Stage the profile without applying it to devices.
+    - **All devices**: Apply the profile to all eligible Windows devices in the tenant.
+    - **Selected devices**: Apply the profile to selected devices or groups that contain devices.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/how-to-create-device-access-profile/select-device-assignment.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Device assignments pane with Selected devices chosen." border="true":::
+
+1. Save the device assignment.
+1. Next to **Device platform assignments**, select **View**, select **Windows**, and then save the platform assignment.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/how-to-create-device-access-profile/configure-profile-assignments.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Assignments page showing device and Windows platform assignments." border="true":::
+
+For a gradual rollout, assign the profile to a pilot group of devices first. For example, target only Microsoft Entra hybrid joined devices that require connectivity to domain controllers during Windows sign-in.
+
+## Verify Device Access
+
+Allow several minutes for the configuration to propagate, and then verify the profile and a pre-sign-in scenario on a target device.
+
+1. On an assigned Windows device, open the **Global Secure Access client**.
+1. Open **Advanced diagnostics**.
+1. Select **Forwarding profile** > **Device**.
+1. Confirm that the expected private pre-sign-in rules, Private DNS definitions, and private network definitions are present.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/how-to-create-device-access-profile/verify-device-forwarding-profile.png" alt-text="Screenshot of Advanced diagnostics showing the Device tab and private pre-sign-in rules." border="true":::
+
+1. Restart the device and remain on the Windows sign-in screen.
+1. Test access to a private resource included in the Device Access profile. For example, sign in with an account whose credentials aren't cached on the device.
+1. For a domain-controller scenario, confirm that sign-in succeeds and that Group Policy is applied. Review Group Policy events in **Event Viewer** under **Applications and Services Logs** > **Microsoft** > **Windows** > **GroupPolicy** > **Operational**.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/how-to-create-device-access-profile/verify-group-policy-events.png" alt-text="Screenshot of Event Viewer with the GroupPolicy Operational log selected." border="true":::
+
+## Monitor Device Access
+
+Use audit logs, traffic logs, and client diagnostics to monitor connections that use the device context.
+
+1. Review audit logs for creation and deletion of Device Access forwarding profiles, assignment changes, application-list changes, and changes to Device Access enablement.
+1. In traffic logs, filter **Security principal type** to **Device** and review the **Security principal type** column.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/how-to-create-device-access-profile/identify-device-traffic-logs.png" alt-text="Screenshot of Global Secure Access traffic logs filtered to device traffic, with Device shown in the Security principal type column." border="true":::
+
+1. In Advanced diagnostics, open the **Traffic** tab to identify whether a tunneled connection used the **Device** or **User** context.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/how-to-create-device-access-profile/identify-traffic-context.png" alt-text="Screenshot of Advanced diagnostics traffic records with User and Device values in the Context column." border="true":::
+
+Client logs for the device context are written to Event Tracing for Windows (ETW) and Event Viewer and are included in the standard client log collection. For more information, see [Troubleshoot the Global Secure Access client for Windows: Advanced diagnostics](troubleshoot-global-secure-access-client-advanced-diagnostics.md).
+
+## Understand device and user contexts
+
+Device Access becomes active in the following situations:
+
+- After the device restarts and before a user signs in.
+- After a user signs out.
+- While the user session is locked.
+- After the device resumes from sleep or hibernation.
+
+When the device starts, the Global Secure Access client services authenticate the device to Global Secure Access. The client receives a Device Access forwarding profile and establishes a device tunnel for the private applications in that profile.
+
+After a user signs in and the user tunnels are established, the client switches to the user context. Existing connections drain over the device tunnel, and new connections use the user tunnel.
+
+The client switches back to the device context when a user context is no longer available.
+
+Device Access supports scenarios such as:
+
+- Signing in with credentials that aren't cached on the device.
+- Reaching domain controllers for authentication and Group Policy processing.
+- Connecting to on-premises device-management services at startup.
+- Changing an expired password when connectivity to a domain controller is required.
+
+Internet Access and Microsoft 365 traffic aren't tunneled in the device context. If you enable those traffic forwarding profiles, their traffic continues to use the user context after a user signs in.
+
+## Remove access for a lost or compromised device
+
+If a device is lost, retired, or compromised, remove its access to the Device Access tunnel.
+
+The minimum role required to disable a device is [Cloud Device Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#cloud-device-administrator).
+
+1. Disable the device object in Microsoft Entra ID.
+1. Remove the device from any assignment to a Device Access traffic forwarding profile.
+
+Disabling the device object prevents the Global Secure Access client from authenticating the device to the service, which blocks the device tunnel. It also prevents the device from authenticating to other Microsoft Entra applications.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Install the Global Secure Access client for Windows](how-to-install-windows-client.md).
+- [Configure connectors](how-to-configure-connectors.md).
+- [Tutorial: Configure per-app access segmentation](tutorial-private-access-app-segmentation.md).

diff --git a/docs/id-governance/tenant-governance/how-to-manage-relationship-expiration.md b/docs/id-governance/tenant-governance/how-to-manage-relationship-expiration.md

+++ b/docs/id-governance/tenant-governance/how-to-manage-relationship-expiration.md
@@ -0,0 +1,134 @@
+---
+title: Manage relationship expiration and renewal (Preview)
+description: Learn how to create, renew, and end time-bound governance relationships in Microsoft Entra Tenant Governance.
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/11/2026
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+# Customer intent: As a tenant administrator, I want to limit the lifetime of governance relationships and renew approved access before it ends.
+---
+
+# Manage relationship expiration and renewal (Preview)
+
+Relationship expiration and renewal lets you make access through a Microsoft Entra Tenant Governance relationship time-bound. The governing tenant proposes a lifetime in a governance policy template, and the governed tenant reviews and approves it.
+
+Expiration is optional. A relationship without a configured lifetime doesn't expire automatically. For a time-bound relationship, the governed tenant must approve renewal before expiration to keep the relationship active.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> A pending renewal doesn't pause expiration. When a relationship expires, Tenant Governance terminates it and removes access granted only through that relationship. Maintain independent administrative access in each tenant.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Have the **Tenant Governance Administrator** role in each tenant where you perform setup or approval.
+- Review the applicable [Tenant Governance licensing requirements](licensing.md).
+- Create or select a [governance policy template](governance-policy-templates.md) in the governing tenant.
+- For delegated administration, have a role-assignable security group in the governing tenant and configure its approved roles in the template. For application access, configure the required multitenant applications in the template.
+
+## Create a time-bound relationship
+
+Configure the lifetime before sending the governance request.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) in the governing tenant.
+1. Browse to **Tenant governance** > **Templates** and create or select a governance policy template.
+1. Configure the delegated administration roles and multitenant applications that the relationship requires.
+1. Set **Relationship lifetime** to a whole number from **1 to 730 days**, and save the template.
+1. [Send a governance request](how-to-set-up-governance-relationship.md) using the template. Complete the invitation step first unless the tenant pair qualifies for the two-step handshake.
+1. In the governed tenant, browse to **Tenant governance** > **Governing tenants** > **Received requests**. Open the request and review its permissions and lifetime.
+1. Accept the request to establish the relationship.
+1. Verify that the relationship is **Active** and **Expires on** shows the expected date in both tenants.
+
+The initial expiration date is the request acceptance time plus the approved lifetime, not the date when the request was sent. The lifetime comes from the template and isn't overridden when sending or accepting the request.
+
+If you leave **Relationship lifetime** unset, the relationship is non-expiring. There's no default lifetime or expiration reminder for that relationship. Invitation validity and request validity are separate from the relationship lifetime.
+
+## Add or change expiration on an active relationship
+
+An accepted relationship uses a policy snapshot. Editing its template doesn't automatically change that snapshot or the relationship's expiration.
+
+1. In the governing tenant, edit the governance policy template used by the active relationship. Set the intended lifetime and save the template.
+1. Send a new **Initial** governance request for the same tenant using the **same template ID**.
+1. In the governed tenant, review and accept the request.
+1. Verify that the existing relationship keeps its ID and receives the updated policy snapshot and expiration.
+
+Use this process to add expiration to an active, non-expiring relationship or to apply different terms. A request using a different template ID can create a separate relationship.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> **Request renewal** doesn't apply an updated template. Renewal preserves the active relationship's existing lifetime, permissions, and policy snapshot.
+
+## Request and approve renewal
+
+The governing tenant can request renewal any time before expiration. Renewal isn't restricted to the 30-day reminder window.
+
+1. In the governing tenant, browse to **Tenant governance** > **Governed tenants** and open the active relationship. You can also open it from the expiration card on **Overview**.
+1. Select **Request renewal**, review the current expiration and lifetime, and submit the request.
+1. In the governed tenant, open the renewal-request card on **Tenant governance** > **Overview** and select **View renewal request**.
+1. Review the request and accept or reject it.
+1. Reopen the relationship and check **Expires on**.
+
+An accepted renewal keeps the same relationship ID, approved permissions, and policy snapshot. The new expiration is **renewal acceptance time + the lifetime stored in the active relationship**. It isn't the old expiration date plus another full lifetime.
+
+For example, a relationship with a 30-day lifetime expires on November 19. If renewal is accepted on November 10 at 12:00 UTC, the new expiration is December 10 at 12:00 UTC, not December 19.
+
+Submitting or rejecting a renewal doesn't change the current expiration. After rejection, the governing tenant can request renewal again while the relationship remains active.
+
+## Monitor expiration and notifications
+
+The **Overview** page shows relationships due to expire within 30 days. A tenant that both governs and is governed has separate expiration cards for each direction. A warning doesn't itself terminate a relationship, and it can remain visible while renewal awaits approval.
+
+Tenant Governance targets the following recipients for expiration and renewal notifications:
+
+| Notification | Recipients |
+| --- | --- |
+| Expiration reminders | Global Administrator recipients in both tenants. |
+| Renewal request awaiting approval | Global Administrator recipients in the governed tenant. |
+| Renewal approved or rejected | Global Administrator recipients in the governing tenant. |
+| Expiration or termination completion | Global Administrator recipients in both tenants. |
+
+Review **Expires on** and pending requests in the admin center rather than relying only on email. A role assignment doesn't by itself provision a mailbox. The recipient roles in this table describe notification routing, not a requirement to use Global Administrator for the setup steps.
+
+## Understand expiration and cleanup
+
+If renewal isn't accepted before expiration, the relationship is automatically terminated. Its Microsoft Graph status is `terminated`, not a separate `expired` state. An old renewal request can't reactivate a terminated relationship.
+
+Cleanup removes access that was provided only through the terminated relationship and preserves access required by other relationships.
+
+| Resource | Cleanup behavior |
+| --- | --- |
+| Delegated role assignments | Remove assignments used only by the terminated relationship. Preserve assignments required by another relationship. The source group and its membership aren't removed. |
+| Applications and permissions | Remove relationship-exclusive grants and injected applications that qualify for cleanup. Preserve shared or preexisting applications, grants required by surviving relationships, unrelated or manually configured grants, and the source application registration. |
+| Cross-tenant access settings | Disable the service-provider setting when no other relationship for the same tenant pair needs GDAP access. Preserve unrelated partner and B2B settings; don't delete the entire partner policy. |
+
+An application remaining visible doesn't necessarily mean the terminated relationship still grants access. Review the actual role assignments and permission grants, and use a fresh sign-in when verifying access.
+
+## Reconnect after a relationship ends
+
+Create a new approved relationship instead of renewing the terminated relationship.
+
+1. Confirm that the governing tenant is eligible to send a request. Use a valid invitation or another qualifying basis, such as a related-tenant billing signal. Otherwise, have the governed tenant send a new invitation.
+1. Send a new **Initial** governance request with the intended template.
+1. Have the governed tenant review and accept the request.
+1. Verify the active relationship and its expiration.
+
+Expired or manually terminated relationships don't appear in the **Governed tenants** tab within **Request to govern**. This doesn't mean their records are removed from every relationship view.
+
+## Limitations
+
+- Relationships created automatically during add-on tenant creation are excluded from expiration. A lifetime in the default template's policy snapshot doesn't by itself create an expiration date or schedule expiration for that flow.
+- Renewal doesn't adopt a newer template or change permissions. Use a new **Initial** request with the same template ID to update an active relationship.
+- A pending renewal doesn't preserve access beyond the existing deadline.
+
+## Troubleshooting
+
+| Issue | What to check |
+| --- | --- |
+| Editing a template didn't change expiration | Send a new **Initial** request using the same template ID, and have the governed tenant accept it. |
+| Renewal is pending but the warning remains | The current expiration still applies until the governed tenant approves renewal. |
+| An expired relationship can't be renewed | Reconnect using a new governance request and the applicable invitation or eligibility requirements. |
+| Access remains after termination | Check whether another active relationship or an unrelated grant still provides that access. |
+| A setup or renewal operation fails | Record the tenant context, relationship/request ID, UTC time, and error or correlation ID for support. Don't include access tokens or credentials. |
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Governance relationships](governance-relationships.md).
+- [Governance policy templates](governance-policy-templates.md).
+- [Update a governance relationship](how-to-update-governance-relationship.md).
+- [Terminate a governance relationship](how-to-terminate-governance-relationship.md).

@@ -0,0 +1,112 @@
+---
+title: Set up multi-tier governance relationships (Preview)
+description: Learn how a Microsoft Entra tenant can be governed by another tenant while governing downstream tenants, with independent approvals and permissions.
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/11/2026
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+# Customer intent: As a tenant administrator, I want to set up multi-tier governance without granting inherited access across the tenant chain.
+---
+
+# Set up multi-tier governance relationships (Preview)
+
+Multi-tier governance lets a Microsoft Entra tenant be governed by another tenant while governing its own downstream tenants. For example, a central IT tenant can govern a regional tenant that separately governs project tenants.
+
+Each direct relationship has its own approval, permissions, policy snapshot, and lifecycle. Multi-tier governance uses existing governance policy templates, invitations, and requests. You don't create a separate hierarchy object.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> Access doesn't flow through a chain. If tenant A governs tenant B and tenant B governs tenant C, users in A don't automatically gain access to C. A needs a separately approved direct relationship with C.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Have the **Tenant Governance Administrator** role in each tenant where you perform setup or approval.
+- Review [Tenant Governance licensing](licensing.md) for each governing tenant.
+- Keep independent administrative access in every participating tenant.
+- Prepare role-assignable security groups in each governing tenant and governance policy templates that define only the required delegated roles and applications.
+- Use separate browser profiles for the tenants, or verify the current tenant ID each time you switch.
+
+## Example: Central, regional, and project tenants
+
+This walkthrough creates **A governs B** and **B governs C**. The arrows `A -> B -> C` describe separate, directional relationships.
+
+| Tenant | Preparation |
+| --- | --- |
+| A: central IT | A role-assignable group named `A-Admins-for-B` and an A-owned template defining the access B will approve. |
+| B: regional IT | An administrator to approve A's request, plus a separate group named `B-Admins-for-C` and a B-owned template for C. |
+| C: project | An administrator to review and accept B's request. C doesn't grant access to A's group by approving B. |
+
+You can establish A-to-B or B-to-C first. Each relationship is approved independently.
+
+## Establish A-to-B
+
+Use the standard governance handshake to establish A's access to B.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) in A.
+1. Browse to **Tenant governance** > **Templates**. Create a template that maps `A-Admins-for-B` to the required Microsoft Entra roles.
+1. In A, enable receiving invitations under **Tenant governance** > **Settings**.
+1. In B, browse to **Tenant governance** > **Governing tenants** > **Sent invitations** and send an invitation to A.
+1. In A, open **Governed tenants** > **Received invitations**. Send a governance request to B using the A-to-B template.
+1. In B, open **Governing tenants** > **Received requests**, review the permissions, and accept the request.
+1. Verify that the relationship is **Active** in both tenants. A lists B under **Governed tenants**, and B lists A under **Governing tenants**.
+1. Disable receiving invitations in A when you no longer need it.
+
+If the pair qualifies for the two-step handshake, follow [Set up a governance relationship](how-to-set-up-governance-relationship.md) without the invitation step. Check that eligibility separately for each pair.
+
+## Establish B-to-C
+
+Keep A-to-B active. Use B's own authorized administrator account to establish B-to-C; don't assume that A's delegated access in B provides the permissions needed for this operation.
+
+1. In B, create a template under **Tenant governance** > **Templates**. Map `B-Admins-for-C` to the roles C will approve.
+1. In B, enable receiving invitations under **Tenant governance** > **Settings**.
+1. In C, open **Governing tenants** > **Sent invitations** and send an invitation to B.
+1. In B, open **Governed tenants** > **Received invitations** and send C a request using the B-to-C template.
+1. In C, open **Governing tenants** > **Received requests**, review the permissions, and accept.
+1. Verify that B-to-C is **Active** and has its own relationship ID and accepted policy snapshot.
+1. Disable receiving invitations in B when you no longer need it.
+
+In B, A now appears under **Governing tenants** and C under **Governed tenants**.
+
+## Verify permissions and visibility
+
+An active member of `A-Admins-for-B` can use the roles approved in B. An active member of `B-Admins-for-C` can use the roles approved in C. Membership in A's group doesn't grant access to C through the chain.
+
+| Tenant context | Direct relationships in this example |
+| --- | --- |
+| A | A-to-B. A doesn't automatically see B-to-C or gain C as a governed tenant. |
+| B | A-to-B and B-to-C. |
+| C | B-to-C. |
+
+If A also needs to administer C, establish a separate A-to-C relationship using an A-owned template and C's approval. That relationship has its own ID and permissions; it doesn't change B-to-C.
+
+Reciprocal relationships, such as A-to-B and B-to-A, also require separate approval for each direction. The same independent-approval and no-inherited-access rules apply to cycles.
+
+## Manage each relationship independently
+
+Updating a template doesn't silently update accepted relationships. Use the existing [request and approval process](how-to-update-governance-relationship.md) to apply new terms to the affected relationship.
+
+If you configure [expiration and renewal](how-to-manage-relationship-expiration.md), each direct relationship retains its own lifetime. Renewing or expiring A-to-B doesn't renew or expire B-to-C.
+
+To terminate A-to-B:
+
+1. In A, open **Tenant governance** > **Governed tenants**, select B, and select **Terminate governance**.
+1. In B, open **Governing tenants**, filter **Relationship status** to **Termination requested**, select A, and select **Confirm termination**.
+1. Verify that A-to-B is **Terminated** and B-to-C remains **Active**.
+
+B can instead terminate A-to-B directly as its governed tenant. That action doesn't require A's approval. For details, see [Terminate a governance relationship](how-to-terminate-governance-relationship.md).
+
+Cleanup removes relationship-exclusive access and preserves resources still required by other relationships or unrelated grants. Keep local administrative access available when testing termination.
+
+## Troubleshooting
+
+| Issue | What to check |
+| --- | --- |
+| A can't administer C through B | This is expected. Establish and approve a direct A-to-C relationship if that access is required. |
+| An invitation or request isn't available | Check the current tenant, receiving-invitation setting, invitation validity, and request validity. Invitations are valid for 30 days and requests for 14 days. |
+| A relationship isn't visible in another tenant's list | Each tenant sees its own direct relationships. Multi-tier governance doesn't expose every downstream relationship. |
+| Ending A-to-B appears to affect B-to-C | Verify the two relationship IDs, the approved groups, and any independent access required by the users. Record the tenant context and error details for support. |
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Governance relationships](governance-relationships.md).
+- [Set up a governance relationship](how-to-set-up-governance-relationship.md).
+- [Use delegated administration](how-to-delegated-administration.md).
+- [Manage relationship expiration and renewal](how-to-manage-relationship-expiration.md).
