+---
+title: Call APIs as a user in a fleet with ASP.NET Core
+description: Use the On-Behalf-Of flow with the routed agent's identity to call APIs for a signed-in user from a shared ASP.NET Core runtime.
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/05/2026
+ms.reviewer: dastrock
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+
+#customer-intent: As a developer building an agent hosting platform with ASP.NET Core, I want agents in my fleet to call APIs on behalf of the signed-in user with their own agent identity.
+---
+
+# Call APIs as a user in a fleet with ASP.NET Core
+
+After the runtime routes a user's request to an agent, the agent can call APIs for that user with the On-Behalf-Of (OBO) flow. Pass the routed agent's identity to `WithAgentIdentity`. The downstream token represents both the signed-in user and that agent.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Complete [Authenticate users and route requests to agents in a fleet with ASP.NET Core](aspnet-core-fleet-authenticate-users.md).
+- Delegated permissions for the target API, [granted to the agent identity](grant-agent-access-microsoft-365.md) or [inherited from the blueprint](set-up-blueprint-agent-fleet.md#optionally-configure-inheritable-permissions).
+
+## Get a token for the signed-in user
+
+Add a method to `FleetTokenService`:
+
+```csharp
+using System.Security.Claims;
+
+public async Task<string> CreateAuthorizationHeaderForUserAsync(
+    string agentId, string scope, ClaimsPrincipal user)
+{
+    AgentRegistration registration = await GetRegistrationAsync(agentId);
+
+    var options = new AuthorizationHeaderProviderOptions()
+        .WithAgentIdentity(registration.AgentIdentityId);
+
+    return await authorizationHeaderProvider
+        .CreateAuthorizationHeaderForUserAsync([scope], options, user);
+}
+```
+
+The `user` argument is the authenticated `HttpContext.User`. *Microsoft.Identity.Web* uses the user's incoming access token as the OBO assertion.
+
+## Call the API
+
+Call the method after the routing and access checks from the previous article pass:
+
+Replace the previous article's placeholder mapping for `POST /agents/{agentId}/messages` with this mapping; don't register both routes. Replace the sample API URL and delegated scope with values from the same downstream API registration.
+
+```csharp
+using System.Net.Http.Headers;
+using Microsoft.Identity.Web.Resource;
+
+app.MapPost("/agents/{agentId}/messages", async (
+    string agentId,
+    HttpContext context,
+    IAgentDirectory directory,
+    IAgentAccessPolicy accessPolicy,
+    FleetTokenService fleetTokenService,
+    IHttpClientFactory httpClientFactory) =>
+{
+    context.VerifyUserHasAnyAcceptedScope("access_agent");
+
+    if (await directory.FindAsync(agentId) is null
+        || !await accessPolicy.CanUseAgentAsync(context.User, agentId))
+    {
+        return Results.NotFound();
+    }
+
+    string authorizationHeader = await fleetTokenService
+        .CreateAuthorizationHeaderForUserAsync(
+            agentId, "api://<custom-api-client-id>/<delegated-scope>", context.User);
+
+    HttpClient client = httpClientFactory.CreateClient();
+    client.DefaultRequestHeaders.Authorization =
+        AuthenticationHeaderValue.Parse(authorizationHeader);
+
+    using HttpResponseMessage response =
+        await client.GetAsync("https://api.contoso.com/user-data");
+    response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();
+
+    return Results.Content(
+        await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync(),
+        response.Content.Headers.ContentType?.ToString());
+})
+.RequireAuthorization();
+```
+
+Always use the agent ID that passed the access check. If the runtime used a different agent's identity, the downstream API would see the wrong agent acting for the user.
+
+Verify the allowed request returns the downstream API's expected user data. Repeat the denied-agent and unknown-agent checks from the previous article: both must still return `404 Not Found` without calling the API. If only the allowed request fails downstream, check the selected agent's delegated grant and the API's user authorization rather than weakening the routing policy.
+
+## Call specific resources
+
+Use the resource scopes and permission setup from the linked articles, while keeping the fleet's blueprint configuration and `AddAgentIdentities` registration. The single-instance examples omit identity overrides. For each fleet request, call `CreateAuthorizationHeaderForUserAsync` with the routed agent ID and authenticated user.
+
+| Resource | Example scope | Guidance |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Custom API | `api://<custom-api-client-id>/<delegated-scope>` | [Call a custom API as a user](aspnet-core-call-custom-api-as-user.md) |
+| Azure services | `https://storage.azure.com/user_impersonation` | [Call Azure services as a user](aspnet-core-call-azure-api-as-user.md) |
+| Microsoft Graph | `https://graph.microsoft.com/User.Read` | [Call Microsoft Graph as a user](aspnet-core-call-graph-as-user.md) |
+
+For Azure REST APIs, use the same helper with the service's delegated scope and endpoint. For example, Azure Resource Manager uses `https://management.azure.com/user_impersonation`. The signed-in user's Azure role assignments determine resource access.
+
+If you use `GraphServiceClient` instead of an HTTP authorization header, install and register it as described in the linked Graph article, but select the fleet agent on each call after the routing and access checks:
+
+```csharp
+using Microsoft.Graph;
+using Microsoft.Identity.Web;
+
+var me = await graphClient.Me.GetAsync(request =>
+    request.Options.WithAuthenticationOptions(options =>
+    {
+        options.Scopes = ["https://graph.microsoft.com/User.Read"];
+        options.User = context.User;
+        options.WithAgentIdentity(registration.AgentIdentityId);
+    }));
+```
+
+Here, `registration` is the directory entry for the agent ID that passed the access check, and `context` is the current `HttpContext`. Don't set `RequestAppToken` for OBO.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Plan an agent fleet on a shared runtime](plan-agent-fleet.md)
+- [Inheritable permissions](concept-inheritable-permissions.md)
+- [OAuth 2.0 On-Behalf-Of flow](/entra/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-on-behalf-of-flow)

diff --git a/docs/agent-id/aspnet-core-fleet-provision-agent-identities.md b/docs/agent-id/aspnet-core-fleet-provision-agent-identities.md
new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..25abe6c7255
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/agent-id/aspnet-core-fleet-provision-agent-identities.md
@@ -0,0 +1,270 @@
+---
+title: Provision agent identities for a fleet with ASP.NET Core
+description: Create an agent identity and an optional agent's user account when an agent is deployed to a shared ASP.NET Core runtime, and delete them when it's retired.
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/05/2026
+ms.reviewer: dastrock
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+
+#customer-intent: As a developer building an agent hosting platform with ASP.NET Core, I want to create an agent identity for each agent I deploy so that every agent in my fleet has its own identity.
+---
+
+# Provision agent identities for a fleet with ASP.NET Core
+
+When an agent is deployed to the fleet, the provisioning service authenticates as the agent identity blueprint and calls Microsoft Graph. It creates an agent identity and, if the agent needs one, an agent's user account. It records both in the agent directory so the runtime can select them on later token requests. When the agent is retired, the service deletes both identities.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Complete [Set up an agent identity blueprint for a fleet](set-up-blueprint-agent-fleet.md).
+- The .NET 8 SDK or later.
+- A user or group to assign as each agent's sponsor.
+- A verified domain in the tenant for agent's user account user principal names, if agents need them.
+- A persistent store for the agent directory, such as a database table.
+
+The snippets extend your ASP.NET Core provisioning service; they aren't a standalone application or a complete `Program.cs`. Implement `IAgentDirectory` with the persistent store and register that implementation before invoking `AgentProvisioner`. Keep the service's existing host startup code.
+
+## Install the packages
+
+```dotnetcli
+dotnet add package Microsoft.Identity.Web
+dotnet add package Microsoft.Identity.Web.DownstreamApi
+```
+
+## Configure the blueprint and Microsoft Graph
+
+Add the blueprint credential and two Microsoft Graph profiles to *appsettings.json*. `RequestAppToken` requests a token for the blueprint itself, not for an agent identity.
+
+```json
+{
+  "AzureAd": {
+    "Instance": "https://login.microsoftonline.com/",
+    "TenantId": "<tenant-id>",
+    "ClientId": "<agent-identity-blueprint-client-id>",
+    "ClientCredentials": [
+      {
+        "SourceType": "SignedAssertionFromManagedIdentity",
+        "ManagedIdentityClientId": "<managed-identity-client-id>"
+      }
+    ]
+  },
+  "DownstreamApis": {
+    "agent-identities": {
+      "BaseUrl": "https://graph.microsoft.com/",
+      "RelativePath": "beta/serviceprincipals/Microsoft.Graph.AgentIdentity",
+      "Scopes": [ "https://graph.microsoft.com/.default" ],
+      "RequestAppToken": true
+    },
+    "agent-users": {
+      "BaseUrl": "https://graph.microsoft.com/",
+      "RelativePath": "v1.0/users/microsoft.graph.agentUser",
+      "Scopes": [ "https://graph.microsoft.com/.default" ],
+      "RequestAppToken": true
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+[!INCLUDE [Dont use secrets](./includes/do-not-use-secrets.md)]
+
+Register the downstream APIs:
+
+```csharp
+using Microsoft.Identity.Web;
+
+var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);
+
+builder.Services
+    .AddMicrosoftIdentityWebApiAuthentication(builder.Configuration)
+    .EnableTokenAcquisitionToCallDownstreamApi()
+    .AddInMemoryTokenCaches();
+
+builder.Services.AddDownstreamApis(
+    builder.Configuration.GetSection("DownstreamApis"));
+builder.Services.AddScoped<AgentProvisioner>();
+// Register your IAgentDirectory implementation.
+```
+
+## Define the agent directory
+
+The agent directory maps the runtime's agent ID to the agent's identities. Later articles in this path use it to select the identity for each token request.
+
+```csharp
+public record AgentRegistration(
+    string AgentId,
+    string AgentIdentityId,
+    string? AgentUserId);
+
+public interface IAgentDirectory
+{
+    Task<AgentRegistration?> FindAsync(string agentId);
+    Task SaveAsync(AgentRegistration registration);
+    Task DeleteAsync(string agentId);
+}
+```
+
+| Field | Value | Used by |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `AgentId` | The runtime's own identifier for the agent. | Lookups |
+| `AgentIdentityId` | The agent identity's ID. For an agent identity, the object ID (`id`) and client ID (`appId`) are the same value. | Token requests, creating the agent's user account, and deleting the agent identity |
+| `AgentUserId` | The agent's user account object ID, or `null`. | `WithAgentUserIdentity` and deletion |
+
+## Provision an agent
+
+Call the provisioning service from the code that deploys agents, not from an endpoint that agents or users can reach.
+
+```csharp
+using System.Text.Json.Serialization;
+using Microsoft.Identity.Abstractions;
+
+public class AgentProvisioner(
+    IDownstreamApi graph,
+    IAgentDirectory directory,
+    IConfiguration configuration)
+{
+    public async Task<AgentRegistration> ProvisionAsync(
+        string agentId,
+        string displayName,
+        string sponsorUserId,
+        string? agentUserPrincipalName = null)
+    {
+        AgentRegistration registration = await directory.FindAsync(agentId)
+            ?? await CreateAgentIdentityAsync(agentId, displayName, sponsorUserId);
+
+        if (agentUserPrincipalName is not null && registration.AgentUserId is null)
+        {
+            registration = await CreateAgentUserAsync(
+                registration, displayName, agentUserPrincipalName);
+        }
+
+        return registration;
+    }
+
+    private async Task<AgentRegistration> CreateAgentIdentityAsync(
+        string agentId, string displayName, string sponsorUserId)
+    {
+        AgentIdentityResponse? identity = await graph
+            .PostForAppAsync<AgentIdentityRequest, AgentIdentityResponse>(
+                "agent-identities",
+                new AgentIdentityRequest(
+                    displayName,
+                    configuration["AzureAd:ClientId"]!,
+                    [$"https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/{sponsorUserId}"]));
+
+        var registration = new AgentRegistration(
+            agentId, identity!.Id, AgentUserId: null);
+        await directory.SaveAsync(registration);
+        return registration;
+    }
+
+    private async Task<AgentRegistration> CreateAgentUserAsync(
+        AgentRegistration registration, string displayName, string userPrincipalName)
+    {
+        AgentUserResponse? agentUser = await graph
+            .PostForAppAsync<AgentUserRequest, AgentUserResponse>(
+                "agent-users",
+                new AgentUserRequest(
+                    AccountEnabled: true,
+                    displayName,
+                    MailNickname: userPrincipalName.Split('@')[0],
+                    userPrincipalName,
+                    IdentityParentId: registration.AgentIdentityId));
+
+        registration = registration with { AgentUserId = agentUser!.Id };
+        await directory.SaveAsync(registration);
+        return registration;
+    }
+}
+
+public record AgentIdentityRequest(
+    [property: JsonPropertyName("displayName")] string DisplayName,
+    [property: JsonPropertyName("agentIdentityBlueprintId")] string AgentIdentityBlueprintId,
+    [property: JsonPropertyName("sponsors@odata.bind")] string[] Sponsors)
+{
+    [JsonPropertyName("@odata.type")]
+    public string ODataType => "#Microsoft.Graph.AgentIdentity";
+}
+
+public record AgentIdentityResponse(
+    [property: JsonPropertyName("id")] string Id);
+
+public record AgentUserRequest(
+    [property: JsonPropertyName("accountEnabled")] bool AccountEnabled,
+    [property: JsonPropertyName("displayName")] string DisplayName,
+    [property: JsonPropertyName("mailNickname")] string MailNickname,
+    [property: JsonPropertyName("userPrincipalName")] string UserPrincipalName,
+    [property: JsonPropertyName("identityParentId")] string IdentityParentId);
+
+public record AgentUserResponse(
+    [property: JsonPropertyName("id")] string Id);
+```
+
+The service saves the agent directory entry after each Microsoft Graph call and reuses saved identities on retries. This isn't an atomic transaction with Microsoft Graph. Serialize provisioning for each agent ID, and reconcile a successful Graph call whose response or directory write failed before retrying, to avoid duplicate identities.
+
+Pass `agentUserPrincipalName` only for agents that need an agent's user account. Use a verified domain and a unique alias for each agent. Creating the account doesn't assign licenses, a mailbox, or team membership. For those steps, see [Use an agent's user account with Microsoft 365](agent-user-oauth-flow.md#provision-access).
+
+A new agent identity can take a short time to become available for permission assignments, agent-user creation, and token requests. If Microsoft Graph or the token service reports that the newly created identity or the agent user's parent can't be found, retry with bounded backoff and reuse the saved registration. A new agent user can also take time to be recognized as the principal in a consent grant. Use the same bounded retry approach if Microsoft Graph explicitly reports that the new principal can't be found.
+
+After granting permissions, allow time for those grants to appear in a newly acquired token; retrying with the same cached token doesn't pick up new grants. Don't treat an authorization failure as successful provisioning.
+
+Before continuing, read the saved registration through `IAgentDirectory.FindAsync` using the runtime's agent ID. Confirm it contains the returned agent identity ID and, when requested, the agent user ID. This verifies the directory handoff; it doesn't yet prove downstream API access.
+
+## Grant the agent access
+
+After the agent identity exists, grant it the access that this agent needs. Grant application permissions, delegated permissions, Azure role assignments, and access to other resources directly to the agent identity. Each agent's access then stays separate and visible on its own identity.
+
+- [Grant application permissions](grant-application-permissions-agent-identity.md)
+- [Grant delegated permissions](grant-agent-access-microsoft-365.md)
+
+Permissions that are [inherited from the blueprint](set-up-blueprint-agent-fleet.md#optionally-configure-inheritable-permissions) apply to the new agent identity without another grant.
+
+## Retire an agent
+
+Stop routing new requests and scheduling work for the agent, and let its in-flight operations finish before deleting its identities. Retire only that agent's resources; don't delete the shared blueprint or runtime credential while other agents still use them.
+
+Delete the agent's user account before the agent identity, and then remove the agent directory entry:
+
+```csharp
+public async Task RetireAsync(string agentId)
+{
+    AgentRegistration? registration = await directory.FindAsync(agentId);
+    if (registration is null)
+    {
+        return;
+    }
+
+    if (registration.AgentUserId is not null)
+    {
+        await graph.DeleteForAppAsync<string>(
+            "agent-users",
+            null!,
+            options => options.RelativePath += $"/{registration.AgentUserId}");
+    }
+
+    await graph.DeleteForAppAsync<string>(
+        "agent-identities",
+        null!,
+        options => options.RelativePath =
+            $"beta/serviceprincipals/{registration.AgentIdentityId}");
+
+    await directory.DeleteAsync(agentId);
+}
+```
+
+Add `RetireAsync` to the `AgentProvisioner` class. Deleted agent identities can be restored for a limited time. For details, see [Delete and restore agent identity objects](howto-delete-agent-identity.md).
+
+Use the single-type `DeleteForAppAsync<TInput>` overload because Microsoft Graph returns `204 No Content`; the two-type overload tries to deserialize a response body. In production, make retirement retry-safe by treating `404 Not Found` as already deleted and reconciling the directory after partial failures.
+
+## Use Agent 365 provisioning instead
+
+If agents are created through Agent 365, Agent 365 creates the agent identity. Instead of calling Microsoft Graph, listen for Agent 365 agent provisioning events, read the agent identity ID from each event, and save an `AgentRegistration` in the agent directory. For event details, see the [Agent 365 developer documentation](/microsoft-agent-365/developer/).
+
+## Next step
+
+[Call APIs as an agent in a fleet with ASP.NET Core](aspnet-core-fleet-call-apis-as-agent.md)
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Create and delete agent identities](create-delete-agent-identities.md)
+- [Create and delete an agent's user account](create-delete-agent-user-account.md)
+- [Plan an agent fleet on a shared runtime](plan-agent-fleet.md)

@@ -0,0 +1,90 @@
+---
+title: Call APIs as a user from a local agent (preview)
+description: Use a local agent to call a protected API for the signed-in user.
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/05/2026
+ms.reviewer: dastrock
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+
+#customer-intent: As a developer, I want my local agent to call a protected API with the permissions of the signed-in user.
+---
+
+# Call APIs as a user from a local agent (preview)
+
+After the local agent [signs in a user](authenticate-local-agent.md), request the delegated scopes required by the protected API. MSAL acquires an access token for the signed-in user and caches it for later calls. The API authorizes the request based on the user, the client Agent ID, and the scopes in the token.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> Local agent authentication is in preview. This preview is provided without a service-level agreement and isn't recommended for production workloads. Some features might be unsupported or have constrained capabilities. For more information, see [Universal License Terms for Online Services](https://www.microsoft.com/licensing/terms/product/ForOnlineServices/all).
+
+- Complete [Sign in users from a local agent](authenticate-local-agent.md). The MSAL.NET snippets here continue in the same application and reuse its public-client application variable, `app`.
+- Obtain the target API's delegated scope and endpoint from its owner. Replace `<resource-client-id>`, `<delegated-scope>`, and `<resource-url>` with values for that API.
+- Arrange consent with a tenant administrator if the requested permission or tenant policy requires it.
+
+## Request the API scope
+
+Request only the delegated scopes needed for the operation:
+
+```csharp
+var scopes = new[] { "api://<resource-client-id>/<delegated-scope>" };
+```
+
+For Microsoft Graph, use Microsoft Graph scopes such as `User.Read` or `Files.Read`.
+
+The resource owner controls which delegated permissions are available. A user or administrator must consent before the agent can use them.
+
+## Acquire a token
+
+Try the MSAL cache before prompting the user again:
+
+```csharp
+AuthenticationResult result;
+var account = (await app.GetAccountsAsync()).FirstOrDefault();
+
+try
+{
+    result = await app.AcquireTokenSilent(scopes, account).ExecuteAsync();
+}
+catch (MsalUiRequiredException)
+{
+    result = await app.AcquireTokenInteractive(scopes).ExecuteAsync();
+}
+```
+
+Don't inspect or modify the access token in the agent. Treat it as an opaque credential for the target API.
+
+## Call the API
+
+Send the token in the HTTP `Authorization` header:
+
+The snippet assumes your application supplies an `HttpClient` named `httpClient`. Keep the token acquisition and API call in the same operation so the call uses the resulting `result.AccessToken`.
+
+```csharp
+using System.Net.Http.Headers;
+
+using var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, "<resource-url>");
+request.Headers.Authorization =
+    new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", result.AccessToken);
+
+using var response = await httpClient.SendAsync(request);
+response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();
+```
+
+Request a token for each resource. A token issued for one API, such as Microsoft Graph, can't be used with another API.
+
+Local public clients support delegated access only. They can't use client credentials to obtain app-only tokens.
+
+Verify that the API returns its expected response for the signed-in user; successful sign-in alone doesn't prove API access. For `401 Unauthorized`, check that the token was requested for this API and that the API's validation settings match its registration. For `403 Forbidden`, check delegated consent and the user's access to the requested resource. If consent requires administrator approval, hand off the client ID, target resource, and requested scopes instead of repeatedly prompting the user.
+
+## Next steps
+
+- For a custom API, configure the API to [validate Agent ID tokens](how-to-validate-agent-tokens-downstream-api.md).
+- For Microsoft Graph permissions, see the [Microsoft Graph permissions reference](/graph/permissions-reference).
+- For consent guidance, see [Permissions and consent in the Microsoft identity platform](/entra/identity-platform/permissions-consent-overview).
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Microsoft identity platform and OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow](/entra/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-auth-code-flow)
+- [Authenticate a local agent with Microsoft Entra ID](authenticate-local-agent.md)

@@ -0,0 +1,62 @@
+---
+title: Single-instance OAuth (preview)
+description: Understand direct authentication with a single-instance Agent ID and find the local, ASP.NET Core, and sidecar walkthroughs.
+ms.topic: concept-article
+ms.date: 11/06/2026
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+# Customer intent: As an agent developer, I want to understand how my single-instance Agent ID authenticates and find the walkthrough for my platform.
+---
+
+# Single-instance agent authentication overview (preview)
+
+A single-instance Agent ID (preview) authenticates directly with the client ID it shares with its blueprint. It uses the same authentication-library APIs as a regular application. It doesn't acquire an intermediate blueprint impersonation token or send `fmi_path`.
+
+The blueprint and Agent ID have different directory object IDs. Configure credentials on the blueprint, grant permissions to the Agent ID, and use their shared OAuth client ID for token requests. A single-instance blueprint has no blueprint principal.
+
+## Choose an integration path
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> Single-instance agent identities are in preview. This preview is provided without a service-level agreement and isn't recommended for production workloads. Some features might be unsupported or have constrained capabilities. For more information, see [Universal License Terms for Online Services](https://www.microsoft.com/licensing/terms/product/ForOnlineServices/all).
+
+Choose a walkthrough based on where your agent runs. If you're building a platform that hosts separate agents for teams or customers, follow the fleet guidance.
+
+| Environment | Walkthrough |
+| --- | --- |
+| Local public client | [Sign in users from a local agent](authenticate-local-agent.md). |
+| Cloud agent with ASP.NET Core | [Call a custom API as an agent](call-api-custom.md). |
+| Cloud agent with the Auth SDK sidecar | [Configure the Auth SDK sidecar](microsoft-entra-sdk-for-agent-identities.md). |
+| Shared runtime with many identities | [Plan an agent fleet](plan-agent-fleet.md). |
+
+Authentication requires a provisioned single-instance Agent ID and a tenant enabled for authentication. Successful Microsoft Graph provisioning alone doesn't establish authentication enablement. For setup, see [Create a single-instance agent identity](create-single-instance-agent.md).
+
+## Sign in a user
+
+Local public clients use authorization code flow with PKCE and no client credential. Confidential clients use a credential on the blueprint. An authentication library handles state, PKCE, token caching, and refresh rather than requiring hand-built protocol requests.
+
+For local sign-in and refresh behavior, follow [Sign in users from a local agent](authenticate-local-agent.md). For a front end that calls a hosted agent API, follow [Authenticate users to an ASP.NET Core agent API](aspnet-core-authenticate-users.md) or [Authenticate users with the sidecar](sidecar-authenticate-users.md).
+
+## Grant application permissions
+
+Declaring permissions on the blueprint doesn't grant them. An administrator grants application permissions to the agent identity. Browser-based admin consent requires a registered `web` redirect URI, even for an unattended agent.
+
+For the consent request and assignment verification, see [Grant application permissions in the cloud-agent walkthrough](call-api-custom.md#grant-application-permissions). For Microsoft Graph, see [Grant application permissions to an agent identity](grant-application-permissions-agent-identity.md).
+
+## Request an app-only token
+
+The standard client credentials flow uses the shared client ID, the blueprint credential, and the resource's `/.default` scope. It doesn't use an Agent ID override.
+
+Follow [Call a custom API with ASP.NET Core](call-api-custom.md#call-the-api) for `CreateAuthorizationHeaderForAppAsync`, or [Call a custom API with the sidecar](sidecar-call-custom-api-as-agent.md) for the corresponding HTTP endpoint. For protocol parameters, see [OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow](~/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-client-creds-grant-flow.md).
+
+## Call a downstream API on behalf of a user
+
+OBO exchanges an incoming user access token for a downstream token. The incoming token must target the agent's shared client ID, not Microsoft Graph or another resource. The agent authenticates with its blueprint credential. The downstream API evaluates the user's delegated access.
+
+Two separate grants are required: front-end access to the agent's exposed scope and the agent's delegated access to the downstream API. During preview, grant front-end access through Microsoft Graph as described in [Grant the upstream client access](aspnet-core-authenticate-users.md#grant-the-upstream-client-access).
+
+Follow [Call a custom API as a user with ASP.NET Core](aspnet-core-call-custom-api-as-user.md) or [Call a custom API as a user with the sidecar](sidecar-call-custom-api-as-user.md). These walkthroughs use standard OBO, without an intermediate blueprint exchange. For protocol parameters, see [OAuth 2.0 On-Behalf-Of flow](~/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-on-behalf-of-flow.md).
+
+## Verify access
+
+A successful token response establishes token issuance, not authorization at the API. API authorization depends on a valid signature, issuer, audience, and lifetime, plus the required scope or role. Requests with insufficient permissions are rejected. Tokens, certificate assertions, and private keys aren't safe diagnostic output.
+
+For API-side validation, see [Secure a web API with Microsoft Entra ID](how-to-validate-agent-tokens-downstream-api.md).

diff --git a/docs/agent-id/choose-agent-integration-path.md b/docs/agent-id/choose-agent-integration-path.md
new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..39be20aee79
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/agent-id/choose-agent-integration-path.md
@@ -0,0 +1,135 @@
+---
+title: Choose an integration path for an agent
+description: Compare ways to add Microsoft Entra authentication to an agent. Choose a path based on its platform, language, and hosting model.
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+ms.topic: concept-article
+ms.date: 11/06/2026
+ms.reviewer: dastrock
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1013
+
+#customer-intent: As an agent developer, I want to choose an integration path that supports my platform, language, hosting model, and authentication requirements.
+---
+
+# Choose an integration path for an agent
+
+Choose an integration path based on where the agent runs and what it needs to do. Agents built on common platforms often have a built-in Microsoft Entra integration. Local agents run on end-user devices and can't store a credential, so they use OAuth public client flows. Cloud agents run in hosted environments and can protect a credential.
+
+Start with your scenario. Each tutorial prescribes the identity setup for that task; you don't need to choose an identity configuration first.
+
+## Start with your scenario
+
+Follow the path that describes what you're building. Multiple replicas of the same agent still use the cloud-agent path.
+
+| What you're building | Start here |
+| --- | --- |
+| An agent on Foundry, Copilot Studio, or another supported platform. | [Use your platform's integration](#common-agent-platforms). |
+| A cloud agent that calls APIs as itself or for signed-in users. | [Build a cloud agent](#cloud-agents), using ASP.NET Core or the Auth SDK sidecar. |
+| A platform that hosts separate agents for teams or customers, each with its own identity and permissions. | [Build an agent fleet](#agent-fleets). |
+| An agent installed on an end-user device. | [Build a local agent](#local-agents). |
+
+For an agent you provision yourself, the tutorial identifies the required administrator approvals and registration outputs. Arrange that handoff before coding, and [record the identifiers your scenario uses](key-concepts.md#record-the-identifiers-for-your-scenario) during setup.
+
+## Common agent platforms
+
+Use this path when the agent is built on a platform with a documented Microsoft Entra Agent ID integration. The platform handles most of the authentication implementation, so prefer it over the other paths when one is available. Supported flows and setup steps vary by platform.
+
+| Integration path | When to use it | Authenticate users | Call APIs as agent | Call APIs as signed-in user | Call APIs as agent's user account | Guidance |
+| --- | --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | --- |
+| Microsoft Foundry | The agent is built with the current Foundry agent model. Foundry creates and manages the agent identity. | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | [Use Agent ID with Microsoft Foundry](integrate-microsoft-foundry-agent.md) |
+| Copilot Studio | The agent is built in Copilot Studio. Copilot Studio creates and manages the agent identity. | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | [Use Agent ID with Copilot Studio](integrate-copilot-studio-agent.md) |
+| Amazon Bedrock | The agent runs in a container on Amazon Bedrock and uses the Auth SDK sidecar. | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | [Secure an Amazon Bedrock agent](integrate-aws-bedrock-agent.md) |
+| Amazon Web Services | The agent runs on AWS and uses an AWS workload identity for app-only access. | No | Yes | No | No | [Use an AWS workload identity](integrate-aws-agent.md) |
+| Google Cloud Platform | The agent runs on Google Cloud and uses a Google service account for app-only access. | No | Yes | No | No | [Use a Google Cloud workload identity](integrate-google-cloud-agent.md) |
+| n8n | The agent is built as an n8n workflow and uses the Agent ID community node. | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | [Secure an n8n agent](integrate-n8n-agent.md) |
+
+## Local agents
+
+A local agent runs on an endpoint device and can't securely store a client credential. Use this path when your agent signs in users through a browser and calls APIs on their behalf.
+
+| Integration path | When to use it | Authenticate users | Call APIs as agent | Call APIs as signed-in user | Call APIs as agent's user account | Guidance |
+| --- | --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | --- |
+| MSAL.NET | The agent is built with C# and .NET and signs in users on an endpoint device. | Yes | No | Yes | No | [Sign in users from a local agent](authenticate-local-agent.md) |
+| Microsoft Entra Client ID Metadata Document (CIMD) support (preview) | The client is distributed or connects to independently operated servers where pre-registration isn't practical. | Yes | No | Yes | No | [Configure a CIMD client](configure-client-id-metadata-document.md) |
+
+### Sign in users with MSAL.NET
+
+Use *Microsoft.Identity.Client* for agents built with C# and .NET that run on endpoint devices. MSAL handles authorization code flow with PKCE, opens the system browser for sign-in, and caches the account and tokens.
+
+Start with [Sign in users from a local agent](authenticate-local-agent.md), then follow the local agent guidance to call APIs as the signed-in user.
+
+### Use a Client ID Metadata Document
+
+A Client ID Metadata Document (CIMD) lets a client use a public HTTPS URL as its `client_id` instead of a registered client ID. Use it when the same distributed client connects to independently operated authorization servers and pre-registration with each isn't practical—for example, an MCP client that connects to third-party MCP servers.
+
+The client publishes a JSON document at a stable HTTPS URL. Microsoft Entra ID retrieves the document and uses its redirect URIs and settings in place of a registered application. CIMD supports authorization code flow with PKCE only. CIMD clients can't use client credentials to obtain app-only tokens.
+
+For metadata requirements and protocol steps, see [Configure a client to use a Client ID Metadata Document](configure-client-id-metadata-document.md).
+
+## Cloud agents
+
+A cloud agent runs in a hosted environment. Choose a path based on the language and hosting environment, then follow the task for the kind of API call you need. Choose ASP.NET Core for a C# application or the sidecar for another language in a containerized environment.
+
+If you're building a platform that hosts separate agents for different teams or customers, use the [agent fleet paths](#agent-fleets). Running multiple replicas of the same agent doesn't by itself require a fleet.
+
+| Integration path | When to use it | Authenticate users | Call APIs as agent | Call APIs as signed-in user | Call APIs as agent's user account | Guidance |
+| --- | --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | --- |
+| ASP.NET Core (Microsoft.Identity.Web) | The agent is built with C# and ASP.NET Core. | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | [Call an API as an agent](call-api-custom.md) or [call a custom API as a signed-in user](aspnet-core-call-custom-api-as-user.md) |
+| Microsoft Entra ID Auth SDK sidecar | The agent uses another language and runs in a containerized environment. | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | [Authentication with the Auth SDK sidecar](authentication-with-auth-sdk-sidecar.md) |
+| Workload identity federation | The agent runs in a supported cloud environment and needs app-only access without an SDK or stored credential. | No | Yes | No | No | [Workload identity federation](~/workload-id/workload-identity-federation.md) |
+| Agent 365 SDK | The agent needs deeper integration with Microsoft 365 channels and services. | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | [Agent 365 SDK documentation](/microsoft-agent-365/developer/) |
+
+### Use ASP.NET Core with Microsoft.Identity.Web
+
+Use *Microsoft.Identity.Web* for agents built with C# and ASP.NET Core. It validates incoming access tokens and gets tokens to call APIs as the agent or on behalf of signed-in users. For a signed-in user's request to a custom API, start with [Call a custom API as a user with ASP.NET Core](aspnet-core-call-custom-api-as-user.md). For an app-only call, see [Call a custom API as an agent with ASP.NET Core](call-api-custom.md).
+
+### Use the Microsoft Entra ID Auth SDK sidecar
+
+The sidecar pattern runs the Microsoft Entra ID Auth SDK as a companion container next to the agent. The agent calls the sidecar to validate incoming tokens or request authorization headers for API calls. The sidecar holds the Microsoft Entra credential and handles token acquisition.
+
+Use the sidecar for:
+
+- Agents built in languages other than C# and .NET.
+- Containerized agents on Docker or Kubernetes.
+- Cloud or on-premises environments that can run a companion container.
+- Teams that want to keep Microsoft Entra credentials and token handling out of the agent code.
+
+The sidecar requires a containerized environment and adds a second service to deploy and manage. For architecture, a diagram, and security guidance, see [Authentication with the Microsoft Entra ID Auth SDK sidecar](authentication-with-auth-sdk-sidecar.md).
+
+### Use workload identity federation
+
+Workload identity federation exchanges a token from an external identity provider for a Microsoft Entra token. Use it when an agent runs in a supported cloud environment, can't run the sidecar, and needs to call APIs as the agent.
+
+This path:
+
+- Doesn't require an authentication SDK or stored client credential.
+- Requires a federated identity credential in Microsoft Entra.
+- Requires a platform that can issue a supported OpenID Connect (OIDC) token.
+- Supports app-only access. It doesn't authenticate users or support calls as a signed-in user or an agent's user account.
+
+The following diagram shows an agent exchanging a token from its cloud identity provider for a Microsoft Entra access token.
+
+:::image type="content" source="media/configure-third-party-agents/federation-pattern-token-exchange.png" alt-text="Diagram that shows a third-party platform agent exchanging an OpenID Connect token through Microsoft Entra Agent ID to access an API." lightbox="media/configure-third-party-agents/federation-pattern-token-exchange.png" border="false":::
+
+For supported issuers and configuration steps, see [workload identity federation](~/workload-id/workload-identity-federation.md).
+
+### Use the Agent 365 SDK
+
+Use the Agent 365 SDK to extend agents with identity, notifications, security, and governed access to Microsoft 365 data. The SDK supports all Agent ID authentication flows. For supported languages, channels, and authentication options, see the [Agent 365 SDK documentation](/microsoft-agent-365/developer/).
+
+## Agent fleets
+
+An agent fleet is a set of agents hosted on a shared cloud runtime, such as a platform where teams or customers deploy their own agents. Choose this path when each agent needs its own identity and access to resources.
+
+Use the advanced fleet paths when your runtime hosts agents that are added and removed over time, or your scenario needs an agent's dedicated user account. For the design and setup choices, see [Plan an agent fleet on a shared runtime](plan-agent-fleet.md).
+
+| Integration path | When to use it | Authenticate users | Call APIs as agent | Call APIs as signed-in user | Call APIs as agent's user account | Guidance |
+| --- | --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | --- |
+| ASP.NET Core (Microsoft.Identity.Web) | The runtime is built with C# and ASP.NET Core. | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | [Provision agent identities with ASP.NET Core](aspnet-core-fleet-provision-agent-identities.md) |
+| Microsoft Entra ID Auth SDK sidecar | The runtime uses another language and runs in a containerized environment. | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | [Provision agent identities with the Auth SDK sidecar](sidecar-fleet-provision-agent-identities.md) |
+
+## Use OAuth protocols directly
+
+Implement OAuth protocols directly only when no supported platform integration or Microsoft SDK meets the requirements. Direct implementations require expertise in token validation, credential protection, token caching, and OAuth security.
+
+Use a supported OAuth or OpenID Connect library instead of constructing protocol requests by hand. For flow selection and protocol references, see [Choose an authentication protocol for an agent](agent-oauth-protocols.md).

index 00000000000..7040fb005bd
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/agent-id/client-id-metadata-documents.md
@@ -0,0 +1,120 @@
+---
+title: Client ID Metadata Documents in Microsoft Entra ID
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+description: Learn how Client ID Metadata Documents let OAuth clients identify themselves to Microsoft Entra ID without prior client registration.
+ms.topic: concept-article
+ms.date: 09/21/2026
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+
+#customer-intent: As an identity architect or developer, I want to understand how Microsoft Entra ID supports Client ID Metadata Documents so that I can decide whether CIMD is appropriate for my MCP client scenario.
+---
+
+# Client ID Metadata Documents in Microsoft Entra ID (preview)
+
+Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD) let an OAuth client identify itself by using an HTTPS URL instead of a preassigned client ID. The document at that URL contains the client's OAuth metadata. Microsoft Entra ID retrieves and validates the document, represents the client as an agent identity in the tenant, and issues tokens under the tenant's existing consent and security policies.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> Client ID Metadata Document support in Microsoft Entra ID is in public preview. This preview is provided without a service-level agreement and isn't recommended for production workloads. Some features might be unsupported or have constrained capabilities. For more information, see [Universal License Terms for Online Services](https://www.microsoft.com/licensing/terms/product/ForOnlineServices/all).
+
+CIMD is useful when a client must connect to many authorization servers with which it has no prior relationship. For example, an MCP client can discover remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers at runtime, and each server might use a different authorization server. Requiring every client to be registered with every authorization server doesn't scale.
+
+CIMD is defined by the [OAuth Client ID Metadata Document specification](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document/). The MCP authorization specification recommends CIMD for clients that don't have another supported registration mechanism.
+
+## How CIMD works with Microsoft Entra ID
+
+A typical CIMD authorization flow has the following steps:
+
+:::image type="content" source="media/client-id-metadata-documents/client-id-metadata-document-authorization-flow.svg" alt-text="Swimlane diagram showing a user connecting an MCP client to an MCP server. The client discovers Microsoft Entra ID, sends an authorization request with a CIMD URL as its client ID, and Entra retrieves and validates the metadata document. Entra obtains consent if required, creates an agent identity if needed, and issues an access token that the client uses to call the MCP server." lightbox="media/client-id-metadata-documents/client-id-metadata-document-authorization-flow.svg":::
+
+1. An MCP client discovers that an MCP server uses Microsoft Entra ID as its authorization server.
+1. The client reads the authorization server metadata and determines that CIMD is supported.
+1. The client sends an authorization request. Its `client_id` is the HTTPS URL of its metadata document.
+1. Microsoft Entra ID retrieves the document and validates its contents, including an exact match between the requested `client_id` and the document's `client_id`.
+1. Microsoft Entra ID derives a stable app ID from the canonical document URL and looks for a matching agent identity in the tenant.
+1. If the identity doesn't exist, tenant policy determines whether it can be created through consent. An administrator can instead add the CIMD client in advance.
+1. Microsoft Entra ID validates the requested redirect URI and permissions, obtains any required consent, and issues an audience-restricted access token.
+1. The client presents the token to the MCP server.
+
+The CIMD URL is the durable identity of the client. Moving the document to another URL creates a different identity and doesn't preserve permissions granted to the old identity.
+
+## How Microsoft Entra represents a CIMD client
+
+Microsoft Entra ID represents a CIMD client as an [agent identity](what-are-agent-identities.md) in each tenant where the client is approved.
+
+A CIMD-backed agent identity:
+
+- Has an app ID derived from the canonical CIMD URL.
+- Stores the CIMD URL as an immutable identifier.
+- Has a read-only agent identity blueprint in each tenant, and no blueprint service principal.
+- Uses the external metadata document as the source of truth for its OAuth configuration.
+- Appears in agent identity inventory, audit logs, and sign-in logs.
+
+Because the metadata remains in the external document, features that inspect OAuth configuration stored on an Entra application object might not evaluate a CIMD client. Review the [governance considerations](#governance-considerations) before adopting CIMD.
+
+## When to use CIMD
+
+Implementers should always prefer pre-registration of a client with Entra when possible. For high-volume or strategic integrations, a conventional registered client ID provides the most stable identity and the broadest Entra capabilities. CIMD should only be used when all of the following conditions apply:
+
+- The client must connect to many independently operated authorization servers.
+- The authorization servers can't reasonably preregister the client.
+- The client uses a user-present, delegated OAuth flow.
+- The client can publish stable metadata on a public HTTPS URL.
+- The client accepts the limitations described in this article.
+
+An MCP client that discovers many remote servers at runtime is the primary scenario.
+
+## Supported capabilities and limitations
+
+The following table summarizes the capabilities and limitations of CIMD-backed agent identities.
+
+| Capability | CIMD support |
+| --- | --- |
+| OAuth authorization code flow with a signed-in user | Supported |
+| Refresh tokens | Supported |
+| Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) | Supported |
+| Client credentials flow | Not supported |
+| Device code flow | Supported |
+| Acting as an OAuth resource or token audience | Not supported |
+| ID tokens or SAML tokens for user sign-in | Not supported |
+| Shared client secrets | Not supported |
+| Publisher verification or Microsoft 365 certification | Not supported |
+| Multiple agent identities sharing one blueprint | Not supported |
+| Agent user accounts | Not supported |
+| Windows Web Account Manager (WAM) | Not supported |
+| In-place conversion to or from a conventional client ID | Not supported |
+
+## Security model
+
+CIMD proves that a client controls a URL. It doesn't prove that the client is trustworthy or should receive access to organizational data.
+
+Microsoft Entra ID applies the following protections:
+
+- **HTTPS-only identifiers:** A CIMD client ID must be an HTTPS URL with a path. User information and fragments aren't allowed in the URL.
+- **Exact identity match:** The `client_id` in the document must exactly match the URL used as the client ID.
+- **Exact redirect matching:** The redirect URI in an authorization request must exactly match a URI in the document.
+- **Consent policy enforcement:** Existing tenant consent policy determines whether users can add the client and which delegated permissions they can grant.
+- **No app-only tokens:** CIMD clients can't use the client credentials grant.
+- **Audience restriction:** Microsoft Entra ID doesn't issue tokens whose audience is the CIMD client.
+
+Under the default recommended consent policy, users can consent only to low-risk OAuth permissions for CIMD clients. Sensitive permissions require administrator consent. For administrator guidance, see [Manage CIMD clients in Microsoft Entra ID](manage-client-id-metadata-document-clients.md).
+
+## Governance considerations
+
+Before using CIMD, account for the following considerations:
+
+- The client owner controls the metadata document and can change its contents.
+- The document URL is immutable in Microsoft Entra ID. A URL change requires a new identity and new consent grants.
+- App management policy and other controls that inspect configuration stored on an application object don't cover metadata that remains only in the CIMD document.
+- CIMD clients don't support publisher verification or Microsoft 365 certification.
+- Entra doesn't provide a tenant-managed domain allowlist or blocklist for CIMD URLs.
+- Losing control of the document URL or its domain can affect every tenant that trusts that client identity.
+
+Use least-privilege delegated permissions, preapprove clients that need sensitive access, monitor their sign-ins, and remove identities that are no longer required.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Authenticate a local agent with Microsoft Entra ID](authenticate-local-agent.md)
+- [Configure a client to use a Client ID Metadata Document](configure-client-id-metadata-document.md)
+- [Manage CIMD clients in Microsoft Entra ID](manage-client-id-metadata-document-clients.md)
+- [Secure an MCP server with Microsoft Entra ID](secure-mcp-server-with-entra-id.md)
+- [Microsoft Entra Agent ID logs](sign-in-audit-logs-agents.md)

+++ b/docs/agent-id/configure-client-id-metadata-document.md
@@ -0,0 +1,215 @@
+---
+title: Configure a client to use a Client ID Metadata Document
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+description: Publish a Client ID Metadata Document and use its URL as the client ID when connecting an OAuth or MCP client to Microsoft Entra ID.
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/05/2026
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+
+#customer-intent: As an MCP client developer, I want to publish a Client ID Metadata Document and request Microsoft Entra tokens so that my client can connect to Entra-protected MCP servers without prior registration.
+---
+
+# Configure a client to use a Client ID Metadata Document (preview)
+
+By using a Client ID Metadata Document (CIMD), your OAuth client can use a public HTTPS URL as its `client_id`. This article explains how to publish a CIMD document and use it to request a delegated access token from Microsoft Entra ID.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> Client ID Metadata Document support in Microsoft Entra ID is in public preview. This preview is provided without a service-level agreement and isn't recommended for production workloads. Some features might be unsupported or have constrained capabilities. For more information, see [Universal License Terms for Online Services](https://www.microsoft.com/licensing/terms/product/ForOnlineServices/all).
+
+Before implementing CIMD, review [Client ID Metadata Documents in Microsoft Entra ID](client-id-metadata-documents.md) to understand the supported scenarios, security model, and limitations.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+To complete this procedure, you need:
+
+- An OAuth client that supports the authorization code flow and PKCE.
+- A stable public HTTPS endpoint where you can publish a JSON document.
+- An MCP server secured with Microsoft Entra ID. See [Prepare the MCP server](#prepare-the-mcp-server).
+- A Microsoft Entra tenant in which CIMD support is available.
+- A tenant administrator who can [add the CIMD client and grant delegated permissions](manage-client-id-metadata-document-clients.md#add-a-cimd-client-in-the-admin-center) when user consent isn't available. Give the administrator the document URL, target resource, and requested scopes before testing sign-in.
+
+The client must be able to open a browser for user sign-in. CIMD clients can't use the client credentials grant.
+
+## Prepare the MCP server
+
+A CIMD client has no app registration, so it learns everything about the MCP server from the server's protected resource metadata and from Microsoft Entra ID. Set up the server by following [Secure an MCP server with Microsoft Entra ID](secure-mcp-server-with-entra-id.md). That article covers registering the server, exposing a delegated scope, publishing protected resource metadata, and validating access tokens.
+
+Then confirm the following settings. The examples in this article use an MCP server at `https://mcp.contoso.com` that exposes the `mcp.access` scope.
+
+| Setting | Required value | Example |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Application ID URI of the server's app registration | The server's canonical URL. | `https://mcp.contoso.com` |
+| `resource` in the protected resource metadata | The same value as the Application ID URI. The client sends this value in its `resource` parameter, and Microsoft Entra ID issues the token with this audience. | `https://mcp.contoso.com` |
+| `authorization_servers` in the protected resource metadata | The Microsoft Entra authorization server URL for the tenant, or `common` for a multitenant server. | `https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/oauth21/2026-08` |
+| `scopes_supported` in the protected resource metadata | The delegated scope that the client requests. | `mcp.access` |
+| Who can consent to the delegated scope | **Admins and users** lets users consent to the client themselves, if the tenant's consent policy permits it. **Admins only** requires an administrator to approve the client. | Admins and users |
+| Supported account types | **Multiple Entra ID tenants** when `authorization_servers` uses `common`. | Single tenant |
+
+Verify that the server publishes its metadata:
+
+```http
+GET https://mcp.contoso.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource
+```
+
+The response must contain the `resource`, `authorization_servers`, and `scopes_supported` values from the preceding table. The MCP server doesn't need CIMD-specific token-validation logic. Microsoft Entra ID issues the access token, and the server validates it like any other access token.
+
+## Publish the metadata document
+
+Publish a JSON document at the URL that you intend to use as the client ID. For example:
+
+```http
+GET https://client.contoso.com/oauth/client-metadata.json
+Content-Type: application/json
+```
+
+```json
+{
+  "client_id": "https://client.contoso.com/oauth/client-metadata.json",
+  "client_name": "Contoso Agent",
+  "client_uri": "https://client.contoso.com",
+  "logo_uri": "https://client.contoso.com/logo.png",
+  "redirect_uris": [
+    "https://client.contoso.com/oauth/callback"
+  ],
+  "grant_types": [
+    "authorization_code",
+    "refresh_token"
+  ],
+  "response_types": [
+    "code"
+  ],
+  "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none",
+  "scope": "offline_access https://mcp.contoso.com/mcp.access"
+}
+```
+
+Follow these requirements:
+
+- Use an HTTPS URL with a nonempty path.
+- Don't include user information or a fragment in the URL.
+- Set `client_id` to the exact URL that serves the document.
+- Keep the URL short and stable. It can appear in consent and administration experiences.
+- List every redirect URI that the client might use. Microsoft Entra ID uses exact string matching.
+- Use HTTPS redirect URIs. Loopback redirect URIs can be used for local native-client scenarios where the applicable OAuth specification permits them.
+- Don't rely on HTTP redirects when Microsoft Entra ID retrieves the document.
+- Return a successful HTTP status and a valid JSON response.
+- Don't use a shared client secret. Set `token_endpoint_auth_method` to `none` for a public client.
+
+The document format is defined by the [OAuth Client ID Metadata Document specification](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document/).
+
+> [!CAUTION]
+> Treat the document URL and its domain as long-lived security assets. If you move the document to another URL, Microsoft Entra ID treats it as a different client. Existing consent grants don't transfer.
+
+## Check authorization server support
+
+Before sending a URL as a client ID, confirm that the authorization server for the target tenant supports CIMD.
+
+1. Identify the authorization server. For an MCP server, fetch its protected resource metadata from `<server-url>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` and read the `authorization_servers` value:
+
+    ```http
+    GET https://mcp.contoso.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource
+    ```
+
+    ```json
+    {
+      "resource": "https://mcp.contoso.com",
+      "authorization_servers": ["https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/oauth21/2026-08"]
+    }
+    ```
+
+    For other protected resources, use `https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/oauth21/2026-08`, where `{tenant}` is `common`, the tenant ID, or a verified domain of the organization.
+
+1. Fetch the authorization server metadata by appending `/.well-known/openid-configuration` to the authorization server URL:
+
+    ```http
+    GET https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/oauth21/2026-08/.well-known/openid-configuration
+    ```
+
+1. Check the response for the `client_id_metadata_document_supported` property. A CIMD-capable authorization server returns `true`:
+
+    ```json
+    {
+      "client_id_metadata_document_supported": true
+    }
+    ```
+
+    The response contains other properties that aren't shown here, including `authorization_endpoint` and `token_endpoint`. A client that uses metadata discovery, such as an MCP client, sends its requests to those endpoints. The following examples use the Microsoft Entra v2.0 endpoints, which also support CIMD client IDs.
+
+Don't send a CIMD client ID when the property is missing or `false`. Fall back to a registered client ID or another registration method that the authorization server supports.
+
+## Send the authorization request
+
+Set `client_id` to the URL of your metadata document. For an MCP server, also include the protected resource URL in the `resource` parameter.
+
+```http
+GET https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/authorize
+    ?client_id=https%3A%2F%2Fclient.contoso.com%2Foauth%2Fclient-metadata.json
+    &response_type=code
+    &redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fclient.contoso.com%2Foauth%2Fcallback
+    &scope=offline_access%20https%3A%2F%2Fmcp.contoso.com%2Fmcp.access
+    &resource=https%3A%2F%2Fmcp.contoso.com
+    &code_challenge={PKCE_challenge}
+    &code_challenge_method=S256
+    &state={opaque_value}
+```
+
+Replace:
+
+- `{tenant}` with the tenant identifier or verified domain for the organization.
+- `{PKCE_challenge}` with the S256 challenge generated from your code verifier.
+- `{opaque_value}` with a value that your client validates when the authorization response returns.
+- The resource and scope values with those published by the MCP server.
+
+Microsoft Entra ID retrieves and validates the metadata document. The requested `redirect_uri` must exactly match one of the values in `redirect_uris`.
+
+Depending on tenant policy and whether an administrator added the client in advance, the user might:
+
+- Continue without a new prompt because an administrator already granted consent.
+- Consent to low-risk delegated permissions.
+- Be told that administrator approval is required.
+- Be blocked from adding the client.
+
+The authorization request is one way to grant delegated permissions to the client's agent identity. For the other methods, including administrator consent, see [Grant delegated permissions to an agent identity](grant-agent-access-microsoft-365.md).
+
+During preview, grant permissions through the sign-in and consent endpoints or Microsoft Graph, not the portal permissions experience. The admin consent request workflow is disabled for Agent ID, including CIMD clients. In a default tenant, plan for an administrator to add the client and grant consent before users sign in; don't rely on user consent being available.
+
+## Redeem the authorization code
+
+After Microsoft Entra ID returns an authorization code, redeem it at the tenant's v2 token endpoint:
+
+```http
+POST https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/token
+Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
+
+client_id=https%3A%2F%2Fclient.contoso.com%2Foauth%2Fclient-metadata.json&
+grant_type=authorization_code&
+code={authorization_code}&
+redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fclient.contoso.com%2Foauth%2Fcallback&
+code_verifier={PKCE_code_verifier}&
+scope=https%3A%2F%2Fmcp.contoso.com%2Fmcp.access&
+resource=https%3A%2F%2Fmcp.contoso.com
+```
+
+Validate the `state` value before redeeming the code. Store tokens using the secure storage provided by the client platform.
+
+The access token is issued to the resource, not to the CIMD client. The client uses the token to call the protected resource in the same way as another OAuth client.
+
+## Troubleshoot common failures
+
+| Failure | What to check |
+| --- | --- |
+| The metadata document can't be retrieved | Confirm that the URL is publicly reachable over HTTPS, returns a successful response directly, and doesn't redirect. |
+| The client ID is rejected | Confirm that the requested `client_id`, the retrieval URL, and the document's `client_id` are identical. |
+| The redirect URI is rejected | Compare the requested redirect URI with the document, including scheme, host, path, port, case, and trailing slash. |
+| The user can't approve the client | Review the tenant's user consent policy and whether the requested permissions require administrator consent. |
+| The token has the wrong audience | Send the MCP server's canonical URL as `resource` and request a scope exposed by that resource. |
+| A client with the URL already exists | Reuse the existing tenant-local identity. Only one CIMD-backed identity for a canonical URL can exist in a tenant. |
+| The client stopped working after a URL change | Restore the original URL or onboard the new URL as a new identity and obtain consent again. |
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Authenticate a local agent with Microsoft Entra ID](authenticate-local-agent.md)
+- [Client ID Metadata Documents in Microsoft Entra ID](client-id-metadata-documents.md)
+- [Grant delegated permissions to an agent identity](grant-agent-access-microsoft-365.md)
+- [Manage CIMD clients in Microsoft Entra ID](manage-client-id-metadata-document-clients.md)
+- [Secure an MCP server with Microsoft Entra ID](secure-mcp-server-with-entra-id.md)

@@ -0,0 +1,96 @@
+---
+title: Create and delete an agent's user account
+description: Learn how to create and delete an agent's user account using the Microsoft Graph API.
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 10/29/2026
+ms.reviewer: dastrock
+
+#customer-intent: As a developer or IT administrator, I want to create an agent's user account so that my agent can act as a digital worker in Microsoft Entra.
+---
+
+# Create and delete an agent's user account
+
+An agent's user account is a specialized identity that lets an agent act as a digital worker—appearing to other systems as a user identity rather than a service principal. Agent user accounts aren't created automatically. You must explicitly create one and associate it with a specific agent identity.
+
+For background on what an agent's user account is and when to use one, see [The agent's user account in Microsoft Entra Agent ID](agent-users.md).
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> Creating an agent's user account through the Microsoft Graph API establishes the identity in Microsoft Entra but doesn't provision Microsoft 365 capabilities such as a mailbox or Teams presence. To provision a full digital worker with Microsoft 365 capabilities, create the agent through Microsoft Teams using the Agent 365 SDK.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- An [agent identity blueprint](create-blueprint.md) and at least one [agent identity](create-delete-agent-identities.md) created from it. Record the agent identity's object ID.
+- The blueprint app registration must have the `AgentIdUser.ReadWrite.IdentityParentedBy` application permission granted with admin consent. See [Grant the blueprint permission to create agent user accounts](#grant-the-blueprint-permission-to-create-agent-user-accounts).
+- An access token for the blueprint app registration with `https://graph.microsoft.com/.default` scope. The blueprint authenticates to Microsoft Graph to create and delete agent user accounts on behalf of the agent identity it parents.
+
+The `identityParentId` value is the agent identity's object ID. The agent user's separate `id` is used to delete the user account. For identifier meanings, see [Record the identifiers for your scenario](key-concepts.md#record-the-identifiers-for-your-scenario).
+
+## Grant the blueprint permission to create agent user accounts
+
+The blueprint app registration doesn't have permission to create agent user accounts by default. Add the `AgentIdUser.ReadWrite.IdentityParentedBy` application permission and grant admin consent before calling the creation API.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
+1. Browse to **Entra ID** > **App registrations** and open the blueprint app registration.
+1. Select **API permissions** > **Add a permission** > **Microsoft Graph** > **Application permissions**.
+1. Search for and select `AgentIdUser.ReadWrite.IdentityParentedBy`.
+1. Select **Add permissions**, then select **Grant admin consent**.
+
+## Create an agent's user account
+
+Create the agent's user account and associate it with an agent identity in a single call. The `identityParentId` property establishes the immutable 1:1 relationship between the user account and its parent agent identity.
+
+```http
+POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/microsoft.graph.agentUser
+Content-Type: application/json
+Authorization: Bearer <blueprint-access-token>
+
+{
+  "accountEnabled": true,
+  "displayName": "Sales Agent",
+  "mailNickname": "SalesAgent",
+  "userPrincipalName": "salesagent@contoso.com",
+  "identityParentId": "<agent-identity-object-id>"
+}
+```
+
+| Property | Description |
+| --- | --- |
+| `accountEnabled` | Set to `true` to enable the account immediately. |
+| `displayName` | Display name shown in the directory. |
+| `mailNickname` | Alias used when provisioning a mailbox. Must be unique in the tenant. |
+| `userPrincipalName` | Sign-in name in `user@domain` format. Must use a verified domain in the tenant. |
+| `identityParentId` | Object ID of the agent identity that owns this user account. This value is immutable after creation. |
+
+A successful request returns `201 Created` with the new agent user object:
+
+```json
+{
+  "@odata.type": "#microsoft.graph.agentUser",
+  "id": "87d349ed-44d7-43e1-9a83-5f2406dee5bd",
+  "displayName": "Sales Agent",
+  "mailNickname": "SalesAgent",
+  "userPrincipalName": "salesagent@contoso.com",
+  "identityParentId": "<agent-identity-object-id>"
+}
+```
+
+Record the `id` value. You need it to configure the agent's user account flow in your agent and to delete the account later.
+
+## Delete an agent's user account
+
+When the agent is decommissioned, delete the user account to remove it from the directory.
+
+```http
+DELETE https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/microsoft.graph.agentUser/<agent-user-id>
+Authorization: Bearer <blueprint-access-token>
+```
+
+A successful request returns `204 No Content`. The agent identity itself is not deleted by this call. To also remove the agent identity, see [Create and delete agent identities](create-delete-agent-identities.md).
+
+## Related content
+
+- [The agent's user account in Microsoft Entra Agent ID](agent-users.md)
+- [Use an agent's user account with Microsoft 365 (ASP.NET Core)](agent-user-oauth-flow.md)
+- [Use an agent's user account with Microsoft 365 (Auth SDK sidecar)](sidecar-call-microsoft-365-as-agent-user.md)
+- [Create and delete agent identities](create-delete-agent-identities.md)
