diff --git a/docs/agent-id/create-single-instance-agent.md b/docs/agent-id/create-single-instance-agent.md
new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..a32499e5977
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/agent-id/create-single-instance-agent.md
@@ -0,0 +1,325 @@
+---
+title: Create an identity for your agent (preview)
+description: Set up your agent's identity with Microsoft Graph, including its registration, redirect URIs, credential, and API permission declarations.
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/06/2026
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+# Customer intent: As an agent developer, I want to register my agent so that it can authenticate and request access to APIs.
+---
+
+# Create an identity for your agent with Microsoft Graph (preview)
+
+Register your agent so it can authenticate with Microsoft Entra ID and request access to APIs. This setup creates one identity for your agent, shared by its installations or replicas.
+
+This procedure uses Microsoft Graph beta. For a cloud agent, configure a credential for its runtime. For an agent installed on an end-user device, use the public-client redirect configuration without a credential. Your calling tutorial identifies the sections you need.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> Single-instance agent identities are in preview. This preview is provided without a service-level agreement and isn't recommended for production workloads. Some features might be unsupported or have constrained capabilities. For more information, see [Universal License Terms for Online Services](https://www.microsoft.com/licensing/terms/product/ForOnlineServices/all).
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A Microsoft Entra tenant enabled for single-instance provisioning in Microsoft Graph. Confirm preview availability and tenant enablement with your Microsoft representative before you begin. To request tokens after setup, also confirm that single-instance authentication is enabled; provisioning and authentication are enabled separately.
+- An account authorized to create and update agent identity blueprints and agent identities, such as an [Agent ID Administrator](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#agent-id-administrator).
+- A separate, single-tenant public management app with administrator consent for the delegated Microsoft Graph permissions `AgentIdentityBlueprint.ReadWrite.All` and `AgentIdentity.ReadWrite.All`, or permission to [set up the management client](#set-up-the-management-client).
+- An administrator who can grant consent to the management app's Graph permissions.
+- The object ID of a user who can be assigned as the blueprint's sponsor. The examples also assign that user as an owner.
+- For interactive sign-in, a redirect URI appropriate for the client type. For browser-based administrator consent, a `web` redirect URI, even if the agent only uses client credentials at runtime.
+- For local confidential-client testing, an X.509 certificate and secure storage for its private key. An Azure-hosted agent can use a managed identity federated credential instead. A public-only client doesn't need a credential.
+- For API access, the resource application's client ID and the IDs of the delegated permissions or app roles the agent needs.
+
+Run the HTTP examples through Microsoft Graph PowerShell as described below, or use a REST client that can send JSON request bodies and headers. In a REST client, send the management token as a bearer token in the `Authorization` header of each Graph request. Never use the agent's runtime access token for management requests.
+
+### Confirm the administrator handoff
+
+Before creating objects, agree on the following handoff. Management consent and the agent's runtime API consent are separate approvals.
+
+| Who | Action | Ready when |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Tenant administrator and Microsoft representative. | Confirm that both preview provisioning and authentication are enabled. | The tenant supports registration and token requests for this setup. |
+| Authorized administrator. | Approve the management client's two Graph permissions listed above. | The operator can sign in to that client with both consented scopes. |
+| Developer or authorized operator. | Complete the registration steps below. | The blueprint object ID, agent identity object ID, and shared client ID are recorded. |
+| API owner and consent administrator. | Supply the API identifiers and approve the permissions required by the calling tutorial. | The required runtime grants are verified before the first API call. |
+
+Send the administrator your tenant ID, management client ID, and requested API permissions. Keep the [identifier worksheet](key-concepts.md#record-the-identifiers-for-your-scenario) alongside the setup steps.
+
+If you're following a local HTTPS tutorial, also confirm that the development HTTPS certificate is trusted on your machine before browser sign-in. Follow your organization's trust process rather than disabling TLS validation.
+
+## Set up the management client
+
+The management client signs in an administrator or authorized operator to create the agent's registration. It's separate from the agent's runtime identity. An existing Azure CLI sign-in doesn't establish this management context.
+
+1. [Register an application](~/identity-platform/quickstart-register-app.md) in the same tenant. Select **Accounts in this organizational directory only**. Under **Authentication**, add the **Mobile and desktop applications** platform with the redirect URI `http://localhost`.
+1. Under **API permissions**, add these **Microsoft Graph > Delegated permissions**:
+
+    - `AgentIdentityBlueprint.ReadWrite.All`.
+    - `AgentIdentity.ReadWrite.All`.
+
+1. Have an authorized administrator grant consent to these permissions. For information about admin consent, see [Permissions and consent in the Microsoft identity platform](~/identity-platform/permissions-consent-overview.md).
+1. Install the Microsoft Graph PowerShell authentication module and sign in with the management app. `Connect-MgGraph` opens a browser for the signed-in user:
+
+    ```powershell
+    Install-Module Microsoft.Graph.Authentication -Scope CurrentUser
+
+    Connect-MgGraph `
+      -ClientId "<management-app-client-id>" `
+      -TenantId "<tenant-id>" `
+      -Scopes "AgentIdentityBlueprint.ReadWrite.All", "AgentIdentity.ReadWrite.All" `
+      -ContextScope Process
+
+    $context = Get-MgContext
+    if (-not $context -or -not $context.Account) {
+        throw "Microsoft Graph sign-in didn't establish a delegated management context. Stop before creating objects."
+    }
+    $context | Select-Object Account, TenantId, ClientId, Scopes
+    ```
+
+    Confirm that `Account`, `TenantId`, and `ClientId` identify the intended operator, tenant, and management app, and that `Scopes` includes both permissions. If a scope is missing or consent is requested again, stop and have an authorized administrator verify the app registration and consent before continuing.
+
+On Windows, if `Connect-MgGraph` fails before sign-in with **A window handle must be configured**, use the [documented browser sign-in option](/powershell/module/microsoft.graph.authentication/set-mggraphoption) for your custom management client:
+
+```powershell
+Set-MgGraphOption -DisableLoginByWAM $true
+```
+
+Run the same `Connect-MgGraph` command again. This changes the authentication UI, not the tenant's access requirements; complete sign-in as the authorized operator and don't bypass a compliance denial. The setting persists across PowerShell sessions. If WAM was enabled before this change, restore it with `Set-MgGraphOption -DisableLoginByWAM $false` when you're done.
+
+Use `Invoke-MgGraphRequest` to run the HTTP examples without copying or displaying an access token. For example, copy the JSON body from **Create the blueprint** into `$body`, replacing the sponsor placeholder:
+
+```powershell
+$body = @'
+<JSON-request-body>
+'@
+
+$blueprint = Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Method POST `
+    -Uri "https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/applications" `
+    -Headers @{ "OData-Version" = "4.0" } `
+    -ContentType "application/json" -Body $body
+
+$blueprintObjectId = $blueprint.id
+$agentClientId = $blueprint.appId
+```
+
+For later requests, use the method, full URI, headers, and JSON body shown in each HTTP example. Omit `-Body` for a GET request. The module supplies the authorization header. For command syntax, see [Invoke-MgGraphRequest](/powershell/module/microsoft.graph.authentication/invoke-mggraphrequest).
+
+If registration or consent is denied, ask your tenant administrator to complete this setup. Don't grant these management permissions to the agent to work around an authorization error.
+
+## Create the blueprint
+
+The blueprint is the registration that holds your agent's authentication settings and credentials.
+
+1. Create the blueprint with `isSingleInstance` set to `true`. Replace `<sponsor-user-object-id>` with the sponsor's object ID. A sponsor is required; the owner assignment is optional.
+
+    Keep `isSingleInstance: true` for this tutorial: it creates one identity for the agent, including its installations or replicas. This property can't be changed after creation.
+
+    ```http
+    POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/applications
+    OData-Version: 4.0
+    Content-Type: application/json
+
+    {
+      "@odata.type": "Microsoft.Graph.AgentIdentityBlueprint",
+      "displayName": "Contoso Operations Agent",
+      "signInAudience": "AzureADMyOrg",
+      "isSingleInstance": true,
+      "sponsors@odata.bind": [
+        "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/<sponsor-user-object-id>"
+      ],
+      "owners@odata.bind": [
+        "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/<sponsor-user-object-id>"
+      ]
+    }
+    ```
+
+1. From the `201 Created` response, save the following values:
+
+    - `id`: The blueprint's object ID, used to address it in Microsoft Graph.
+    - `appId`: The application (client) ID, used in OAuth requests.
+
+The example creates a single-tenant blueprint with `signInAudience` set to `AzureADMyOrg`.
+
+## Provision the agent identity
+
+Create the identity separately from its blueprint registration. Follow the request below directly; this setup doesn't require a blueprint principal.
+
+1. Create the Agent ID. Set `agentIdentityBlueprintId` to the blueprint's **object ID**, not its `appId`.
+
+    ```http
+    POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/servicePrincipals/microsoft.graph.agentIdentity
+    OData-Version: 4.0
+    Content-Type: application/json
+
+    {
+      "displayName": "Contoso Operations Agent",
+      "agentIdentityBlueprintId": "<blueprint-object-id>",
+      "sponsors@odata.bind": [
+        "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/<sponsor-user-object-id>"
+      ]
+    }
+    ```
+
+1. Save the identity's `id` from the `201 Created` response. This is the agent identity's object ID, not the blueprint object ID or OAuth client ID.
+1. Read the identity to verify the result:
+
+    ```http
+    GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/servicePrincipals/<agent-identity-object-id>?$select=id,appId,displayName,agentIdentityBlueprintId,instanceMode
+    ```
+
+    Check the returned values:
+
+    | Property | Expected value |
+    | --- | --- |
+    | `@odata.type` | `#microsoft.graph.agentIdentity`. |
+    | `appId` | The blueprint's `appId`. |
+    | `agentIdentityBlueprintId` | The blueprint's object ID. |
+    | `instanceMode` | `singleInstance`. |
+
+Don't provision a new identity for each installation, process, or user session. They use the same client ID.
+
+## Configure redirect URIs
+
+For authorization code flow, register the redirect URI under the platform that matches the client. A confidential client uses `web`; a public client uses `publicClient`.
+
+The [browser-based administrator consent procedure](authenticate-single-instance-agent.md#grant-application-permissions) also requires a `web` redirect URI, even for an agent that only uses client credentials at runtime. The redirect handles the consent callback, not the client credentials token request. Skip this section only if neither authorization code flow nor browser-based administrator consent is needed.
+
+1. Read the current redirect configuration:
+
+    ```http
+    GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/applications/<blueprint-object-id>?$select=id,appId,web,publicClient
+    ```
+
+1. Update the appropriate redirect collection. The following example shows both client types; include only the platforms your agent uses. Keep all existing redirect URIs that are still needed.
+
+    ```http
+    PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/applications/<blueprint-object-id>
+    OData-Version: 4.0
+    Content-Type: application/json
+
+    {
+      "@odata.type": "#microsoft.graph.agentIdentityBlueprint",
+      "web": {
+        "redirectUris": [
+          "https://agent.contoso.com/signin"
+        ]
+      },
+      "publicClient": {
+        "redirectUris": [
+          "http://localhost"
+        ]
+      }
+    }
+    ```
+
+    A successful update returns `204 No Content`. Redirect URI collections are replaced, not appended. Don't copy this example over an existing configuration without preserving its URIs.
+
+The same blueprint can register both platforms. Each authorization request uses the redirect URI for its client type. A public client doesn't send a credential, even if a confidential component uses a certificate on the same blueprint. Don't change `isFallbackPublicClient` to switch between these authorization-code scenarios.
+
+## Add a certificate for confidential clients
+
+For local confidential-client testing, register only the public certificate on the blueprint. The runtime keeps the private key for authentication.
+
+Skip this section for a public-only client. For an Azure-hosted agent using managed identity federation, [configure the federated credential](create-blueprint.md#configure-credentials-for-the-agent-identity-blueprint) instead, then continue with **Declare the API permissions**.
+
+For a Windows development machine, you can [create a self-signed certificate](~/identity-platform/howto-create-self-signed-certificate.md) and export its public certificate and password-protected PFX. Keep the PFX outside your source tree. Use the Base64-encoded DER public certificate for `key` below, not the PFX or a PEM file's header and footer. For example:
+
+```powershell
+$publicCertificate = Get-PfxCertificate -FilePath "<absolute-path-to-public-cer>"
+$publicCertificateBase64 = [Convert]::ToBase64String($publicCertificate.RawData)
+```
+
+Paste `$publicCertificateBase64` into the registration request. The public value isn't a credential; the PFX and its password are. For non-Windows development or production, use your organization's certificate issuance and private-key storage process.
+
+1. Read the current certificate collection:
+
+    ```http
+    GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/applications/<blueprint-object-id>?$select=id,appId,keyCredentials
+    ```
+
+1. Add your public certificate while retaining any existing key credentials that are still needed. The following request shows an initial registration with no existing certificates:
+
+    ```http
+    PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/applications/<blueprint-object-id>
+    OData-Version: 4.0
+    Content-Type: application/json
+
+    {
+      "@odata.type": "#microsoft.graph.agentIdentityBlueprint",
+      "keyCredentials": [
+        {
+          "type": "AsymmetricX509Cert",
+          "usage": "Verify",
+          "key": "<base64-encoded-DER-certificate>",
+          "displayName": "Contoso Operations Agent certificate"
+        }
+      ]
+    }
+    ```
+
+    A successful update returns `204 No Content`. Never upload the private key or distribute it with a public client.
+
+For certificate format and client assertion guidance, see [Microsoft identity platform certificate credentials](~/identity-platform/certificate-credentials.md).
+
+## Declare the API permissions
+
+Declare only the permissions the agent needs. Use `Scope` for a delegated permission and `Role` for an application permission. The values in `resourceAccess` are permission IDs exposed by the resource application, not permission names.
+
+1. Read the current declarations:
+
+    ```http
+    GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/applications/<blueprint-object-id>?$select=id,appId,requiredResourceAccess
+    ```
+
+1. Add the resource and permission entries, preserving existing declarations that are still needed. The example shows one delegated permission and one application permission; remove either entry if your agent doesn't need it.
+
+    ```http
+    PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/applications/<blueprint-object-id>
+    OData-Version: 4.0
+    Content-Type: application/json
+
+    {
+      "@odata.type": "#microsoft.graph.agentIdentityBlueprint",
+      "requiredResourceAccess": [
+        {
+          "resourceAppId": "<resource-app-id>",
+          "resourceAccess": [
+            {
+              "id": "<delegated-permission-id>",
+              "type": "Scope"
+            },
+            {
+              "id": "<app-role-id>",
+              "type": "Role"
+            }
+          ]
+        }
+      ]
+    }
+    ```
+
+    A successful update returns `204 No Content`.
+
+These declarations don't grant access. User or administrator consent grants delegated permissions, and an administrator grants application permissions. Grants belong to the Agent ID directly.
+
+If the agent also receives calls from a front-end application, [expose an identifier URI and delegated scope on the blueprint](create-blueprint.md#configure-identifier-uri-and-scope). Preserve any existing API scopes and set `requestedAccessTokenVersion` to `2`. The front end requests that scope to obtain a token whose audience is the shared client ID.
+
+## Troubleshoot Graph requests
+
+If a request fails, inspect the HTTP status and the Graph error response before changing permissions or retrying the operation.
+
+| Response | Check |
+| --- | --- |
+| `400 Bad Request` | Read `error.code` and `error.message`. Check the endpoint's request schema, required sponsor references, object IDs, and property values. |
+| `401 Unauthorized` | Acquire a valid access token for Microsoft Graph and send it in the `Authorization` header. |
+| `403 Forbidden` | Confirm the management app has the required delegated permissions and admin consent, the signed-in user is authorized for the operation, and the tenant is enabled for the preview. |
+
+For details, see [Microsoft Graph error responses](/graph/errors). When you contact an administrator or Microsoft support, include the HTTP status, error code, and `request-id` response header. Don't include access tokens or other credentials.
+
+## Next step
+
+Return to the tutorial that brought you here:
+
+- [Authenticate users to an ASP.NET Core agent API](aspnet-core-authenticate-users.md).
+- [Call a custom API as an agent with ASP.NET Core](call-api-custom.md).
+- [Configure the Auth SDK sidecar](microsoft-entra-sdk-for-agent-identities.md).
+- [Sign in users from an agent on an end-user device](authenticate-local-agent.md).
+
+For direct OAuth requests and the identity model behind this setup, see [Authenticate the agent identity](authenticate-single-instance-agent.md) and [Agent identity blueprint instance modes](agent-blueprint.md#instance-modes-preview).

diff --git a/docs/agent-id/grant-application-permissions-agent-identity.md b/docs/agent-id/grant-application-permissions-agent-identity.md
new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..2a36546e825
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/agent-id/grant-application-permissions-agent-identity.md
@@ -0,0 +1,139 @@
+---
+title: Grant Microsoft Graph application permissions to an agent identity
+description: Grant application permissions to an agent identity with an authorization request, the admin consent endpoint, or Microsoft Graph.
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/05/2026
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+ms.reviewer: dastrock
+
+#customer-intent: As a developer or administrator, I want to grant Microsoft Graph application permissions to an agent identity so that it can call APIs as itself without a signed-in user.
+---
+
+# Grant Microsoft Graph application permissions to an agent identity
+
+Application permissions let an agent call Microsoft Graph as itself, without a signed-in user. All application permissions require administrator approval. Users can't consent to them.
+
+You can grant application permissions to an agent identity in three ways:
+
+| Method | Who grants consent | Use it when |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| [Authorization request](#method-1-request-administrator-consent-with-an-authorization-request) | An administrator who signs in through the agent's consent flow | The agent or its setup experience prompts an administrator interactively. |
+| [Admin consent endpoint](#method-2-request-administrator-consent-with-the-admin-consent-endpoint) | An administrator, for the organization | You send an administrator a link to approve the agent. |
+| [Microsoft Graph](#method-3-assign-application-permissions-with-microsoft-graph) | An administrator or automation | You grant permissions programmatically, such as when you provision an agent. |
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> For Azure services, grant the agent identity an Azure RBAC role on the target resource rather than an application permission. See [Call Azure services as an agent with ASP.NET Core](call-api-azure-services.md).
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- An agent identity created from a blueprint. Record its client ID for methods 1 and 2, and its service principal object ID for method 3. For identifier meanings, see [Record the identifiers for your scenario](key-concepts.md#record-the-identifiers-for-your-scenario).
+- Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator role to grant admin consent.
+- For methods 1 and 2, a web redirect URI registered on the blueprint.
+- For method 3, a Microsoft Graph management client with `AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All` and `Application.Read.All`. For delegated access, the signed-in administrator also needs **Privileged Role Administrator** to assign Microsoft Graph app roles. See the [app role assignment API permissions](/graph/api/serviceprincipal-post-approleassignments#permissions).
+
+## Method 1: Request administrator consent with an authorization request
+
+Direct an administrator to the authorization endpoint. Use the agent identity client ID as the OAuth client. For single-instance agents, it is shared with the blueprint; for fleets, use the selected agent's client ID, not the blueprint's. Use the `role` parameter to specify each required permission. The consent-only request uses `response_type=none`, so it records consent without returning a token.
+
+```text
+https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/oauth2/v2.0/authorize
+?client_id=<agent-identity-client-id>
+&response_type=none
+&redirect_uri=<registered-redirect-uri>
+&response_mode=query
+&role=User.Read.All
+&role=Mail.Read
+&state=<opaque-state-value>
+```
+
+The administrator signs in and approves the permissions for the organization. Validate `state` when the browser returns to the redirect URI to prevent request forgery.
+
+## Method 2: Request administrator consent with the admin consent endpoint
+
+Direct an administrator to the admin consent endpoint. Use the `role` parameter to specify each required permission:
+
+```text
+https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/v2.0/adminconsent
+?client_id=<agent-identity-client-id>
+&role=User.Read.All
+&redirect_uri=<registered-redirect-uri>
+&state=<opaque-state-value>
+```
+
+To request multiple permissions in a single request, repeat the `role` parameter:
+
+```text
+https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/v2.0/adminconsent
+?client_id=<agent-identity-client-id>
+&role=User.Read.All
+&role=Mail.Read
+&redirect_uri=<registered-redirect-uri>
+&state=<opaque-state-value>
+```
+
+| Parameter | Description |
+| --- | --- |
+| `client_id` | Client ID of the agent identity. For single-instance agents, this is shared with the blueprint. For fleets, don't use the blueprint client ID. |
+| `role` | Permission name to grant, such as `User.Read.All`. Repeat for each permission. |
+| `redirect_uri` | A registered redirect URI on the blueprint app registration. |
+| `state` | Opaque value validated on return to prevent request forgery. |
+
+After the administrator authenticates and approves, Microsoft Entra redirects to the redirect URI. Validate `state` before processing the response.
+
+## Method 3: Assign application permissions with Microsoft Graph
+
+Create an app role assignment directly on the agent identity's service principal:
+
+Use the management client's access token, not the agent's runtime credential. Don't grant these directory-management permissions to the agent just to let it call a downstream API.
+
+```http
+POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals/<agent-identity-id>/appRoleAssignments
+Content-Type: application/json
+Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>
+
+{
+  "principalId": "<agent-identity-id>",
+  "resourceId": "<microsoft-graph-service-principal-object-id>",
+  "appRoleId": "<app-role-id>"
+}
+```
+
+| Property | Description |
+| --- | --- |
+| `principalId` | ID of the agent identity. |
+| `resourceId` | Object ID of the Microsoft Graph service principal in your tenant. |
+| `appRoleId` | GUID of the specific application permission to grant. |
+
+Grant one permission per request.
+
+**Find the Microsoft Graph service principal object ID:**
+
+```http
+GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals?$filter=appId eq '00000003-0000-0000-c000-000000000000'&$select=id,displayName
+```
+
+**Find the app role ID for a specific permission:**
+
+```http
+GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals?$filter=appId eq '00000003-0000-0000-c000-000000000000'&$select=appRoles
+```
+
+In the response, find the entry in `appRoles` where `value` matches the permission name, such as `User.Read.All`. Use its `id` as `appRoleId`.
+
+## Verify the assignment
+
+After granting permissions, verify that each app role assignment was created:
+
+```http
+GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals/<agent-identity-id>/appRoleAssignments
+```
+
+Each entry in the response represents one granted application permission. The agent identity can request tokens with `https://graph.microsoft.com/.default` to receive the granted roles in the token's `roles` claim.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Grant delegated permissions to an agent identity](grant-agent-access-microsoft-365.md)
+- [Call Microsoft Graph as an agent with ASP.NET Core](call-api-microsoft-graph.md)
+- [Call Microsoft Graph as an agent with the Auth SDK sidecar](sidecar-call-graph-as-agent.md)
+- [Microsoft Graph permissions reference](/graph/permissions-reference)

diff --git a/docs/agent-id/integrate-aws-agent.md b/docs/agent-id/integrate-aws-agent.md
new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..d3155aae229
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/agent-id/integrate-aws-agent.md
@@ -0,0 +1,168 @@
+---
+title: Use an AWS workload identity with Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+description: Use an AWS token to get an Agent ID token and call a protected API.
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/05/2026
+ms.reviewer: dastrock
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+
+#customer-intent: As a developer hosting an agent on AWS, I want to use its AWS identity to get an Agent ID token without storing a Microsoft Entra secret.
+---
+
+# Use an AWS workload identity with Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+
+Use workload identity federation when an agent hosted on Amazon Web Services (AWS) calls a Microsoft Entra-protected resource as itself. AWS Security Token Service (STS) issues a short-lived JSON Web Token (JWT). Microsoft Entra ID trusts that token as a federated credential for the agent identity blueprint.
+
+This path supports app-only access. It doesn't authenticate users or perform an On-Behalf-Of flow.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- An [agent identity blueprint](create-blueprint.md) and [Agent ID](create-delete-agent-identities.md).
+- An AWS IAM role for the hosted workload.
+- Permission to enable AWS IAM Outbound Identity Federation and update the IAM role.
+- An application permission, app role, or resource role assigned to the Agent ID.
+- Python 3 with current `boto3` and `requests` packages for the example.
+- An execution environment authenticated as the AWS workload role. Run the example there so `boto3` uses that role, not an unrelated developer identity.
+
+## Enable AWS outbound identity federation
+
+Enable the feature for the AWS account:
+
+```azurecli
+aws iam enable-outbound-web-identity-federation
+```
+
+Record the account-specific issuer URL returned by AWS. The `GetWebIdentityToken` API requires a regional STS endpoint and isn't available through the global endpoint.
+
+Grant the workload role permission to request only tokens intended for Microsoft Entra ID:
+
+```json
+{
+  "Version": "2012-10-17",
+  "Statement": [
+    {
+      "Effect": "Allow",
+      "Action": "sts:GetWebIdentityToken",
+      "Resource": "*",
+      "Condition": {
+        "ForAllValues:StringEquals": {
+          "sts:IdentityTokenAudience": "api://AzureADTokenExchange"
+        },
+        "NumericLessThanEquals": {
+          "sts:DurationSeconds": 300
+        }
+      }
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+For the complete AWS procedure, see [Getting started with outbound identity federation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_providers_outbound_getting_started.html).
+
+## Add the AWS identity to the blueprint
+
+Add a federated credential to the agent identity blueprint:
+
+1. Open the blueprint in the Microsoft Entra admin center.
+1. Select **Credentials** > **Federated credentials** > **Add credential**.
+1. Select **Other issuer**.
+1. Enter the AWS account-specific issuer URL.
+1. Enter the IAM role ARN as the subject, such as `arn:aws:iam::<account-id>:role/<role-name>`.
+1. Enter `api://AzureADTokenExchange` as the audience.
+1. Add the credential.
+
+The issuer, subject, and audience must exactly match the `iss`, `sub`, and `aud` claims in the AWS token. Wildcards aren't supported. For more information, see [Add a federated credential to an agent identity blueprint](manage-agent-blueprint.md#add-a-federated-credential) and [AWS outbound token claims](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_providers_outbound_token_claims.html).
+
+## Grant access to the Agent ID
+
+Grant the Agent ID the application permission or resource role required by the target API. The federated credential only authenticates the blueprint; it doesn't authorize access to a downstream resource.
+
+For a custom API, expose and assign an application role. For an Azure resource, assign the Agent ID the required Azure role.
+
+## Exchange the AWS token
+
+Install the example dependencies:
+
+```bash
+pip install --upgrade boto3 requests
+```
+
+The following example gets an AWS token, exchanges it for an Agent ID resource token, and calls the protected API:
+
+```python
+import boto3
+import requests
+
+TENANT_ID = "<tenant-id>"
+BLUEPRINT_CLIENT_ID = "<agent-identity-blueprint-client-id>"
+AGENT_ID_CLIENT_ID = "<agent-identity-client-id>"
+RESOURCE_SCOPE = "api://<resource-client-id>/.default"
+RESOURCE_URL = "https://api.contoso.com/data"
+
+token_endpoint = (
+    f"https://login.microsoftonline.com/{TENANT_ID}/oauth2/v2.0/token"
+)
+
+
+def exchange_token(client_id, scope, assertion, fmi_path=None):
+    data = {
+        "client_id": client_id,
+        "scope": scope,
+        "grant_type": "client_credentials",
+        "client_assertion_type":
+            "urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer",
+        "client_assertion": assertion,
+    }
+    if fmi_path:
+        data["fmi_path"] = fmi_path
+
+    response = requests.post(token_endpoint, data=data, timeout=30)
+    response.raise_for_status()
+    return response.json()["access_token"]
+
+
+sts = boto3.client("sts", region_name="<aws-region>")
+aws_token = sts.get_web_identity_token(
+    Audience=["api://AzureADTokenExchange"],
+    SigningAlgorithm="RS256",
+    DurationSeconds=300,
+)["WebIdentityToken"]
+
+blueprint_token = exchange_token(
+    BLUEPRINT_CLIENT_ID,
+    "api://AzureADTokenExchange/.default",
+    aws_token,
+    AGENT_ID_CLIENT_ID,
+)
+
+resource_token = exchange_token(
+    AGENT_ID_CLIENT_ID,
+    RESOURCE_SCOPE,
+    blueprint_token,
+)
+
+resource_response = requests.get(
+    RESOURCE_URL,
+    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {resource_token}"},
+    timeout=30,
+)
+resource_response.raise_for_status()
+```
+
+Don't log the AWS assertion, blueprint token, or resource token. Request a new AWS token for each exchange rather than storing it.
+
+Verify that the resource call returns the API's expected successful response. If the AWS token request fails, check the workload role, regional STS endpoint, and outbound federation permission. If the Microsoft Entra exchange fails, check the blueprint's federated credential and the selected agent ID. If only the resource call fails, check the resource scope and the permissions assigned to the Agent ID; successful federation doesn't grant API access.
+
+For the Agent ID exchanges, see [Agent autonomous app OAuth flow](agent-autonomous-app-oauth-flow.md). For the AWS token API, see [GetWebIdentityToken](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/STS/latest/APIReference/API_GetWebIdentityToken.html).
+
+## Clean up test access
+
+Remove test-only resource permissions and the federated credential when you no longer need this integration. Coordinate with the AWS account owner before removing role permissions or disabling account-wide outbound federation; other workloads might depend on them. Delete the Agent ID or blueprint only if no remaining agent uses those resources.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Microsoft Entra workload identity federation](/entra/workload-id/workload-identity-federation)
+- [Configure an app to trust an external identity provider](/entra/workload-id/workload-identity-federation-create-trust)
+- [AWS IAM Outbound Identity Federation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_providers_outbound_getting_started.html)
+- [Validate Agent ID tokens in the protected API](how-to-validate-agent-tokens-downstream-api.md)

+---
+title: Use Microsoft Entra Agent ID with Copilot Studio
+description: Find and manage the Agent ID that Copilot Studio creates for a new agent.
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 10/28/2026
+ms.reviewer: dastrock
+
+#customer-intent: As a Copilot Studio maker or administrator, I want to find and govern the Agent ID created for my agent.
+---
+
+# Use Microsoft Entra Agent ID with Copilot Studio
+
+Microsoft Copilot Studio automatically creates a Microsoft Entra Agent ID for each new agent. Copilot Studio manages the blueprint, Agent ID, and platform credentials. You don't register the identity or implement token acquisition.
+
+Automatic Agent ID creation is built in for new agents and can't be turned off. Agents created before the integration rollout can continue to use legacy app registrations until they migrate.
+
+## Create the agent
+
+Create an agent by following [Create and delete agents in Copilot Studio](/microsoft-copilot-studio/authoring-first-bot). Copilot Studio creates the Agent ID as part of the agent lifecycle.
+
+When the first Agent ID is created, Copilot Studio adds the **Microsoft Copilot Studio agent identity blueprint** to the tenant. Copilot Studio manages this shared blueprint and its credentials.
+
+Don't create a separate blueprint or Agent ID for the Copilot Studio agent.
+
+## Find the Agent ID
+
+1. Open the agent in Copilot Studio.
+1. Go to **Settings** > **Advanced**.
+1. Expand **Metadata**.
+1. Copy the GUID under **Entra Agent ID**.
+1. Use the GUID to find the Agent ID in the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
+
+For the current lifecycle, metadata, and deletion behavior, see [Manage Entra Agent IDs in Copilot Studio](/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-use-entra-agent-identities).
+
+## Review connector permissions
+
+When you publish the agent, Copilot Studio attaches API permissions for its Power Platform connectors to the Agent ID. Review those permissions in Microsoft Entra ID and keep the agent's connectors and data policies aligned with the intended scenario.
+
+Copilot Studio manages the connector runtime and platform credential. Don't add credentials to the Agent ID.
+
+## Handle an existing agent
+
+An older agent might still use an app-registration identity. You can wait for the platform migration or use the self-service migration process.
+
+For current migration options, see [Migrate Copilot Studio agents to Microsoft Entra Agent ID](/microsoft-copilot-studio/govern-migrate-api-entra-agent-identity). For planning guidance in this documentation, see [Recreate Copilot Studio agents with Microsoft Entra Agent ID](migrate-copilot-studio-agents-to-agent-id.md).
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Manage Entra Agent IDs in Copilot Studio](/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-use-entra-agent-identities)
+- [Agent identities and authentication in Copilot Studio](/microsoft-copilot-studio/govern-agents-identities-overview)
+- [Migrate Copilot Studio agents to Agent ID](/microsoft-copilot-studio/govern-migrate-api-entra-agent-identity)

diff --git a/docs/agent-id/integrate-google-cloud-agent.md b/docs/agent-id/integrate-google-cloud-agent.md

+++ b/docs/agent-id/integrate-google-cloud-agent.md
@@ -0,0 +1,141 @@
+---
+title: Use a Google Cloud workload identity with Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+description: Use a Google token to get an Agent ID token and call a protected API.
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/05/2026
+ms.reviewer: dastrock
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+
+#customer-intent: As a developer hosting an agent on Google Cloud, I want to use its service account identity to get an Agent ID token without storing a Microsoft Entra secret.
+---
+
+# Use a Google Cloud workload identity with Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+
+Use workload identity federation when an agent hosted on Google Cloud calls a Microsoft Entra-protected resource as itself. Google issues a short-lived OpenID Connect ID token for the workload's service account. Microsoft Entra ID trusts that token as a federated credential for the agent identity blueprint.
+
+This path supports app-only access. It doesn't authenticate users or perform an On-Behalf-Of flow.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- An [agent identity blueprint](create-blueprint.md) and [Agent ID](create-delete-agent-identities.md).
+- A Google Cloud service account attached to the workload.
+- The service account's unique numeric ID.
+- An application permission, app role, or resource role assigned to the Agent ID.
+- Python 3 with the `requests` package for the example.
+- A supported Google Cloud workload where the metadata server is available. Run the example on that workload with the intended service account attached, not on an unconfigured local workstation.
+
+## Add the Google identity to the blueprint
+
+Add a federated credential to the agent identity blueprint:
+
+1. Open the blueprint in the Microsoft Entra admin center.
+1. Select **Credentials** > **Federated credentials** > **Add credential**.
+1. Select **Other issuer**.
+1. Enter `https://accounts.google.com` as the issuer.
+1. Enter the service account's unique numeric ID as the subject.
+1. Enter `api://AzureADTokenExchange` as the audience.
+1. Add the credential.
+
+The values must exactly match the Google token:
+
+| Federated credential | Google token claim | Value |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Issuer | `iss` | `https://accounts.google.com` |
+| Subject | `sub` | Service account unique ID |
+| Audience | `aud` | `api://AzureADTokenExchange` |
+
+For the complete Microsoft procedure, see [Federate a Google Cloud workload identity with Microsoft Entra ID](/entra/workload-id/workload-identity-federation-google-cloud). For blueprint steps, see [Add a federated credential to an agent identity blueprint](manage-agent-blueprint.md#add-a-federated-credential).
+
+## Grant access to the Agent ID
+
+Grant the Agent ID the application permission or resource role required by the target API. The Google service account and the Agent ID remain separate identities. The federated credential lets the Google identity authenticate the blueprint; the target resource authorizes the Agent ID.
+
+## Exchange the Google token
+
+Install the example dependency:
+
+```bash
+pip install requests
+```
+
+The following example requests a Google ID token from the metadata server, exchanges it for an Agent ID resource token, and calls the protected API:
+
+```python
+import requests
+
+TENANT_ID = "<tenant-id>"
+BLUEPRINT_CLIENT_ID = "<agent-identity-blueprint-client-id>"
+AGENT_ID_CLIENT_ID = "<agent-identity-client-id>"
+RESOURCE_SCOPE = "api://<resource-client-id>/.default"
+RESOURCE_URL = "https://api.contoso.com/data"
+
+token_endpoint = (
+    f"https://login.microsoftonline.com/{TENANT_ID}/oauth2/v2.0/token"
+)
+
+
+def exchange_token(client_id, scope, assertion, fmi_path=None):
+    data = {
+        "client_id": client_id,
+        "scope": scope,
+        "grant_type": "client_credentials",
+        "client_assertion_type":
+            "urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer",
+        "client_assertion": assertion,
+    }
+    if fmi_path:
+        data["fmi_path"] = fmi_path
+
+    response = requests.post(token_endpoint, data=data, timeout=30)
+    response.raise_for_status()
+    return response.json()["access_token"]
+
+
+metadata_response = requests.get(
+    "http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/"
+    "service-accounts/default/identity",
+    params={"audience": "api://AzureADTokenExchange"},
+    headers={"Metadata-Flavor": "Google"},
+    timeout=10,
+)
+metadata_response.raise_for_status()
+google_token = metadata_response.text
+
+blueprint_token = exchange_token(
+    BLUEPRINT_CLIENT_ID,
+    "api://AzureADTokenExchange/.default",
+    google_token,
+    AGENT_ID_CLIENT_ID,
+)
+
+resource_token = exchange_token(
+    AGENT_ID_CLIENT_ID,
+    RESOURCE_SCOPE,
+    blueprint_token,
+)
+
+resource_response = requests.get(
+    RESOURCE_URL,
+    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {resource_token}"},
+    timeout=30,
+)
+resource_response.raise_for_status()
+```
+
+The metadata server is available only to supported Google Cloud workloads with an attached service account. Don't log the Google assertion, blueprint token, or resource token.
+
+Verify that the resource call returns the API's expected successful response. If metadata retrieval fails, check the hosting environment and attached service account. If the Microsoft Entra exchange fails, compare the configured issuer, numeric service account subject, and audience with the required trust values. If only the resource call fails, check its scope and the permissions granted to the Agent ID rather than changing the Google service account's permissions.
+
+For the Google token procedure, see [Get an ID token from the metadata server](https://cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/get-id-token#metadata-server). For the Agent ID exchanges, see [Agent autonomous app OAuth flow](agent-autonomous-app-oauth-flow.md).
+
+## Clean up test access
+
+Remove test-only resource permissions and the blueprint's federated credential when testing is complete. Delete the Agent ID or blueprint only if no remaining agent needs it. Don't delete a shared Google service account or detach it from other workloads as part of this cleanup.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Federate a Google Cloud workload identity with Microsoft Entra ID](/entra/workload-id/workload-identity-federation-google-cloud)
+- [Google Cloud service account ID tokens](https://cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/get-id-token)
+- [Configure an app to trust an external identity provider](/entra/workload-id/workload-identity-federation-create-trust)
+- [Validate Agent ID tokens in the protected API](how-to-validate-agent-tokens-downstream-api.md)

+---
+title: Use Microsoft Entra Agent ID with Microsoft Foundry
+description: Use the built-in Agent ID for a new Microsoft Foundry agent.
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 10/28/2026
+ms.reviewer: dastrock
+
+#customer-intent: As a Foundry developer, I want my agent to use its built-in Agent ID when it accesses protected resources.
+---
+
+# Use Microsoft Entra Agent ID with Microsoft Foundry
+
+Microsoft Foundry has built-in support for Microsoft Entra Agent ID. Foundry creates and manages the agent identity blueprint, Agent ID, and platform credential. You don't add a client secret or implement the Agent ID token exchange.
+
+Use the current Foundry agent object model to opt in to this integration. Agents that use the legacy model continue to use a shared project identity or an Agent Application identity.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A [Microsoft Foundry project](/azure/foundry/how-to/create-projects).
+- Permission to create agents in the project.
+- Permission to grant the Agent ID access to each downstream resource.
+
+## Create an agent with Agent ID
+
+Create a new agent by using the current Foundry agent model. A new agent receives:
+
+- A unique agent identity blueprint.
+- A unique Agent ID for its default instance.
+- A stable agent endpoint.
+- A platform-managed federated credential that Foundry uses for token exchange.
+
+Follow [Configure and share your Microsoft Foundry agent](/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/configure-agent) to create and configure the agent.
+
+If the project contains a legacy agent, create a new agent from the same definition. Foundry doesn't add a unique Agent ID to a legacy agent in place. For the opt-in and migration steps, see [Migrate from Agent Applications to the new Microsoft Foundry agent model](/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/migrate-agent-applications#migration-paths).
+
+## Verify the agent identity
+
+Retrieve or inspect the agent and confirm that `instance_identity` isn't null. A non-null value identifies an agent created with the current model.
+
+Foundry manages the blueprint credential and runtime token exchange. Don't create another credential for the Foundry-managed blueprint.
+
+For details about the objects that Foundry creates, see [Agent identity concepts in Microsoft Foundry](/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-identity#how-foundry-provisions-identities).
+
+## Grant access to a resource
+
+New Agent IDs start without resource permissions. Grant access to the Agent ID used by the tool call:
+
+- For an Azure resource, assign the least-privileged Azure role at the narrowest practical scope.
+- For a custom API, assign the required application permission or app role.
+- For delegated access, configure a supported user-delegation connection and obtain consent.
+
+Use the Agent ID's object ID, not its client ID, when an Azure role assignment requires a principal ID.
+
+For supported tools and authorization models, see [Permissions and access boundaries in Microsoft Foundry](/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-identity#permissions-and-access-boundaries).
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Agent identity concepts in Microsoft Foundry](/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-identity)
+- [Configure and share a Foundry agent](/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/configure-agent)
+- [Migrate to the current Foundry agent model](/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/migrate-agent-applications)
+- [Azure role-based access control in Foundry](/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry)

@@ -0,0 +1,271 @@
+---
+title: Manage CIMD clients in Microsoft Entra ID
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+description: Add, approve, find, monitor, and remove Client ID Metadata Document clients in Microsoft Entra ID.
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 09/21/2026
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+
+#customer-intent: As an Entra administrator, I want to control and monitor CIMD clients in my tenant so that users can connect approved MCP clients without bypassing organizational consent and security policies.
+---
+
+# Manage CIMD clients in Microsoft Entra ID (preview)
+
+Microsoft Entra ID represents a client discovered through a Client ID Metadata Document (CIMD) as an agent identity in your tenant. You can add a trusted CIMD client in advance, grant delegated permissions, monitor its activity, and disable or delete it by using the same management surfaces used for other agent identities.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> Client ID Metadata Document support in Microsoft Entra ID is in public preview. This preview is provided without a service-level agreement and isn't recommended for production workloads. Some features might be unsupported or have constrained capabilities. For more information, see [Universal License Terms for Online Services](https://www.microsoft.com/licensing/terms/product/ForOnlineServices/all).
+
+Before enabling CIMD scenarios, review [Client ID Metadata Documents in Microsoft Entra ID](client-id-metadata-documents.md), including the limitations and governance considerations.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+To manage CIMD clients, you need:
+
+- A Microsoft Entra tenant in which CIMD support is available.
+- The CIMD URL supplied by the client owner.
+- An account with a role that can create agent identities, such as **Global Administrator**, **Agent ID Administrator**, **AI Administrator**, or **Agent ID Developer**.
+- Administrator consent for the Microsoft Graph permissions used by any automation:
+  - `AgentIdentity.Create.All` to create a CIMD-backed agent identity.
+  - `AgentIdentity.Read.All` to read and list agent identities.
+- To change consent policy programmatically:
+  - The **Privileged Role Administrator** role.
+  - `Policy.ReadWrite.PermissionGrant` to create or update a permission grant policy.
+  - `Policy.ReadWrite.Authorization` to assign a permission grant policy to the default user role.
+
+Use the least-privileged role and permissions that meet your requirements.
+
+## Choose a tenant posture
+
+Before you configure CIMD, decide who can add a new CIMD client to your tenant.
+
+| Approach | Behavior | Consider when |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Administrator-curated | Disable user-initiated CIMD use. An administrator reviews each client, creates its agent identity, and grants the required permissions. | Your organization requires a security or application-onboarding review before creating an identity. |
+| Policy-controlled user consent | Let users add CIMD clients when the client and requested delegated permissions satisfy consent policy. Permissions outside the policy still require an administrator. | Your organization permits low-risk self-service integrations and monitors newly created identities. |
+
+Both postures use consent policy to control user-initiated creation. Neither posture automatically grants a CIMD client access to every resource. Consent grants and tenant policy continue to determine which delegated permissions the client can use.
+
+### Disable user-initiated CIMD use
+
+To prevent users from adding CIMD clients:
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as a **Global Administrator**.
+1. Browse to **Entra ID** > **Enterprise apps** > **Consent and permissions** > **User consent settings**.
+1. Disable **Allow user consent for unregistered apps and agents using Client ID Metadata Documents**.
+1. Select **Save**.
+
+When user consent for CIMD clients is disabled, users can't approve a new CIMD client themselves. During preview, the admin consent request workflow is disabled for Agent ID, including CIMD clients. Arrange a manual handoff: the user or client owner supplies the CIMD URL, target resource, and requested delegated scopes to an administrator, who adds the client and grants the required permissions before the user retries.
+
+Disabling user consent doesn't delete existing CIMD-backed agent identities or revoke existing consent grants. Review and revoke those grants separately if you want to stop use of clients that are already approved.
+
+### Enable user-initiated CIMD use with a custom consent policy
+
+Use a custom permission grant policy when you want users to add CIMD clients and consent to a controlled set of permissions. The following Microsoft Graph PowerShell example:
+
+1. Creates a CIMD-specific permission grant policy.
+1. Adds an include condition that allows delegated permissions classified as low impact.
+1. Assigns the policy to the default user role without removing existing policy assignments.
+
+The CIMD condition is available on the Microsoft Graph beta endpoint.
+
+```powershell
+Connect-MgGraph -Scopes @(
+    "Policy.ReadWrite.PermissionGrant",
+    "Policy.ReadWrite.Authorization"
+)
+
+$policyId = "contoso-user-consent-cimd-low"
+
+# Create a custom permission grant policy for CIMD clients.
+$policy = @{
+    id = $policyId
+    displayName = "Allow low-impact user consent for CIMD clients"
+    description = "Users can consent to delegated permissions classified as low impact for CIMD clients."
+}
+
+Invoke-MgGraphRequest `
+    -Method POST `
+    -Uri "https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/policies/permissionGrantPolicies" `
+    -Body ($policy | ConvertTo-Json)
+
+# Add an include condition that matches only CIMD clients.
+$condition = @{
+    permissionType = "delegated"
+    permissionClassification = "low"
+    resourceApplication = "any"
+    permissions = @("all")
+    clientApplicationIds = @("all")
+    clientApplicationTenantIds = @("all")
+    clientApplicationPublisherIds = @("all")
+    clientApplicationsFromVerifiedPublisherOnly = $false
+    cimdClientApplications = @{
+        "@odata.type" = "#microsoft.graph.allCimdClientApplications"
+    }
+}
+
+Invoke-MgGraphRequest `
+    -Method POST `
+    -Uri "https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/policies/permissionGrantPolicies/$policyId/includes" `
+    -Body ($condition | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4)
+
+# Preserve existing assignments and add the CIMD-specific policy.
+$authorizationPolicy = Invoke-MgGraphRequest `
+    -Method GET `
+    -Uri "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/policies/authorizationPolicy"
+
+$assignments = @(
+    $authorizationPolicy.defaultUserRolePermissions.permissionGrantPoliciesAssigned
+)
+$assignmentId = "managePermissionGrantsForSelf.$policyId"
+
+if ($assignments -notcontains $assignmentId) {
+    $assignments += $assignmentId
+}
+
+$update = @{
+    defaultUserRolePermissions = @{
+        permissionGrantPoliciesAssigned = $assignments
+    }
+}
+
+Invoke-MgGraphRequest `
+    -Method PATCH `
+    -Uri "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/policies/authorizationPolicy" `
+    -Body ($update | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4)
+```
+
+If you already have a custom policy for user consent, add the CIMD include condition to that policy instead of creating another policy. Don't edit a Microsoft-managed policy; built-in policies can't be changed.
+
+The example uses `permissionClassification = "low"`. Only permissions classified as low impact can be granted under this condition. Review your tenant's [permission classifications](/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/configure-permission-classifications) before assigning the policy.
+
+To verify the update, list the policy's include conditions and confirm that the authorization policy contains the assignment:
+
+```http
+GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/policies/permissionGrantPolicies/contoso-user-consent-cimd-low/includes
+
+GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/policies/authorizationPolicy
+```
+
+To disable this custom CIMD policy later, remove `managePermissionGrantsForSelf.contoso-user-consent-cimd-low` from `permissionGrantPoliciesAssigned` and update the authorization policy again. Preserve every unrelated assignment in the collection.
+
+For more information about how include and exclude condition sets are evaluated, see [Manage app consent policies](/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/manage-app-consent-policies).
+
+## Add a CIMD client in the admin center
+
+In the administrator-curated posture, review a client and create its agent identity before users connect.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> CIMD verifies control of a URL. It doesn't establish that the client is trustworthy. Review the client owner, document URL, redirect URIs, requested permissions, and business purpose before approval.
+
+To add a trusted client before a user connects:
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
+1. Browse to **Entra ID** > **Agents** > **Agent identities**.
+1. Select **Add CIMD client (Preview)**.
+1. Enter the client's CIMD URL and continue.
+1. Review the metadata retrieved from the document.
+1. Complete the creation process.
+1. [Grant only the delegated permissions required by the protected resource](grant-agent-access-microsoft-365.md). During preview, use the sign-in and consent endpoints or Microsoft Graph, not the portal permissions experience.
+
+Creating the identity doesn't by itself authorize access to every resource. Consent grants and tenant policy continue to determine which delegated permissions the client can use.
+
+## Add a CIMD client with Microsoft Graph
+
+You can create the tenant-local agent identity by using the Microsoft Graph beta endpoint.
+
+```http
+POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/servicePrincipals/microsoft.graph.agentIdentity
+Authorization: Bearer {token}
+Content-Type: application/json
+
+{
+  "displayName": "Contoso Agent",
+  "clientIdMetadataDocumentUrl": "https://client.contoso.com/oauth/client-metadata.json"
+}
+```
+
+Microsoft Entra ID retrieves and validates the document before creating the identity. A successful response resembles:
+
+```json
+{
+  "@odata.type": "#microsoft.graph.agentIdentity",
+  "id": "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555",
+  "agentIdentityBlueprintId": "aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee",
+  "displayName": "Contoso Agent",
+  "clientIdMetadataDocumentUrl": "https://client.contoso.com/oauth/client-metadata.json",
+  "isClientIdMetadataDocument": true
+}
+```
+
+The `agentIdentityBlueprintId` value is derived for identity and correlation purposes. Creating a CIMD client doesn't create a separately manageable agent identity blueprint.
+
+The request fails if the URL isn't HTTPS, the document can't be retrieved or validated, its `client_id` doesn't exactly match the URL, or the canonical URL already identifies another agent identity in the tenant.
+
+## Find CIMD clients with Microsoft Graph
+
+To list all CIMD-backed agent identities, use an advanced query:
+
+```http
+GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/servicePrincipals/microsoft.graph.agentIdentity?$filter=isClientIdMetadataDocument eq true&$count=true
+Authorization: Bearer {token}
+ConsistencyLevel: eventual
+```
+
+To find an identity by its canonical CIMD URL:
+
+```http
+GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/servicePrincipals/microsoft.graph.agentIdentity?$filter=clientIdMetadataDocumentUrl eq 'https://client.contoso.com/oauth/client-metadata.json'&$count=true
+Authorization: Bearer {token}
+ConsistencyLevel: eventual
+```
+
+Both filters require `$count=true` and the `ConsistencyLevel: eventual` request header.
+
+## Monitor a CIMD client
+
+CIMD-backed identities appear in Microsoft Entra sign-in and audit logs as agent identities.
+
+Monitor:
+
+- Successful and failed sign-ins.
+- Users who authorize or use the client.
+- Resources and delegated scopes the client accesses.
+- Creation, update, disablement, deletion, and consent-grant events.
+- Unexpected changes in client behavior or redirect destinations.
+
+The app ID shown in logs is derived from the CIMD URL. The client has no home application tenant. For more information, see [Microsoft Entra Agent ID logs](sign-in-audit-logs-agents.md).
+
+## Respond to a compromised or untrusted client
+
+If a CIMD client, its signing material, or its domain might be compromised:
+
+1. Disable the agent identity to stop new token issuance.
+1. Revoke its delegated permission grants.
+1. Revoke affected user sessions when required by your incident-response process.
+1. Review sign-in and audit logs for unexpected activity.
+1. Delete the agent identity when you no longer need investigation data or a disabled record.
+1. Contact the client owner through a trusted channel.
+
+If the publisher loses control of the CIMD URL or moves the document, don't update the existing identity to a new URL. The URL is immutable. Review and onboard the new URL as a new client, then grant permissions again.
+
+## Understand governance gaps
+
+The external CIMD document remains the source of truth for OAuth client configuration. Microsoft Entra ID doesn't copy the complete configuration to an application object.
+
+Consider the following governance gaps:
+
+- App management policy doesn't evaluate configuration that exists only in the CIMD document.
+- Inventory and recommendations that inspect stored application credentials or redirect URIs might not include CIMD metadata.
+- CIMD clients can't be publisher verified or Microsoft 365 certified.
+- There is no tenant-managed domain allowlist or blocklist for CIMD URLs.
+- CIMD clients can't be used for app-only authentication or as protected resources.
+
+Maintain an independent inventory of approved CIMD URLs and review it regularly.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Client ID Metadata Documents in Microsoft Entra ID](client-id-metadata-documents.md)
+- [Configure a client to use a Client ID Metadata Document](configure-client-id-metadata-document.md)
+- [Manage agent identities in your organization](manage-agent-identities-admin.md)
+- [Microsoft Entra Agent ID logs](sign-in-audit-logs-agents.md)

--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/agent-id/plan-agent-fleet.md
@@ -0,0 +1,104 @@
+---
+title: Plan an agent fleet on a shared runtime
+description: Learn how to design authentication for many agents hosted on a shared cloud runtime, with one blueprint and one agent identity per agent.
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+ms.topic: concept-article
+ms.date: 11/05/2026
+ms.reviewer: dastrock
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+
+#customer-intent: As a developer building an agent hosting platform, I want to understand how to provision and use an agent identity for each agent in my fleet so that every agent authenticates with its own identity.
+---
+
+# Plan an agent fleet on a shared runtime
+
+An agent fleet is a set of agents that run on a shared cloud runtime. For example, a platform that lets teams or customers deploy their own agents hosts each new agent on the same compute and code base. Each agent in the fleet gets its own [agent identity](what-are-agent-identities.md), so its sign-ins, permissions, and audit records stay separate from the other agents.
+
+The runtime holds a single [agent identity blueprint](agent-blueprint.md) credential and uses it to acquire tokens for any agent identity created from that blueprint. The runtime chooses which agent identity to use on each token request.
+
+## Choose between a single agent and a fleet
+
+| Consideration | Single agent | Agent fleet |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Number of agents per deployment | One | Many, added and removed at runtime |
+| When agent identities are created | Before the agent is deployed, by a developer or administrator | When each agent is deployed, by the runtime or by Agent 365 |
+| Where the agent identity ID comes from | Configuration | A lookup on each request |
+| How access is granted | To the agent identity, before the agent is deployed | To each agent identity, when the agent is provisioned |
+| Guidance | [Build cloud agents with ASP.NET Core](call-api-custom.md) or [the Auth SDK sidecar](authentication-with-auth-sdk-sidecar.md) | This article and the fleet articles that follow it |
+
+The fleet runtime selects an agent's identity for each operation. Follow the fleet examples throughout this journey: the cloud-agent tutorials use one configured identity and omit the per-request identity selection required by a fleet.
+
+## Components
+
+| Component | Purpose | Cardinality |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Agent identity blueprint | Defines the fleet's permissions, inbound scope, and app roles. Creates and deletes agent identities. | One per fleet, or one per agent type |
+| Blueprint credential | Authenticates the runtime as the blueprint. Use a managed identity federated credential in production. | One per blueprint |
+| Agent identity | Represents one agent. Receives the access tokens used to call APIs. | One per agent |
+| Agent's user account | Gives an agent a user object for Microsoft 365 workloads such as a mailbox or Teams membership. | Optional, at most one per agent identity |
+| Agent directory | The runtime's store that maps each agent to its agent identity and agent's user account. | One per fleet |
+| Provisioning service | Creates and deletes identities when agents are deployed and retired. | One per fleet |
+| Token broker | Acquires tokens for a given agent identity. *Microsoft.Identity.Web* in the runtime process, or the Auth SDK sidecar. | One or more per runtime |
+
+## Agent lifecycle
+
+1. **Deploy.** A user or pipeline deploys a new agent to the runtime.
+1. **Provision.** The provisioning service creates an agent identity from the blueprint. If the agent needs Microsoft 365 user capabilities, it also creates an agent's user account. It records both IDs in the agent directory, and the agent identity is granted the access that this agent needs.
+1. **Run.** For each operation, the runtime looks up the agent's identity in the agent directory and passes it to the token broker.
+1. **Retire.** The provisioning service deletes the agent's user account and then the agent identity, and removes the agent directory entry.
+
+## Choose how agents are provisioned
+
+| Option | How it works | Use it when |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| The runtime provisions identities | The provisioning service authenticates as the blueprint and calls Microsoft Graph to create and delete agent identities and agent's user accounts. | The runtime controls agent deployment. |
+| Agent 365 provisions identities | Agent 365 creates the agent identity when an agent is provisioned. The runtime listens for agent provisioning events, which include the agent identity ID, and records it in the agent directory. | Agents are created through Microsoft 365 experiences. For details, see the [Agent 365 developer documentation](/microsoft-agent-365/developer/). |
+
+Both options produce the same agent directory entry. The rest of the fleet guidance applies to either option.
+
+## Select the agent identity on each request
+
+The blueprint credential can acquire tokens for every agent identity created from the blueprint. The runtime code that chooses the agent identity is therefore a security boundary.
+
+- Resolve the agent identity from the agent directory by using a key that the runtime controls, such as its own agent ID.
+- Don't accept an agent identity client ID or agent's user account ID from a request, prompt, or tool output.
+- Confirm that the caller is allowed to use the target agent before you request a token for it.
+
+## Plan trust boundaries
+
+- **Keep the credential away from agent code.** Hold the blueprint credential in the runtime or in the sidecar, never in code that an agent author or model controls.
+- **Isolate the token broker.** If agents run untrusted or customer-supplied code, don't let that code call the token broker directly. A process that can reach the broker can request a token for any agent in the fleet.
+- **Separate provisioning from token acquisition.** The provisioning service uses blueprint tokens that can create and delete identities. Run it with its own access path so agent code can't request those tokens.
+- **Limit the blast radius.** Use more than one blueprint when groups of agents run in different trust zones or belong to different customers.
+
+## Plan for limits
+
+A blueprint principal can create at most 250 agent identities. For a larger fleet, create more blueprints and assign each agent to a blueprint when it's provisioned. Record the blueprint in the agent directory entry. For details, see [Agent identity blueprint principals](agent-id-creation-channels.md#agent-identity-blueprint-principals).
+
+The implementation articles that follow use one blueprint per runtime configuration. If you extend them to multiple blueprints, also resolve the matching blueprint configuration and credential for each agent; selecting an agent ID alone doesn't select a different blueprint. The sample directory record needs to be extended for that design.
+
+## Grant access to each agent
+
+Give each agent identity only the access that its agent needs. Grant application permissions, delegated permissions, Azure role assignments, and access to other resources directly to the agent identity, as part of provisioning or soon after. Per-agent grants keep each agent's access separate, so you can review, change, or revoke one agent's access without affecting the rest of the fleet. For the ways to grant access, see [Grant application permissions](grant-application-permissions-agent-identity.md) and [Grant delegated permissions](grant-agent-access-microsoft-365.md).
+
+For permissions that every agent in the fleet needs, you can use [inheritable permissions](concept-inheritable-permissions.md) as a convenience. An administrator grants those permissions once on the blueprint principal, and every agent identity created from the blueprint receives them in its tokens. Inherited permissions don't appear on the agent identity, so per-agent grants are easier to audit.
+
+## Route user requests to agents
+
+Users call a fleet agent with an access token for the blueprint's `access_agent` scope. Every agent in the fleet shares that audience, so the token proves who the user is but doesn't identify the agent. The runtime must:
+
+1. Determine the target agent from the request, such as from a route segment.
+1. Confirm that the user is allowed to use that agent. App roles on the blueprint apply to the whole fleet, so enforce per-agent access in the runtime.
+1. Use the target agent's identity for any On-Behalf-Of (OBO) token request.
+
+## Next step
+
+[Set up an agent identity blueprint for a fleet](set-up-blueprint-agent-fleet.md)
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Agent ID design patterns](concept-agent-id-design-patterns.md)
+- [Plan your agent identity architecture](how-to-plan-agent-identity-architecture.md)
+- [Agent creation channels](agent-id-creation-channels.md)
+- [Grant application permissions](grant-application-permissions-agent-identity.md)
+- [Inheritable permissions](concept-inheritable-permissions.md)

+---
+title: Set up an agent identity blueprint for a fleet
+description: Configure an agent identity blueprint, credential, permissions, and inbound scope for a fleet of agents on a shared runtime.
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/05/2026
+ms.reviewer: dastrock
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+
+#customer-intent: As a developer building an agent hosting platform, I want to configure one blueprint for my fleet so that the runtime can provision agent identities and acquire tokens for each agent.
+---
+
+# Set up an agent identity blueprint for a fleet
+
+A fleet runtime uses one [agent identity blueprint](agent-blueprint.md) to create agent identities and to acquire tokens for them. Configure the blueprint once, before the first agent is deployed. For the overall design, see [Plan an agent fleet on a shared runtime](plan-agent-fleet.md).
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- The Agent ID Developer role, to create the blueprint.
+- An administrator who can grant tenant-wide admin consent for Microsoft Graph application permissions.
+- An Azure compute resource for the runtime with a user-assigned managed identity.
+
+## Create the blueprint and its principal
+
+1. [Create an agent identity blueprint](create-blueprint.md#create-an-agent-identity-blueprint). Record its client ID.
+1. [Create the agent identity blueprint principal](create-blueprint.md#create-an-agent-blueprint-principal) in the tenant. The principal creates agent identities and receives admin consent.
+
+Record the tenant ID, blueprint client ID and object ID, blueprint principal object ID, and runtime managed identity client ID for the developer who configures provisioning. Use [Record the identifiers for your scenario](key-concepts.md#record-the-identifiers-for-your-scenario) to distinguish these values.
+
+## Add the blueprint credential
+
+[Add the runtime's managed identity as a federated identity credential](create-blueprint.md#configure-credentials-for-the-agent-identity-blueprint) on the blueprint. The runtime and the provisioning service use this credential to authenticate as the blueprint.
+
+Don't use client secrets in production. Every agent in the fleet depends on this credential.
+
+## Grant provisioning permissions
+
+The blueprint principal needs the following Microsoft Graph application permissions to provision identities. Neither permission is granted by default.
+
+| Permission | Required for |
+| --- | --- |
+| `AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager` | Creating and deleting agent identities |
+| `AgentIdUser.ReadWrite.IdentityParentedBy` | Creating and deleting agent's user accounts |
+
+Skip `AgentIdUser.ReadWrite.IdentityParentedBy` if no agent in the fleet needs an agent's user account. Skip both if [Agent 365 provisions your agents](plan-agent-fleet.md#choose-how-agents-are-provisioned).
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
+1. Browse to **Entra ID** > **App registrations** and open the blueprint app registration.
+1. Select **API permissions** > **Add a permission** > **Microsoft Graph** > **Application permissions**.
+1. Select `AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager` and, if needed, `AgentIdUser.ReadWrite.IdentityParentedBy`.
+1. Select **Add permissions**, and then select **Grant admin consent**.
+
+Before handing setup back to the runtime developer, confirm that admin consent is granted for each selected Microsoft Graph application permission on this blueprint. A permission listed without consent doesn't make the provisioning service ready. Keep these provisioning permissions separate from the downstream permissions granted to agents.
+
+For more information about these permissions, see [Agent identity blueprint principals](agent-id-creation-channels.md#agent-identity-blueprint-principals).
+
+## Plan how agents get access
+
+Grant access to each agent identity individually. This approach is recommended because each agent's access stays separate and visible on its agent identity. After the provisioning service creates an agent identity, grant it the application permissions, delegated permissions, Azure role assignments, or other access that the agent needs:
+
+- [Grant application permissions](grant-application-permissions-agent-identity.md)
+- [Grant delegated permissions](grant-agent-access-microsoft-365.md)
+
+### Optionally configure inheritable permissions
+
+If every agent in the fleet needs the same permissions, you can grant them once on the blueprint principal and let each agent identity inherit them. This approach is a convenience: new agent identities receive the permissions without a separate grant.
+
+1. Add the shared permissions to the blueprint's required resource access.
+1. [Configure inheritable permissions](configure-inheritable-permissions-blueprints.md) for each resource app, such as Microsoft Graph or your custom API.
+1. Have an administrator grant admin consent for those permissions on the blueprint principal.
+
+Inherited permissions don't appear on agent identities in the admin center or through Microsoft Graph. They appear only in the tokens that agent identities receive. For the rules that determine which permissions are inherited, see [Inheritable permissions](concept-inheritable-permissions.md#declaration-grant-and-inheritance).
+
+## Expose the inbound scope
+
+If users or client applications call agents in the fleet, [configure an identifier URI and the `access_agent` scope](create-blueprint.md#configure-identifier-uri-and-scope) on the blueprint. Every agent in the fleet shares this audience.
+
+To limit who can call the fleet, [define app roles and require assignment](control-user-access-agents.md) on the blueprint principal. App roles apply to every agent in the fleet. Enforce per-agent access in the runtime.
+
+## Next steps
+
+Continue with the integration path for the runtime:
+
+- [Provision agent identities with ASP.NET Core](aspnet-core-fleet-provision-agent-identities.md)
+- [Provision agent identities with the Auth SDK sidecar](sidecar-fleet-provision-agent-identities.md)
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Plan an agent fleet on a shared runtime](plan-agent-fleet.md)
+- [Create an agent identity blueprint](create-blueprint.md)
+- [Inheritable permissions](concept-inheritable-permissions.md)
+- [Agent creation channels](agent-id-creation-channels.md)
