@@ -0,0 +1,171 @@
+---
+title: Authenticate users with the Auth SDK sidecar
+description: Validate an access token sent by an upstream client and read the signed-in user's claims with the Auth SDK sidecar.
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/06/2026
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+ms.reviewer: dastrock
+
+#customer-intent: As an agent developer, I want my cloud agent to authenticate callers before it processes user requests.
+---
+
+# Authenticate users with the Auth SDK sidecar
+
+An upstream client signs in the user and sends an access token to the agent. The agent passes that token to the sidecar for validation before it uses the user's claims or performs an On-Behalf-Of (OBO) exchange.
+
+The sidecar doesn't provide the user interface for sign-in. Use MSAL in the upstream web, desktop, or mobile client.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Completion of [Configure the Auth SDK sidecar](microsoft-entra-sdk-for-agent-identities.md), including the agent's registration and credential.
+- An upstream client that signs in a user and requests a token for the agent's exposed scope.
+- Completion of [Configure the delegated permission](aspnet-core-authenticate-users.md#configure-the-delegated-permission) and [Grant the upstream client access](aspnet-core-authenticate-users.md#grant-the-upstream-client-access). These registration and Microsoft Graph consent steps also apply to the sidecar; don't use the ASP.NET Core code from that article.
+
+## Configure the audience
+
+Register a scope exposed by the agent's API. The upstream client requests that scope so the resulting access token is intended for the agent.
+
+Don't send a token issued for Microsoft Graph or another resource to the agent API.
+
+Configure the sidecar to validate the agent API's audience and delegated scope:
+
+Set `AzureAd:ClientId` to the client ID recorded during setup, not a directory object ID. Set `AzureAd:Scopes` to `access_agent`. The upstream client requests `api://<agent-client-id>/access_agent`.
+
+```json
+{
+  "AzureAd": {
+    "Instance": "https://login.microsoftonline.com/",
+    "TenantId": "<tenant-id>",
+    "ClientId": "<agent-client-id>",
+    "Scopes": "access_agent"
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Use the same `AzureAd` section to configure the blueprint credential. For the complete container and credential setup, see [Configure the Auth SDK sidecar](microsoft-entra-sdk-for-agent-identities.md).
+
+## Validate the token
+
+Forward the complete inbound authorization header to the sidecar:
+
+```http
+GET /Validate
+Authorization: ******
+```
+
+The response includes the validated protocol, token, and claims. Use the claims to identify the user and enforce the agent's authorization policy.
+
+Don't trust claims decoded by the client or agent before validation.
+
+## Invoke the sidecar
+
+Validate the inbound authorization header with the sidecar before using its returned claims. Require `protocol` to be `Bearer`, nonempty `oid` and `tid` claims, and `access_agent` in the space-separated `scp` claim. Identify the caller by the combination of `tid` and `oid`. Reject the request if any check fails, and apply the agent's authorization policy before processing it.
+
+# [Python](#tab/python)
+
+```python
+import requests
+
+SIDECAR_URL = "http://localhost:5000"
+
+def validate_caller(inbound_auth_header: str) -> dict:
+    """Validate an inbound access token with the sidecar and return the token claims."""
+    response = requests.get(
+        f"{SIDECAR_URL}/Validate",
+        headers={"Authorization": inbound_auth_header},
+        timeout=5,
+    )
+
+    if response.status_code in (401, 403):
+        raise PermissionError("The sidecar rejected the caller's access token.")
+
+    response.raise_for_status()
+    result = response.json()
+
+    if result.get("protocol", "").lower() != "bearer":
+        raise PermissionError("The validated token used an unexpected protocol.")
+
+    claims = result.get("claims", {})
+    object_id = claims.get("oid")
+    tenant_id = claims.get("tid")
+
+    if not object_id or not tenant_id:
+        raise PermissionError("The validated token doesn't identify a user and tenant.")
+
+    if "access_agent" not in claims.get("scp", "").split():
+        raise PermissionError("The caller doesn't have the required delegated scope.")
+
+    return claims
+
+
+# Call before processing each request:
+claims = validate_caller(request.headers.get("Authorization"))
+# Use claims["oid"] and claims["tid"] as the stable caller identity.
+# Apply the agent's authorization policy before processing the request.
+```
+
+# [JavaScript](#tab/javascript)
+
+```javascript
+const SIDECAR_URL = "http://localhost:5000";
+
+async function validateCaller(inboundAuthHeader) {
+    const response = await fetch(`${SIDECAR_URL}/Validate`, {
+        headers: { Authorization: inboundAuthHeader },
+    });
+
+    if (response.status === 401 || response.status === 403) {
+        throw new Error("The sidecar rejected the caller's access token.");
+    }
+
+    if (!response.ok) {
+        throw new Error(`Sidecar validation failed with status ${response.status}.`);
+    }
+
+    const result = await response.json();
+
+    if (result.protocol?.toLowerCase() !== "bearer") {
+        throw new Error("The validated token used an unexpected protocol.");
+    }
+
+    const claims = result.claims ?? {};
+    const { oid: objectId, tid: tenantId } = claims;
+
+    if (!objectId || !tenantId) {
+        throw new Error("The validated token doesn't identify a user and tenant.");
+    }
+
+    if (!(claims.scp ?? "").split(" ").includes("access_agent")) {
+        throw new Error("The caller doesn't have the required delegated scope.");
+    }
+
+    return claims;
+}
+
+// Call before processing each request:
+const claims = await validateCaller(req.headers.authorization);
+// Use claims.oid and claims.tid as the stable caller identity.
+// Apply the agent's authorization policy before processing the request.
+```
+
+---
+
+Keep `SIDECAR_URL` on loopback in the shared network namespace. Replace the authorization-header placeholder with the complete `Authorization` header received by the agent. If you use a scope other than `access_agent`, update both the sidecar configuration and the helper's scope check.
+
+The response also contains the validated token, but the example doesn't deserialize it. Don't return or log the token. If the sidecar rejects the token, reject the agent request instead of decoding the token locally or continuing without an authenticated user.
+
+Return `401 Unauthorized` for a missing or invalid token and `403 Forbidden` when an authenticated caller lacks the required scope or access. Don't continue to the downstream API after either rejection.
+
+The example also rejects credentials that the sidecar validated with another protocol, such as an app-only proof-of-possession token. Use the validated tenant ID and object ID as the stable user key. Apply the agent's authorization policy before processing the request.
+
+## Next steps
+
+1. [Control which users can access the agent](sidecar-control-user-access-agents.md).
+1. [Request consent for delegated permissions](grant-agent-access-microsoft-365.md).
+1. [Call a custom API as the user](sidecar-call-custom-api-as-user.md).
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Protected web API: Verify scopes and app roles](/entra/identity-platform/scenario-protected-web-api-verification-scope-app-roles)
+- [Auth SDK sidecar endpoint reference](/entra/msidweb/agent-id-sdk/endpoints)

@@ -0,0 +1,86 @@
+---
+title: Call Azure services as an agent with the Auth SDK sidecar
+description: Use an app-only Agent ID token from the Auth SDK sidecar to call an Azure service.
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/06/2026
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+ms.reviewer: dastrock
+---
+
+# Call Azure services as an agent with the Auth SDK sidecar
+
+Use this pattern when an autonomous agent needs access to an Azure service that accepts Microsoft Entra application tokens.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Completion of [Configure the Auth SDK sidecar](microsoft-entra-sdk-for-agent-identities.md), including the agent's registration and client ID.
+- A resource group and subscription where an administrator can assign the Agent ID an Azure role.
+
+## Configure access
+
+1. Assign the Azure built-in **Reader** role to the Agent ID at the target resource group scope.
+1. Configure the Azure service in the sidecar with its resource scope. For Azure Resource Manager, use `https://management.azure.com/.default`.
+1. Record the sidecar API configuration name.
+
+For this example, Azure Resource Manager uses Azure RBAC: the Agent ID's **Reader** assignment authorizes the read. The `/.default` scope requests an app-only token for Azure Resource Manager; it isn't an Azure role or an additional OAuth permission grant.
+
+## Configure the sidecar
+
+The following profile requests app-only tokens for Azure Resource Manager with the configured client ID:
+
+```json
+{
+  "DownstreamApis": {
+    "azure-management": {
+      "BaseUrl": "https://management.azure.com/",
+      "Scopes": [
+        "https://management.azure.com/.default"
+      ],
+      "RequestAppToken": true
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+For another Azure service, replace the base URL and scope with the values documented by that service. For the blueprint identity, credential, and container configuration, see [Configure the Auth SDK sidecar](microsoft-entra-sdk-for-agent-identities.md).
+
+## Read a resource group
+
+This example uses Node.js 18 or later and the built-in Fetch API. Run it in the agent container, which shares the sidecar's loopback network namespace. Set `subscriptionId` and `resourceGroupName` to the target resource group.
+
+The sidecar request uses the configured app-only profile:
+
+```http
+GET /AuthorizationHeaderUnauthenticated/azure-management
+```
+
+```javascript
+async function getResourceGroupAsAgent(subscriptionId, resourceGroupName) {
+  const tokenResponse = await fetch("http://localhost:5000/AuthorizationHeaderUnauthenticated/azure-management");
+  if (!tokenResponse.ok) {
+    throw new Error(`Sidecar token request failed (HTTP ${tokenResponse.status}); check the profile and blueprint credential.`);
+  }
+  const { authorizationHeader } = await tokenResponse.json();
+
+  const url = `https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/${encodeURIComponent(subscriptionId)}/resourceGroups/${encodeURIComponent(resourceGroupName)}?api-version=2021-04-01`;
+  const response = await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: authorizationHeader } });
+  if (!response.ok) {
+    throw new Error(`Azure Resource Manager returned HTTP ${response.status}; verify the Agent ID's Reader role at this resource group.`);
+  }
+  return response.json();
+}
+```
+
+Call `getResourceGroupAsAgent(subscriptionId, resourceGroupName)` from the agent. A successful request returns `200 OK` with the resource group's name, ID, and location. A `403` from Azure Resource Manager means the Agent ID lacks access at that scope; assign **Reader** to the Agent ID on this resource group and retry after the role assignment takes effect. If the sidecar returns `401`, check the credential and `azure-management` profile. Don't pass an identity override. Request a separate token for each different API audience.
+
+The [Resource Groups - Get API](/rest/api/resources/resource-groups/get?view=rest-resources-2021-04-01&preserve-view=true) documents this request and its `200 OK` response. The Azure built-in [Reader role](/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles/general#reader) grants read-only access at the scope where you assign it.
+
+## Next step
+
+[Authenticate users to the agent](sidecar-authenticate-users.md)
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Azure role-based access control](/azure/role-based-access-control/overview)
+- [Auth SDK sidecar endpoint reference](/entra/msidweb/agent-id-sdk/endpoints)

+---
+title: Call Azure services as a user with the Auth SDK sidecar
+description: Use the Auth SDK sidecar and On-Behalf-Of flow to call an Azure service for the signed-in user.
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID

+
+# Call Azure services as a user with the Auth SDK sidecar
+
+Use this pattern when an Azure service supports delegated access and should evaluate the signed-in user's permissions.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Completion of [Authenticate users with the Auth SDK sidecar](sidecar-authenticate-users.md), including consent for the upstream client to call the agent.
+- A target Azure resource group, and an administrator who can assign the signed-in user an Azure role on it.
+
+## Configure access
+
+1. Assign the signed-in user the Azure built-in **Reader** role at the target resource group scope.
+1. Declare the Azure Resource Manager delegated permission `user_impersonation` on the blueprint and [grant consent to the agent identity](grant-agent-access-microsoft-365.md).
+1. Configure the Azure Resource Manager audience and `user_impersonation` scope in the sidecar.
+
+This example uses both authorization systems: `user_impersonation` lets the agent request an Azure Resource Manager token on behalf of the user, and the user's **Reader** role allows the read at the resource group scope. Some Azure services accept only application tokens; use [app-only access](sidecar-call-azure-api-as-agent.md) for those services.
+
+## Configure the sidecar
+
+The following profile requests delegated tokens for Azure Resource Manager:
+
+```json
+{
+  "DownstreamApis": {
+    "azure-management": {
+      "BaseUrl": "https://management.azure.com/",
+      "Scopes": [
+        "https://management.azure.com/user_impersonation"
+      ]
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+For another Azure service, replace the base URL and scope with the values documented by that service. Use the shared client ID and keep identity overrides disabled as described in [Configure the Auth SDK sidecar](microsoft-entra-sdk-for-agent-identities.md).
+
+## Read a resource group as the signed-in user
+
+This example uses Node.js 18 or later and the built-in Fetch API. Pass the access token issued to the signed-in user for your agent API to the function. Don't pass an ID token or an app-only token.
+
+The sidecar request uses the configured delegated profile and the inbound user token:
+
+```http
+GET /AuthorizationHeader/azure-management
+Authorization: Bearer <agent-api-access-token>
+```
+
+```javascript
+async function getResourceGroupAsUser(agentApiAccessToken, subscriptionId, resourceGroupName) {
+  const tokenResponse = await fetch("http://localhost:5000/AuthorizationHeader/azure-management", {
+    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${agentApiAccessToken}` }
+  });
+  if (!tokenResponse.ok) {
+    throw new Error(`Sidecar token request failed (HTTP ${tokenResponse.status}); check the inbound user token and delegated consent.`);
+  }
+  const { authorizationHeader } = await tokenResponse.json();
+
+  const url = `https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/${encodeURIComponent(subscriptionId)}/resourceGroups/${encodeURIComponent(resourceGroupName)}?api-version=2021-04-01`;
+  const response = await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: authorizationHeader } });
+  if (!response.ok) {
+    throw new Error(`Azure Resource Manager returned HTTP ${response.status}; verify the signed-in user's Reader role at this resource group.`);
+  }
+  return response.json();
+}
+```
+
+Call `getResourceGroupAsUser(agentApiAccessToken, subscriptionId, resourceGroupName)` while handling that user's request. A successful request returns `200 OK` with the resource group's name, ID, and location. A `403` from Azure Resource Manager means the signed-in user lacks access at that scope; assign **Reader** to that user on this resource group and retry after the role assignment takes effect. If the sidecar returns `401`, verify that the inbound token is for the agent API and that `user_impersonation` consent is in place. After changing consent, retry with a newly issued agent API access token. Don't switch to the unauthenticated endpoint: it would call as the Agent ID, not as the user.
+
+The [Resource Groups - Get API](/rest/api/resources/resource-groups/get?view=rest-resources-2021-04-01&preserve-view=true) documents this request and its `200 OK` response. The Azure built-in [Reader role](/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles/general#reader) grants read-only access at the scope where you assign it.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Microsoft identity platform On-Behalf-Of flow](/entra/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-on-behalf-of-flow)
+- [Azure role-based access control](/azure/role-based-access-control/overview)

+
+# Call a custom API as an agent with the Auth SDK sidecar
+
+Use app-only access when a cloud agent performs scheduled, event-driven, or other autonomous work without a signed-in user. This article calls a custom API, but the same sidecar flow applies to Azure services and Microsoft Graph.
+
+In this article, you configure application permissions and use the sidecar to acquire an app-only authorization header or call the API.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Completion of [Configure the Auth SDK sidecar](microsoft-entra-sdk-for-agent-identities.md), including the agent's registration, client ID, and credential.
+- An application permission exposed by the custom API.
+
+## Configure access
+
+1. Expose an application permission on the custom API.
+1. [Grant that permission to the Agent ID and verify administrator consent](call-api-custom.md#grant-application-permissions). Use the shared client ID for consent and the agent identity's object ID when verifying the app role assignment.
+1. Configure the API in the sidecar with its base URL and `api://<api-client-id>/.default` scope.
+1. Configure the API to validate the Agent ID token and required app role.
+
+## Configure the sidecar
+
+The agent calls the sidecar through loopback in their shared network namespace. The sidecar uses the configured client ID and credential to acquire an authorization header for the API.
+
+Add an app-only profile for the custom API. Keep identity overrides disabled as described in the sidecar setup:
+
+```json
+{
+  "DownstreamApis": {
+    "custom-api": {
+      "BaseUrl": "https://api.contoso.com/",
+      "Scopes": [
+        "api://<custom-api-client-id>/.default"
+      ],
+      "RequestAppToken": true
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+For the blueprint identity, credential, and container configuration, see [Configure the Auth SDK sidecar](microsoft-entra-sdk-for-agent-identities.md).
+
+## Get a token and call the API
+
+```http
+GET /AuthorizationHeaderUnauthenticated/custom-api
+```
+
+Send the returned `authorizationHeader` to the custom API. Don't pass an `AgentIdentity` override or send the blueprint credential to the API.
+
+The API must verify the token's signature, issuer, audience, expiry, Agent ID claims, and required `roles` value.
+
+Alternatively, use `POST /DownstreamApiUnauthenticated/custom-api` to have the sidecar call the configured API. No identity override is needed.
+
+Confirm that the API operation succeeds with the required role and rejects a request without that role. A successful token response alone doesn't establish API authorization. Don't log the authorization header.
+
+## Next step
+
+[Authenticate users to the agent](sidecar-authenticate-users.md)
+

@@ -0,0 +1,140 @@
+---
+title: Call a custom API as a user with the Auth SDK sidecar
+description: Use the Auth SDK sidecar and On-Behalf-Of flow to call a custom API for the signed-in user.
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/06/2026
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+ms.reviewer: dastrock
+---
+
+# Call a custom API as a user with the Auth SDK sidecar
+
+Use the OAuth On-Behalf-Of (OBO) flow when an upstream client calls an agent for a signed-in user and the agent calls a custom API for that user.
+
+The agent first validates the inbound access token, then forwards the same authorization header to the sidecar. The sidecar uses its configured credential to get a downstream authorization header for that user.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Completion of [Authenticate users with the Auth SDK sidecar](sidecar-authenticate-users.md), including consent for the upstream client to call the agent.
+- A delegated scope exposed by the downstream API.
+- Consent for the agent to call that API for the user.
+
+## Configure access
+
+1. Expose a delegated scope on the custom API.
+1. Declare the scope in the blueprint's `requiredResourceAccess`.
+1. [Obtain user or administrator consent](grant-agent-access-microsoft-365.md) for the agent identity to use that scope.
+1. Configure the API and scope in the sidecar.
+
+## Configure the sidecar
+
+Add a delegated profile for the custom API:
+
+```json
+{
+  "DownstreamApis": {
+    "custom-api": {
+      "BaseUrl": "https://api.contoso.com/",
+      "Scopes": [
+        "api://<custom-api-client-id>/<delegated-scope>"
+      ]
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Use the shared client ID and keep identity overrides disabled as described in [Configure the Auth SDK sidecar](microsoft-entra-sdk-for-agent-identities.md).
+
+## Get a downstream token
+
+Forward the token issued for the agent API:
+
+```http
+GET /AuthorizationHeader/custom-api
+Authorization: ******
+```
+
+Send the returned `authorizationHeader` to the custom API. The custom API must validate the token and enforce the required scope and user authorization.
+
+Don't send the inbound token directly to the custom API. It is intended for the agent, not the downstream resource. Don't return or log either authorization header.
+
+## Call the sidecar and custom API
+
+The following example forwards the inbound user authorization header to the sidecar, reads the downstream authorization header, and calls the custom API:
+
+# [Python](#tab/python)
+
+```python
+import requests
+
+SIDECAR_URL = "http://localhost:5000"
+
+inbound_auth_header = "<authorization-header-from-agent-request>"
+
+sidecar_response = requests.get(
+    f"{SIDECAR_URL}/AuthorizationHeader/custom-api",
+    headers={"Authorization": inbound_auth_header},
+    timeout=5,
+)
+
+if sidecar_response.status_code in (401, 403):
+    raise PermissionError("The sidecar rejected the user token or OBO request.")
+
+sidecar_response.raise_for_status()
+authorization_header = sidecar_response.json()["authorizationHeader"]
+
+api_response = requests.get(
+    "https://api.contoso.com/user-data",
+    headers={"Authorization": authorization_header},
+    timeout=10,
+)
+api_response.raise_for_status()
+response_body = api_response.json()
+```
+
+# [JavaScript](#tab/javascript)
+
+```javascript
+const SIDECAR_URL = "http://localhost:5000";
+
+const inboundAuthHeader = "<authorization-header-from-agent-request>";
+
+const sidecarResponse = await fetch(
+    `${SIDECAR_URL}/AuthorizationHeader/custom-api`,
+    { headers: { Authorization: inboundAuthHeader } }
+);
+
+if (sidecarResponse.status === 401 || sidecarResponse.status === 403) {
+    throw new Error("The sidecar rejected the user token or OBO request.");
+}
+
+if (!sidecarResponse.ok) {
+    throw new Error(`Sidecar request failed with status ${sidecarResponse.status}.`);
+}
+
+const { authorizationHeader } = await sidecarResponse.json();
+
+const apiResponse = await fetch("https://api.contoso.com/user-data", {
+    headers: { Authorization: authorizationHeader },
+});
+
+if (!apiResponse.ok) {
+    throw new Error(`API request failed with status ${apiResponse.status}.`);
+}
+
+const responseBody = await apiResponse.json();
+```
+
+---
+
+Keep `SIDECAR_URL` on loopback in the shared network namespace. Replace the authorization-header placeholder with the complete `Authorization` header received by the agent. Process `responseBody` according to the custom API's response contract.
+
+Treat the sidecar response as a credential. Don't log or return `authorizationHeader`.
+
+Verify that the API enforces the delegated scope and the user's access. If OBO reports missing consent, check upstream access to the agent separately from downstream consent; the OBO exchange can't display a consent prompt.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Validate Agent ID tokens in a downstream API](how-to-validate-agent-tokens-downstream-api.md)
+- [Microsoft identity platform On-Behalf-Of flow](/entra/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-on-behalf-of-flow)

+
+# Call Microsoft Graph as an agent with the Auth SDK sidecar
+
+Use application permissions when an autonomous agent calls Microsoft Graph without a signed-in user.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Completion of [Configure the Auth SDK sidecar](microsoft-entra-sdk-for-agent-identities.md), including the agent's registration and client ID.
+- Administrator consent for the Microsoft Graph application permission `Organization.Read.All` on the Agent ID.
+
+## Configure access
+
+1. [Grant the Microsoft Graph application permission `Organization.Read.All`](grant-application-permissions-agent-identity.md) to the Agent ID and have an administrator consent to it.
+1. Configure a sidecar API, such as `graph-app`, with the Microsoft Graph base URL and `https://graph.microsoft.com/.default` scope.
+
+Application permissions can provide broad tenant access. Grant only the permissions required by the scenario.
+
+## Configure the sidecar
+
+Add an app-only profile for Microsoft Graph with the configured client ID:
+
+```json
+{
+  "DownstreamApis": {
+    "graph-app": {
+      "BaseUrl": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/",
+      "Scopes": [
+        "https://graph.microsoft.com/.default"
+      ],
+      "RequestAppToken": true
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+For the blueprint identity, credential, and container configuration, see [Configure the Auth SDK sidecar](microsoft-entra-sdk-for-agent-identities.md).
+
+## Read the organization with Microsoft Graph
+
+This example uses Node.js 18 or later and the built-in Fetch API. Run it from the agent; don't pass a user token or identity override.
+
+The sidecar request uses the configured app-only profile:
+
+```http
+GET /AuthorizationHeaderUnauthenticated/graph-app
+```
+
+```javascript
+async function getOrganizationAsAgent() {
+  const tokenResponse = await fetch("http://localhost:5000/AuthorizationHeaderUnauthenticated/graph-app");
+  if (!tokenResponse.ok) {
+    throw new Error(`Sidecar token request failed (HTTP ${tokenResponse.status}); check the profile, credential, and admin consent.`);
+  }
+  const { authorizationHeader } = await tokenResponse.json();
+
+  const response = await fetch("https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/organization?$select=id,displayName", {
+    headers: { Authorization: authorizationHeader }
+  });
+  if (!response.ok) {
+    throw new Error(`Microsoft Graph returned HTTP ${response.status}; verify Organization.Read.All is consented for the Agent ID.`);
+  }
+  return response.json();
+}
+```
+
+Call `getOrganizationAsAgent()` from the agent. A successful request returns `200 OK` and one organization object containing its ID and display name. If Graph returns `403`, verify that `Organization.Read.All` is granted to the Agent ID and admin consent is current; then retry. If the sidecar returns `401`, check token acquisition and the `graph-app` profile. Don't log the authorization header. See the [List organizations API](/graph/api/organization-list) for its application permission requirements.
+
+## Next step
+
+[Authenticate users to the agent](sidecar-authenticate-users.md)
+

+
+- [Microsoft Graph permissions reference](/graph/permissions-reference)
+- [Auth SDK sidecar endpoint reference](/entra/msidweb/agent-id-sdk/endpoints)

+# Call Microsoft Graph as a user with the Auth SDK sidecar
+
+Use delegated Microsoft Graph permissions when an operation should run with the signed-in user's access.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Completion of [Authenticate users with the Auth SDK sidecar](sidecar-authenticate-users.md), including consent for the upstream client to call the agent.
+- Consent for the Microsoft Graph delegated permissions required by the operation.

+## Configure access
+
+1. Declare the Microsoft Graph delegated permission `User.Read` on the blueprint.
+1. [Obtain user or administrator consent](grant-agent-access-microsoft-365.md) for `User.Read` on the agent identity.
+1. Configure a sidecar API, such as `graph`, with the Microsoft Graph base URL and delegated scopes.

+Request only the scopes required by the operation.
+
+## Configure the sidecar
+
+Add a delegated profile for Microsoft Graph:
+
+```json
+{
+  "DownstreamApis": {
+    "graph": {
+      "BaseUrl": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/",
+      "Scopes": [
+        "User.Read"
+      ]
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Replace `User.Read` with the delegated Microsoft Graph permissions required by the operation. Use the shared client ID and keep identity overrides disabled as described in [Configure the Auth SDK sidecar](microsoft-entra-sdk-for-agent-identities.md).
+
+## Read the signed-in user's profile
+
+This example uses Node.js 18 or later and the built-in Fetch API. Pass the access token issued to the signed-in user for your agent API to the function. `User.Read` is the least-privileged delegated permission for this request.
+
+The sidecar request uses the configured delegated profile and the inbound user token:
+
+```http
+GET /AuthorizationHeader/graph
+Authorization: Bearer <agent-api-access-token>
+```
+
+```javascript
+async function getMyGraphProfile(agentApiAccessToken) {
+  const tokenResponse = await fetch("http://localhost:5000/AuthorizationHeader/graph", {
+    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${agentApiAccessToken}` }
+  });
+  if (!tokenResponse.ok) {
+    throw new Error(`Sidecar token request failed (HTTP ${tokenResponse.status}); check the inbound user token and User.Read consent.`);
+  }
+  const { authorizationHeader } = await tokenResponse.json();
+
+  const response = await fetch("https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me?$select=id,displayName", {
+    headers: { Authorization: authorizationHeader }
+  });
+  if (!response.ok) {
+    throw new Error(`Microsoft Graph returned HTTP ${response.status}; verify User.Read consent and the signed-in user's access.`);
+  }
+  return response.json();
+}
+```
+
+Call `getMyGraphProfile(agentApiAccessToken)` while handling that user's request. A successful request returns `200 OK` with that user's ID and display name. If Graph returns `403`, verify that `User.Read` is consented and the access token represents the expected signed-in user; then retry. If the sidecar returns `401`, check that the inbound token is an access token for the agent API and that delegated consent is in place. After changing consent, retry with a newly issued agent API access token. Don't replace this flow with an app-only token or `/AuthorizationHeaderUnauthenticated`; Microsoft Graph doesn't support application permissions for `/me`. See the [Get a user API](/graph/api/user-get) for the delegated permission requirement.

+---
+title: Access Microsoft 365 as an agent's user account with the Auth SDK sidecar
+description: Use the Auth SDK sidecar to call Microsoft 365 as an agent's user account.
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/05/2026
+ms.reviewer: dastrock
+
+#customer-intent: As an agent developer, I want to use the Auth SDK sidecar to call Microsoft 365 as an agent's user account.
+---
+
+# Access Microsoft 365 as an agent's user account with the Auth SDK sidecar
+
+Some Microsoft 365 scenarios require a user object rather than an application identity. Use an [agent's user account](agent-users.md) when an autonomous agent needs capabilities such as:
+
+- Membership in a Microsoft Teams team.
+- An Exchange Online mailbox.
+- Direct access to shared SharePoint or OneDrive content.
+- A Microsoft 365 license assigned to the agent.
+
+Don't use an agent's user account when the service supports the required application permission. App-only access is easier to govern and doesn't consume a user license.
+
+## Configure the account
+
+1. [Create an agent's user account](create-delete-agent-user-account.md) and associate it with the Agent ID.
+1. Assign only the licenses and service access required by the scenario.
+1. [Grant the Agent ID the delegated permissions](grant-agent-access-microsoft-365.md) required by the Microsoft 365 workload, such as `Mail.ReadWrite` or `Files.ReadWrite`.
+1. Configure the Microsoft 365 API in the sidecar.
+1. Record the Agent ID and the agent user's object ID or user principal name.
+
+## Configure the sidecar
+
+Enable agent overrides for the unauthenticated authorization-header endpoint. Configure the Microsoft Graph delegated scopes required by the agent:
+
+```json
+{
+  "Sidecar": {
+    "AllowOverrides": {
+      "GetAuthorizationHeaderUnauthenticated": true
+    }
+  },
+  "DownstreamApis": {
+    "MsGraph": {
+      "BaseUrl": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/",
+      "Scopes": [
+        "User.Read"
+      ]
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Replace `User.Read` with the delegated Microsoft Graph permissions required by the operation. Don't use the application-permission `.default` scope for the agent user pattern.
+
+Enabling overrides lets a caller select the Agent ID and agent's user account used for token acquisition. Keep the sidecar on a private network that only trusted agent code can access. Don't populate `AgentIdentity`, `AgentUserId`, or `AgentUsername` directly from untrusted request input.
+
+## Get an authorization header
+
+Request a token without an inbound human-user token:
+
+```http
+GET /AuthorizationHeaderUnauthenticated/MsGraph?AgentIdentity={agent-id}&AgentUserId={agent-user-object-id}
+```
+
+The endpoint doesn't require an inbound `Authorization` header. You can use `AgentUsername` instead of `AgentUserId` when the user principal name is the stable identifier available to the application. Don't send both parameters.
+
+Send the returned `authorizationHeader` to the configured Microsoft 365 API.
+
+## Call Microsoft Graph
+
+The following example requests an authorization header for the agent's user account and uses it to call Microsoft Graph:
+
+# [Python](#tab/python)
+
+```python
+import requests
+
+SIDECAR_URL = "http://localhost:5000"
+AGENT_IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID = "<agent-identity-client-id>"
+AGENT_USER_OBJECT_ID = "<agent-user-object-id>"
+
+sidecar_response = requests.get(
+    f"{SIDECAR_URL}/AuthorizationHeaderUnauthenticated/MsGraph",
+    params={
+        "AgentIdentity": AGENT_IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID,
+        "AgentUserId": AGENT_USER_OBJECT_ID,
+    },
+    timeout=5,
+)
+sidecar_response.raise_for_status()
+authorization_header = sidecar_response.json()["authorizationHeader"]
+
+graph_response = requests.get(
+    "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me",
+    headers={"Authorization": authorization_header},
+    timeout=10,
+)
+graph_response.raise_for_status()
+profile = graph_response.json()
+```
+
+# [JavaScript](#tab/javascript)
+
+```javascript
+const SIDECAR_URL = "http://localhost:5000";
+const AGENT_IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID = "<agent-identity-client-id>";
+const AGENT_USER_OBJECT_ID = "<agent-user-object-id>";
+
+const params = new URLSearchParams({
+    AgentIdentity: AGENT_IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID,
+    AgentUserId: AGENT_USER_OBJECT_ID,
+});
+
+const sidecarResponse = await fetch(
+    `${SIDECAR_URL}/AuthorizationHeaderUnauthenticated/MsGraph?${params}`
+);
+
+if (!sidecarResponse.ok) {
+    throw new Error(`Sidecar request failed with status ${sidecarResponse.status}.`);
+}
+
+const { authorizationHeader } = await sidecarResponse.json();
+
+const graphResponse = await fetch("https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me", {
+    headers: { Authorization: authorizationHeader },
+});
+
+if (!graphResponse.ok) {
+    throw new Error(`Microsoft Graph request failed with status ${graphResponse.status}.`);
+}
+
+const profile = await graphResponse.json();
+```
+
+---
+
+Keep `SIDECAR_URL` on loopback in the shared network namespace. Treat `authorizationHeader` as a credential, and don't log it.
+
+## Configure the Microsoft 365 resource
+
+The access token doesn't add the agent user to a team, create a mailbox, share a file, or assign a license. Configure those resources through their supported administration or Microsoft Graph APIs:
+
+- [Add a member to a team](/graph/api/team-post-members)
+- [Create user mailboxes in Exchange Online](/exchange/recipients-in-exchange-online/create-user-mailboxes)
+- [Share a drive item](/graph/api/driveitem-invite)
+- [Assign a license to a user](/graph/api/user-assignlicense)
+
+## Next step
+
+[Authenticate users](sidecar-authenticate-users.md) if the agent also handles requests from signed-in users.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Agent's user account impersonation protocol](agent-user-oauth-flow.md)
+- [Request consent for delegated permissions](grant-agent-access-microsoft-365.md)
+- [Auth SDK sidecar endpoint reference](/entra/msidweb/agent-id-sdk/endpoints)

+++ b/docs/agent-id/sidecar-control-user-access-agents.md
@@ -0,0 +1,188 @@
+---
+title: Control user access to agents with the Auth SDK sidecar
+description: Use app roles to control which users, groups, and applications can access an agent that uses the Auth SDK sidecar.
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/06/2026
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+ms.reviewer: dastrock
+#Customer intent: As a developer using the Auth SDK sidecar, I want to use app roles to control which users and applications can access my agent.
+---
+
+# Control user access to agents with the Auth SDK sidecar
+
+App roles define who can access an agent and what they can do. Define and assign an inbound access role, then enforce it by checking the `roles` claim returned by the sidecar. The user-access helpers in this article require the `Agent.User` role and a delegated user scope.
+
+For the single-instance cloud journey, use the **agent identity's object ID** as `<agent-api-service-principal-object-id>` in the requests in this article; a single-instance blueprint has no blueprint principal. For the advanced fleet journey, use the fleet's **blueprint principal** instead; its assignments apply across the fleet.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A blueprint and the service principal that represents the agent API.
+- The [management permissions and administrator roles for app role configuration and assignment](control-user-access-agents.md#prerequisites).
+- An agent that validates inbound tokens with the sidecar, as described in [Authenticate users with the Auth SDK sidecar](sidecar-authenticate-users.md).
+
+## Define app roles
+
+Use the same [role definition procedure as the ASP.NET Core agent](control-user-access-agents.md#define-app-roles):
+
+- **Single-instance:** Declare `Agent.User` on the blueprint, then publish the same GUID and value directly on the Agent ID service principal, with `allowedMemberTypes` set to `["User"]`. Don't rely on a blueprint-only declaration.
+- **Fleet:** Define the role on the blueprint application and use its blueprint principal for assignments.
+
+[Verify the role on the resource principal](control-user-access-agents.md#verify-the-role-on-the-resource-principal) before continuing. Save its GUID for `<app-role-id>` below. Role values must stay stable because the agent checks them in the claims returned by the sidecar.
+
+## Require an app role assignment
+
+Set `appRoleAssignmentRequired` on the agent API service principal. When the property is `true`, Microsoft Entra ID issues an access token for the agent API only to assigned users and applications.
+
+```http
+PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals/<agent-api-service-principal-object-id>
+Content-Type: application/json
+Authorization: Bearer <access-token>
+
+{
+  "appRoleAssignmentRequired": true
+}
+```
+
+For more information, see the [Microsoft Graph update API reference](/graph/api/serviceprincipal-update).
+
+## Assign an app role
+
+Assign the app role to a user on the agent API service principal:
+
+```http
+POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/<user-object-id>/appRoleAssignments
+Content-Type: application/json
+Authorization: Bearer <access-token>
+
+{
+  "principalId": "<user-object-id>",
+  "resourceId": "<agent-api-service-principal-object-id>",
+  "appRoleId": "<app-role-id>"
+}
+```
+
+For a group, create the assignment through the group's app role assignments. Use the agent API service principal's object ID as `resourceId`. These helpers authorize signed-in users; they don't authorize application-only callers.
+
+## Enforce app roles with the sidecar
+
+After the sidecar validates the inbound token, its response includes the token's claims. Check the `roles` claim before processing the request.
+
+The following user-access helpers require the `Bearer` protocol, nonempty `oid` and `tid` claims, `access_agent` in the space-separated `scp` claim, and the required value in the `roles` array. Use `Agent.User` as the required role for this example. These helpers don't authorize app-only callers or an agent's dedicated user account.
+
+# [Python](#tab/python)
+
+Call the sidecar's `/Validate` endpoint and verify the required role before processing each request:
+
+```python
+import requests
+
+SIDECAR_URL = "http://localhost:5000"
+
+def validate_and_check_role(inbound_auth_header: str, required_role: str) -> dict:
+    """Validate an inbound token and verify the caller has the required app role."""
+    response = requests.get(
+        f"{SIDECAR_URL}/Validate",
+        headers={"Authorization": inbound_auth_header},
+        timeout=5,
+    )
+
+    if response.status_code in (401, 403):
+        raise PermissionError("The sidecar rejected the caller's access token.")
+
+    response.raise_for_status()
+    result = response.json()
+    claims = result.get("claims", {})
+    if (
+        result.get("protocol", "").lower() != "bearer"
+        or not claims.get("oid")
+        or not claims.get("tid")
+        or "access_agent" not in claims.get("scp", "").split()
+    ):
+        raise PermissionError("The caller isn't an authorized user of the agent API.")
+
+    roles = claims.get("roles", [])
+
+    if required_role not in roles:
+        raise PermissionError(
+            f"The caller doesn't have the required '{required_role}' role."
+        )
+
+    return claims
+```
+
+Call the helper before processing each request:
+
+```python
+claims = validate_and_check_role(
+    inbound_auth_header=request.headers.get("Authorization"),
+    required_role="Agent.User",
+)
+# Use claims["oid"] and claims["tid"] as the stable caller identity.
+```
+
+# [JavaScript](#tab/javascript)
+
+Call the sidecar's `/Validate` endpoint and verify the required role before processing each request:
+
+```javascript
+const SIDECAR_URL = "http://localhost:5000";
+
+async function validateAndCheckRole(inboundAuthHeader, requiredRole) {
+    const response = await fetch(`${SIDECAR_URL}/Validate`, {
+        headers: { Authorization: inboundAuthHeader },
+    });
+
+    if (response.status === 401 || response.status === 403) {
+        throw new Error("The sidecar rejected the caller's access token.");
+    }
+
+    if (!response.ok) {
+        throw new Error(`Sidecar validation failed with status ${response.status}.`);
+    }
+
+    const result = await response.json();
+    const claims = result.claims ?? {};
+    if (
+        result.protocol?.toLowerCase() !== "bearer" ||
+        !claims.oid ||
+        !claims.tid ||
+        !(claims.scp ?? "").split(" ").includes("access_agent")
+    ) {
+        throw new Error("The caller isn't an authorized user of the agent API.");
+    }
+
+    const roles = claims.roles ?? [];
+
+    if (!roles.includes(requiredRole)) {
+        throw new Error(`The caller doesn't have the required '${requiredRole}' role.`);
+    }
+
+    return claims;
+}
+```
+
+Call the helper before processing each request:
+
+```javascript
+const claims = await validateAndCheckRole(
+    req.headers.authorization,
+    "Agent.User"
+);
+// Use claims.oid and claims.tid as the stable caller identity.
+```
+
+---
+
+Return `403 Forbidden` when the role check fails. Return `401 Unauthorized` only when the token itself is missing or invalid. Request a new access token after changing an assignment. When troubleshooting, verify the assignment on the agent API service principal and check the `roles` claim in the response from `/Validate`.
+
+## Next step
+
+[Request consent for delegated permissions](grant-agent-access-microsoft-365.md)
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Authenticate users with the Auth SDK sidecar](sidecar-authenticate-users.md)
+- [Control user access to agents with ASP.NET Core](control-user-access-agents.md)
+- [Add app roles to an application](/entra/identity-platform/howto-add-app-roles-in-apps)
+- [Auth SDK sidecar endpoint reference](/entra/msidweb/agent-id-sdk/endpoints)

@@ -0,0 +1,140 @@
+---
+title: Authenticate users and route requests to agents in a fleet with the Auth SDK sidecar
+description: Validate user access tokens with the Auth SDK sidecar, route each request to an agent in a shared runtime, and enforce per-agent access.
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/05/2026
+ms.reviewer: dastrock
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+
+#customer-intent: As a developer building an agent hosting platform with the Auth SDK sidecar, I want to authenticate users and make sure they can only reach the agents they're allowed to use.
+---
+
+# Authenticate users and route requests to agents in a fleet with the Auth SDK sidecar
+
+Users call a fleet agent with an access token for the blueprint's `access_agent` scope. Every agent in the fleet shares that audience, so token validation proves who the user is but not which agent they're allowed to use. The runtime routes each request to an agent and enforces per-agent access itself.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Complete [Call APIs as an agent in a fleet with the Auth SDK sidecar](sidecar-fleet-call-apis-as-agent.md).
+- The `access_agent` scope [exposed on the blueprint](set-up-blueprint-agent-fleet.md#expose-the-inbound-scope).
+- An upstream client that signs in users and requests the scope `api://<agent-identity-blueprint-client-id>/access_agent`.
+
+## Configure token validation
+
+Token validation is the same as for a single agent. Configure the sidecar with the blueprint client ID and the `access_agent` scope, and validate each inbound token with `GET /Validate`. For details, see [Authenticate users with the Auth SDK sidecar](sidecar-authenticate-users.md). Keep the fleet's per-request identity overrides from the preceding articles and the shared network namespace for local sidecar requests; don't replace them with the single-instance defaults.
+
+To limit which users can call the fleet at all, [require an app role assignment](sidecar-control-user-access-agents.md) on the blueprint principal. Those app roles apply to every agent in the fleet.
+
+## Enforce per-agent access
+
+Decide who can use each agent, and store that decision in the runtime. For example, record the users and groups that an agent's owner shares it with. Identify the user by the validated `tid` and `oid` claims. Don't use the user principal name or email as a stable key.
+
+## Route requests to agents
+
+Put the runtime's agent ID in the route. Validate the token, confirm the agent exists, and check the access policy before running the agent. The following examples assume an `access_policy` object that implements the runtime's per-agent access check.
+
+# [Python](#tab/python)
+
+```python
+import requests
+
+SIDECAR_URL = "http://localhost:5000"
+
+
+class AgentNotFound(Exception):
+    """Return 404 Not Found to the caller."""
+
+
+def authorize_agent_request(inbound_auth_header: str, agent_id: str) -> dict:
+    response = requests.get(
+        f"{SIDECAR_URL}/Validate",
+        headers={"Authorization": inbound_auth_header},
+        timeout=5,
+    )
+    if response.status_code in (401, 403):
+        raise PermissionError("The sidecar rejected the caller's access token.")
+    response.raise_for_status()
+
+    result = response.json()
+    claims = result.get("claims", {})
+    object_id = claims.get("oid")
+    tenant_id = claims.get("tid")
+    if (
+        result.get("protocol", "").lower() != "bearer"
+        or not object_id
+        or not tenant_id
+    ):
+        raise PermissionError("The token isn't a validated user bearer token.")
+
+    scopes = claims.get("scp", "").split()
+    if "access_agent" not in scopes:
+        raise PermissionError("The token doesn't contain the access_agent scope.")
+
+    if directory.find(agent_id) is None or not access_policy.can_use_agent(
+        tenant_id, object_id, agent_id
+    ):
+        raise AgentNotFound(agent_id)
+
+    return claims
+
+
+# For a request to POST /agents/{agent_id}/messages:
+claims = authorize_agent_request(request.headers.get("Authorization"), agent_id)
+```
+
+# [JavaScript](#tab/javascript)
+
+```javascript
+const SIDECAR_URL = "http://localhost:5000";
+
+class AgentNotFoundError extends Error {}
+
+async function authorizeAgentRequest(inboundAuthHeader, agentId) {
+    const response = await fetch(`${SIDECAR_URL}/Validate`, {
+        headers: { Authorization: inboundAuthHeader },
+    });
+    if (response.status === 401 || response.status === 403) {
+        throw new Error("The sidecar rejected the caller's access token.");
+    }
+    if (!response.ok) {
+        throw new Error(`Sidecar validation failed with status ${response.status}.`);
+    }
+
+    const { protocol, claims = {} } = await response.json();
+    const objectId = claims.oid;
+    const tenantId = claims.tid;
+    if (protocol?.toLowerCase() !== "bearer" || !objectId || !tenantId) {
+        throw new Error("The token isn't a validated user bearer token.");
+    }
+
+    const scopes = (claims.scp ?? "").split(" ");
+    if (!scopes.includes("access_agent")) {
+        throw new Error("The token doesn't contain the access_agent scope.");
+    }
+
+    if (!(await directory.find(agentId))
+        || !(await accessPolicy.canUseAgent(tenantId, objectId, agentId))) {
+        throw new AgentNotFoundError(agentId);
+    }
+
+    return claims;
+}
+
+// For a request to POST /agents/:agentId/messages:
+const claims = await authorizeAgentRequest(req.headers.authorization, req.params.agentId);
+```
+
+---
+
+Return `401 Unauthorized` when the token is missing or invalid. Return `404 Not Found` both for an unknown agent and for an agent the user can't use, so callers can't discover other agents in the fleet. After these checks pass, use the same agent ID for every token request made while handling the request.
+
+## Next step
+
+[Call APIs as a user in a fleet with the Auth SDK sidecar](sidecar-fleet-call-apis-as-user.md)
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Authenticate users with the Auth SDK sidecar](sidecar-authenticate-users.md)
+- [Control user access to agents with the Auth SDK sidecar](sidecar-control-user-access-agents.md)
+- [Plan an agent fleet on a shared runtime](plan-agent-fleet.md)

@@ -0,0 +1,115 @@
+---
+title: Call APIs as an agent's user account in a fleet with the Auth SDK sidecar
+description: Select the agent identity and agent's user account for each token request to the Auth SDK sidecar in a shared runtime that hosts many agents.
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/04/2026
+ms.reviewer: dastrock
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+
+#customer-intent: As a developer building an agent hosting platform with the Auth SDK sidecar, I want agents in my fleet to call Microsoft 365 as their own agent's user accounts.
+---
+
+# Call APIs as an agent's user account in a fleet with the Auth SDK sidecar
+
+Some agents in a fleet need a user object for Microsoft 365 workloads, such as a mailbox or Teams membership. For those agents, look up both the agent identity and its agent's user account in the agent directory, and pass them in the `AgentIdentity` and `AgentUserId` parameters.
+
+To decide whether an agent needs an agent's user account, see [Use an agent's user account with Microsoft 365](agent-user-oauth-flow.md#determine-whether-the-agent-needs-a-user-object).
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Complete [Call APIs as an agent in a fleet with the Auth SDK sidecar](sidecar-fleet-call-apis-as-agent.md).
+- An agent's user account [provisioned for the agent](sidecar-fleet-provision-agent-identities.md#provision-an-agent).
+- Delegated permissions for the target API, such as `Mail.ReadWrite`, [granted to the agent identity](grant-agent-access-microsoft-365.md) or [inherited from the blueprint](set-up-blueprint-agent-fleet.md#optionally-configure-inheritable-permissions).
+- The Microsoft 365 licenses and resource access that the agent's user account needs. For details, see [Configure the account](sidecar-call-microsoft-365-as-agent-user.md#configure-the-account).
+
+## Configure the sidecar
+
+Add a delegated Microsoft Graph profile to the runtime sidecar:
+
+```json
+{
+  "DownstreamApis": {
+    "MsGraph": {
+      "BaseUrl": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/",
+      "Scopes": [
+        "Mail.ReadWrite"
+      ]
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Replace `Mail.ReadWrite` with the delegated permissions the agents need. The `GetAuthorizationHeaderUnauthenticated` override from the previous article also covers the `AgentUserId` parameter.
+
+## Get a token for an agent's user account
+
+# [Python](#tab/python)
+
+```python
+def authorization_header_for_agent_user(agent_id: str, api_name: str) -> str:
+    registration = directory.find(agent_id)
+    if registration is None or not registration["agent_user_id"]:
+        raise LookupError(f"Agent '{agent_id}' doesn't have an agent's user account.")
+
+    response = requests.get(
+        f"{SIDECAR_URL}/AuthorizationHeaderUnauthenticated/{api_name}",
+        params={
+            "AgentIdentity": registration["agent_identity_id"],
+            "AgentUserId": registration["agent_user_id"],
+        },
+        timeout=5,
+    )
+    response.raise_for_status()
+    return response.json()["authorizationHeader"]
+
+
+graph_response = requests.get(
+    "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/messages",
+    headers={"Authorization": authorization_header_for_agent_user(agent_id, "MsGraph")},
+    timeout=10,
+)
+graph_response.raise_for_status()
+```
+
+# [JavaScript](#tab/javascript)
+
+```javascript
+async function authorizationHeaderForAgentUser(agentId, apiName) {
+    const registration = await directory.find(agentId);
+    if (!registration?.agentUserId) {
+        throw new Error(`Agent '${agentId}' doesn't have an agent's user account.`);
+    }
+
+    const params = new URLSearchParams({
+        AgentIdentity: registration.agentIdentityId,
+        AgentUserId: registration.agentUserId,
+    });
+    const response = await fetch(
+        `${SIDECAR_URL}/AuthorizationHeaderUnauthenticated/${apiName}?${params}`
+    );
+    if (!response.ok) {
+        throw new Error(`Sidecar request failed with status ${response.status}.`);
+    }
+    const { authorizationHeader } = await response.json();
+    return authorizationHeader;
+}
+
+const graphResponse = await fetch("https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/messages", {
+    headers: { Authorization: await authorizationHeaderForAgentUser(agentId, "MsGraph") },
+});
+```
+
+---
+
+The token represents the agent's user account, so `/me` returns that account's data. Each agent can reach only the mailbox, files, and teams that its own account was given.
+
+## Next step
+
+[Authenticate users and route requests to agents in a fleet with the Auth SDK sidecar](sidecar-fleet-authenticate-users.md)
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Access Microsoft 365 as an agent's user account with the Auth SDK sidecar](sidecar-call-microsoft-365-as-agent-user.md)
+- [Agent's user accounts](agent-users.md)
+- [Plan an agent fleet on a shared runtime](plan-agent-fleet.md)

+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+
+#customer-intent: As a developer building an agent hosting platform with the Auth SDK sidecar, I want each agent in my fleet to call APIs with its own agent identity.
+---
+
+# Call APIs as an agent in a fleet with the Auth SDK sidecar
+
+In a fleet, the sidecar acquires app-only tokens for many agents with one blueprint credential. Look up the agent's identity in the agent directory, and pass it in the `AgentIdentity` parameter on each request. The request is otherwise the same as for a single agent.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Complete [Provision agent identities for a fleet with the Auth SDK sidecar](sidecar-fleet-provision-agent-identities.md).
+- Application permissions for the target API, [granted to the agent identity](grant-application-permissions-agent-identity.md) or [inherited from the blueprint](set-up-blueprint-agent-fleet.md#optionally-configure-inheritable-permissions).
+
+## Configure the runtime sidecar
+
+Configure the sidecar with the blueprint credential, as described in [Configure the Auth SDK sidecar](microsoft-entra-sdk-for-agent-identities.md). Set `AzureAd:ClientId` to the fleet's blueprint client ID. Unlike the single-instance setup, the fleet runtime must enable `GetAuthorizationHeaderUnauthenticated` and define an app-only profile for each API:
+
+```json
+{
+  "Sidecar": {
+    "AllowOverrides": {
+      "GetAuthorizationHeaderUnauthenticated": true
+    }
+  },
+  "DownstreamApis": {
+    "custom-api": {
+      "BaseUrl": "https://api.contoso.com/",
+      "Scopes": [
+        "api://<custom-api-client-id>/.default"
+      ],
+      "RequestAppToken": true
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+The sidecar accepts only local requests. Colocate the trusted runtime and its sidecar in the same network namespace, such as a Kubernetes pod. For Docker Compose, use `network_mode: "service:sidecar"` on the runtime container and call `http://localhost:5000`, not `http://sidecar:5000`. Don't publish the sidecar port.
+
+With the override enabled, any process that can reach the sidecar can request a token for any agent in the fleet. Only trusted runtime code should reach the sidecar. If agents run untrusted or customer-supplied code, run them outside the sidecar's network namespace and route their token requests through runtime code that selects the agent identity.
+
+## Get a token for an agent
+
+Resolve the agent identity from the runtime's own agent ID, never from a value in a request or in agent output:
+
+# [Python](#tab/python)
+
+```python
+import requests
+
+SIDECAR_URL = "http://localhost:5000"
+
+
+def authorization_header_for_agent(agent_id: str, api_name: str) -> str:
+    registration = directory.find(agent_id)
+    if registration is None:
+        raise LookupError(f"Agent '{agent_id}' isn't provisioned.")
+
+    response = requests.get(
+        f"{SIDECAR_URL}/AuthorizationHeaderUnauthenticated/{api_name}",
+        params={"AgentIdentity": registration["agent_identity_id"]},
+        timeout=5,
+    )
+    response.raise_for_status()
+    return response.json()["authorizationHeader"]
+
+
+api_response = requests.get(
+    "https://api.contoso.com/data",
+    headers={"Authorization": authorization_header_for_agent(agent_id, "custom-api")},
+    timeout=10,
+)
+api_response.raise_for_status()
+```
+
+# [JavaScript](#tab/javascript)
+
+```javascript
+const SIDECAR_URL = "http://localhost:5000";
+
+async function authorizationHeaderForAgent(agentId, apiName) {
+    const registration = await directory.find(agentId);
+    if (!registration) {
+        throw new Error(`Agent '${agentId}' isn't provisioned.`);
+    }
+
+    const params = new URLSearchParams({
+        AgentIdentity: registration.agentIdentityId,
+    });
+    const response = await fetch(
+        `${SIDECAR_URL}/AuthorizationHeaderUnauthenticated/${apiName}?${params}`
+    );
+    if (!response.ok) {
+        throw new Error(`Sidecar request failed with status ${response.status}.`);
+    }
+    const { authorizationHeader } = await response.json();
+    return authorizationHeader;
+}
+
+const apiResponse = await fetch("https://api.contoso.com/data", {
+    headers: { Authorization: await authorizationHeaderForAgent(agentId, "custom-api") },
+});
+```
+
+---
+
+Treat the returned `authorizationHeader` as a credential, and don't log it.
+
+## Call specific resources
+
+Use the scopes and endpoints from the linked resource articles, while keeping the fleet's blueprint client ID and override settings. The single-instance requests omit `AgentIdentity`. In the fleet, call `authorization_header_for_agent` or `authorizationHeaderForAgent` for every resource to supply the identity selected from the directory.
+
+| Resource | Guidance |
+| --- | --- |
+| Custom API | [Call a custom API as an agent](sidecar-call-custom-api-as-agent.md) |
+| Azure services | [Call Azure services as an agent](sidecar-call-azure-api-as-agent.md) |
+| Microsoft Graph | [Call Microsoft Graph as an agent](sidecar-call-graph-as-agent.md) |
+
+## Next step
+
+[Call APIs as an agent's user account in a fleet with the Auth SDK sidecar](sidecar-fleet-call-apis-as-agent-user.md)
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Plan an agent fleet on a shared runtime](plan-agent-fleet.md)
+- [Auth SDK sidecar endpoint reference](/entra/msidweb/agent-id-sdk/endpoints)

+---
+title: Call APIs as a user in a fleet with the Auth SDK sidecar
+description: Use the On-Behalf-Of flow with the routed agent's identity to call APIs for a signed-in user through the Auth SDK sidecar in a shared runtime.
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/05/2026
+ms.reviewer: dastrock
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+
+#customer-intent: As a developer building an agent hosting platform with the Auth SDK sidecar, I want agents in my fleet to call APIs on behalf of the signed-in user with their own agent identity.
+---
+
+# Call APIs as a user in a fleet with the Auth SDK sidecar
+
+After the runtime routes a user's request to an agent, the agent can call APIs for that user with the On-Behalf-Of (OBO) flow. Forward the user's token to the sidecar, and pass the routed agent's identity in the `AgentIdentity` parameter. The downstream token represents both the signed-in user and that agent.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Complete [Authenticate users and route requests to agents in a fleet with the Auth SDK sidecar](sidecar-fleet-authenticate-users.md).
+- Delegated permissions for the target API, [granted to the agent identity](grant-agent-access-microsoft-365.md) or [inherited from the blueprint](set-up-blueprint-agent-fleet.md#optionally-configure-inheritable-permissions).
+
+## Configure the sidecar
+
+Add a delegated profile for each API to the runtime sidecar:
+
+```json
+{
+  "Sidecar": {
+    "AllowOverrides": {
+      "GetAuthorizationHeader": true
+    }
+  },
+  "DownstreamApis": {
+    "custom-api-user": {
+      "BaseUrl": "https://api.contoso.com/",
+      "Scopes": [
+        "api://<custom-api-client-id>/<delegated-scope>"
+      ]
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Explicitly enable `GetAuthorizationHeader` as shown, even if you previously disabled overrides by following the single-instance setup. Otherwise the sidecar ignores `AgentIdentity`. Only trusted runtime code should select and send identity overrides.
+
+## Get a token for the signed-in user
+
+After routing the request and confirming the user can access the agent, call the sidecar:
+
+# [Python](#tab/python)
+
+```python
+def authorization_header_for_user(
+    inbound_auth_header: str, agent_id: str, api_name: str
+) -> str:
+    registration = directory.find(agent_id)
+
+    response = requests.get(
+        f"{SIDECAR_URL}/AuthorizationHeader/{api_name}",
+        params={"AgentIdentity": registration["agent_identity_id"]},
+        headers={"Authorization": inbound_auth_header},
+        timeout=5,
+    )
+    if response.status_code in (401, 403):
+        raise PermissionError("The sidecar rejected the user token or OBO request.")
+    response.raise_for_status()
+    return response.json()["authorizationHeader"]
+
+
+inbound_auth_header = request.headers.get("Authorization")
+authorize_agent_request(inbound_auth_header, agent_id)
+
+api_response = requests.get(
+    "https://api.contoso.com/user-data",
+    headers={
+        "Authorization": authorization_header_for_user(
+            inbound_auth_header, agent_id, "custom-api-user"
+        )
+    },
+    timeout=10,
+)
+api_response.raise_for_status()
+```
+
+# [JavaScript](#tab/javascript)
+
+```javascript
+async function authorizationHeaderForUser(inboundAuthHeader, agentId, apiName) {
+    const registration = await directory.find(agentId);
+
+    const params = new URLSearchParams({
+        AgentIdentity: registration.agentIdentityId,
+    });
+    const response = await fetch(
+        `${SIDECAR_URL}/AuthorizationHeader/${apiName}?${params}`,
+        { headers: { Authorization: inboundAuthHeader } }
+    );
+    if (response.status === 401 || response.status === 403) {
+        throw new Error("The sidecar rejected the user token or OBO request.");
+    }
+    if (!response.ok) {
+        throw new Error(`Sidecar request failed with status ${response.status}.`);
+    }
+    const { authorizationHeader } = await response.json();
+    return authorizationHeader;
+}
+
+const inboundAuthHeader = req.headers.authorization;
+await authorizeAgentRequest(inboundAuthHeader, req.params.agentId);
+
+const apiResponse = await fetch("https://api.contoso.com/user-data", {
+    headers: {
+        Authorization: await authorizationHeaderForUser(
+            inboundAuthHeader, req.params.agentId, "custom-api-user"
+        ),
+    },
+});
+```
+
+---
+
+Always use the agent ID that passed the access check. If the runtime used a different agent's identity, the downstream API would see the wrong agent acting for the user. Don't send the inbound token directly to the downstream API, and don't log either authorization header.
+
+## Call specific resources
+
+Use the scopes and endpoints from the linked resource articles, while keeping the fleet's blueprint client ID and override settings. The single-instance requests omit `AgentIdentity`. For each fleet resource request, call `authorization_header_for_user` or `authorizationHeaderForUser` to supply the routed agent identity and inbound user token.
+
+| Resource | Guidance |
+| --- | --- |
+| Custom API | [Call a custom API as a user](sidecar-call-custom-api-as-user.md) |
+| Azure services | [Call Azure services as a user](sidecar-call-azure-api-as-user.md) |
+| Microsoft Graph | [Call Microsoft Graph as a user](sidecar-call-graph-as-user.md) |
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Plan an agent fleet on a shared runtime](plan-agent-fleet.md)
+- [Inheritable permissions](concept-inheritable-permissions.md)
+- [OAuth 2.0 On-Behalf-Of flow](/entra/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-on-behalf-of-flow)

diff --git a/docs/agent-id/sidecar-fleet-provision-agent-identities.md b/docs/agent-id/sidecar-fleet-provision-agent-identities.md
new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..dfa0d10c0d6
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/agent-id/sidecar-fleet-provision-agent-identities.md
@@ -0,0 +1,290 @@
+---
+title: Provision agent identities for a fleet with the Auth SDK sidecar
+description: Use an app-only blueprint token from the Auth SDK sidecar to create and delete agent identities and agent's user accounts as agents are deployed and retired.
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/05/2026
+ms.reviewer: dastrock
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+
+#customer-intent: As a developer building an agent hosting platform with the Auth SDK sidecar, I want to create an agent identity for each agent I deploy so that every agent in my fleet has its own identity.
+---
+
+# Provision agent identities for a fleet with the Auth SDK sidecar
+
+When an agent is deployed to the fleet, the provisioning service gets an app-only token for the agent identity blueprint from the sidecar and calls Microsoft Graph. It creates an agent identity and, if the agent needs one, an agent's user account. It records both in the agent directory so the runtime can select them on later token requests. When the agent is retired, the service deletes both identities.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Complete [Set up an agent identity blueprint for a fleet](set-up-blueprint-agent-fleet.md).
+- A user or group to assign as each agent's sponsor.
+- A verified domain in the tenant for agent's user account user principal names, if agents need them.
+- A persistent store for the agent directory, such as a database table.
+
+## Configure a provisioning sidecar
+
+Run a sidecar for the provisioning service with the blueprint credential, as described in [Configure the Auth SDK sidecar](microsoft-entra-sdk-for-agent-identities.md). Set `AzureAd:ClientId` to the fleet's blueprint client ID, and keep identity overrides disabled on this provisioning instance. Add an app-only Microsoft Graph profile:
+
+```json
+{
+  "DownstreamApis": {
+    "graph-provisioning": {
+      "BaseUrl": "https://graph.microsoft.com/",
+      "Scopes": [
+        "https://graph.microsoft.com/.default"
+      ],
+      "RequestAppToken": true
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+The provisioning service requests a token without an `AgentIdentity` parameter, so the sidecar returns a token for the blueprint itself. That token can create and delete identities across the fleet.
+
+Use a separate sidecar instance for provisioning. The sidecar accepts only local requests, so colocate it with the provisioning service in the same network namespace, such as a Kubernetes pod. For Docker Compose, use `network_mode: "service:provisioning-sidecar"` on the provisioning service and call `http://localhost:5000`, not the sidecar's DNS name. Don't publish the sidecar port or add the `graph-provisioning` profile to the sidecar that agents use for their own tokens.
+
+## Define the agent directory
+
+The agent directory maps the runtime's agent ID to the agent's identities. Later articles in this path use it to select the identity for each token request.
+
+| Field | Value | Used by |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `agent_id` | The runtime's own identifier for the agent. | Lookups |
+| `agent_identity_id` | The agent identity's ID. For an agent identity, the object ID (`id`) and client ID (`appId`) are the same value. | The `AgentIdentity` parameter, creating the agent's user account, and deleting the agent identity |
+| `agent_user_id` | The agent's user account object ID, or empty. | The `AgentUserId` parameter and deletion |
+
+The examples use a `directory` object with `find`, `save`, and `delete` methods. Replace it with your store.
+
+## Provision an agent
+
+Call the provisioning code from the code that deploys agents, not from an endpoint that agents or users can reach.
+
+# [Python](#tab/python)
+
+```python
+import requests
+
+SIDECAR_URL = "http://localhost:5000"
+GRAPH_URL = "https://graph.microsoft.com"
+BLUEPRINT_CLIENT_ID = "<agent-identity-blueprint-client-id>"
+
+
+def graph_headers() -> dict:
+    """Get an app-only blueprint authorization header from the sidecar."""
+    response = requests.get(
+        f"{SIDECAR_URL}/AuthorizationHeaderUnauthenticated/graph-provisioning",
+        timeout=5,
+    )
+    response.raise_for_status()
+    return {"Authorization": response.json()["authorizationHeader"]}
+
+
+def provision_agent(agent_id, display_name, sponsor_user_id, agent_upn=None) -> dict:
+    registration = directory.find(agent_id)
+
+    if registration is None:
+        response = requests.post(
+            f"{GRAPH_URL}/beta/serviceprincipals/Microsoft.Graph.AgentIdentity",
+            headers=graph_headers(),
+            json={
+                "@odata.type": "#Microsoft.Graph.AgentIdentity",
+                "displayName": display_name,
+                "agentIdentityBlueprintId": BLUEPRINT_CLIENT_ID,
+                "sponsors@odata.bind": [
+                    f"{GRAPH_URL}/v1.0/users/{sponsor_user_id}"
+                ],
+            },
+            timeout=10,
+        )
+        response.raise_for_status()
+        identity = response.json()
+        registration = {
+            "agent_id": agent_id,
+            "agent_identity_id": identity["id"],
+            "agent_user_id": None,
+        }
+        directory.save(registration)
+
+    if agent_upn and registration["agent_user_id"] is None:
+        response = requests.post(
+            f"{GRAPH_URL}/v1.0/users/microsoft.graph.agentUser",
+            headers=graph_headers(),
+            json={
+                "accountEnabled": True,
+                "displayName": display_name,
+                "mailNickname": agent_upn.split("@")[0],
+                "userPrincipalName": agent_upn,
+                "identityParentId": registration["agent_identity_id"],
+            },
+            timeout=10,
+        )
+        response.raise_for_status()
+        registration["agent_user_id"] = response.json()["id"]
+        directory.save(registration)
+
+    return registration
+```
+
+# [JavaScript](#tab/javascript)
+
+```javascript
+const SIDECAR_URL = "http://localhost:5000";
+const GRAPH_URL = "https://graph.microsoft.com";
+const BLUEPRINT_CLIENT_ID = "<agent-identity-blueprint-client-id>";
+
+async function graphHeaders() {
+    const response = await fetch(
+        `${SIDECAR_URL}/AuthorizationHeaderUnauthenticated/graph-provisioning`
+    );
+    if (!response.ok) {
+        throw new Error(`Sidecar request failed with status ${response.status}.`);
+    }
+    const { authorizationHeader } = await response.json();
+    return {
+        Authorization: authorizationHeader,
+        "Content-Type": "application/json",
+    };
+}
+
+async function graphPost(path, body) {
+    const response = await fetch(`${GRAPH_URL}${path}`, {
+        method: "POST",
+        headers: await graphHeaders(),
+        body: JSON.stringify(body),
+    });
+    if (!response.ok) {
+        throw new Error(`Microsoft Graph request failed with status ${response.status}.`);
+    }
+    return response.json();
+}
+
+async function provisionAgent(agentId, displayName, sponsorUserId, agentUpn) {
+    let registration = await directory.find(agentId);
+
+    if (!registration) {
+        const identity = await graphPost(
+            "/beta/serviceprincipals/Microsoft.Graph.AgentIdentity",
+            {
+                "@odata.type": "#Microsoft.Graph.AgentIdentity",
+                displayName,
+                agentIdentityBlueprintId: BLUEPRINT_CLIENT_ID,
+                "sponsors@odata.bind": [`${GRAPH_URL}/v1.0/users/${sponsorUserId}`],
+            }
+        );
+        registration = {
+            agentId,
+            agentIdentityId: identity.id,
+            agentUserId: null,
+        };
+        await directory.save(registration);
+    }
+
+    if (agentUpn && !registration.agentUserId) {
+        const agentUser = await graphPost("/v1.0/users/microsoft.graph.agentUser", {
+            accountEnabled: true,
+            displayName,
+            mailNickname: agentUpn.split("@")[0],
+            userPrincipalName: agentUpn,
+            identityParentId: registration.agentIdentityId,
+        });
+        registration.agentUserId = agentUser.id;
+        await directory.save(registration);
+    }
+
+    return registration;
+}
+```
+
+---
+
+The code saves the agent directory entry after each Microsoft Graph call and reuses saved identities on retries. This isn't an atomic transaction with Microsoft Graph. Serialize provisioning for each agent ID, and reconcile a successful Graph call whose response or directory write failed before retrying, to avoid duplicate identities.
+
+Pass a user principal name only for agents that need an agent's user account. Use a verified domain and a unique alias for each agent. Creating the account doesn't assign licenses, a mailbox, or team membership. For those steps, see [Access Microsoft 365 as an agent's user account](sidecar-call-microsoft-365-as-agent-user.md#configure-the-account).
+
+A new agent identity can take a short time to become available for token requests. If the agent's first token request reports that the identity can't be found, retry with backoff.
+
+## Grant the agent access
+
+After the agent identity exists, grant it the access that this agent needs. Grant application permissions, delegated permissions, Azure role assignments, and access to other resources directly to the agent identity. Each agent's access then stays separate and visible on its own identity.
+
+- [Grant application permissions](grant-application-permissions-agent-identity.md)
+- [Grant delegated permissions](grant-agent-access-microsoft-365.md)
+
+Permissions that are [inherited from the blueprint](set-up-blueprint-agent-fleet.md#optionally-configure-inheritable-permissions) apply to the new agent identity without another grant.
+
+## Retire an agent
+
+Delete the agent's user account before the agent identity, and then remove the agent directory entry:
+
+# [Python](#tab/python)
+
+```python
+def retire_agent(agent_id) -> None:
+    registration = directory.find(agent_id)
+    if registration is None:
+        return
+
+    if registration["agent_user_id"]:
+        requests.delete(
+            f"{GRAPH_URL}/v1.0/users/microsoft.graph.agentUser/{registration['agent_user_id']}",
+            headers=graph_headers(),
+            timeout=10,
+        ).raise_for_status()
+
+    requests.delete(
+        f"{GRAPH_URL}/beta/serviceprincipals/{registration['agent_identity_id']}",
+        headers=graph_headers(),
+        timeout=10,
+    ).raise_for_status()
+
+    directory.delete(agent_id)
+```
+
+# [JavaScript](#tab/javascript)
+
+```javascript
+async function graphDelete(path) {
+    const response = await fetch(`${GRAPH_URL}${path}`, {
+        method: "DELETE",
+        headers: await graphHeaders(),
+    });
+    if (!response.ok) {
+        throw new Error(`Microsoft Graph request failed with status ${response.status}.`);
+    }
+}
+
+async function retireAgent(agentId) {
+    const registration = await directory.find(agentId);
+    if (!registration) {
+        return;
+    }
+
+    if (registration.agentUserId) {
+        await graphDelete(`/v1.0/users/microsoft.graph.agentUser/${registration.agentUserId}`);
+    }
+
+    await graphDelete(`/beta/serviceprincipals/${registration.agentIdentityId}`);
+    await directory.delete(agentId);
+}
+```
+
+---
+
+Deleted agent identities can be restored for a limited time. For details, see [Delete and restore agent identity objects](howto-delete-agent-identity.md).
+
+In production, make retirement retry-safe by treating `404 Not Found` as already deleted and reconciling the directory after partial failures.
+
+## Use Agent 365 provisioning instead
+
+If agents are created through Agent 365, Agent 365 creates the agent identity. Instead of calling Microsoft Graph, listen for Agent 365 agent provisioning events, read the agent identity ID from each event, and save it in the agent directory. For event details, see the [Agent 365 developer documentation](/microsoft-agent-365/developer/).
+
+## Next step
+
+[Call APIs as an agent in a fleet with the Auth SDK sidecar](sidecar-fleet-call-apis-as-agent.md)
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Create and delete agent identities](create-delete-agent-identities.md)
+- [Create and delete an agent's user account](create-delete-agent-user-account.md)
+- [Plan an agent fleet on a shared runtime](plan-agent-fleet.md)
+- [Auth SDK sidecar endpoint reference](/entra/msidweb/agent-id-sdk/endpoints)
