diff --git a/docs/external-id/custom-html-javascript.md b/docs/external-id/custom-html-javascript.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..023379e14c2 --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/external-id/custom-html-javascript.md @@ -0,0 +1,428 @@ +--- +title: Microsoft Entra External ID Custom HTML +titleSuffix: "" +description: Create branded page layouts and step-aware guidance with custom HTML and custom JavaScript around Microsoft-rendered sign-in controls. +ms.topic: concept-article +ms.date: 11/16/2026 +ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1026 +ai-usage: ai-generated +#customer intent: As an administrator, I want to understand custom HTML capabilities and boundaries so that I can choose an appropriate branded experience for my customers. +--- + +# Microsoft Entra External ID custom HTML and JavaScript overview + +[!INCLUDE [applies-to-external-only](includes/applies-to-external-only.md)] + +Create a sign-in experience that feels like part of your application. Custom HTML in Microsoft Entra External ID gives your brand a broader canvas, with your own layout, imagery, navigation, and content around Microsoft's sign-in and sign-up controls. Put onboarding guidance where your users need it, make support easy to find, and keep your brand recognizable throughout the journey. + +Bring the page to life with custom JavaScript that adapts your content to the current step. From timely verification guidance to clear progress indicators, help your users move forward with confidence. + +:::image type="content" source="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/overview-custom-html.png" alt-text="Screenshot of a Contoso Journeys custom HTML page with branded navigation, contextual guidance, and a progress indicator around the sign-in box." lightbox="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/overview-custom-html.png"::: + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> Custom HTML and custom JavaScript are scheduled to become available in preview on December 7, 2026. This information relates to a prerelease product that may be substantially modified before it's released. Microsoft makes no warranties, expressed or implied, with respect to the information provided here. +> +> For an overview of the customization options, see [Customize your authentication experience](customization-overview.md). + +## When to choose custom HTML + +Use custom HTML when you need your own page layout and content around the sign-in box. + +| Customer need | How custom HTML helps | +|---|---| +| **A recognizable brand experience** | Create a richer page with your own header, footer, background, imagery, navigation, and layout around the sign-in box. | +| **Guidance when users need it** | Add instructions, disclaimers, support links, and next-step messaging that give users context around sign-in. | +| **A guided onboarding experience** | Use custom JavaScript and documented events to adapt your guidance and progress text as the sign-in view changes. | +| **A layout tailored to your audience** | Build the surrounding page to accommodate desktop and mobile screens, browser zoom, and different localized text lengths. | +| **Defined customization contracts** | Customize your page and documented content slots while Microsoft provides the sign-in controls and authentication flow. | + +A custom page isn't required for supported logos, sign-in guidance, colors, or typography. Use built-in branding properties or [Basic and Advanced styling](styling.md) for those changes. You can also combine custom HTML with Advanced styling to carry your page's design into the supported authentication controls. + + + +## Prerequisites + +Before you begin, you need: + +- An **external tenant** with the customization preview and [modern authentication experience (Fluent)](modern-authentication-experience.md) enabled. +- A **custom domain** configured for your application's authentication experience. +- If you use **custom JavaScript**, an organization-controlled public HTTPS location to host the scripts. Reference them from the HTML and ensure the page's security policy allows them; don't weaken the policy to load blocked resources. + +You're responsible for ensuring your custom HTML and JavaScript changes keep the page keyboard-accessible, readable, and usable across screen sizes, without obscuring the sign-in box. + +## What you control and what Microsoft controls + +You own the surrounding page shell: header, footer, navigation, background, support content, compliance messaging, and other customer-owned content around the sign-in box. Microsoft provides the sign-in controls and authentication flow, including credential fields, challenge controls, and submit actions. Inside the sign-in box, customize only through the documented content slots and event contracts described in this article. + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> You're responsible for securing your custom domain and all HTML, scripts, and external resources loaded into your page. + +| You can | You must not | +|---|---| +| **Design the surrounding page** with branding, navigation, campaign, compliance, help, privacy, and contextual content. | Recreate, replace, cover, obscure, or intercept authentication controls. | +| **Leave `
` empty** so Microsoft can render authentication there. | Place your own fields, buttons, or fallback content inside it. | +| **Use supported static HTML and CSS** for the surrounding page. | Inspect, copy, alter, click, relabel, disable, restyle, or attach handlers to Microsoft-owned inputs, buttons, or challenge controls. | +| **Use documented content areas and UI events** to update your content. | Depend on undocumented DOM structure, internal or generated Fluent/Fabric classes, current element locations, event ordering, or returned element IDs remaining stable across views. | +| **Use approved externally hosted resources that fail gracefully.** | Make sign-in depend on a script, resource, or event being available. | +| **Use the application's authentication response for the result.** | Read or collect credentials, verification codes, secrets, tokens, protocol data, or entered values; automate controls; or skip authentication steps. | + +:::image type="content" source="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/custom-html-ownership-unified.png" alt-text="Diagram of one page shell showing customer-owned header, footer, background, layout, and content around Microsoft-owned sign-in controls rendered at the required sisuBox mount point." lightbox="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/custom-html-ownership-unified.png"::: + + + + + +## Content areas and Microsoft-owned controls + +The sign-in box includes areas for your content and authentication controls that remain Microsoft-owned. Event metadata can identify both; an element's ID doesn't grant permission to customize it. + +### Content areas and placement metadata + +Supported content slots let you add guidance without changing Microsoft's controls. The bottom area provides placement metadata rather than a general-purpose injection slot. + +| Area | Purpose and boundary | +|---|---| +| **Subheading area** (`subHeadingSection`) | Content you provide between the Microsoft-rendered title and description. | +| **Form area** (`formSection`) | Content you provide after Microsoft fields and before submit actions. | +| **Bottom area** (`bottomSection`) | Identifies the area after the actions, including display message box text. Doesn't allow arbitrary script injection. | + +:::image type="content" source="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/custom-html-content-areas.png" alt-text="Screenshot of annotated sign-in content areas showing the subheading and form slots above the actions and the bottom area after them." lightbox="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/custom-html-content-areas.png"::: + +### Microsoft-owned controls + +| Control | Ownership and restrictions | +|---|---| +| **Authentication controls** | Inputs, buttons, and challenge UI remain Microsoft-controlled, even when their IDs appear in metadata. | +| **Action buttons** (`primaryButton`, `secondaryButton`) | Microsoft-owned controls. Don't click, relabel, disable, replace, style, or attach handlers through the returned IDs. | + + + +## Respond to supported sign-in UI events + +Supported sign-in UI events let your custom JavaScript react to the current sign-in view without taking over authentication. An event is a read-only notification from the Microsoft-rendered sign-in box. Your page can use its information to keep customer-owned guidance, progress text, accessibility hints, or busy indicators in sync with what the user sees. + +For example, use an event to show guidance for a verification step or explain why profile information is needed. The event tells your page which view is displayed, not whether the user completed that step or signed in successfully. + +| Event | What it tells your page | How you can use it | +|---|---|---| +| **`sisuBox:scenariochange`** | The active sign-in scenario or its metadata changed. Its `detail` object includes `schemaVersion`, `activeAction`, and optional `elements` metadata. | Update customer-owned explanations, progress text, or accessibility context for the current view. | +| **`sisuBox:actionprocessing`** | An authentication action started or stopped processing. Its `detail` object includes `schemaVersion` and the Boolean `actionProcessing`. | Show coarse busy feedback or pause duplicate actions in your own content. A value of `false` doesn't mean authentication succeeded or failed. | + +Register listeners on `#sisuBox`, preferably before it initializes. The events bubble, so a listener on `window` can also receive them. For scripts that load later, the container exposes the latest event details through current-state properties. See [Event names and readable information](#event-names-and-readable-information) for the reference and [the JavaScript sample](#sample-javascript) for listener setup. + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> Ensure your event handlers and added content don't compromise page security or authentication data. Validate and sanitize any HTML inserted into supported content slots. + +### Event do's and don'ts + +| Do | Don't | +|---|---| +| Use events to update customer-owned explanatory, progress, or accessibility content. | Use events to determine whether authentication succeeded or failed. | +| Validate `schemaVersion === 1` and ignore versions or fields your code doesn't understand. | Assume event order, timing, or repetition will always be the same. | +| Use only documented content slots and elements returned by the event. | Use undocumented DOM structure, internal CSS classes, or arbitrary element IDs as customization contracts. | +| Re-resolve exposed element IDs whenever scenario metadata changes. | Retain returned IDs or slot elements across views, or assume their locations remain stable. | +| Keep the static shell useful when events are unavailable. | Allow event handlers, scripts, or external resources to block sign-in. | +| Register listeners before initialization. If your script loads late, register listeners before reading the current-state properties. | Rely on a late-loading script receiving events that already occurred. | +| Allow only supported `activeAction` values and ignore unknown actions. | Treat unknown actions or payload fields as supported behavior. | +| Use `sisuBox:scenariochange` only for customer-owned content or accessibility context. | Use scenario changes to perform, skip, or bypass authentication steps. | +| Use `sisuBox:actionprocessing` only as a coarse busy signal. | Treat `actionProcessing=false` as success or failure. | +| Make handlers safe to run repeatedly, without duplicating content or actions. | Assume an event fires only once. | +| Inject customer-owned content only into `subHeadingSection` or `formSection`. | Inject content into arbitrary sign-in-box locations or treat `bottomSection` as an injection slot. | +| Use the application callback or protocol response for the final authentication outcome. | Modify `event.detail`, log user-entered values, collect data from Microsoft controls, or cancel or modify authentication. | + +## Understand scenario actions + +The `activeAction` value in `sisuBox:scenariochange` describes the kind of step currently displayed. Use it to choose relevant guidance, not to direct the authentication flow. For example, `verify` can prompt a reminder about verification codes, while `collectAttributes` can explain why profile information is needed. + +Allow only the supported values below. Ignore unknown values and leave the page usable when an event isn't available. + +| Value | Meaning | +|---|---| +| **`discover`** | Enter an identifier and begin account or tenant discovery. | +| **`select`** | Choose an available account, tenant, credential, or other option. | +| **`challenge`** | Choose an authentication method or challenge. | +| **`verify`** | Enter and submit proof, such as a password or one-time code. | +| **`disambiguate`** | Choose among matching accounts or tenants after ambiguous discovery. | +| **`collectAttributes`** | Provide required registration or profile attributes. | +| **`enroll`** | Choose and begin setting up a new authentication method. | +| **`activate`** | Complete activation of a newly enrolled authentication method. | +| **`consent`** | Review and respond to a consent or confirmation experience. | +| **`prompt`** | Respond to a standalone prompt or decision. | +| **`update`** | Update an existing credential, such as setting a new password. | + +For field definitions and implementation notes, see [Appendix: Custom HTML and event-listener reference](#appendix-custom-html-and-event-listener-reference). + + + +## Configure custom HTML in the admin center + +1. Open your branding theme's **Custom HTML** settings. + + :::image type="content" source="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/custom-html-upload-pane.png" alt-text="Screenshot of Edit Custom HTML with template download links, the custom-domain requirement, and the HTML file upload area." lightbox="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/custom-html-upload-pane.png"::: + +1. Select **Download the HTML template** to get started, or adapt the [sample HTML](#sample-html) below. Replace the organization text, links, and layout. +1. Define exactly one empty `
` in the document's body, after the closing `` tag. Microsoft renders the sign-in experience in this container. Don't put your own content inside it or use `sisuBox` as another element's ID. +1. Under **Upload file**, drag and drop your HTML file or select the upload area to browse for it. + + :::image type="content" source="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/custom-html-editor-pane.png" alt-text="Screenshot of an uploaded custom HTML template in the editor with Save, Remove, Upload, and Download controls." lightbox="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/custom-html-editor-pane.png"::: + +1. Select **Apply** to apply the custom HTML to the theme. +1. Preview and test the authentication experience through your application's configured custom domain. Start without JavaScript and check that users can complete sign-in, including with a keyboard and on mobile screens. + +To add dynamic guidance, download the **JavaScript event-listener template** or adapt the [sample JavaScript](#sample-javascript). Host the script at an organization-controlled public HTTPS URL, reference it from your HTML, and upload the updated HTML. Confirm the page's security policy allows the script and that sign-in still works if it fails to load. + +## Sample HTML + +This starter creates a responsive page shell with organization text, a support link, customer-owned guidance, and the required empty sign-in container. Replace the example content and URLs. Remove the external script reference for your initial static-page validation, then add it after hosting [the JavaScript sample](#sample-javascript). + +The examples illustrate the documented contracts, not a complete production design. Adapt and validate their content, localization, accessibility, and layout for your application. See [How the samples work](#how-the-samples-work) for an annotated walkthrough. + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> Review the template, external resources, and script dependencies before use. Load only approved HTTPS resources, and don't weaken the page's security policy. + +
+ +
+Expand the custom HTML sample + +```html + + + + + + Organization account access + + + +
Organization name
+
+
+

Welcome to your account

+

Sign in to continue to the requested service.

+

+ Follow the instructions in the sign-in box. +

+

+
+
+ +
+
+
+
+ Get help +
+ + + +``` + +
+ +## Sample JavaScript + +Host this script at your own public HTTPS URL and update the HTML reference. It listens for both events, validates schema and action values, and updates only the two customer-owned paragraphs outside the sign-in box. It also reads the current state when loaded after an event. + +
+ +
+Expand the custom JavaScript sample + +```javascript +(function () { + "use strict"; + + const box = document.getElementById("sisuBox"); + const guidance = document.getElementById("customer-guidance"); + const processing = document.getElementById("customer-processing"); + + if (!box || !guidance || !processing) { + console.warn("Custom page guidance is unavailable: required elements are missing."); + return; + } + + const defaultGuidance = guidance.textContent; + const messages = new Map([ + ["discover", "Enter the account information requested in the sign-in box."], + ["select", "Review the available options before continuing."], + ["challenge", "Choose from the available authentication methods."], + ["verify", "Complete the requested security check. Never share a verification code."], + ["disambiguate", "Choose the account you intended to use."], + ["collectAttributes", "Provide the required profile information to continue."], + ["enroll", "Set up the requested sign-in method."], + ["activate", "Follow the instructions to finish activation."], + ["consent", "Review the request before making your selection."], + ["prompt", "Respond to the request in the sign-in box."], + ["update", "Update the requested credential in the sign-in box."] + ]); + + function applyScenario(detail) { + if (detail?.schemaVersion !== 1 || !messages.has(detail.activeAction)) { + if (guidance.textContent !== defaultGuidance) { + guidance.textContent = defaultGuidance; + } + return; + } + + const message = messages.get(detail.activeAction); + if (guidance.textContent !== message) { + guidance.textContent = message; + } + } + + function applyProcessing(detail) { + if (detail?.schemaVersion !== 1 || + typeof detail.actionProcessing !== "boolean") { + if (processing.textContent !== "") { + processing.textContent = ""; + } + return; + } + + const message = detail.actionProcessing ? "Working on your request..." : ""; + if (processing.textContent !== message) { + processing.textContent = message; + } + } + + function onScenarioChange(event) { + applyScenario(event.detail); + } + + function onActionProcessing(event) { + applyProcessing(event.detail); + } + + // Subscribe before reading current state so an intervening event isn't missed. + box.addEventListener("sisuBox:scenariochange", onScenarioChange); + box.addEventListener("sisuBox:actionprocessing", onActionProcessing); + + if (box.sisuBoxScenarioChange) { + applyScenario(box.sisuBoxScenarioChange); + } + if (box.sisuBoxActionProcessing) { + applyProcessing(box.sisuBoxActionProcessing); + } +})(); +``` + +
+ +## Appendix: Custom HTML and event-listener reference + +Use this reference with the [HTML](#sample-html) and [JavaScript](#sample-javascript) samples. It describes the supported event surface, current-view metadata, and ways to customize your content around Microsoft's authentication UI. + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> You're responsible for securing your custom domain and all HTML, scripts, and external resources loaded into your page. + +### Event names and readable information + +Event payload fields are available on `event.detail`. Treat them as versioned, read-only presentation context. + +| Name or property | What it is | Usage | +|---|---|---| +| **`sisuBox` / `#sisuBox`** | Required mount point. | Microsoft renders authentication here. Recommended listener target for supported events. | +| **`sisuBox:scenariochange`** | Scenario-change event. | The active scenario or its metadata changed. Read `schemaVersion`, `activeAction`, and optional `elements`. | +| **`sisuBox:actionprocessing`** | Processing-state event. | An authentication action started or stopped processing. Read `schemaVersion` and `actionProcessing`. | +| **`schemaVersion`** | Schema version in both events. | Process only `1`; ignore unknown versions. | +| **`activeAction`** | Current scenario action. | Match only the [supported action values](#understand-scenario-actions). It isn't a result or a guaranteed sequence position. | +| **`elements`** | Optional purpose-to-element-ID metadata for the current scenario. | Resolve only documented content areas using their current IDs. IDs and elements can change between views. | +| **`actionProcessing`** | Boolean processing state. | Use for coarse customer-owned busy feedback. `false` doesn't establish success or failure. | +| **`sisuBoxScenarioChange`** | Latest scenario details on the `#sisuBox` element, when available. | After registering listeners, read this property to initialize a late-loading script. Apply the same schema and action checks as for event details. | +| **`sisuBoxActionProcessing`** | Latest processing details on the `#sisuBox` element, when available. | After registering listeners, read this property to initialize busy feedback. Validate the schema and Boolean value. | + + + +### Working with current-view element metadata + +For `subHeadingSection` or `formSection`, resolve the returned ID again after every scenario change. If the ID or element is absent, leave your surrounding page usable. Follow the [content-area boundaries](#supported-content-areas-inside-the-sign-in-box) and [event do's and don'ts](#event-dos-and-donts). + +### How the samples work + +Expand these notes alongside the samples when adapting them. The samples update surrounding content; using a supported inner content slot isn't required. + +
+ +
+HTML walkthrough: page shell and sign-in container + +The header, introduction, guidance paragraphs, and support link belong to your page. The responsive grid changes to a single column on narrower screens. Its CSS targets the page shell, not Microsoft-owned fields or buttons. + +The unique, empty `sisuBox` element is the Microsoft mount point. Don't add customer-created username, password, one-time-code, passkey, or submit controls, or reproduce Microsoft's authentication UI elsewhere. + +The two `role="status"` paragraphs provide customer-owned announcements without moving keyboard focus. Review the wording and announcement frequency with assistive technology. Static guidance remains visible without JavaScript. + +The external script reference is a placeholder for your approved HTTPS asset host. The sign-in experience must remain usable when that resource fails or is blocked. + +
+ +
+ +
+JavaScript walkthrough: notifications, validation, and late loading + +The script finds the required container and the two customer-owned paragraphs. Its action-to-message map is an allowlist for schema version `1`. Unsupported versions or actions leave generic guidance instead of guessing at authentication state. + +Each listener reads `event.detail` without changing it. The scenario listener updates guidance; the processing listener accepts only a Boolean and clears busy text when processing stops. Neither listener reads Microsoft-owned controls or treats a notification as a result. + +The listeners are registered before the script reads `sisuBoxScenarioChange` and `sisuBoxActionProcessing`. This handles late loading without relying on another event arriving. Repeated notifications don't append duplicate content or repeat unchanged status text. + +The script doesn't use `elements` because it updates only surrounding content. If you adapt it to insert guidance into a supported content slot, resolve that slot from the current event metadata each time, as described in [Working with current-view element metadata](#working-with-current-view-element-metadata). + +
+ +## Related content + +- [Authentication customization overview](customization-overview.md). +- [Modern authentication experience](modern-authentication-experience.md). +- [Basic and Advanced styling](styling.md).

The capability is scheduled for preview on December 7, 2026, with prerequisites including an external tenant, a custom domain, and HTTPS script hosting for JavaScript.

+---
+title: Microsoft Entra External ID agent toolkit overview
+description: Learn about the Microsoft Entra External ID agent toolkit and choose a skill for onboarding or native authentication migration.
+ms.topic: overview
+ms.date: 11/11/2026
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1030
+# Customer intent: As an app developer, I want to understand the Microsoft Entra External ID agent toolkit and choose a skill so that I can find guidance for my app's task.
+---
+
+# Microsoft Entra External ID agent toolkit overview
+
+The Microsoft Entra External ID agent toolkit is a collection of skills for AI coding agents that help you work on Microsoft Entra External ID apps. Choose a task-specific skill to help onboard an app or migrate an existing native authentication implementation.
+
+[!INCLUDE [applies-to-external-only](../includes/applies-to-external-only.md)]
+
+## Skills catalog
+
+Choose a skill based on the task you want to complete. Each linked guide provides that skill's prerequisites and workflow. Start with the shared installation guide if you haven't set up the toolkit.
+
+| Skill identifier | Customer task | Guide |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| **`eeid-onboarding`** | Select an authentication approach and onboard an app to Microsoft Entra External ID. | [Onboard an app with the toolkit](how-to-ai-agent-toolkit-onboard.md). |
+| **`eeid-native-auth-migrate-v2`** | Migrate an existing app from native authentication V1 to V2. | [Migrate native authentication with the toolkit](how-to-ai-agent-toolkit-migrate-native-auth-v2.md). |
+
+
+## Next steps
+
+- [Install the Microsoft Entra External ID agent toolkit](how-to-install-ai-agent-toolkit.md).
+- [Onboard an app with the toolkit](how-to-ai-agent-toolkit-onboard.md).
+- [Migrate native authentication from V1 to V2 with the toolkit](how-to-ai-agent-toolkit-migrate-native-auth-v2.md).
+
+## Related content
+
+- Learn about [native authentication](~/identity-platform/concept-native-authentication.md).
+- Explore the [Microsoft Entra External ID agent toolkit source repository](https://github.com/AzureAD/ms-eeid-agent-toolkit).

newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/external-id/customers/concept-bring-your-own-ux.md b/docs/external-id/customers/concept-bring-your-own-ux.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..132a129550e --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/external-id/customers/concept-bring-your-own-ux.md @@ -0,0 +1,167 @@ +--- +title: Bring Your Own UX authentication overview +description: Understand Bring Your Own UX authentication in Microsoft Entra External ID, including page ownership, policy boundaries, and developer responsibilities. +author: adamstoffel +ms.author: adamstoffel +ms.topic: overview +ms.date: 11/13/2026 +ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1030 +ai-usage: ai-generated + +#customer intent: As an application developer, I want to understand Bring Your Own UX authentication so that I can design a self-hosted authentication page with clear application and service responsibilities. +--- + +# Bring Your Own UX authentication overview + +Bring Your Own UX (BYO UX) is an authentication approach in Microsoft Entra External ID that lets your team host and manage a browser-based authentication page. You control the page's presentation and application logic. Microsoft Entra External ID applies authentication policy and verifies credentials. + +BYO UX connects a relying application's OAuth or OpenID Connect (OIDC) authorization request to your self-hosted page. The page uses the Native Authentication API for sign-up, sign-in, or password recovery, then returns control to Microsoft Entra External ID to finish the original authorization request. + +[!INCLUDE [applies-to-external-only](../includes/applies-to-external-only.md)] + +[!INCLUDE [bring-your-own-ux-preview](../includes/bring-your-own-ux-preview.md)] + + + +## Architecture and ownership + +The relying application and self-hosted page have separate endpoints and responsibilities. + +| Component | Responsibility | +| --- | --- | +| **Relying application** | Starts authorization, validates the response at its registered reply URL, redeems the authorization code, and manages its application session. | +| **Self-hosted authentication page** | Receives the handoff, collects input, and follows the actions and links returned by the Native Authentication API. | +| **Application-controlled server or proxy** | Mediates browser API calls where needed and restricts their destinations. It handles sensitive authentication requests and responses. | +| **Microsoft Entra External ID** | Enforces policy, verifies credentials, protects transaction state, creates the browser session, and completes authorization. | +| **Browser** | Carries the handoff and completion through the same top-level browser flow, with normal cookie handling. | + +The self-hosted page URL isn't the relying application's OAuth reply URL. Your team owns the page's hosting, maintenance, monitoring, and integration code. + +The relying application uses the same OAuth or Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL) integration as a Microsoft-hosted flow. Use the maintained [authorization-code flow](~/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-auth-code-flow.md) and [MSAL guidance](~/identity-platform/msal-overview.md) for that application. BYO UX implementation focuses on the authentication website's handoff, API calls, and browser completion. + +### BYO UX and the other authentication choices + +Unlike Microsoft-hosted company branding or branding themes, BYO UX gives your team responsibility for hosting the authentication page. Embedded native authentication integrates authentication interactions into the application; BYO UX introduces a self-hosted browser page into the relying application's authorization flow. + +Sharing the Native Authentication API doesn't make these approaches' initialization, completion, sessions, or supported capabilities interchangeable. An OAuth library used by the relying application doesn't implement the page's BYO UX handoff or native authentication transaction. + +For the decision framework, see [Choose an authentication approach](concept-choose-authentication-approach.md). + + + +## Common policy boundaries and supported journeys + +The authentication approaches use the same Microsoft Entra External ID tenant and user-flow policy foundation. BYO UX changes presentation and integration responsibilities, not who decides whether authentication requirements are satisfied. + +Your page can offer returned actions to the user or select an available action through application logic. Required credentials, attributes, and policy checks still apply. + +| Journey | Supported behavior | +| --- | --- | +| **Sign-up** | Email with password or passwordless email one-time passcode, as configured by the user flow. | +| **Sign-in** | Email with password, username with password for configured local accounts (preview), or email one-time passcode. | +| **Password recovery** | Email or SMS one-time-passcode verification for accounts that use an email address and password, from an available handoff link or inline during sign-in. | +| **Multifactor authentication (MFA)** | Email or SMS verification and inline method registration when requested by the service. An email one-time-passcode first factor uses SMS, not email, as its second factor. | + +Passwordless accounts have no password to reset. Sign-up, password recovery, or successful first-factor verification can lead to more MFA or policy interactions rather than immediate authorization completion. + +BYO UX supports custom authentication extensions for email one-time passcode sending (`OnOtpSend`) and token issuance (`OnTokenIssuanceStart`). Attribute collection start and submit extension events aren't supported for BYO UX. See [Custom authentication extensions](concept-custom-extensions.md) for event-specific configuration and behavior. + +Availability can differ by approach, journey, and user flow. See [Supported features](concept-supported-features-customers.md) for the capabilities available with each approach. + + + +## Browser handoff and protocol lifecycle + +BYO UX keeps the relying application's authorization request active while your page handles authentication: + +- **Authorization:** The relying application starts an authorization-code request in the top-level browser. +- **Handoff:** Microsoft Entra External ID sends a form POST to the configured self-hosted page, with initialization information and the initial authentication response. +- **Authentication:** Your page follows the Native Authentication API's returned actions and links with the latest continuation token. +- **Completion:** At `state: continue`, your page submits the final token to the returned BYO UX finish link through a top-level browser form POST. +- **Authorization response:** Microsoft Entra External ID resumes authorization and returns the response to the relying application's registered reply URL. + +The sequence shows an interactive authorization-code flow. A browser session that already satisfies the request can skip the self-hosted page. + +:::image type="complex" source="media/bring-your-own-ux/bring-your-own-ux-sequence.svg" alt-text="Sequence diagram of the BYO UX browser handoff, Native Authentication API interactions, finish form POST, and authorization-code exchange." lightbox="media/bring-your-own-ux/bring-your-own-ux-sequence.svg"::: + The relying application starts authorization in the top-level browser. Microsoft Entra External ID returns an HTML handoff form, and the browser posts `context` and `initialResponse` to the configured self-hosted page. + + The page decodes the envelopes and checks the expected configuration and authentication destinations. It follows native authentication links through its configured browser/proxy integration, using the current input and continuation token and replacing its response model after every reply. + + At `state: continue`, the page submits the returned finish link through a top-level browser form with `continuation_token`. The browser handles Microsoft Entra cookies automatically; the page doesn't read or manually forward HTTP-only cookies. + + Microsoft Entra External ID completes the original authorization request. The browser delivers the code and original OAuth state to the relying application, which validates the response and redeems the code for tokens. +:::image-end::: + + + +Use the same response handling for initialization and every later response. The initial response can already request attributes, verification, enrollment, or completion; it isn't limited to journey selection. Some actions, such as polling, don't require a new input form. + +The page's API requests and its browser finish operation are different transports. Finish isn't a background API request. The browser handles Microsoft Entra cookies automatically; the page doesn't read or manually forward HTTP-only cookies. + +For the envelopes and transport, see the [BYO UX API and protocol reference](reference-bring-your-own-ux.md). For shared response handling, see [Native authentication flow concepts](~/identity-platform/concept-native-authentication-flow.md). + + + +## Sessions, navigation, and fallback + +An existing single sign-on (SSO) browser session that satisfies the authorization request skips the self-hosted page. Successful interactive BYO UX completion creates a Microsoft Entra browser session. Manage the relying application's session separately. + +BYO UX doesn't currently support customizing the account/session picker, application consent page, logout page, or user opt-in for **Stay signed in?**. When a required interaction isn't supported by BYO UX, the current implementation falls back to Microsoft-hosted UX. + +The following scenarios can display Microsoft-hosted UX. Configure the relying application and tenant to avoid these interactions: + +| Scenario | Microsoft-hosted experience | Workaround | +| --- | --- | --- | +| **Sign-out without an account hint** | Account selection during sign-out. | Include `logout_hint` in the relying application's logout request to identify the account to sign out. See [Send a sign-out request](~/identity-platform/v2-protocols-oidc.md#send-a-sign-out-request). | +| **Multiple browser sessions** | Account selection when the authorization request doesn't identify the intended account. | Include `login_hint` in the relying application's authorization request to identify the intended account, or use `prompt=login` to require fresh authentication. `prompt=login` disables SSO for that request. See [Authorization request parameters](~/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-auth-code-flow.md#request-an-authorization-code). | +| **Stay signed in?** | A prompt asking the user whether to persist the browser session. | Configure the Conditional Access **Persistent browser session** control as **Always persistent** or **Never persistent**, according to your requirements. Either setting suppresses the prompt. See [Configure the tenant-level session policy](how-to-configure-bring-your-own-ux.md#configure-session-persistence). | +| **Application consent** | A consent interaction for the relying application's requested API permissions. | Have an administrator review and grant admin consent for the required API permissions on the **relying application registration** before users sign in. See [Grant admin consent in App registrations](~/identity/enterprise-apps/grant-admin-consent.md#grant-admin-consent-in-app-registrations-pane). | + +The authorization and logout parameters belong to the relying application's OAuth integration, not the self-hosted page's Native Authentication API requests. These workarounds address the listed interactions; they don't guarantee that every request avoids Microsoft-hosted UX. + +> [!TIP] +> Even when you use BYO UX, configure [custom branding](how-to-customize-branding-customers.md) or custom HTML for Microsoft-hosted flows to match your self-hosted page. This helps minimize disruption to the user experience when Microsoft-hosted fallback occurs. + +Support for managing account selection on the self-hosted page is planned. See [Future account selection](reference-bring-your-own-ux.md#future-account-selection) for the reserved `disambiguate` action and current handling requirements. + +Keep the latest continuation token and its links together for the active transaction. Browser Back/Forward navigation or a restored page can contain stale transaction state. If the current token expires or the service requires a restart, start a new authorization request from the relying application instead of replaying that state. + + + +## Security responsibilities + +Treat continuation tokens as opaque, sensitive transaction state. Use each token only with the links from its response, and keep transactions separate. + +Use a tenant-verified custom domain for the OAuth service authority, every Native Authentication API call, and the finish link. The self-hosted page and service can use different domains, but both must meet the same tenant's domain-ownership checks. + +Resolve relative authentication links against the Microsoft Entra authority that handled authorization, not the self-hosted page's origin. Validate destinations before sending authentication data. Keep credentials, passcodes, and tokens out of URLs, diagnostic logs, analytics, and support attachments. + +Decoded handoff data and matching tenant/client IDs don't authenticate the sender or establish user intent. Microsoft Entra External ID validates protected continuation state; the relying application remains responsible for validating its original OAuth state. + +The page handles credential input, so its hosting, proxy, and diagnostics are part of your authentication security boundary. Use HTTPS and service-provided masked hints, and avoid messages that reveal whether an account exists. Keep confidential-client credentials on the server. + + + +## Integration boundaries + +Use these boundaries when designing the page and relying application: + +- Use OAuth 2.0 or OIDC authorization-code flow. SAML and WS-Federation aren't yet supported. +- Register a web-type reply URL for both public and confidential relying applications. +- Use the Native Authentication API inside the page. The BYO UX transaction doesn't provide direct Microsoft Graph or Credential API access. +- Finish with the current, unexpired continuation token. Start a new authorization request if that token expires or the service requires a restart. + + + + + +## Implement BYO UX + +- [Configure Bring Your Own UX authentication](how-to-configure-bring-your-own-ux.md). +- [Implement the BYO UX handoff and finish protocol](reference-bring-your-own-ux.md). +- [Handle native authentication flow responses](~/identity-platform/concept-native-authentication-flow.md). + +## Related content + +- [Choose an authentication approach](concept-choose-authentication-approach.md). +- [Native authentication user attributes](~/identity-platform/concept-native-authentication-user-attributes.md).

@@ -0,0 +1,105 @@
+---
+title: Migrate native authentication with the AI agent toolkit
+description: Use the eeid-native-auth-migrate-v2 skill to plan, approve, apply, and validate a native authentication V1-to-V2 migration in your app.
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/11/2026
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1030
+# Customer intent: As an app developer, I want to migrate selected native authentication flows from V1 to V2 with an AI coding agent so that I can review the scope, approve changes, and validate the result.
+---
+
+# Migrate native authentication from V1 to V2 with the AI agent toolkit
+
+Use the `eeid-native-auth-migrate-v2` skill to migrate an existing app's native authentication from V1 to V2. The skill inventories your code, creates a reviewable plan, applies approved changes, reviews those changes for security, and reports validation results.
+
+You can migrate sign-in, sign-up, and self-service password reset together or one flow at a time. Multifactor authentication and strong authentication method registration move with the flow they belong to.
+
+[!INCLUDE [applies-to-external-only](../includes/applies-to-external-only.md)]
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Completion of [Install the AI agent toolkit](how-to-install-ai-agent-toolkit.md).
+- An existing app that uses native authentication V1, with source code the agent can inspect and change.
+
+Build and unit test tools are recommended for validation, but they aren't required to use the skill. If you choose to run validation commands, make sure your project's tools are available.
+
+Use the skill with one of these integration approaches:
+
+- An app that calls the native authentication API directly.
+- A JavaScript single-page app that uses MSAL native authentication.
+- An Android app that uses MSAL native authentication.
+- An iOS or macOS app that uses MSAL native authentication.
+
+The direct API approach isn't limited to the SDK platforms listed here. The skill needs access to the app-owned HTTP calls and flow code. It isn't a guide for adding authentication to a new app, upgrading an MSAL package on its own, or changing browser-redirect authentication.
+
+## Start the migration and choose its scope
+
+Start in the app you want to migrate. The skill inspects V1 usage before proposing code changes.
+
+1. Open your app's source folder in your coding agent. If the workspace contains several apps, identify the app to migrate.
+1. Ask the agent to use `eeid-native-auth-migrate-v2`. Choose the request that matches your intended scope:
+
+    - To migrate all flows, enter `Migrate my app's native auth from V1 to V2`.
+    - To migrate sign-in only, enter `Migrate only sign-in to native auth V2 and keep the other flows on V1`.
+
+1. Review the agent's inventory and any questions about the integration approach or scope.
+
+If the skill doesn't start, name it explicitly in your request. In coding agents that support it, you can enter `/eeid-native-auth-migrate-v2`.
+
+The skill writes `.native-auth-v2-migration/plan.md` in your app's root folder. It doesn't change application code before you approve the plan.
+
+## Review and revise the migration plan
+
+The plan records what changes, what stays on V1, what users will notice, and how the migration is validated.
+
+1. Open `.native-auth-v2-migration/plan.md`.
+1. Confirm the selected flows and deferred flows. Check that changes to shared code preserve the flows that remain on V1.
+1. Review the proposed behavior changes, implementation tasks, and open decisions.
+1. Review any planned validation commands and their baseline and post-change runs. Adjust the plan's validation settings with the agent if needed.
+1. Answer open decisions and request revisions until the scope is correct. For example, enter `Remove password reset from the migration plan`.
+
+Different flows can use different versions, but a single flow can't mix V1 and V2. This boundary includes MFA and method registration that occur within the flow.
+
+Each plan change needs approval of the new revision. Resolve open decisions before approving.
+
+## Approve and apply the plan
+
+Approval authorizes the current plan revision, including its validation commands. Review the plan before giving that approval.
+
+1. Confirm that the plan matches your intended scope and has no unresolved decisions.
+1. Approve the plan in chat. For example, enter:
+
+    ```text
+    The plan looks good. Approved, go ahead.
+    ```
+
+1. Let the agent perform its pre-apply check and any planned baseline validation. If files changed since planning or an in-scope file has uncommitted changes, resolve the conflict and review any revised plan before continuing.
+1. Let the agent apply the approved changes, update the applicable tests, review its changes for security, and run any planned validation commands.
+
+The `eeid-native-auth-migrate-v2` workflow doesn't commit, push, or create branches. It leaves changes in your working tree for you to review.
+
+## Check the report and test the app
+
+The migration report records the outcome rather than assuming every check passed.
+
+1. Open `.native-auth-v2-migration/report.md`.
+1. Review the outcome, deviations from the plan, security review findings, and baseline and post-change validation results. Check the reasons for any failed or not-run checks.
+1. Review the application changes in your working tree.
+1. Perform the manual tests listed in the report for the migrated flows and any deferred flows that share code.
+
+Keep unresolved findings and manual tests visible when deciding whether the migration is ready for your own commit and release.
+
+## Continue a migration or migrate deferred flows
+
+The migration folder records progress so that the skill can determine the next step.
+
+1. To resume an interrupted migration, ask the agent to use the skill and enter `Continue my native auth migration`.
+1. After a phase is reported, review the outcome before starting deferred flows. To continue with the remaining flows, enter `Start the next phase and migrate the remaining flows to V2`.
+
+An unfinished plan created by a different version of the skill can't be continued as-is. The skill requires its version-change restart procedure instead.
+
+## Related content
+
+- Explore the [AI agent toolkit overview and available skills](ai-agent-toolkit-overview.md).
+- Learn how to [onboard an app with the toolkit](how-to-ai-agent-toolkit-onboard.md).
+- Review the [native authentication overview](~/identity-platform/concept-native-authentication.md).

+---
+title: Add authentication with the AI agent toolkit
+description: Use the eeid-onboarding skill to choose an authentication experience, plan or implement app changes, and get manual tenant setup instructions.
+ms.topic: how-to

+# Customer intent: As an app developer, I want to use an AI coding agent to onboard my app to Microsoft Entra External ID so that I can choose an authentication experience and review the required app and tenant changes.
+---
+
+# Add Microsoft Entra External ID authentication with the AI agent toolkit
+
+Use the `eeid-onboarding` skill to choose an authentication experience for your app, create an implementation plan or apply approved code changes, and get tenant configuration instructions. You make the authentication choices, approve application changes, and complete tenant setup manually.
+
+[!INCLUDE [applies-to-external-only](../includes/applies-to-external-only.md)]
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Completion of [Install the AI agent toolkit](how-to-install-ai-agent-toolkit.md).
+- Your application's source code, available to your coding agent.
+- A Microsoft Entra external tenant and its tenant ID. If you need a tenant, [create an external tenant](how-to-create-external-tenant-portal.md).
+- An account with permission to complete the tenant configuration steps for your selected authentication experience.
+- Your project's existing build and test tools, if you choose to implement code changes.
+
+## Start the onboarding skill
+
+Start in your app's source folder so that the agent can base its recommendations on your project.
+
+1. Open the application's source folder in your coding agent.
+1. Ask the agent to use the `eeid-onboarding` skill. For example, enter:
+
+    ```text
+    /eeid-onboarding Help me add Microsoft Entra External ID authentication to this app.
+    ```
+
+1. Choose **Hosted authentication (faster setup)** or **Custom authentication experience (more control)** when prompted. Select **Other / help me choose** to discuss the trade-offs before continuing.
+1. Let the agent inspect your repository without changing it. Review its recommended authentication approach and confirm your choice.
+
+The skill presents **Web authentication**, **Native authentication**, or **BYO UX** according to your selected experience and the repository findings. It asks for your choice before moving on.
+
+## Select journeys, tenant details, and factors
+
+Your choices determine the application changes and the manual tenant setup instructions.
+
+1. Select the journeys you want to enable: **Sign in**, **Sign up**, **MFA**, or **Self-service password reset (SSPR)**.
+1. Provide your tenant ID. The agent attempts to resolve the external-tenant subdomain from authenticated tenant metadata. If it can't resolve the subdomain, provide it when prompted.
+1. Confirm the tenant details the agent presents.
+1. Select the sign-in factors. Without MFA, choose **Email + password** or **Email one-time passcode**. With MFA, review and select the first-factor and second-factor combination the agent presents.
+
+## Choose a plan or approved implementation
+
+Choose whether you want a technical plan to review or application code changes. Tenant setup remains manual in either mode.
+
+1. Review the selected authentication approach, journeys, tenant details, and factors with the agent.
+1. Choose an implementation mode:
+
+    - **Create a dry-run plan** produces a dependency-ordered technical plan without changing your repository or tenant. Review the proposed files, packages, configuration, routes, scopes, tests, tenant steps, and rollback guidance.
+    - **Implement changes** prepares application code changes for your approval. Review the exact files and package changes, repository checkpoint information, and targeted rollback procedure before confirming.
+
+The onboarding skill requires approval before changing code, installing packages, or replacing an existing authentication stack. For implementation, it records the Git branch, commit, and working-tree status. For dirty or non-Git projects, its checkpoint procedure copies the files it will change to a location outside the repository.
+
+## Complete the manual tenant setup
+
+Use the tailored instructions the agent provides for your chosen approach. The standard onboarding workflow doesn't run tenant automation scripts.
+
+1. Review the generated Microsoft Entra admin center instructions. Each step should identify the action, its purpose, the expected result, and how to verify it.
+1. Complete the applicable tenant configuration steps manually. Check that the application registration, platform, redirect URIs, scopes, and selected journeys match the application code or dry-run plan.
+1. If you selected Web authentication and want branding, review the offered branding package and follow the generated upload and configuration instructions.
+
+## Verify the result and review the handoff
+
+Distinguish changes the agent completed from configuration and tests that you still need to perform.
+
+1. If the agent implemented code changes, review the changed files and the results of your project's applicable format, lint, type, build, and test commands.
+1. If you chose a dry run, confirm that the plan includes dependency-ordered implementation tasks, acceptance checks, tenant instructions, tests, and rollback guidance.
+1. Complete the manual checks for your selected journeys and factors. Compare redirect URIs exactly and check the applicable authority, scopes, protected routes, and logout behavior.
+1. Review the handoff for completed checks, remaining tenant steps, and blocked items. Don't treat a generated instruction as a completed tenant configuration step.
+
+## Related content
+
+- Explore the [AI agent toolkit overview and available skills](ai-agent-toolkit-overview.md).
+- Review how to [choose an authentication approach](concept-choose-authentication-approach.md).
+- Learn how to [migrate native authentication with the toolkit](how-to-ai-agent-toolkit-migrate-native-auth-v2.md).

Use each response to determine the next action. When it returns a new continuation token, replace the previous token and its links together for the active transaction. +1. If the current token expires or the service requires a restart, stop the transaction and start a new authorization request from the relying application. +1. When the service returns `state: continue`, submit the latest unexpired token as the `continuation_token` form field to the returned BYO UX finish link through top-level browser navigation. +1. Show a clear error for malformed initialization, missing essential links, or unsupported required actions. Don't treat these conditions as successful authentication or automatically replay a credential submission. + +Matching tenant/client IDs and decoded handoff data don't authenticate the sender or establish user intent. Microsoft Entra External ID validates protected continuation state. The relying application retains its normal OAuth response and state validation. + +For the wire contract, see the [BYO UX API and protocol reference](reference-bring-your-own-ux.md). API operations use JSON requests; finish uses a browser form POST, not `fetch`, XHR, an iframe, or a server-to-server call. Let the browser generate `Origin` and handle Microsoft Entra cookies. Don't read or manually forward HTTP-only cookies. + +## Verify the configured integration + +Validate the browser flow and its security boundaries before making your page available to customers. + +1. Verify that an eligible authorization request reaches the configured self-hosted page with both initialization fields. +1. Check the tenant-verified custom domain in each Microsoft Entra service URL, including OAuth, native authentication, proxy upstream, and finish URLs. Verify the tenant GUID in service paths and preserve returned paths and query parameters. +1. Exercise each enabled sign-up, sign-in, and password-recovery journey, including email one-time-passcode sign-in and email or SMS recovery. Test available handoff and inline recovery entries. +1. Verify registered-factor challenges and inline multifactor authentication (MFA) registration when requested. Continue handling returned actions after sign-up, credential verification, or password updates. +1. Verify that completion returns the authorization response to the registered reply URL, with the response transport and application state from the original OAuth request. +1. Check invalid passcodes, continuation-token expiry, service-directed restart, cancellation, and ambiguous network failures. Ensure that the page gives a usable error and doesn't automatically replay credential verification or password updates. +1. Test existing-session bypass, browser Back/Forward, restored pages, and form resubmission. Verify that session persistence follows the configured policy and stale pages restart rather than replay old tokens. +1. Confirm that diagnostics retain request IDs, correlation IDs, trace IDs, and timestamps without credentials, tokens, passcodes, or personal data. + +## Remove the BYO UX configuration + +Remove the custom authentication configuration when you no longer want the application to use the page. + +- Use the same Microsoft Graph beta application `PATCH` route and set `web.customAuthenticationUx` to `null`. + + ```json + { + "web": { + "customAuthenticationUx": null + } + } + ``` + +## Related content + +- [Bring Your Own UX authentication overview](concept-bring-your-own-ux.md). +- [BYO UX API and protocol reference](reference-bring-your-own-ux.md).

diff --git a/docs/external-id/customers/how-to-install-ai-agent-toolkit.md b/docs/external-id/customers/how-to-install-ai-agent-toolkit.md
new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..de23646553c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/external-id/customers/how-to-install-ai-agent-toolkit.md
@@ -0,0 +1,85 @@
+---
+title: Install the Microsoft Entra External ID agent toolkit
+description: Set up the Microsoft Entra External ID agent toolkit with your AI coding agent, then choose the skill for your app's task.
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/11/2026
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1030
+# Customer intent: As an app developer, I want to install the Microsoft Entra External ID agent toolkit for my coding agent so that I can use its skills in my app.
+---
+
+# Install the Microsoft Entra External ID agent toolkit
+
+Install the Microsoft Entra External ID agent toolkit for your AI coding agent so you can choose a skill for your app's task. Installation is shared across the toolkit; follow the guide for your chosen skill after setup.
+
+[!INCLUDE [applies-to-external-only](../includes/applies-to-external-only.md)]
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download) 22.20 or later, only if you use the Skills CLI installation option.
+- An AI coding agent, such as GitHub Copilot CLI, Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio Code, or Cursor.
+
+## Install the toolkit
+
+Choose the tab for your coding agent. The plugin installation options use the identifier `eeid-toolkit`. The Skills CLI option installs the toolkit's skills for agents such as GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio Code and Cursor.
+
+### [GitHub Copilot CLI](#tab/github-copilot)
+
+- Run these commands in your terminal:
+
+    ```bash
+    copilot plugin marketplace add AzureAD/ms-eeid-agent-toolkit
+    copilot plugin install eeid-toolkit@ms-eeid-agent-toolkit
+    ```
+
+### [Claude Code](#tab/claude-code)
+
+- Run these commands in a Claude Code session:
+
+    ```text
+    /plugin marketplace add AzureAD/ms-eeid-agent-toolkit
+    /plugin install eeid-toolkit@ms-eeid-agent-toolkit
+    ```
+
+### [Codex](#tab/codex)
+
+1. Run this command in your terminal:
+
+    ```bash
+    codex plugin marketplace add AzureAD/ms-eeid-agent-toolkit
+    ```
+
+1. Start Codex, enter `/plugins`, and install `eeid-toolkit` from the plugin list.
+
+### [Other agents](#tab/other-agents)
+
+Use the [Skills CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) to install all the toolkit's skills for Cursor, GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio Code, and other agents.
+
+- Run this command in your terminal:
+
+    ```bash
+    npx skills add AzureAD/ms-eeid-agent-toolkit --all
+    ```
+
+To install all the skills for a specific agent instead, use `--agent` with the agent's name. For example, use this optional form for Cursor:
+
+```bash
+npx skills add AzureAD/ms-eeid-agent-toolkit --skill '*' --agent cursor
+```
+
+---
+
+## Choose your next skill
+
+Select the guide for the task you want to complete. The guides describe skill-specific prerequisites and procedures without requiring you to repeat toolkit installation.
+
+1. Review the [skills catalog](ai-agent-toolkit-overview.md#skills-catalog) and choose the skill for your task.
+1. Follow the corresponding guide:
+
+    - Use [`eeid-onboarding`](how-to-ai-agent-toolkit-onboard.md) to onboard an app to Microsoft Entra External ID.
+    - Use [`eeid-native-auth-migrate-v2`](how-to-ai-agent-toolkit-migrate-native-auth-v2.md) to migrate an existing app from native authentication V1 to V2.
+
+## Related content
+
+- Explore the [Microsoft Entra External ID agent toolkit overview](ai-agent-toolkit-overview.md).
+- Learn about [native authentication](~/identity-platform/concept-native-authentication.md).

newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/external-id/customers/reference-bring-your-own-ux.md b/docs/external-id/customers/reference-bring-your-own-ux.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..4a09a271e65 --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/external-id/customers/reference-bring-your-own-ux.md @@ -0,0 +1,188 @@ +--- +title: Bring Your Own UX API and protocol reference +description: Reference the browser handoff, initialization envelopes, continuation-token transport, and finish contract for Bring Your Own UX. +author: adamstoffel +ms.author: adamstoffel +ms.topic: reference +ms.date: 11/13/2026 +ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1030 +ai-usage: ai-generated + +#customer intent: As an application developer, I want the BYO UX handoff and completion contract so that my self-hosted page can handle authentication and resume the relying application's authorization flow. +--- + +# Bring Your Own UX API and protocol reference + +Bring Your Own UX (BYO UX) connects an OAuth 2.0 or OpenID Connect authorization-code request to a self-hosted authentication page. This reference describes the browser handoff and finish contract, and the boundaries around the page's Native Authentication API calls. + +[!INCLUDE [applies-to-external-only](../includes/applies-to-external-only.md)] + +[!INCLUDE [bring-your-own-ux-preview](../includes/bring-your-own-ux-preview.md)] + +## Protocol boundaries + +BYO UX starts with the relying application's browser authorization request and completes through browser form navigation. The self-hosted page calls the Native Authentication API between those boundaries. + +| Phase | Transport | Contract | +| --- | --- | --- | +| **Authorization** | Top-level browser navigation to `/{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/authorize`. | The relying application's OAuth authorization-code request. | +| **Page initialization** | Browser form POST to the configured self-hosted page. | Required `context` and `initialResponse` fields. | +| **Authentication operations** | JSON requests to links returned by the service. | The [shared Native Authentication API contract](~/identity-platform/reference-native-authentication.md). | +| **Completion** | Top-level browser form POST to the returned `_links.continue.href`. | BYO UX finish form containing `continuation_token`. | +| **Authorization response** | The original OAuth response mode at the registered reply URL. | Authorization code and original application state, or an OAuth error. | + +BYO UX uses the initialization response from the browser handoff and completes through the returned finish link. Don't call the standalone native authentication `/authorize-challenge` operation within a BYO UX transaction. + +## Authorization request + +The relying application starts an authorization-code request at its tenant-specific custom-domain authority: + +```http +GET https://{custom_domain}/{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/authorize +``` + +`{custom_domain}` is the tenant's verified custom-domain service hostname, and `{tenant}` is the external tenant's GUID. Don't use `/common`. + +Use a tenant-verified custom domain for every Microsoft Entra service URL in this flow. This includes the OAuth authority, all Native Authentication API URLs, proxy upstream URLs, and the returned finish link. This requirement applies to service URLs, not the relying application's callback or resource URLs. The self-hosted page can use a different domain that meets the same tenant's domain-ownership checks. + +The browser-facing proxy URL is a transport route, not the service authority. Resolve returned service links against the configured Microsoft Entra service authority, not a local proxy address. + +The OAuth request carries the relying application's `client_id`, registered `redirect_uri`, requested scopes, `response_type=code`, and application state. The `redirect_uri` is the relying application's web-type reply URL, not the self-hosted page URL. Both public and confidential relying applications use a web-type reply URL for BYO UX. + +The relying application uses the same OAuth or Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL) integration as a Microsoft-hosted flow. It validates the OAuth response, including its original state, and redeems the code. Use the maintained [authorization-code protocol reference](~/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-auth-code-flow.md) and [MSAL guidance](~/identity-platform/msal-overview.md). Keep confidential-client credentials on the server, outside the browser page. + +## Authorization handoff + +For a request that requires the self-hosted page, Microsoft Entra External ID returns `200 OK` with an HTML page that automatically submits a form to the configured page URL. The browser sends that form as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. + +| Field | Required | Encoding and contents | +| --- | --- | --- | +| **`context`** | Yes. | Base64url-encoded UTF-8 JSON with page initialization identifiers. | +| **`initialResponse`** | Yes. | Base64url-encoded UTF-8 JSON with the initial native authentication HAL response and continuation token. | + +Require both fields and decode each from base64url to UTF-8 JSON. Validate tenant and client IDs against your deployment configuration and reject unexpected authentication destinations. Decoded handoff data, matching IDs, and destination checks don't authenticate the sender or establish user intent. + +Microsoft Entra External ID validates protected continuation state when resuming the original OAuth request. The relying application validates its original OAuth state. + +Ignore unknown optional form fields, JSON properties, and HAL relations. Missing required fields or unsupported required actions aren't valid initialization. + +### Context properties + +The `context` envelope identifies the tenant and relying application. + +| Property | Type | Meaning | +| --- | --- | --- | +| **`tenantId`** | GUID string. | Canonical tenant identifier. | +| **`clientId`** | GUID string. | Application identifier from the original authorization request. | + +These identifiers initialize the page. The envelope doesn't contain credentials, the original OAuth request or state, decrypted continuation state, or an OAuth result. Don't rely on `login_hint`, `domain_hint`, or arbitrary application context being passed to the page. + +### Initial authentication response + +The decoded `initialResponse` is a native authentication HAL response with the current `continuationToken`, `state`, and the links and metadata for the current action. Use the same [response handling](~/identity-platform/concept-native-authentication-flow.md) for initialization and every later response. + +The handoff can already request attributes, verification, enrollment, or completion; it isn't restricted to journey discovery. When it offers journeys, the page can present them or select an available journey through application logic. + +### Future account selection + +Account selection on the self-hosted page isn't currently supported. The reserved future response-handling case is `state: interactionRequired` with `action: disambiguate`, not a separate transaction state. + +Prepare a distinct handling case without implementing an account-selection payload or endpoint yet. Until support is documented, stop this unsupported required interaction explicitly rather than continuing authentication or treating it as ordinary credential verification. See the [reserved account-selection action](~/identity-platform/reference-native-authentication.md#account-selection-action-reserved). + +## Native authentication operations + +Use the [shared API reference](~/identity-platform/reference-native-authentication.md) for JSON request bodies, response metadata, and errors. The page calls the Native Authentication API through its configured browser/proxy integration. The relying application's OAuth library doesn't implement the page's handoff-to-finish sequence. + +Resolve relative links against the tenant-verified custom-domain authority origin that handled `/authorize`, not the self-hosted page. Validate the destination against that expected HTTPS authority and reject unexpected cross-origin destinations before sending authentication data. Preserve returned paths, including the tenant GUID, versions, and query parameters rather than rebuilding the URLs. + + + + + +For actions, method selection, enrollment, and activation, follow the shared [flow concepts](~/identity-platform/concept-native-authentication-flow.md). For requested fields and validation metadata, see [Native authentication user attributes](~/identity-platform/concept-native-authentication-user-attributes.md). + +### Shared journey references + +Within BYO UX, the browser handoff replaces the shared references' authorization-start operation, and BYO UX finish replaces their authorization-resume operation. + +| Journey | Shared operations | +| --- | --- | +| **[Sign-in](~/identity-platform/reference-native-authentication-sign-in.md)** | Identifier discovery, credential verification, and additional factors. | +| **[Sign-up](~/identity-platform/reference-native-authentication-sign-up.md)** | Attribute collection and credential verification. | +| **[Password recovery](~/identity-platform/reference-native-authentication-password-reset.md)** | Recovery from an available handoff link or inline during sign-in, password update, and polling. | + +Use the [BYO UX journey scope](concept-bring-your-own-ux.md#common-policy-boundaries-and-supported-journeys) and current links to identify the capabilities available for this transaction. Continue handling returned actions after sign-up, password updates, or method activation. + +## Continuation-token handling + +Use the latest continuation token together with the links from the same response and transaction. Replace the stored response and token when the service returns a new one. + +| Location | Token field | Transport | +| --- | --- | --- | +| **Decoded `initialResponse`** | `continuationToken` | Inside the initialization JSON envelope. | +| **Native Authentication API request or response** | `continuationToken` | JSON property. | +| **BYO UX finish request** | `continuation_token` | URL-encoded field in the form body. | + +Treat continuation tokens as opaque. Parse neither their contents nor a token-derived destination. Keep them only for the active transaction, and exclude them from URLs, logs, telemetry, analytics, exceptions, and support attachments. A token from an earlier response or another transaction isn't a substitute for the latest token. + +Finish with the current, unexpired token. If that token expires or the service requires a restart, stop the transaction and start a new authorization request from the relying application. For response and continuation-token handling, see [Native authentication flow concepts](~/identity-platform/concept-native-authentication-flow.md). + +## Complete the BYO UX flow + +When the Native Authentication API returns `state: continue`, its `_links.continue.href` identifies the BYO UX finish endpoint. Submit the latest token through a top-level browser form POST: + +```http +POST https://{custom_domain}/{tenant}/v2.0/customAuthUx/finish +Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded + +continuation_token={url_encoded_final_token} +``` + +The path above identifies the finish operation on the tenant's verified custom domain, with the tenant GUID in the path. Use the returned link for the active transaction without rebuilding it. API JSON uses `continuationToken`, while this form uses `continuation_token`. + +Finish through the same top-level browser flow that initiated authorization. `fetch`, XHR, iframe navigation, and server-to-server calls aren't supported completion transports. The browser returns Microsoft Entra cookies automatically; the self-hosted page doesn't read or manually forward HTTP-only cookies. + +Serve the self-hosted page with `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin`. Use the browser-generated `Origin` header for the finish POST. + +The finish request domain and the hostname in the page's origin must be DNS-verified custom domains, or their subdomains, owned by the same tenant. They don't have to be equal. `Origin` must contain one HTTPS origin without a path, query, fragment, or user information. Missing, repeated, opaque (`null`), non-HTTPS, and unowned origins are rejected. + +Domain ownership and `Origin` checks aren't proof of user intent. + + + +### Success response and sessions + +The finish operation resumes the original OAuth request and creates the Microsoft Entra browser session. It doesn't return a native authentication JSON success body. + +For authorization-code flow, the browser delivers the authorization code and original application state to the registered `redirect_uri`. The original `response_mode` determines whether that response uses a redirect or form POST. Code redemption remains the relying application's responsibility. + +Session persistence is controlled separately through tenant policy. For existing-session bypass, account pickers, consent, and sign-out, see [Sessions, navigation, and fallback](concept-bring-your-own-ux.md#sessions-navigation-and-fallback). + +## Errors and diagnostics + +API operations use the [shared native authentication error contract](~/identity-platform/reference-native-authentication.md#errors). The browser handoff and finish operation have different failure surfaces: + +| Condition | Handling | +| --- | --- | +| **Malformed handoff or unexpected tenant/client IDs** | Stop initialization and return to the relying application to start again. | +| **Unexpected authentication destination** | Reject the destination before sending credentials or transaction state. | +| **Invalid or expired current continuation token, or service-directed restart** | Stop the transaction and start a new relying-app authorization request. | +| **Finish failure** | Handle the OAuth error response or Microsoft Entra error page delivered through browser navigation, not native authentication JSON. | + +Stop explicitly on unsupported required actions or missing essential links. Unknown optional metadata alone isn't a failure. Don't treat an unhandled enrollment action as successful authentication. + +Retain request IDs, correlation IDs, trace IDs, and timestamps for diagnostics. Exclude credentials, tokens, passcodes, and personal data, and don't display raw internal error details. Avoid automatically replaying credential verification or password updates after an ambiguous network failure. + + + +## Microsoft-hosted fallback + +BYO UX doesn't support leaving a transaction for a Microsoft-hosted authentication step and resuming the same transaction. Starting a new relying-app authorization request is a separate authentication attempt, not a resumable continuation. Don't construct a fallback URL or reuse a standalone native authentication fallback recipe. + +Microsoft-hosted consent or account-selection pages can still appear during normal OAuth processing. Their appearance doesn't provide a page-controlled fallback mechanism. + +## Related content + +- [Bring Your Own UX authentication overview](concept-bring-your-own-ux.md). +- [Configure Bring Your Own UX authentication](how-to-configure-bring-your-own-ux.md). +- [Native authentication flow concepts](~/identity-platform/concept-native-authentication-flow.md).
