newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/external-id/customization-overview.md b/docs/external-id/customization-overview.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..503ce014f99 --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/external-id/customization-overview.md @@ -0,0 +1,146 @@ +--- +title: Microsoft Entra External ID Customization +titleSuffix: "" +description: Help your users recognize your brand and understand their next step with content, styling, and custom HTML in Microsoft Entra External ID. +ms.topic: overview +ms.date: 11/16/2026 +ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1026 +ai-usage: ai-generated +#customer intent: As an administrator, I want to understand the customization options so that I can choose the right experience for my users. +--- + +# Microsoft Entra External ID customizations overview + +[!INCLUDE [applies-to-external-only](includes/applies-to-external-only.md)] + +Every sign-in shapes how your users experience your brand. Make that interaction distinctly yours, with recognizable design, clear guidance, and support where your users need it. Microsoft Entra External ID is introducing a new, modern authentication experience and expanded customization capabilities to help you deliver that experience without building and maintaining authentication controls yourself. + +Bring your brand to life, with as much customization as your experience needs. Make the polished, modern foundation yours with built-in branding and styling, or create a broader canvas with custom HTML and JavaScript that helps your users navigate each step with confidence. + + + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> The modern Fluent experience, Basic and Advanced styling, and custom HTML with custom JavaScript are scheduled to become available in preview on December 7, 2026. This information relates to a prerelease product that may be substantially modified before it's released. Microsoft makes no warranties, expressed or implied, with respect to the information provided here. + + + + + + + + + +## Choose the customization your brand needs + +Start with a polished foundation and layer in the customization your brand needs, from coordinated colors to a distinctive page experience. + +All options build on the familiar branding themes platform, so each application can have its own distinct brand identity while Microsoft continues to provide the secure, trusted authentication experience underneath. + +| Customization option | What you can deliver | +|---|---| +| [Modern authentication experience (Fluent)](modern-authentication-experience.md) | Your brand identity layered onto a polished, modern foundation with built-in branding and content properties, clear guidance, and familiar controls. | +| [Basic styling](styling.md#configure-basic-styling) | Your brand color carried across supported UI elements in light and dark modes, configurable in minutes. | +| [Advanced styling](styling.md#configure-advanced-styling) | Your design system reflected in supported typography, spacing, and UI details, with precise styling control. | +| [Custom HTML and JavaScript](custom-html-javascript.md) | Your own page layout and content, shaped with HTML and brought to life with JavaScript for step-aware guidance, while the familiar Microsoft authentication experience remains underneath. | + + + + + +## Modern authentication experience (Fluent) + +The modern authentication experience is more than a visual refresh. Using Microsoft's Fluent design language, it brings clearer guidance, familiar controls, and new dark mode support to supported sign-up and sign-in journeys. That attention to detail carries through the journey, with clear instructions, visual cues, and thoughtful interactions that work together to create a seamless experience. + +Essential customization is built into this foundation. Add supported logos, backgrounds, text, and links through the same familiar branding themes experience, without writing code. New properties for dark mode assets keep your brand recognizable across themes, while new content properties let you add custom guidance where your users need it. + +:::image type="content" source="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/overview-modern-light.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Contoso sign-in experience in light mode with a branded background, logo, and guidance." lightbox="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/overview-modern-light.png"::: + +:::image type="content" source="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/overview-modern-dark.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Contoso sign-in experience in dark mode with a dark background and sign-in box." lightbox="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/overview-modern-dark.png"::: + +Learn how to enable and personalize the experience in [Modern authentication experience](modern-authentication-experience.md). + + + +## Basic styling + +Your brand color sets the tone for a cohesive authentication experience. Start by entering your brand color to generate coordinated light and dark palettes. Basic styling then carries that color automatically across supported buttons, links, and other UI elements, giving you a branded experience in minutes without styling each element individually. + +:::image type="content" source="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/brand-color-ramp.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the light-theme and dark-theme brand-color ramps in the admin center, each with 16 stops numbered 10 through 160." lightbox="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/brand-color-ramp.png"::: + +Learn how to [apply your brand color with basic styling](styling.md#configure-basic-styling). + +## Advanced styling + +When color alone isn't enough, bring the finer details of your design system into the authentication experience. Advanced styling uses **design tokens**: named settings that define how UI components look, such as font sizes, colors, and corner radii. These settings give you precise control over typography, colors, layout and spacing, borders, shadows, and animation across more than 23 component types. + +Build on your basic styling palette with targeted changes to the visual details that matter to your application, or define your styling from the ground up using supported tokens. Separate light and dark configurations let you adapt colors, contrast, and visual details to suit each mode. + +:::image type="content" source="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/overview-advanced-styling.png" alt-text="Screenshot of a Contoso Airways sign-in page with customized purple colors, typography, and rounded controls." lightbox="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/overview-advanced-styling.png"::: + +Learn how to [customize your authentication experience with advanced styling](styling.md#configure-advanced-styling). + + + +## Custom HTML and JavaScript + +Your experience. Microsoft's authentication. Custom HTML gives your brand more room around the Microsoft-rendered sign-in controls. Shape the page with your own layout, imagery, navigation, and content. Place onboarding guidance beside the sign-in box, make support easy to find, or add branded footers with privacy notices and compliance information relevant to your application. + +Pair custom HTML with advanced styling to carry your page's design into the sign-in box using supported design tokens. + +Custom JavaScript enables dynamic content that adapts to your users' current step, from relevant instructions during verification to progress indication throughout the flow, using documented events for screen changes and action processing. The page doesn't just look branded. It helps your users move forward. + +:::image type="content" source="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/overview-custom-html.png" alt-text="Screenshot of a Contoso Journeys custom HTML page with branded navigation, contextual guidance, and a progress indicator around the sign-in box." lightbox="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/overview-custom-html.png"::: + +Learn how to [build branded, interactive authentication pages with custom HTML and JavaScript](custom-html-javascript.md). + + + +## Availability and scope + +The modern authentication experience, styling, and custom HTML and JavaScript are scheduled to become available in preview on **December 7, 2026**, for Microsoft Entra External ID tenants with the preview enabled. Branding themes let you scope the new customizations to specific applications. + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> Enabling the preview applies the modern authentication experience to all authentication flows in your tenant, even when customizations are scoped to specific applications. Flows listed under "Not supported or limited" might not work or might continue to use the current experience. Review these limitations before enabling the preview. +> +> Features in preview might change or not work as expected. Some edge-case screens might still appear in the current experience. + +### Supported in the preview + +- Modern authentication experience with light and dark modes. +- Basic styling with generated color palettes +- Advanced styling using design tokens. +- Custom HTML with external JavaScript. A custom domain is required. + +### Not supported or limited + +- Federation flows aren't supported. +- The end-user UX for administrators is partially supported. Unsupported administrator flows and some edge-case screens use the current experience. +- Custom CSS isn't honored. +- Branding theme language settings in the Microsoft Entra admin center don't support the new properties. You can still configure these properties per locale through the API. +- New properties aren't available through tenant-wide company branding and don't apply to custom interfaces built with native authentication. + +For theme creation and assignment, see [Customize branding themes](~/fundamentals/how-to-customize-branding-themes-apps.md). + +The preview also introduces a redesigned branding themes experience in the Microsoft Entra admin center, with a new, modern layout for configuring your customizations. + +## Get started with customization + +After enabling the preview, start with a test application and choose the customization options that fit your brand and your users' needs. Combine built-in branding, styling, and custom HTML and JavaScript as needed. + +1. Identify the branding, guidance, and languages your application's audience needs. +1. [Create or select a branding theme and assign it to your test application](~/fundamentals/how-to-customize-branding-themes-apps.md). +3. Configure the [modern authentication experience](modern-authentication-experience.md) with your text, assets, and theme mode. +4. Add [Basic or Advanced styling](styling.md) to customize supported visual properties. Use [custom HTML and JavaScript](custom-html-javascript.md#set-up-a-custom-page) to create your own page layout and add content that adapts to each step of your users' journey. +1. Test the complete supported journey across languages, light and dark modes, and mobile layouts, including error and recovery paths. If you use externally hosted resources, confirm that your users can still complete authentication when those resources are unavailable. + +## Programmatic customization + +Microsoft Graph provides the [branding theme](/graph/api/resources/organizationalbrandingtheme?view=graph-rest-beta&preserve-view=true) and [theme localization](/graph/api/resources/organizationalbrandingthemelocalization?view=graph-rest-beta&preserve-view=true) references for automated or programmatic configuration. + + + +## Next steps + +- [Modern authentication experience](modern-authentication-experience.md). +- [Basic and Advanced styling](styling.md). +- [Custom HTML and JavaScript](custom-html-javascript.md).

newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/external-id/modern-authentication-experience.md b/docs/external-id/modern-authentication-experience.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..d9bc361a06d --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/external-id/modern-authentication-experience.md @@ -0,0 +1,132 @@ +--- +title: Microsoft Entra External ID Sign-In Experience +titleSuffix: "" +description: Give your users a recognizable, clearly guided sign-in experience with modern controls, light and dark modes, and new branding and content properties. +ms.topic: concept-article +ms.date: 11/16/2026 +ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1026 +ai-usage: ai-generated +#customer intent: As an administrator, I want to understand the modern authentication experience so that I can personalize branding and guidance for my users. +--- + +# Microsoft Entra External ID modern authentication experience overview + +[!INCLUDE [applies-to-external-only](includes/applies-to-external-only.md)] + +Help your users recognize your brand and navigate the authentication experience with confidence. Built on Microsoft's Fluent design language, Microsoft Entra External ID's refreshed experience brings clearer guidance, familiar controls, and light and dark modes to supported journeys. + +Make this polished foundation yours with built-in branding and content properties. Add your logos, tailor sign-in guidance, and make support easy to find through the supported branding settings. + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> The modern authentication experience (Fluent) is scheduled to become available in preview on December 7, 2026. This information relates to a prerelease product that may be substantially modified before it's released. Microsoft makes no warranties, expressed or implied, with respect to the information provided here. +> +> For an overview of the customization options, see [Customize your authentication experience](customization-overview.md). + +## What's improved for your users + +The modern experience is more than a visual refresh. Thoughtful interactions help your users understand what's being requested and what to do next. Examples include: + +- **Floating labels** keep field prompts visible as your users enter information. +- **Show and hide password controls** let your users check what they've entered and hide it again when they're done. +- **Auto-progressing code-entry boxes** show the code length and make individual digits easier to check. +- **Easier switching between sign-in methods** gives your users a consistent way to choose another available credential throughout the flow. +- **Clearer consent explanations** help your users understand what they're agreeing to. +- **Plain-language error guidance** helps them find a way forward when something goes wrong. +- **Familiar controls and consistent visual cues** make the next action easier to recognize without relearning each screen. +- **Responsive layouts** keep the experience usable as your users move between desktop and mobile devices. +- **Upfront guidance and support options** keep essentials visible, with more detail just an expansion away. + +The controls and layouts are part of the Microsoft-provided experience, not components you need to build. You can add your own guidance and support text through [branding themes](~/fundamentals/how-to-customize-branding-themes-apps.md). Branding settings don't enable new authentication methods, add sign-up steps, or change consent requirements. + +:::row::: + :::column span=""::: + :::image type="content" source="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/modern-code-entry-light.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Contoso code-entry experience in light mode with individual boxes for verification-code digits." lightbox="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/modern-code-entry-light.png"::: + :::column-end::: + :::column span=""::: + :::image type="content" source="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/modern-code-entry-dark.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Contoso code-entry experience in dark mode with individual boxes for verification-code digits." lightbox="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/modern-code-entry-dark.png"::: + :::column-end::: +:::row-end::: + + + +## Light and dark modes + +Use **Theme mode** to set the authentication experience to light or dark mode, or have it adapt to your users' device preferences. + +Branding themes support separate light and dark versions of the header image, background image, square logo, and banner logo. Each version is used in its corresponding mode. + +:::row::: + :::column span=""::: + :::image type="content" source="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/overview-modern-light.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Contoso sign-in experience in light mode with a branded background, logo, and guidance." lightbox="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/overview-modern-light.png"::: + :::column-end::: + :::column span=""::: + :::image type="content" source="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/overview-modern-dark.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Contoso sign-in experience in dark mode with a dark background and sign-in box." lightbox="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/overview-modern-dark.png"::: + :::column-end::: +:::row-end::: + +| Theme mode | Behavior | +|---|---| +| **Light only** | The page stays in light mode. | +| **Dark only** | The page stays in dark mode. | +| **Both (adaptive)** (default) | The page follows the user's device theme setting. | + +:::image type="content" source="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/ignite-layout-appearance.png" alt-text="Screenshot of layout and appearance settings showing alignment templates and theme modes." lightbox="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/ignite-layout-appearance.png"::: + +## New branding and content properties + +The following properties are added to [branding themes](~/fundamentals/how-to-customize-branding-themes-apps.md) in this preview. Existing branding properties, including light-mode images, page titles, descriptions, and username hints, remain available. + +:::image type="content" source="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/modern-branding-property-map.png" alt-text="Annotated screenshot identifying the header, favicon, logos, background, sign-in text, create-account link, guidance, and Help on a Contoso sign-in page." lightbox="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/modern-branding-property-map.png"::: + +### Dark mode assets + +| Property | Description | Image requirements | +|---|---|---| +| **Header image (dark mode)** | Image displayed in the page header in dark mode when the header is shown. | PNG or JPG, 245 x 36 px. Maximum file size: 10 KB. | +| **Background image (dark mode)** | Image displayed behind the sign-in box in dark mode. | PNG or JPG, 1920 x 1080 px. Maximum file size: 300 KB. | +| **Banner logo (dark mode)** | Logo displayed at the top of the sign-in box in dark mode. | PNG or JPG, 245 x 36 px. Maximum file size: 50 KB. | + +Dark-mode images are configured separately from existing light-mode images and have the same format, dimensions, and file size requirements as their light-mode counterparts. + +### Sign-in guidance and support + +| Property | Description and example use | Format and recommended length | +|---|---|---| +| **Display message box (short)** | Always-visible guidance below the sign-in box, such as which account to use. | Markdown; 150 characters or fewer recommended. | +| **Display message box (long)** | Additional guidance in an expandable section below the sign-in box, such as account-recovery instructions. | Markdown; 1,024 characters or fewer recommended. | +| **Support text** | Troubleshooting details, reached through Help or certain errors, such as a help desk link or phone number. | Markdown; 300 characters or fewer recommended. | + +:::image type="content" source="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/modern-expanded-guidance.png" alt-text="Annotated screenshot of short guidance and expanded long guidance below the sign-in controls." lightbox="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/modern-expanded-guidance.png"::: + +:::image type="content" source="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/modern-troubleshooting-support.png" alt-text="Annotated screenshot of the Help panel with support text and expanded troubleshooting details while long guidance is collapsed." lightbox="customers/media/modern-ux-customization/modern-troubleshooting-support.png"::: + +### Create-account link + +The **Create account** settings control the visibility, display text, and destination of the account-creation link shown during sign-in. + +| Setting | Description | +|---|---| +| **Show create account link** | Specifies whether the link is displayed. | +| **Create account display text** | Text displayed for the link. | +| **Create account link** | URL opened when the user selects the link. | + +When the link is enabled, configure its display text and destination URL. These settings don't change the application's sign-up user-flow configuration. + + + +## Preview availability and configuration + +The modern authentication experience and new properties are scheduled to become available in preview on **December 7, 2026**, for external tenants with the preview enabled. Customizations are configured through branding themes assigned to specific applications. The new properties aren't available through tenant-wide company branding and don't apply to custom interfaces built with native authentication. + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> Enabling the preview applies the modern authentication experience to all authentication flows in your tenant, even when customizations are scoped to specific applications. Federation flows aren't supported at this time, and end-user experiences for administrators are partially supported. Unsupported flows might not work or might continue to use the current experience. Review [Availability and scope](customization-overview.md#availability-and-scope) before enabling the preview. + +The preview also introduces a redesigned branding themes experience in the Microsoft Entra admin center. For theme creation and assignment, see [Customize branding themes](~/fundamentals/how-to-customize-branding-themes-apps.md). + +Language-specific text and assets are configured per locale. Branding theme language settings in the admin center don't support the new properties. During the preview, use the [Microsoft Graph theme localization API](/graph/api/resources/organizationalbrandingthemelocalization?view=graph-rest-beta&preserve-view=true) to configure these properties per locale. For general language behavior, see [Customize the language of the authentication experience](customers/how-to-customize-languages-customers.md). + +## Related content + +- [Authentication customization overview](customization-overview.md). +- [Basic and Advanced styling](styling.md). +- [Custom HTML and JavaScript](custom-html-javascript.md).

+ +### Ramp behavior and configuration + +Ramp changes affect only parts of built-in controls that use these tokens. An input's branded underline and keyboard focus outline are separate, as are a checkbox's indicator and label. + +The ramp doesn't change neutral body or title text, page or sign-in-card backgrounds, logos, images, error or success colors, or normal secondary- and subtle-button backgrounds. Customize these separately with supported Advanced styling properties. Disabled controls and high-contrast mode can use neutral or system colors. + +Settings in `themeColorOverrides`, `colorStyles`, or component-specific categories can override ramp colors. If a color doesn't change, check for overrides and whether that part of the page uses a brand token. + +The admin center generates a ramp from your brand color. + +### `typographyStyles` + +The shared type scale: font sizes, line heights, font-family stacks, and numeric font weights. A font-family value selects a font but does not download it. + +Reference: [Fluent typography](https://storybooks.fluentui.dev/react/?path=/docs/theme-typography--docs) and [font tokens](https://storybooks.fluentui.dev/react/?path=/docs/theme-fonts--docs). + +

+ +### `spacingStyles` + +Horizontal and vertical spacing scales. Names identify direction and size, from `None` through `XXXL`; a shared spacing change can affect several components. + +Reference: [Fluent spacing tokens](https://storybooks.fluentui.dev/react/?path=/docs/theme-spacing--docs). + +
+ +
+Properties and example values + +```json +{ + "spacingStyles": { + "spacingHorizontalNone": "0", + "spacingHorizontalXXS": "2px", + "spacingHorizontalXS": "4px", + "spacingHorizontalSNudge": "6px", + "spacingHorizontalS": "8px", + "spacingHorizontalMNudge": "10px", + "spacingHorizontalM": "12px", + "spacingHorizontalL": "16px", + "spacingHorizontalXL": "20px", + "spacingHorizontalXXL": "24px", + "spacingHorizontalXXXL": "32px", + "spacingVerticalNone": "0", + "spacingVerticalXXS": "2px", + "spacingVerticalXS": "4px", + "spacingVerticalSNudge": "6px", + "spacingVerticalS": "8px", + "spacingVerticalMNudge": "10px", + "spacingVerticalM": "12px", + "spacingVerticalL": "16px", + "spacingVerticalXL": "20px", + "spacingVerticalXXL": "24px", + "spacingVerticalXXXL": "32px" + } +} +``` + +
+ +### `borderStyles` + +Shared corner-radius and stroke-width scales. Use a component-specific category when the change should apply to only one type of control. + +Reference: [Fluent border radii](https://storybooks.fluentui.dev/react/?path=/docs/theme-border-radii--docs) and [stroke widths](https://storybooks.fluentui.dev/react/?path=/docs/theme-stroke-widths--docs). + +
+ +
+Properties and example values + +```json +{ + "borderStyles": { + "borderRadiusNone": "0", + "borderRadiusSmall": "2px", + "borderRadiusMedium": "4px", + "borderRadiusLarge": "6px", + "borderRadiusXLarge": "8px", + "borderRadiusCircular": "10000px", + "strokeWidthThin": "1px", + "strokeWidthThick": "2px", + "strokeWidthThicker": "3px", + "strokeWidthThickest": "4px" + } +} +``` + +
+ +### `shadowStyles` + +Standard and brand-colored elevation shadows. The numeric suffix identifies the Fluent elevation level. + +Reference: [Fluent shadow tokens](https://storybooks.fluentui.dev/react/?path=/docs/theme-shadows--docs). + +

+ +### `animationStyles` + +Durations and easing curves for supported transitions. Duration values use time units; curve values describe the transition timing function. + +
+ +
+Properties and example values + +```json +{ + "animationStyles": { + "durationUltraFast": "50ms", + "durationFaster": "100ms", + "durationFast": "150ms", + "durationNormal": "200ms", + "durationGentle": "250ms", + "durationSlow": "300ms", + "durationSlower": "400ms", + "durationUltraSlow": "500ms", + "curveAccelerateMax": "cubic-bezier(0.9,0.1,1,0.2)", + "curveAccelerateMid": "cubic-bezier(1,0,1,1)", + "curveAccelerateMin": "cubic-bezier(0.8,0,0.78,1)", + "curveDecelerateMax": "cubic-bezier(0.1,0.9,0.2,1)", + "curveDecelerateMid": "cubic-bezier(0,0,0,1)", + "curveDecelerateMin": "cubic-bezier(0.33,0,0.1,1)", + "curveEasyEaseMax": "cubic-bezier(0.8,0,0.2,1)", + "curveEasyEase": "cubic-bezier(0.33,0,0.67,1)", + "curveLinear": "cubic-bezier(0,0,1,1)" + } +} +``` + +
+ +## Appendix 3: Component-specific styling reference + +These categories configure custom fonts or target a supported page area or control. Each description remains visible; expand the category's example to view its properties and value formats. + +### `fontFaceStyles` + +An array of custom font declarations. `fontFamily` names the font, `srcUrl` identifies its HTTPS resource, and the remaining properties describe its weight, style, stretch, and loading strategy. Use a supported custom-domain surface and select the registered family in `typographyStyles`. + +
+ +
+Properties and example values + +```json +{ + "fontFaceStyles": [ + { + "fontFamily": "CustomBrandFont", + "srcUrl": "https://cdn.example.com/fonts/custom-brand-font.woff2", + "fontWeight": "100 900", + "fontStyle": "normal", + "fontStretch": "normal", + "fontDisplay": "swap" + } + ] +} +``` + +
+ +### `backgroundStyles` + +Background-layer settings. `opacity` uses a number from `0` through `1`; `fillColor` supplies a fill color. + +
+ +
+Properties and example values + +```json +{ + "backgroundStyles": { + "opacity": 1, + "fillColor": "#ffffff" + } +} +``` + +
+ +### `buttonContainerStyles` + +Button-group layout. `flexDirection` sets the arrangement direction, `justifyContent` and `alignItems` set axis alignment, `flexWrap` controls wrapping, and the gap properties set spacing. + +
+ +
+Properties and example values + +```json +{ + "buttonContainerStyles": { + "flexDirection": "column", + "justifyContent": "flex-start", + "alignItems": "stretch", + "columnGap": "12px", + "rowGap": "12px", + "flexWrap": "nowrap" + } +} +``` + +
+ +### `footerStyles` + +Footer appearance and spacing properties. Color values describe the background and foreground; horizontal and vertical padding apply to the corresponding pair of sides. + +
+ +
+Properties and example values + +```json +{ + "footerStyles": { + "textAlign": "center", + "textDecoration": "none", + "maxWidth": "100%", + "opacity": 1, + "borderStyle": "none", + "backgroundColor": "#ffffff", + "color": "#424242", + "paddingVertical": "12px", + "paddingHorizontal": "12px" + } +} +``` + +
+ +### `headerStyles` + +Header dimensions, appearance, logo settings, and padding. Use size values with units where appropriate, and a number from `0` through `1` for opacity. + +
+ +
+Properties and example values + +```json +{ + "headerStyles": { + "borderRadius": "0", + "height": "48px", + "maxWidth": "100%", + "minWidth": "0", + "opacity": 1, + "logoPosition": "left", + "logoSize": "24px", + "logoPadding": "0", + "backgroundColor": "transparent", + "paddingHorizontal": "16px", + "paddingVertical": "12px", + "color": "#242424" + } +} +``` + +
+ +### `inputStyles` + +Input and floating-label appearance, spacing, validation-text size, and transition settings. Placeholder colors, label margins, and transition properties can be configured independently. + +
+ +
+Properties and example values + +```json +{ + "inputStyles": { + "borderRadius": "4px", + "textAlign": "left", + "textDecoration": "none", + "maxWidth": "100%", + "minWidth": "0", + "borderStyle": "solid", + "opacity": 1, + "lineHeight": "22px", + "floatingPlaceholderColor": "#707070", + "floatingPlaceholderBackgroundColor": "#ffffff", + "disabledPlaceholderColor": "#bdbdbd", + "floatingLabelMarginTop": "8px", + "stackedInputMarginTop": "24px", + "validationErrorFontSize": "12px", + "transitionDuration": "200ms", + "transitionTimingFunction": "cubic-bezier(0,0,0,1)" + } +} +``` + +
+ +### `linkStyles` + +Link text-alignment and decoration properties. Use semantic color tokens when configuring link colors and their interaction states. + +
+ +
+Properties and example values + +```json +{ + "linkStyles": { + "textAlign": "left", + "textDecoration": "none" + } +} +``` + +
+ +### `paragraphStyles` + +Paragraph text-alignment, decoration, and maximum-width properties. + +
+ +
+Properties and example values + +```json +{ + "paragraphStyles": { + "textAlign": "left", + "textDecoration": "none", + "maxWidth": "100%" + } +} +``` + +
+ +### `primaryButtonStyles` + +Primary-button appearance, alignment, dimensions, and opacity. `borderSize` is the button border-width property; use `color` for text and `backgroundColor` for the surface. + +
+ +
+Properties and example values + +```json +{ + "primaryButtonStyles": { + "alignSelf": "auto", + "backgroundColor": "#0f6cbd", + "borderColor": "transparent", + "borderRadius": "4px", + "borderSize": "1px", + "borderStyle": "none", + "color": "#ffffff", + "textAlign": "center", + "textDecoration": "none", + "maxWidth": "100%", + "minWidth": "auto", + "opacity": 1, + "width": "auto" + } +} +``` + +
+ +### `secondaryButtonStyles` + +Secondary-button appearance, alignment, dimensions, and opacity. These values are separate from the primary-button category. + +
+ +
+Properties and example values + +```json +{ + "secondaryButtonStyles": { + "alignSelf": "auto", + "backgroundColor": "#ffffff", + "borderColor": "#d1d1d1", + "borderRadius": "4px", + "borderSize": "1px", + "borderStyle": "solid", + "color": "#242424", + "textAlign": "center", + "textDecoration": "none", + "maxWidth": "100%", + "minWidth": "auto", + "opacity": 1, + "width": "auto" + } +} +``` + +
+ +### `signInContainerStyles` + +Sign-in-container dimensions, logo settings, background, border treatment, radius, and padding. Check sizing changes at narrow widths and with longer localized content. + +
+ +
+Properties and example values + +```json +{ + "signInContainerStyles": { + "maxWidth": "440px", + "minWidth": "320px", + "maxHeight": "none", + "minHeight": "0", + "height": "auto", + "width": "440px", + "borderStyle": "none", + "opacity": 1, + "logoPosition": "center", + "logoSize": "36px", + "logoPadding": "0", + "backgroundColor": "#ffffff", + "borderRadius": "12px", + "padding": "40px" + } +} +``` + +
+ +### `slotSubHeadingStyles` + +Colors, border, radius, and padding for the supported custom HTML subheading content slot. Horizontal and vertical padding apply to both sides of the corresponding axis. + +
+ +
+Properties and example values + +```json +{ + "slotSubHeadingStyles": { + "backgroundColor": "transparent", + "color": "inherit", + "borderColor": "transparent", + "borderRadius": "0", + "borderStyle": "none", + "borderWidth": "0", + "paddingHorizontal": "0", + "paddingVertical": "0" + } +} +``` + +
+ +### `slotFormStyles` + +Colors, border, radius, and padding for the supported custom HTML form content slot. These settings style the slot rather than changing authentication-control behavior. + +
+ +
+Properties and example values + +```json +{ + "slotFormStyles": { + "backgroundColor": "transparent", + "color": "inherit", + "borderColor": "transparent", + "borderRadius": "0", + "borderStyle": "none", + "borderWidth": "0", + "paddingHorizontal": "0", + "paddingVertical": "0" + } +} +``` + +
+ +### `subtleButtonStyles` + +Subtle-button appearance, alignment, dimensions, and opacity. These values are separate from the primary- and secondary-button categories. + +
+ +
+Properties and example values + +```json +{ + "subtleButtonStyles": { + "alignSelf": "auto", + "backgroundColor": "transparent", + "borderColor": "transparent", + "borderRadius": "4px", + "borderSize": "1px", + "borderStyle": "none", + "color": "#424242", + "textAlign": "center", + "textDecoration": "none", + "maxWidth": "100%", + "minWidth": "auto", + "opacity": 1, + "width": "auto" + } +} +``` + +
+ +### `tileStyles` + +Primary and secondary tile text colors and sizes, primary-text weight, and the vertical gap between tile rows. + +
+ +
+Properties and example values + +```json +{ + "tileStyles": { + "mainTextColor": "#242424", + "mainTextFontSize": "14px", + "mainTextFontWeight": 600, + "secondaryTextColor": "#616161", + "secondaryTextFontSize": "12px", + "listRowGap": "12px" + } +} +``` + +
+ +### `titleStyles` + +Title text-alignment, decoration, maximum-width, and color properties. + +
+ +
+Properties and example values + +```json +{ + "titleStyles": { + "textAlign": "center", + "textDecoration": "none", + "maxWidth": "100%", + "color": "#242424" + } +} +``` + +
+ +## Related content + +- [Authentication customization overview](customization-overview.md). +- [Modern authentication experience](modern-authentication-experience.md). +- [Custom HTML and JavaScript](custom-html-javascript.md).

diff --git a/docs/identity-platform/concept-native-authentication-cors.md b/docs/identity-platform/concept-native-authentication-cors.md
new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..9a41615d2d8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/identity-platform/concept-native-authentication-cors.md
@@ -0,0 +1,93 @@
+---
+title: Embedded native authentication CORS concepts
+description: Understand CORS and proxy requirements for SPAs with Embedded native authentication and BYO UX websites, and why native Android and iOS calls don't need CORS.
+ms.topic: concept-article
+ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1030
+ms.date: 11/13/2026
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+#customer intent: As an application developer, I want to understand browser proxy requirements so that I can plan a native authentication integration that preserves the API contract.
+---
+
+# Embedded native authentication CORS concepts
+
+Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) controls whether browser code can read a response from another origin. Single-page applications (SPAs) with Embedded native authentication and Bring Your Own UX (BYO UX) websites need a proxy or edge CORS policy for cross-origin Native Authentication API calls.
+
+Android and iOS apps that call the API through native HTTP transports don't need CORS or a CORS proxy. They call the configured service authority directly. The requirements in this article apply to browser requests, not those native API calls.
+
+[!INCLUDE [applies-to-external-only](../external-id/includes/applies-to-external-only.md)]
+
+[!INCLUDE [applies-to-authentication-native](../external-id/includes/applies-to-authentication-native.md)]
+
+[!INCLUDE [native-authentication-public-preview](~/external-id/includes/native-authentication-public-preview.md)]
+
+## Why browser CORS applies
+
+A browser app and its tenant authentication endpoint typically have different origins. For cross-origin requests, the browser checks the server's CORS response headers before exposing the response to application code.
+
+An origin includes the scheme, host, and port. Sharing a parent domain doesn't make two origins the same.
+
+The API's JSON `POST` requests and password-update `PUT` requests require a preflight check. The browser sends `OPTIONS` with the requested method and headers before sending the authentication request. A header such as `client-request-id` also triggers preflight. Form-encoded OAuth requests are part of the same integration; their method and headers determine whether preflight is required.
+
+Browser code remains subject to CORS even when it runs in an embedded webview. CORS governs browser response access; caller authentication and abuse prevention require separate controls.
+
+## Why a proxy is required
+
+The native authentication service handles `OPTIONS` before parsing the API request or invoking its credential action. It returns an empty HTTP `200`. When the request includes `Origin`, the service advertises the action's accepted methods and echoes requested headers in `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`. No additional preflight feature flag is needed.
+
+The service doesn't supply `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` or `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`. Your proxy or edge supplies the explicit allowed-origin policy. It can forward the service's preflight response or answer a validated preflight locally. An HTML error page with an outer HTTP `200` isn't a successful preflight response.
+
+The proxy preserves the API operations, bodies, and transaction state. Forwarding or omitting the upstream `Origin` header is an implementation choice, not a universal requirement to remove it. Apply your choice consistently and check authorization, native operations, and token exchange together.
+
+## Service authority and proxy transport
+
+Current Embedded native authentication and BYO UX service API URLs use a tenant-verified custom authentication domain and the tenant GUID:
+
+```text
+https://<tenant-verified-custom-domain>/<tenant-GUID>
+```
+
+For example, the service authority might be `https://login.contoso.com/aaaabbbb-0000-cccc-1111-dddd2222eeee`. A local transport prefix might instead be `http://localhost:3001/api`. These values serve different purposes:
+
+| Value | Purpose |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Service authority** | Identifies the tenant's authentication service. Configure this custom domain and tenant GUID as the upstream authority and validate service-returned links against it. |
+| **Transport prefix** | Identifies the browser-facing proxy. It can replace the authority portion of a validated API request for transport, but doesn't change the service authority or transaction. |
+
+With that local prefix, a service path of `/<tenant-GUID>/api/v2.0/signin/start` maps to `/api/api/v2.0/signin/start`. The first `/api` is the proxy prefix; the second belongs to the service path. OAuth requests similarly map to `/api/oauth2/v2.0/authorize-challenge` or `/api/oauth2/v2.0/token`.
+
+Don't configure a `ciamlogin.com` address as the application's service API authority. Platform-managed origin routing behind a verified custom domain doesn't replace this requirement. See [Configure the API authority](how-to-native-authentication-configure-app.md#configure-the-api-authority).
+
+## Proxy contract
+
+Configure these settings in your reverse proxy. Forward API bodies and service status codes directly.
+
+| Setting | Configuration |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Upstream authority** | Set `https://<tenant-verified-custom-domain>/<tenant-GUID>` as the fixed destination. For a custom-domain edge, use the platform's documented service-origin configuration. |
+| **Routes** | Allow `/api/v2.0/*`, `/oauth2/v2.0/authorize-challenge`, and `/oauth2/v2.0/token` under the tenant-GUID prefix. |
+| **Methods and preflight** | Enable `POST`, password-update `PUT`, and `OPTIONS`. Handle preflight locally or forward it to the service. Approve only configured methods and headers; return `Access-Control-Allow-Methods: POST, PUT`. |
+| **Browser origin** | Set `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` to your app's exact origin, such as `https://app.contoso.com`. Return it only for matching `Origin` requests, including on error responses. |
+| **Allowed request headers** | Set `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` to `Content-Type, Accept, client-request-id`. For Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL) clients, also allow `x-client-sku`, `x-client-ver`, `x-client-os`, `x-client-cpu`, `x-client-current-telemetry`, and `x-client-last-telemetry`. |
+| **Exposed response headers** | Set `Access-Control-Expose-Headers` to `Retry-After, client-request-id, x-ms-request-id, x-ms-clitelem`. |
+| **Caching** | Disable proxy and CDN caching. Add `Cache-Control: no-store` to every response. |
+| **Redirects and failures** | Disable automatic upstream redirects and remove response `Location` headers. Return explicit proxy errors for connection failures and timeouts. |
+
+The [API reference](reference-native-authentication.md) defines the operation-specific methods, headers, request bodies, and responses.
+
+## Proxy implementations
+
+Choose an implementation that fits your hosting environment and meets the same contract:
+
+- [Local proxy](how-to-native-authentication-cors-local.md) for JavaScript sample development.
+- [Azure Functions proxy](how-to-native-authentication-cors-azure-functions.md) with an adapted HTTP-trigger handler.
+- [Azure Front Door proxy](how-to-native-authentication-cors-front-door.md) on the tenant's custom authentication domain.
+
+The JavaScript SDK's `customAuth.authApiProxyUrl` doesn't remap absolute HAL links. Use CORS policy at the custom-domain edge for those SDK requests. The local and Functions recipes instead show a custom-client transport that validates and maps service links.
+
+The local proxy binds to a loopback interface and isn't a shared hosting recipe. For a deployed proxy, also review capacity, cost, access controls, diagnostics retention, and recovery procedures for your environment.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Fetch Standard CORS protocol](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#http-cors-protocol).
+- [Embedded native authentication flow](concept-native-authentication-flow.md).
+- [The Native Authentication API reference](reference-native-authentication.md).

diff --git a/docs/identity-platform/concept-native-authentication-flow.md b/docs/identity-platform/concept-native-authentication-flow.md
new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..8f5a55a751d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/identity-platform/concept-native-authentication-flow.md
@@ -0,0 +1,120 @@
+---
+title: Native authentication flow concepts
+description: Understand authorization, continuation tokens, actions, method selection, and policy-driven interactions in the Native Authentication API.
+author: adamstoffel
+ms.author: adamstoffel
+ms.service: identity-platform
+ms.subservice: external
+ms.topic: concept-article
+ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1030
+ms.date: 11/13/2026
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+#customer intent: As an application developer, I want to understand the authentication flow so that my client handles policy changes without assuming a fixed endpoint sequence.
+---
+
+# Native authentication flow concepts
+
+[!INCLUDE [applies-to-external-only](../external-id/includes/applies-to-external-only.md)]
+
+[!INCLUDE [applies-to-authentication-native](../external-id/includes/applies-to-authentication-native.md)]
+
+The native authentication flow is a response-driven transaction. Microsoft Entra External ID returns the current state, required action, and allowed operations. Your application presents the interface and selects an allowed operation through user choice or application flow logic.
+
+## Authorization surrounds the journey
+
+[!INCLUDE [native-authentication-public-preview](../external-id/includes/native-authentication-public-preview.md)]
+
+The initial authorization challenge request contains the application ID, requested scopes, and optional claims. If authentication is required, its `401 InsufficientAuthorization` response contains a continuation token and journey links. This response is an invitation to interact, not a failed password check.
+
+Use the configured tenant-verified custom domain and tenant GUID for every service API call. This authority applies to authorization, native interactions, and token exchange. See [Operations and authority](reference-native-authentication.md#operations-and-authority).
+
+Sign-in, sign-up, and password reset all return to authorization when the service returns `state: continue`. Your application posts the latest continuation token to the returned `continue` link. It then exchanges the resulting authorization code at the token endpoint.
+
+After password verification, account creation, or a password update, the app handles any remaining policy requirements and resumes authorization before requesting tokens.
+
+These authorization boundaries describe Embedded native authentication. BYO UX uses the shared native interaction operations between its browser handoff and returned finish link. Its self-hosted page doesn't start or resume `/authorize-challenge`; the relying application completes the original browser authorization flow. See [Choose an authentication approach](../external-id/customers/concept-choose-authentication-approach.md#when-to-use-bring-your-own-ux).
+
+| Boundary | Request or response |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Start authorization** | Form-encoded `client_id`, `scope`, `response_type=code`, and optional `claims`. |
+| **Enter a journey** | Top-level `sign_in`, `sign_up`, or `reset_password` URL and `continuation_token` from the OAuth response. |
+| **Interact** | JSON requests and HAL responses with `continuationToken`, state, actions, and links. |
+| **Resume authorization** | Form-encoded `continuation_token`, sent only when the current response allows continuation. |
+| **Request tokens** | Form-encoded authorization-code exchange. |
+
+The following sequence illustrates the authorization boundary and response-driven interaction loop. Follow the current response rather than hard-coding the diagram's order.
+
+:::image type="complex" source="media/native-authentication-v2/native-authentication-sequence.svg" alt-text="Sequence diagram of native authentication from authorization through response-driven interactions to token exchange." lightbox="media/native-authentication-v2/native-authentication-sequence.svg":::
+   The user starts authentication in the client application. When interaction is required, the authorization challenge returns a continuation token and journey links.
+
+   The application follows an offered journey and handles each required action with the links and token from the latest response. Actions can repeat or change order. Some actions, such as polling, don't require user input.
+
+   At `state: continue`, the application resumes authorization through the returned link, receives an authorization code, and exchanges that code for tokens. Completing an earlier interaction doesn't issue tokens.
+:::image-end:::
+
+## The current response is the control model
+
+Each successful native authentication response replaces the previous interaction model. Tenant policies, the application's user flow, and transaction state can add, repeat, or reorder actions. The app selects operations from the latest response and organizes its screens around the returned requirements.
+
+| State or action | Meaning for the client |
+| --- | --- |
+| **`interactionRequired`** | Handle `action` through an allowed operation, collecting user input where needed. |
+| **`continue`** | Follow `_links.continue` to resume authorization. |
+| **`redirect`** | Stop the native transaction. This response can contain only `state`, without a continuation token or browser URL. A configured browser sign-in starts a new attempt. |
+| **`discover`** | Collect the user's sign-in identifier. |
+| **`disambiguate`** | Identifies account selection under `state: interactionRequired`. |
+| **`collectAttributes`** | Collect the requested sign-up attributes. |
+| **`challenge`** | Start the selected method's challenge. |
+| **`verify`** | Submit the requested password or one-time passcode. |
+| **`enroll`** | Select an advertised method and submit its enrollment details. |
+| **`activate`** | Submit a one-time passcode to activate the enrolled method. |
+| **`update`** | Submit a replacement password. |
+| **`poll`** | Check an asynchronous password update. |
+
+For example, sign-in can return a password method, then a verification action, then email or SMS methods for multifactor authentication (MFA). The app handles the additional factor before resuming authorization.
+
+During sign-up, submitting an email can send a passcode immediately and return `verify`. The app collects that passcode and uses the returned verification link.
+
+Completing an individual operation doesn't mean that the application has tokens. In the native journeys described here, `continue` permits authorization to resume; the subsequent code exchange acquires tokens. The `completed` state indicates completion of that operation; it doesn't necessarily indicate a signed-in result or include another link.
+
+## Continuation tokens bind the next operation
+
+A continuation token represents the transaction at a particular stage. It is bound to the tenant, client, scenario, and current action. OAuth messages name it `continuation_token`; native authentication messages name it `continuationToken`.
+
+Keep only the latest token for the active transaction. Pair it with the links from that same response. Don't parse, alter, log, or persist it beyond the transaction, and don't use it for a different user or journey. Restart authorization after expiration rather than replaying an older token.
+
+The documented default validity is 10 minutes for an individual continuation token. A newer token isn't a guarantee of extending the whole journey. A continuation token and a one-time passcode have separate lifetimes; handle expiration according to the service response.
+
+Method IDs and returned URLs are opaque. The Native Authentication API examples use `/api/v2.0`. Follow the returned link; don't substitute a version or construct a URL from the method type. Resolve relative links against the configured authority origin and validate the destination before sending credentials.
+
+## Method discovery isn't method registration
+
+A method resource describes an available authentication method. Its `type`, masked `hint`, optional `isPreferred`, and links let your app present a choice and complete a challenge. `codeLength` describes the passcode input when returned.
+
+The `challenge` and `verify` links operate on available methods. Registering a method is a separate policy-driven interaction with its own action and request contract. Profile attribute collection has a separate contract too.
+
+Inline method registration uses `enroll` and `activate` actions. Phone enrollment advertises `type: phone` with `channels: ["sms"]`; email enrollment uses `type: email`. Activation submits the code in the root `otp` field to the `activate` link, not a credential's `verify` link. Registration can satisfy an MFA requirement, so another challenge isn't guaranteed. See [Authentication-method enrollment](reference-native-authentication.md#authentication-method-enrollment).
+
+## Policy and attribute interactions
+
+The user flow determines the email sign-up method and requested attributes. Email-with-password sign-up collects a password attribute. Email one-time passcode sign-up creates a passwordless account and doesn't collect a password.
+
+Attribute descriptors can contain labels, input types, `validation.validationRegEx`, and initial values. Use each exact `attributeId` as a submission key. Page-grouping metadata isn't required to render the form. Server validation remains authoritative. See [Native authentication user attributes](concept-native-authentication-user-attributes.md).
+
+MFA through system policies is supported. After sign-up or password reset, MFA and Conditional Access can require more interactions before authorization completes. Your app continues handling responses instead of maintaining a separate "already signed in" path that skips these requirements.
+
+## Errors and unsupported interactions
+
+OAuth and native authentication errors have different envelopes. Use stable codes for handling, not localized messages. Keep safe request identifiers and timestamps for diagnostics; don't record credential bodies or tokens.
+
+Ignore unknown optional properties and link relations. In contrast, an unknown required action, missing required field, or malformed response prevents safe continuation. Stop the native operation when a required interaction can't be processed.
+
+An OAuth error with `invalid_grant` and `web_redirect_required`, or a native response with `state: redirect`, signals that the native transaction can't continue. Neither response establishes a resumable browser handoff. Offer a separately configured browser sign-in or a clear failure. Keep the native continuation token within the native transaction.
+
+Federation, TOTP, passkeys, phone first-factor authentication, later-operation step-up, and profile or credential-management interoperability aren't supported through this native contract. See the [support matrices](../external-id/customers/concept-supported-features-customers.md#methods-and-journeys-by-approach).
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Native Authentication API reference](reference-native-authentication.md).
+- [Sign-in API reference](reference-native-authentication-sign-in.md).
+- [SDK sign-in quickstart](quickstart-native-authentication.md).

@@ -0,0 +1,100 @@
+---
+title: Native authentication user attribute concepts
+description: Understand attribute descriptors, sign-up forms, email verification order, and validation in the Native Authentication API.
+author: adamstoffel
+ms.author: adamstoffel
+ms.service: identity-platform
+ms.subservice: external
+ms.topic: concept-article
+ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1030
+ms.date: 11/13/2026
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+#customer intent: As an application developer, I want to understand user attribute collection so that I can render sign-up forms from service responses.
+---
+
+# Native authentication user attribute concepts
+
+[!INCLUDE [applies-to-external-only](../external-id/includes/applies-to-external-only.md)]
+
+[!INCLUDE [applies-to-authentication-native](../external-id/includes/applies-to-authentication-native.md)]
+
+Native authentication user attributes are values that your application collects during sign-up according to the application's user flow. The service describes the fields and validation requirements in its response. Your application controls the interface and collection logic, satisfies the returned requirements, and submits values by their returned identifiers.
+
+## Descriptors define the form
+
+[!INCLUDE [native-authentication-public-preview](../external-id/includes/native-authentication-public-preview.md)]
+
+A response with `action: collectAttributes` contains an `attributes` array and a `submitAttributes` link. Use the descriptors for the current interaction when deciding which values need user input.
+
+| Descriptor | Client use |
+| --- | --- |
+| **`attributeId`** | Use this exact value as the key in the submitted `attributes` object. |
+| **`inputType`** | Select the appropriate input control. Examples include `text`, `boolean`, `date`, and `checkboxMultiSelect`. |
+| **`required`** | Indicate that a value is required before the flow can complete. |
+| **`hidden`** | Determine whether the field is visible. |
+| **`canChange`** | Use the returned editability information when included. |
+| **`label`** | Present the returned label when included. |
+| **`initialValue`** | Use the prepopulated value when included. |
+| **`validation.validationRegEx`** | Help the customer correct invalid input without replacing service validation. |
+| **`options`** | Present the returned choices, using each option's `label` and `value`. |
+| **`confirmationInput`** | Apply the indicated confirmation behavior, such as `retype`, `reveal`, or `none`. |
+
+For example, an email-only form can be described as:
+
+```json
+{
+  "attributeId": "email",
+  "inputType": "text",
+  "hidden": false,
+  "required": true,
+  "canChange": true,
+  "label": "Email"
+}
+```
+
+The submission uses `"email"` as the key, not the display label `"Email"`. Render labels and validation messages as text, not executable HTML.
+
+## Pages group the requested attributes
+
+Your application can group fields into screens, but it doesn't need a `pages` member to render attribute collection. Field definitions and requirements come from the current `attributes` array. If page-grouping metadata is returned, treat it as additional presentation information, not a requirement for every response.
+
+If the service asks for another collection round, replace the prior form model with the new response. Sign-up can require multiple attribute-collection steps.
+
+## Collection order and email verification
+
+The service determines the collection and verification order. It can request email before other account details, collect several attributes together, or return to collection after verification. Submit only the attributes requested by the latest response, then follow the next response's action.
+
+All required attributes and proofs still need to be satisfied. When the response returns `verify` for email, the service has sent the passcode. Your app collects it and follows the returned verification link instead of sending an extra challenge.
+
+Email-with-password sign-up requests a password as an attribute. Email one-time passcode sign-up doesn't request a password. Collect the values requested for the selected user flow.
+
+## Values and validation
+
+Attribute submission contains the latest continuation token and an object of string values:
+
+```json
+{
+  "continuationToken": "******",
+  "attributes": {
+    "email": "user@contoso.com"
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Use the returned identifiers for built-in and custom fields, including any custom-attribute prefix. Optional attributes can be omitted. Missing required values can cause a validation error or another collection response. An input control type doesn't change the request's string-value contract; don't substitute a JSON Boolean or array based only on the control.
+
+Structured validation entries in `error.innerError.details` can identify affected `attributeIds` and include `code`, `message`, optional `suggestions`, and optional `recovery`. Associate a field error with the matching control. A corrected request still needs service validation; accepting input locally doesn't complete sign-up.
+
+## Profile values, methods, and tokens are different
+
+Profile attribute collection, authentication-method registration, and credential verification have separate contracts. For example, a phone number collected as a profile attribute still requires the applicable registration and verification operations before use as an MFA method.
+
+Submitted profile values aren't necessarily included in every token. Token requests use the scopes and claims established at the beginning of authorization. Avoid logging either submitted profile values or the issued tokens.
+
+After account creation, don't replay successful attribute submissions. Follow the latest action, including additional policy requirements, until authorization can continue.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Sign-up API reference](reference-native-authentication-sign-up.md).
+- [Native authentication flow](concept-native-authentication-flow.md).
+- [Configure an application](how-to-native-authentication-configure-app.md).
