newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/identity-platform/how-to-migrate-native-authentication-v1-v2.md b/docs/identity-platform/how-to-migrate-native-authentication-v1-v2.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..75fc523ca65 --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/identity-platform/how-to-migrate-native-authentication-v1-v2.md @@ -0,0 +1,249 @@ +--- +title: Migrate Embedded native authentication from V1 to V2 +description: Update a V1 integration for response-driven Embedded native authentication, including SDK interfaces, authorization, attributes, errors, and tokens. +ms.topic: how-to +ms.date: 11/13/2026 +ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1030 +ai-usage: ai-generated +#customer intent: As an application developer, I want to migrate my V1 integration so that my app follows the V2 authentication contract. +--- + +# Migrate embedded native authentication from V1 to V2 + +[!INCLUDE [applies-to-external-only](../external-id/includes/applies-to-external-only.md)] + +[!INCLUDE [applies-to-authentication-native](../external-id/includes/applies-to-authentication-native.md)] + +The Native Authentication API uses service-provided states, actions, and links to drive authentication journeys in Microsoft Entra External ID. This guide helps you migrate an existing V1 integration to that response-driven contract. It covers direct HTTP integration and SDK compatibility. The V1 API reference and linked SDK library references remain available for existing integrations. + +[!INCLUDE [native-authentication-public-preview](~/external-id/includes/native-authentication-public-preview.md)] + +## Prerequisites + +- An existing integration whose behavior you can compare with the [V1 API reference](reference-native-authentication-api-v1.md) and the [SDK library references](reference-native-authentication-api-v1.md#sdk-references) for your installed package. +- A test application and user flow configured according to [Configure an application for native authentication](how-to-native-authentication-configure-app.md). +- Test users for each authentication method and policy your app uses, including password reset and additional authentication where configured. +- The [V2 API contract](reference-native-authentication.md) and a way to inspect request methods, response states, and diagnostic IDs without recording credentials or tokens. + +## Identify the integration boundary + +Separate native HTTP calls from browser-delegated authentication before changing your app: + +1. Inventory calls to `/signup/v1.0/...`, `/resetpassword/v1.0/...`, `/oauth2/v2.0/initiate`, `/oauth2/v2.0/challenge`, `/oauth2/v2.0/introspect`, and V1 registration operations. Also inventory token requests using V1 grant types. +1. If the app uses an SDK, identify its package version and native interfaces. Verify support for each required V2 scenario in that library's documentation. Use the direct API where a V2 wrapper contract is unavailable. +1. Record the user flow, required attributes, API scopes, multifactor authentication (MFA) policies, registration requirements, browser fallback, and custom-header integrations that the app depends on. +1. Compare those dependencies with the shared [method and journey matrix](../external-id/customers/concept-supported-features-customers.md#methods-and-journeys-by-approach). Choose the supported integration for each required capability before migrating it. + +The `/oauth2/v2.0` segment identifies the OAuth endpoint used by both V1 and V2. Native V2 routes use `/api/v2.0`. Preserve returned paths, query strings, and opaque method identifiers rather than constructing the next operation. + +## Configure the service authority + +Use a tenant-verified custom domain for every current API call, including OAuth authorization start, native operations, authorization continuation, and token redemption. + +1. Set the service authority to `https:///`. +1. Configure that authority through the selected SDK's existing properties: + + - **Android:** Set `authorities[0].type` to `CIAM` and `authorities[0].authority_url` to the full service authority. + - **iOS and macOS:** Create `MSALCIAMAuthority` with the full URL and pass it to `MSALNativeAuthPublicClientApplicationConfig(clientId:authority:challengeTypes:)`. Don't use the `tenantSubdomain` convenience initializer, which constructs the default login host. + - **JavaScript:** Set `auth.authority` to the full service authority and `auth.knownAuthorities` to an array containing only the verified hostname. + +1. For SDK browser calls, set the required `customAuth.authApiProxyUrl` string to the same full custom-domain authority and configure CORS at that edge. This route doesn't use an application proxy's local transport prefix. Apply the [shared proxy contract](concept-native-authentication-cors.md#proxy-contract) for origins, preflight, SDK headers, and success and error responses. +1. For direct HTTP integration, resolve relative returned links against the service authority. Before sending credentials or continuation tokens, reject an unexpected hostname or tenant path. If your browser integration uses proxy transport mapping, apply it only after validating the service destination. + +CORS and proxy configuration apply to cross-origin browser calls from SPAs with Embedded native authentication and BYO UX websites. Android and iOS apps using native HTTP transports call the service authority directly and don't need a CORS proxy. + +## SDK compatibility + +Use the following Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL) versions or later for V1-to-V2 migration. See the linked SDK documentation for platform prerequisites and setup instructions. + +| Platform | SDK and minimum version | V2 interface | +| --- | --- | --- | +| **Android** | [MSAL for Android](https://github.com/AzureAD/microsoft-authentication-library-for-android) (`com.microsoft.identity.client:msal`) 8.7.0 or later. | `INativeAuthPublicClientApplication.signInV2`, `signUpV2`, and `resetPasswordV2`; unified `NativeAuthResultV2` results. | +| **iOS and macOS** | [MSAL for iOS and macOS](https://github.com/AzureAD/microsoft-authentication-library-for-objc) 2.18.1 or later. | `MSALNativeAuthPublicClientApplication` V2 entry points; scenario-specific parameter types, shared `MSALNativeAuthFlowDelegate`, and typed per-state delegates. | +| **JavaScript and TypeScript** | [MSAL for JavaScript](https://github.com/AzureAD/microsoft-authentication-library-for-js) (`@azure/msal-browser`) 5.29.0 or later. | `ICustomAuthPublicClientApplicationV2` with `signInV2`, `signUpV2`, and `resetPasswordV2`; use the matching V2 input, result, and state types. | + +Display only methods returned for the transaction. Use the shared [method and journey matrix](../external-id/customers/concept-supported-features-customers.md#methods-and-journeys-by-approach) for service capabilities, then check the selected SDK implementation: + +- **Android:** Email and SMS strong-auth registration, activation-code submission, and resend are implemented. Other enrollment channels aren't implemented. +- **Apple:** Registration, verification, and MFA resend have implementations. Use the returned states to identify the methods available for the current transaction. +- **JavaScript:** The V2 interfaces are experimental and aren't intended for production applications. The package implements method selection, MFA, registration, activation, and resend. Use each returned state to determine the next step. + +### Android migration + +Keep the existing client factory, but replace V1 parameter objects with `NativeAuthSignInParametersV2`, `NativeAuthSignUpParametersV2`, and `NativeAuthResetPasswordParametersV2`. Pass them to `signInV2`, `signUpV2`, and `resetPasswordV2`. Select V2 through these entry points, not a configuration flag. + +The [Android sample](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ms-identity-ciam-native-auth-android-sample/tree/adacfe21414333128300c722c9031d4663938d7c) demonstrates V1 and V2 journeys. + +- Dispatch `NativeAuthResultV2` after every entry point and continuation. Retain the returned `nextState`. +- Classify rejected attributes with `NativeAuthErrorV2.isInvalidAttributes()` and retry `AttributesRequiredStateV2.submitAttributes(...)` on the retained state. Attribute-validation errors don't expose a new state. +- Handle `NativeAuthResultV2.StrongAuthRegistrationRequired` with `nextState.selectAuthMethod(method, verificationContact)`. Handle `StrongAuthVerificationRequired` with `nextState.submitChallenge(code)` or `nextState.resendChallenge()`. +- Handle `SignInAfterSignUpRequired` and `SignInAfterResetPasswordRequired` separately from `Complete`. Call `nextState.signIn()` when sign-in is wanted; only `Complete` represents token acquisition. +- For callback integrations, use `NativeAuthPublicClientApplication.NativeAuthV2Callback` and the V2 state's operation-specific callback. An SDK error can arrive through `onResult`; `onError` isn't the only error path. +- Keep V1 `challenge_types` and `capabilities` when V1 calls still use the client. V2 doesn't send these settings and doesn't use them to select methods or enable enrollment. + + + +### iOS and macOS migration + +Use `MSALNativeAuthSignInParametersV2`, `MSALNativeAuthSignUpParametersV2`, and `MSALNativeAuthResetPasswordParametersV2` with their respective V2 entry points. + +The [Apple sample](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ms-identity-ciam-native-auth-ios-sample/tree/85ef82afd59572ade876011bad516fd631761dd4) demonstrates V1 and V2 journeys. Follow the sample's setup instructions for its platform requirements. + +- Implement `MSALNativeAuthFlowDelegate` and each required per-state protocol. The callback handler needs to conform to the corresponding state protocol. +- Handle `onFlowCompleted(result:scenario:)` and `onFlowError(error:scenario:)`. Missing state-protocol implementation produces `isNotImplemented`. +- Retain separate scenario handlers and prevent concurrent requests. Callbacks run on the main actor; `scenario` isn't a transaction ID. +- Update continuation types and argument labels. For example, V2 code submission uses `submitCode(_:delegate:)`. +- Use `MSALNativeAuthMFAVerificationRequiredState.resendChallenge(delegate:)` for MFA resend. Registration uses `MSALNativeAuthStrongAuthRegistrationRequiredState.selectAuthMethod(_:verificationContact:delegate:)`; its verification state exposes `submitChallenge(_:delegate:)` and `resendChallenge(delegate:)`. +- Keep challenge types and capabilities needed by coexisting V1 calls. V2 ignores those settings. + +### JavaScript migration + +The factory remains `CustomAuthPublicClientApplication.create(customAuthConfig)` and returns `ICustomAuthPublicClientApplicationV2`. The [unified JavaScript sample](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ms-identity-ciam-native-javascript-samples/tree/49c4e250a1e6eb97e2b813e9fce6670c996a2808/typescript/native-auth/react-nextjs-sample) demonstrates the matching V2 interfaces. + +- Replace V1 entry points with `signInV2`, `signUpV2`, and `resetPasswordV2`, passing the intended scopes and claims. +- Check `result.isFailed()` before inspecting state. Then use `result.isState("stateName")` and retain `result.state`. +- Use matching result and state types, such as `SignInStartResultV2`, `PasswordRequiredStateV2`, and `CodeRequiredStateV2`. Don't cast V1 states to V2. +- Submit a password through `PasswordRequiredStateV2.submitPassword(password)`. Use `CodeRequiredStateV2.submitCode(code)` and `resendCode()` for primary verification codes. +- Use `AuthMethodSelectionRequiredStateV2.selectAuthMethod(method)` for method selection and process the returned state. For MFA, use `MFAVerificationRequiredStateV2.submitChallenge(code)` and `resendChallenge()`. +- Register a returned method through `AuthMethodRegistrationRequiredStateV2.selectAuthMethod(method, verificationContact)`. Activate it through `AuthMethodVerificationRequiredStateV2.submitChallenge(code)`, or request another activation code with `resendChallenge()`. +- When sign-up or password reset returns `signInContinuation`, call `result.state.signIn()` without arguments. The SDK retains the original authorization context; don't pass replacement scopes or claims to the continuation. + +Follow the [React quickstart](quickstart-native-authentication.md#get-the-sample) to set up the sample, configure the custom-domain edge, and select V2. The sample uses the SDK's default scopes without custom claims; supply any required scopes and claims when starting your own journey. + +The SDK leaves absolute HAL links unchanged. Links for the configured custom-domain authority reach the same edge without local remapping. Preserve opaque links and follow the [service authority and proxy transport guidance](concept-native-authentication-cors.md#service-authority-and-proxy-transport), rather than repairing links to another authority. + + + +### Plan the migration rollout + +Choose V1 or V2 in your application when a new journey starts. Keep that choice for all continuation operations and post-sign-up or post-reset sign-in. + +1. Keep the existing path available while validating the replacement journeys. +1. Compare safe error categories, completion, and user experience before switching new journeys. +1. To roll back, route new journeys to V1. Finish or explicitly abandon active V2 journeys; don't replay their credentials or operations through V1. + +MSAL doesn't automatically switch a failed V2 journey to V1. Keep the existing session and token cache when changing the version used to start new journeys. + +## Replace the request and response model + +Update your transport layer and orchestration together to implement the V2 request and response model. + +1. Add the authorization-challenge operation and V2 native JSON requests. +1. Separate OAuth form encoding from native JSON encoding. Use the latest continuation token with the correct property spelling for the endpoint. +1. Replace constructed next-operation URLs with the links in the latest response. Resolve relative links against the custom-domain service authority, validate the hostname and tenant path, and reject an unexpected destination before sending secrets. +1. Replace V1 challenge-type and capability branching with dispatch on the latest `state` and `action`. Select an available operation through application flow logic or user choice. Handle unknown optional fields and links without interrupting supported operations. + +| Integration point | V1 | V2 | +| --- | --- | --- | +| **Authorization start** | Start a journey directly, for example `/signup/v1.0/start` or `/oauth2/v2.0/initiate`. | `POST /{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/authorize-challenge` with form-encoded inputs. Use the [shared reference](reference-native-authentication.md) for the parameters supported by this request. | +| **Interaction required** | Journey-specific continuation and challenge responses. | Initial HTTP `401` with `InsufficientAuthorization`, `continuation_token`, and enabled `sign_in`, `sign_up`, or `reset_password` links is an interaction response, not necessarily a terminal failure. | +| **Native request encoding** | Form-encoded journey requests. | JSON for `/api/v2.0/...`; request the HAL representation with `Accept: application/hal+json`. OAuth endpoints remain form-encoded. | +| **Continuation field** | `continuation_token`. | `continuationToken` in native JSON; `continuation_token` at the OAuth authorization-challenge boundary. | +| **Next operation** | Endpoint-specific sequences using `challenge_type`, grant types, and suberrors. | `state`, `action`, `_links`, and returned metadata determine the next operation. | +| **Method selection** | V1 challenge declarations and introspection/registration operations. | `_embedded.methods` supplies opaque method IDs, types, hints, and allowed links. | +| **Credential submission** | Password or one-time passcode (OTP) values can be submitted to the V1 token endpoint; the OTP parameter is `oob`. | Submit `password` or `otp` to the advertised method's `verify` link; don't send credentials in the authorization-code exchange. | +| **Finish authentication** | V1 token grant depends on the flow, including `password`, `oob`, `mfa_oob`, or `continuation_token`. | Follow `continue` to resume authorization, obtain a code, then use `grant_type=authorization_code` at the token endpoint. | +| **Native errors** | Flat OAuth-style `error`, `suberror`, and diagnostic fields. | Native errors have an `error` object with `code`, `message`, diagnostic fields, and optional `innerError`; OAuth endpoint errors retain their OAuth shape. | + +For browser applications, review edge routes and permitted HTTP methods as well as encoding. V2 password update uses `PUT`; other V2 operations include `POST`. See [Native authentication CORS concepts](concept-native-authentication-cors.md) for the shared requirements. The [local proxy guidance](how-to-native-authentication-cors-local.md) covers custom HTTP clients, not the SDK quickstart's edge route. + +## Migrate each journey + +Use a response-processing loop across journeys. Your app can expose available actions or use application flow logic to select an allowed operation; the returned requirements determine what needs to be completed. + +1. Start authorization and follow an enabled journey link. +1. If a native response returns `state: redirect`, stop native processing. That response can omit `continuationToken`, `action`, and `_links`; it doesn't provide a browser handoff URL. +1. For `state: interactionRequired`, handle the returned action, collecting user input where needed. Use the available methods and attribute requirements when selecting operations and organizing the interface. +1. After each operation, replace the previous token and response with the latest values. Keep the token and allowed links together for the same transaction. +1. For `state: continue`, follow the authorization continuation rather than requesting tokens with a V1 grant. Handle other documented states according to their returned links. + +### Sign-in + +Follow the returned `sign_in` link and submit `username` with `continuationToken`. Method discovery replaces a hard-coded choice of the V1 challenge endpoint. + +- Select an advertised method and follow its `challenge` link. +- Submit the credential to its `verify` link. An OTP request uses `otp`, not V1's `oob`; password verification uses `password`. +- Use the returned `codeLength` and masked `hint` for OTP UI instead of hard-coding a code length or displaying an unmasked identifier. +- Process additional challenge/verification actions when policy requires another factor. A successful first-factor verification isn't proof that token issuance is next. + +See the [sign-in reference](reference-native-authentication-sign-in.md) for request and response details. + +### Sign-up and attributes + +Follow the returned `sign_up` link with `continuationToken`. The user flow selects the sign-up method; don't send a V1 `challenge_type` list to choose it. + +| V1 implementation | Migration change | +| --- | --- | +| Attributes are a JSON-formatted string in a form body. | Submit `attributes` as a JSON object with string values through the advertised `submitAttributes` link. | +| Attribute names are selected from configured programmable names. | Use the exact `attributeId` values and the requirements and input metadata returned by the service, including `required`, `hidden`, and `canChange` when present. | +| A password is submitted as a V1 request parameter. | For email-with-password sign-up, submit `password` as an attribute when requested. Email-OTP sign-up doesn't collect a password. | +| The app assumes a single attribute form followed by verification. | Handle repeated `collectAttributes` and `verify` actions. Submit only attributes requested by the current response, then use the next response to determine the next action. | +| The app explicitly starts every email challenge. | When attribute submission returns `action: verify`, the OTP has already been sent. Use the advertised `resend` link only when another code is needed. | + +Supply all required attributes before completion. Apply V2's descriptor and collection rules to optional values. See [User attributes](concept-native-authentication-user-attributes.md) and the [sign-up reference](reference-native-authentication-sign-up.md). + +### Password reset + +Follow the returned `reset_password` link, then use the advertised method operations: + +1. Submit `username` and `continuationToken` to start recovery. +1. Challenge an advertised verification method and submit the OTP to its `verify` link. +1. When the response requires password update, follow its `update` link with `PUT`, submitting `newPassword` and the latest `continuationToken`. +1. Follow `poll` with `POST` while the service requests polling. Wait for the current response's `pollInterval` before each request, as described in the password-reset reference. +1. On `state: continue`, resume authorization. Don't interpret the first update response as a completed reset or submit a V1 `continuation_token` token grant. + +The V2 flow replaces V1's `/resetpassword/v1.0/submit` and `/poll_completion` plus `status` handling. Use the [password-reset reference](reference-native-authentication-password-reset.md) for the V2 contract. + +Recovery can also start within sign-in by following a password method's `recover` link with only the current continuation token. Don't resubmit the username or password or start another authorization transaction. Recovery supports email and SMS one-time passcodes. + +### MFA and registration + +V1 uses `mfa_required` and `registration_required` capability declarations and token suberrors. V2 uses returned methods and actions for additional authentication. + +The direct API supports inline email and SMS registration. The [enrollment contract](reference-native-authentication.md#authentication-method-enrollment) defines `enroll` and `activate`. Phone registration uses `type: phone` with an advertised `sms` channel; an existing SMS verification method uses `type: sms`. Follow the operations advertised for the transaction, and apply the platform-specific SDK limits in [SDK compatibility](#sdk-compatibility). + +## Replace token acquisition and failure handling + +Complete authorization only after the service indicates that the native journey can continue: + +1. Follow `_links.continue` and submit the latest token as form-encoded `continuation_token`. Don't resend initial authorization parameters on this continuation. +1. Read the returned authorization `code`. +1. Exchange it at `/oauth2/v2.0/token` with `client_id`, `grant_type=authorization_code`, and `code`, following the request contract in the shared reference. The code is short-lived and single-use. +1. Use the resulting access token only for its intended resource. Token fields depend on the initial scopes; a refresh token requires `offline_access` on the initial authorization request. +1. Update error handling to distinguish initial `InsufficientAuthorization`, recoverable input errors, invalid/expired transactions, throttling, and browser-required errors. Use stable error codes rather than localized messages. + +Handle both native `state: redirect` and the separate OAuth `invalid_grant` / `web_redirect_required` signal. Also handle a required response the app can't interpret. Unknown optional fields alone aren't a reason to fall back. See [Web fallback](concept-native-authentication-web-fallback.md). + +Offer a separately configured browser sign-in when your application has a supported integration, or show a clear failure. A new browser sign-in restarts authentication; it doesn't continue native progress. + +## Verify the migrated integration + +Verify each supported journey against your test tenant before replacing the existing implementation: + +1. Prepare the test configuration and implement the V2 operations from the API references, or use the [SDK quickstart](quickstart-native-authentication.md) for the React Next.js sample. +1. Run the cases below for every method and policy the app supports. +1. Check that no migrated journey still submits V1 grant types or calls V1-only journey endpoints. +1. Review redacted diagnostics and the user-visible outcome. Don't record passwords, OTPs, continuation tokens, authorization codes, or security tokens in test output. + +| Case | Expected client behavior | +| --- | --- | +| **Initial interaction response** | HTTP `401 InsufficientAuthorization` opens an enabled journey instead of displaying an unconditional authentication failure. | +| **Invalid OTP or password** | No signed-in state or token-dependent operation is shown before verification succeeds. | +| **Resend** | Direct calls follow the latest `resend` link; SDK calls use the selected package's implemented continuation. Both use the newest transaction state. | +| **Required and optional attributes** | Required values are collected; repeated attribute actions and changed verification order don't break the flow. | +| **MFA required** | The app follows the returned method list and completes required factors instead of stopping after first-factor success. | +| **Asynchronous password update** | The app polls only as required and resumes authorization only after the service permits continuation. | +| **Expired or wrong-stage token** | The app reports the failure and restarts the applicable flow, rather than replaying an older continuation token. | +| **Unknown optional metadata** | The app continues with known required fields and links. | +| **Native redirect or browser-required error** | The app stops native processing even when the response has no continuation token or links, then offers only a separately configured browser integration. | +| **Unusable required response** | The app shows a clear failure or offers a supported browser sign-in without promising preservation of native progress. | +| **Throttling or ambiguous network failure** | The app respects retry guidance and doesn't automatically replay credential verification or password updates. | +| **Custom-domain routing** | OAuth start, native operations, authorization continuation, and token redemption use the verified custom domain and tenant GUID. A local proxy prefix remains transport configuration only. | +| **Unexpected link authority** | No credential or continuation token is sent to a different hostname or tenant path. | +| **API access and sign-out** | The intended resource accepts the correctly scoped access token; app-managed credentials and account UI are cleared on sign-out. Native logout doesn't terminate other application or browser sessions. | + +## Related content + +- [The Native Authentication API reference](reference-native-authentication.md). +- [Native Authentication API V1 reference](reference-native-authentication-api-v1.md). +- [SDK library references for existing V1 integrations](reference-native-authentication-api-v1.md#sdk-references).

englishSummary.headline: Migration guidance for Embedded native authentication V1 to V2
englishSummary.summary: A new guide explains migrating existing V1 integrations to the response-driven V2 contract, including SDK compatibility, service authority, API routes, authorization, attributes, errors, and tokens.
englishSummary.adminImpact: Review any Embedded native authentication integrations and coordinate with application owners on SDK support, verified custom domains, API routing, and browser CORS or proxy settings.

This guide prepares a public client application for Embedded native authentication through direct API calls or an SDK. + +[!INCLUDE [native-authentication-public-preview](~/external-id/includes/native-authentication-public-preview.md)] + +## Prerequisites + +- An [external tenant](../external-id/customers/how-to-create-external-tenant-portal.md). +- An account authorized to create or manage the application registration. +- Access to create or select the user flow and associate the application with it. Coordinate policy changes and consent with the appropriate tenant administrator. +- A [tenant-verified custom URL domain](../external-id/customers/how-to-custom-url-domain.md) configured for the authentication service. + +An application owner can manage the registration's authentication settings. For delegated access, use [application-scoped permissions](~/identity/role-based-access-control/delegate-app-roles.md) rather than assigning a tenant-wide administrator role solely for this task. + +## Register the application + +Create the registration in the external tenant that owns the customer accounts. + +1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center and switch to your external tenant. +1. Browse to **Entra ID** > **App registrations** > **New registration**. +1. Enter an application **Name** and select the single-tenant supported account type for your external tenant. +1. Select **Register**. +1. On **Overview**, record the **Application (client) ID** and **Directory (tenant) ID**. +1. Record the tenant subdomain if your selected SDK requires it. Configure service API URLs with your tenant-verified custom domain as described in [Configure the API authority](#configure-the-api-authority). + +For registration details, see [Register an application](quickstart-register-app.md). The client ID identifies this public client; it isn't a secret. Don't create or embed a client secret for these direct API requests. + +## Configure the API authority + +Use your tenant-verified custom domain for all service API calls in the current native authentication integration. The authority has the form `https://{custom_domain}/{tenant}`, where `custom_domain` is the verified authentication domain, such as `login.contoso.com`, and `tenant` is the Directory (tenant) ID, a GUID. + +1. [Verify and configure the custom URL domain](../external-id/customers/how-to-custom-url-domain.md) in the external tenant. +1. Configure the application or SDK to use that domain for authorization challenges, native interaction operations, authorization continuation, and token exchange. +1. Validate returned links against the configured authority. Keep their paths, versions, and query parameters unchanged. + +For SPAs with Embedded native authentication and BYO UX websites, configure a cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) proxy or edge policy for cross-origin browser API calls. A proxy address is a transport setting, not a replacement service authority. Its upstream calls still use the tenant-verified custom domain and tenant GUID. See the [provider-neutral proxy requirements](concept-native-authentication-cors.md#proxy-contract). + +Android and iOS apps using native HTTP transports call the service authority directly. They don't need CORS configuration or a CORS proxy. + +## Enable public client and native authentication flows + +The API requires native authentication to be enabled on this application. + +1. In the app registration, under **Manage**, select **Authentication**. +1. On **Redirect URI configuration**, set **Enable the following mobile and desktop flows** to **Yes**. +1. Set **Enable native authentication** to **Yes**. +1. Select **Save**. + +These application settings enable the integration. The app then uses returned methods, actions, and links to select allowed operations through user choice or application flow logic. + +Configure redirect URIs separately for any platform SDK or browser-delegated integration you use. Browser sign-in needs its registered callback and the platform's URL-scheme or manifest configuration. Direct native authorization-code redemption doesn't establish a browser session and isn't a reason to require a browser redirect URI on every direct HTTP client. + +See [Redirect URI configuration](reply-url.md) for browser and platform registration requirements. + + + +## Choose an integration + +Choose direct API calls or Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL) entry points for your platform. For direct calls, native routes use `/api/v2.0` and OAuth routes use `/oauth2/v2.0`; follow the [API reference](reference-native-authentication.md). + +Use the [SDK compatibility guidance](how-to-migrate-native-authentication-v1-v2.md#sdk-compatibility) for the documented package versions, entry points, and enrollment support. Installing a new package doesn't migrate V1 calls. Keep V1 and V2 continuation states separate. + +For direct inline email and SMS method registration, use the [enrollment contract](reference-native-authentication.md#authentication-method-enrollment). + +## Create and associate a user flow + +The associated user flow determines the email sign-up/sign-in method and requested attributes. Tenant and user-flow policies apply to Microsoft-hosted authentication, Embedded native authentication, and Bring Your Own UX (BYO UX). Use the [shared method and journey matrix](../external-id/customers/concept-supported-features-customers.md#methods-and-journeys-by-approach) to check which interactions each approach supports. + +1. Browse to **Entra ID** > **External Identities** > **User flows**. +1. Select **New user flow**, or open the existing user flow you intend to use. +1. For a new flow, enter a **Name**. Under **Identity providers**, select **Email Accounts** and choose **Email with password** or **Email one-time passcode**. +1. Under **User attributes**, choose the attributes your application needs to collect. For a first integration, keep the required profile fields to the minimum your application needs. +1. Select **Create** for the new flow. +1. Open the flow. Under **Use**, select **Applications** > **Add application**. +1. Select the app registration, then choose **Select**. + +An application has one user flow; a user flow can serve multiple applications. For an existing flow, verify the selected identity provider and attributes before changing settings used by other applications. + +If you select email one-time passcode, enable it at the tenant level as described in [Create a user flow](../external-id/customers/how-to-user-flow-sign-up-sign-in-customers.md). The sign-up API doesn't have a parameter that overrides the user flow's method selection. + +## Configure scopes and consent + +Establish permissions before starting authorization. + +1. Identify the target resource and delegated scopes your application needs. The authorization request's `scope` parameter establishes the requested access. +1. If the app calls a protected API, configure its delegated permission on the client registration and arrange consent from an administrator authorized for that permission. +1. In **API permissions**, inspect the requested permissions and consent status. Don't add broad Microsoft Graph permissions just to enable native authentication. +1. Request the selected scopes in the initial authorization challenge. Add `offline_access` only if your app needs a refresh token. + +The tenant's permissions and consent requirements apply to the target resource. See [Add permissions to access your web API](quickstart-configure-app-access-web-apis.md). + +## Prepare MFA and password reset + +Configure multifactor authentication (MFA) through the tenant's authentication-method and Conditional Access policies. The service enforces these requirements; the client handles the returned authentication steps. + +1. If your application uses password accounts, [enable self-service password reset](../external-id/customers/how-to-enable-password-reset-customers.md) for the intended customers and recovery methods. +1. Configure the [MFA requirements](../external-id/customers/how-to-multifactor-authentication-customers.md) for the application and customers. +1. Prepare a customer account with the methods needed by the policy. Verify its recovery methods before testing password reset. +1. Test a flow with additional authentication required. Continue processing returned actions after sign-up or password reset rather than treating either operation as final authorization. + +Inline method registration has a separate contract from profile attribute collection. The [flow concept](concept-native-authentication-flow.md#method-discovery-isnt-method-registration) links to the enrollment and activation contract. + +## Verify the configuration + +Use the request and response contracts in the [API reference](reference-native-authentication.md) for a direct integration, or run the [SDK quickstart](quickstart-native-authentication.md) with the React Next.js sample. Validate the selected integration with your application and user flow. + +1. Start authorization. An unauthenticated request normally returns `401 InsufficientAuthorization` with a continuation token and enabled journey links. +1. Confirm that the intended journey link is present. If it isn't, check the app's user-flow association and policy configuration instead of constructing a missing URL. +1. Complete an advertised method, resume authorization, and exchange the code. + +| Symptom | Configuration to check | +| --- | --- | +| **`invalid_client`** | Tenant/client ID match and native authentication enabled for the selected app. | +| **`invalid_scope`** | Scope spelling, resource registration, configured permissions, and consent. | +| **No expected journey link** | User-flow association and enabled authentication/recovery options. | +| **Browser preflight failure** | The proxy's allowed browser origin, `OPTIONS` handling, headers, JSON `POST`, and `PUT`. The service answers `OPTIONS` but doesn't grant browser-origin access. | +| **Browser callback failure** | The redirect URI and platform configuration for that browser integration, separately from direct native code redemption. | + +## Next step + +> [!div class="nextstepaction"] +> [Review the Native Authentication API contract](reference-native-authentication.md)

newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/identity-platform/how-to-native-authentication-cors-azure-functions.md b/docs/identity-platform/how-to-native-authentication-cors-azure-functions.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..049bb6002e4 --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/identity-platform/how-to-native-authentication-cors-azure-functions.md @@ -0,0 +1,312 @@ +--- +title: Configure an Azure Functions CORS proxy +description: Adapt and deploy the Azure Functions CORS proxy sample for Embedded native authentication with a tenant-verified custom-domain authority. +ms.topic: how-to +ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1030 +ms.date: 11/13/2026 +ai-usage: ai-generated +#customer intent: As an application developer, I want an Azure Functions CORS proxy so that my browser application can call the Native Authentication API through a bounded transport. +--- + +# Configure an Azure Functions CORS proxy for embedded native authentication + +Use an Azure Functions HTTP trigger for Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) between your custom browser client and the Native Authentication API. Start with a configured app and tenant-verified custom domain. This guide adapts the sample's handler and configuration, then deploys its Flex Consumption infrastructure. + +CORS applies to browser API calls from single-page applications with Embedded native authentication and Bring Your Own UX (BYO UX) websites. Native Android and iOS HTTP clients don't need this CORS proxy. + + + +[!INCLUDE [applies-to-external-only](../external-id/includes/applies-to-external-only.md)] + +[!INCLUDE [applies-to-authentication-native](../external-id/includes/applies-to-authentication-native.md)] + +[!INCLUDE [native-authentication-public-preview](~/external-id/includes/native-authentication-public-preview.md)] + +## Prerequisites + +- An Azure subscription and permission to deploy subscription-scoped templates and create the resource group. The template also creates Azure role assignments, so the deployment identity needs `Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write` at the resource scopes. **Contributor** alone doesn't grant that action; use an appropriately scoped role-assignment operator rather than granting tenant-wide administration. +- Completion of [Configure an app for Embedded native authentication](how-to-native-authentication-configure-app.md). +- A working [tenant-verified custom authentication domain](~/external-id/customers/how-to-custom-url-domain.md), the tenant GUID, and the exact browser origin, such as `https://app.contoso.com`. +- Node.js 22, npm, Git, and [Azure Developer CLI](/azure/developer/azure-developer-cli/install-azd). +- An Azure location supported by both Flex Consumption and the sample's `location` parameter. + +The template creates a function app, Flex Consumption plan, storage, managed identity, virtual network, storage private endpoints, Application Insights, and Log Analytics. Review [Azure Functions pricing](https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/functions/) and the costs of those supporting resources. + +The managed identity uses **Storage Blob Data Owner** on the storage account and **Monitoring Metrics Publisher** on Application Insights. These grants don't authenticate callers of the anonymous HTTP trigger. + +## Get the sample + +Use the [sample revision](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ms-identity-extid-cors-proxy-function/tree/613e76012b61098e37d4bc51ae68c1d6a36954c3). Make the following changes in your own checkout, not in an already running deployment. + +1. Get the source: + + ```powershell + git clone https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ms-identity-extid-cors-proxy-function.git + Set-Location .\ms-identity-extid-cors-proxy-function + git checkout 613e76012b61098e37d4bc51ae68c1d6a36954c3 + ``` + +1. Initialize an Azure Developer CLI environment: + + ```powershell + azd init + ``` + +## Configure preflight and forwarding + +The pinned handler constructs a `ciamlogin.com` host and an `onmicrosoft.com` tenant path from `TENANT_SUBDOMAIN`. That isn't the current custom-domain/GUID authority contract. Keep the sample's HTTP trigger and Axios transport, but change the authority and forwarding policy. + +1. Replace `src\functions\httpProxyFunction.js` with the following handler. `SERVICE_AUTHORITY` and `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` are settings added by this guide, not settings supplied by the unchanged sample. + + ```javascript + const { app } = require("@azure/functions"); + const axios = require("axios"); + + const authority = new URL(process.env.SERVICE_AUTHORITY); + const allowedOrigin = process.env.CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN; + if (authority.protocol !== "https:" || authority.port || + authority.username || authority.password || authority.search || authority.hash || + /(^|\.)(ciamlogin\.com|onmicrosoft\.com|microsoftonline\.com)$/.test(authority.hostname) || + !/^\/[0-9a-f]{8}(-[0-9a-f]{4}){3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i.test(authority.pathname) || + new URL(allowedOrigin).origin !== allowedOrigin) { + throw new Error("Configure an HTTPS custom authority, tenant GUID, and exact browser origin."); + } + const allowedHeaders = [ + "content-type", "accept", "client-request-id", + "x-client-sku", "x-client-ver", "x-client-os", "x-client-cpu", + "x-client-current-telemetry", "x-client-last-telemetry", + ]; + const responseHeaders = [ + "content-type", "content-encoding", "retry-after", + "client-request-id", "x-ms-request-id", "x-ms-clitelem", + ]; + const oauthPaths = new Set([ + "/oauth2/v2.0/authorize-challenge", + "/oauth2/v2.0/token", + ]); + function allows(path, method) { + return (method === "POST" && + (path.startsWith("/api/v2.0/") || oauthPaths.has(path))) || + (method === "PUT" && + /^\/api\/v2\.0\/auth\/methods\/password\/[^/]+$/.test(path)); + } + + app.http("httpProxyFunction", { + methods: ["POST", "PUT", "OPTIONS"], + route: "{*path}", + authLevel: "anonymous", + handler: async request => { + const headers = { "Cache-Control": "no-store", Vary: "Origin" }; + const fail = (status, error) => ({ + status, + headers: { ...headers, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, + body: JSON.stringify({ error }), + }); + if (request.headers.get("origin") !== allowedOrigin) { + return fail(403, "proxy_origin_rejected"); + } + headers["Access-Control-Allow-Origin"] = allowedOrigin; + headers["Access-Control-Expose-Headers"] = responseHeaders.slice(2).join(", "); + try { + const incoming = new URL(request.url); + const path = incoming.pathname; + const rawTarget = request.url.match(/^https?:\/\/[^/?#]+([^#]*)$/i)?.[1]; + if (rawTarget === undefined) return fail(400, "proxy_path_rejected"); + const split = rawTarget.indexOf("?"); + const rawPath = (split < 0 ? rawTarget : rawTarget.slice(0, split)) || "/"; + const rawQuery = split < 0 ? "" : rawTarget.slice(split); + if (path !== rawPath || incoming.search !== rawQuery || + /[\\\u0000-\u0020]/.test(path) || /%(2f|5c|25)/i.test(path)) { + return fail(400, "proxy_path_rejected"); + } + const target = new URL(`${authority.href}${path}${incoming.search}`); + if (target.pathname !== `${authority.pathname}${path}` || + target.search !== incoming.search || target.hash) { + return fail(400, "proxy_path_rejected"); + } + const method = request.method === "OPTIONS" + ? request.headers.get("access-control-request-method") : request.method; + if (!allows(path, method)) { + return fail(405, "proxy_method_or_path_rejected"); + } + if (request.method === "OPTIONS") { + const requested = (request.headers.get("access-control-request-headers") || "") + .split(",").map(value => value.trim().toLowerCase()).filter(Boolean); + if (requested.some(value => !allowedHeaders.includes(value))) { + return fail(403, "proxy_header_rejected"); + } + return { + status: 204, + headers: { + ...headers, + "Access-Control-Allow-Methods": "POST, PUT", + "Access-Control-Allow-Headers": allowedHeaders.join(", "), + }, + }; + } + const body = Buffer.from(await request.arrayBuffer()); + if (body.length > 1024 * 1024) { + return fail(413, "proxy_body_too_large"); + } + const forwarded = { origin: allowedOrigin }; + for (const name of allowedHeaders) { + const value = request.headers.get(name); + if (value !== null) forwarded[name] = value; + } + const response = await axios.request({ + url: target.href, + method: request.method, + headers: forwarded, + data: body, + timeout: 30_000, + maxBodyLength: 1024 * 1024, + maxContentLength: 1024 * 1024, + maxRedirects: 0, + proxy: false, + decompress: false, + responseType: "arraybuffer", + validateStatus: () => true, + }); + if (response.status >= 300 && response.status < 400) { + return fail(502, "proxy_redirect_rejected"); + } + for (const name of responseHeaders) { + if (response.headers[name] !== undefined) { + headers[name] = response.headers[name]; + } + } + return { status: response.status, headers, body: response.data }; + } catch (error) { + return fail( + ["ECONNABORTED", "ETIMEDOUT"].includes(error?.code) ? 504 : 502, + "proxy_upstream_failed" + ); + } + }, + }); + ``` + +1. If your application uses additional API headers, review and add their exact names to `allowedHeaders`. Don't add browser cookies, bearer authorization, function keys, or proxy credentials. The handler forwards the validated `Origin` consistently for native and OAuth calls. +1. Keep `extensions.http.routePrefix` set to `""` in `host.json`. The browser-facing paths are `/api/v2.0/...` and `/oauth2/v2.0/...`; the handler adds the configured tenant authority. + +The handler answers validated preflight locally with HTTP `204`; it doesn't invoke an authentication operation. The service also supports empty HTTP `200` native preflight, without an additional feature flag. Neither behavior supplies your origin policy automatically. + +The handler's 1-MiB request/response bounds and 30-second upstream timeout are proxy limits, not service limits. A rejected redirect, oversized response, or transport failure becomes an explicit proxy error. It isn't retried with the user's credentials. + +## Adapt the deployment configuration + +Wire the new settings into the existing infrastructure before deployment. + +1. In `infra\main.bicep`, replace the `tenantSubdomain` parameter and its description with: + + ```bicep + @description('HTTPS tenant-verified custom-domain authority, including the tenant GUID.') + param serviceAuthority string + ``` + +1. In the same file's `proxy` module, change `runtimeVersion` from `'20'` to `'22'`. Replace `appSettings` and `corsAllowedOrigins` with: + + ```bicep + appSettings: { + SERVICE_AUTHORITY: serviceAuthority + CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN: corsAllowedOrigin + } + corsAllowedOrigins: [] + ``` + + The handler owns CORS in this configuration. The empty platform allowlist avoids a second preflight policy and removes the sample's extra Azure portal origin. + +1. Add `'22'` to the `runtimeVersion` allowed values in `infra\core\host\functions-flexconsumption.bicep`. Keep its other values. Node.js 22 is a [supported Functions runtime](/azure/azure-functions/functions-versions). +1. Replace `infra\main.parameters.json` with the following mapping. This also removes the pinned sample's trailing-space `"tenantSubdomain "` key. + + ```json + { + "$schema": "https://schema.management.azure.com/schemas/2019-04-01/deploymentParameters.json#", + "contentVersion": "1.0.0.0", + "parameters": { + "environmentName": { "value": "${AZURE_ENV_NAME}" }, + "location": { "value": "${AZURE_LOCATION}" }, + "corsAllowedOrigin": { "value": "${CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN}" }, + "serviceAuthority": { "value": "${SERVICE_AUTHORITY}" } + } + } + ``` + +1. In `host.json`, replace the `logging` object with the following settings. Keep the existing extension bundle and empty HTTP route prefix. These settings disable automatic request and dependency capture, which can record full authentication URLs. + + ```json + { + "logLevel": { + "default": "Warning", + "Host.Results": "None", + "Host.Aggregator": "None" + }, + "applicationInsights": { + "enableDependencyTracking": false, + "samplingSettings": { "isEnabled": true } + } + } + ``` + + + +## Deploy the proxy + +Supply your own nonsecret domain and origin values, then deploy the adapted project. + +1. Set the added environment value and the existing CORS input: + + ```powershell + azd env set SERVICE_AUTHORITY "https://login.contoso.com/aaaabbbb-0000-cccc-1111-dddd2222eeee" + azd env set CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN "https://app.contoso.com" + ``` + +1. Sign in to Azure Developer CLI and deploy: + + ```powershell + azd auth login + azd up + ``` + +1. Select the subscription and a supported location when prompted. Record the HTTPS endpoint printed for the `proxy` service. `SERVICE_PROXY_NAME` and `AZURE_FUNCTION_NAME` identify the deployed function app. +1. Configure your custom client's service authority as the custom-domain/GUID authority. Use the function's HTTPS endpoint as its transport prefix, without a tenant path or an added `/api` prefix. The [local guide's checked transport helper](how-to-native-authentication-cors-local.md#route-the-browsers-requests) can use this endpoint as `proxyPrefix`. + +The function endpoint is a transport prefix, not your service authority. A request to `/api/v2.0/signin/start` forwards to `https:////api/v2.0/signin/start`. Validate service-returned links against the custom authority before mapping them to this transport. + +The JavaScript SDK's `customAuth.authApiProxyUrl` doesn't remap absolute HAL links and has no supported URL-rewrite setting. Setting `authApiProxyUrl` to the Functions endpoint alone doesn't route all SDK requests through the proxy. For SDK calls that retain absolute service links, configure [CORS policy at the custom-domain edge](how-to-native-authentication-cors-front-door.md). + +## Verify the deployed proxy + +Check the browser-facing endpoint and the complete authentication journey. + +1. Send a credential-free preflight probe, replacing the endpoint and allowed origin: + + ```powershell + $proxy = "https://" + $origin = "https://app.contoso.com" + curl.exe --include --request OPTIONS "$proxy/api/v2.0/signin/start" --header "Origin: $origin" --header "Access-Control-Request-Method: POST" --header "Access-Control-Request-Headers: content-type,client-request-id" + ``` + + Expect HTTP `204`, the exact allowed origin, allowed methods and headers, and no credentials header. Repeat with an unapproved origin or header and confirm rejection. + +1. In browser developer tools, check JSON `POST` and password-update `PUT` preflight. Confirm that authorization challenge and token exchange retain their form encoding and that current returned links remain on the configured tenant route. +1. Complete the journeys your app implements, including any additional authentication and password-update polling. Confirm that service errors, status codes, and `Retry-After` reach the client unchanged. +1. Check that cookies and proxy secrets aren't forwarded, responses have `Cache-Control: no-store`, and diagnostics contain no authentication bodies or full URLs. Check explicit failure behavior without replaying credentials. + +## Clean up resources + +Remove only the environment created for this proxy when you no longer need it. + +1. Point the application back to its previous transport or remove the test configuration. +1. From this sample checkout and Azure Developer CLI environment, run: + + ```powershell + azd down + ``` + +1. Review the deletion prompt and remove only this environment's resources. Keep your preexisting tenant, app registration, custom authentication domain, and any separate custom-domain hosting resources. + +## Related content + +- [Embedded native authentication CORS concepts](concept-native-authentication-cors.md). +- [Secure Azure Functions](/azure/azure-functions/security-concepts).

newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/identity-platform/how-to-native-authentication-cors-front-door.md b/docs/identity-platform/how-to-native-authentication-cors-front-door.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..ae7af83ffee --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/identity-platform/how-to-native-authentication-cors-front-door.md @@ -0,0 +1,342 @@ +--- +title: Configure an Azure Front Door CORS proxy +description: Adapt the Azure Front Door CORS proxy template for Embedded native authentication with a custom-domain authority, explicit browser policy, and uncached API routes. +ms.topic: how-to +ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1030 +ms.date: 11/13/2026 +ai-usage: ai-generated +#customer intent: As an application developer, I want a custom-domain CORS edge so that my browser application can call the Native Authentication API without changing its transaction contract. +--- + +# Configure an Azure Front Door CORS proxy for embedded native authentication + +Configure Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) on your tenant's verified custom authentication domain with Azure Front Door. Start with a configured app and tenant domain setup. The edge forwards preflight and credential requests to the service; it doesn't need a separate origin just to answer `OPTIONS`. + +Use these CORS rules for single-page applications with Embedded native authentication and Bring Your Own UX (BYO UX) websites. Android and iOS apps using native HTTP transports don't require CORS configuration. + + + +[!INCLUDE [applies-to-external-only](../external-id/includes/applies-to-external-only.md)] + +[!INCLUDE [applies-to-authentication-native](../external-id/includes/applies-to-authentication-native.md)] + +[!INCLUDE [native-authentication-public-preview](~/external-id/includes/native-authentication-public-preview.md)] + + + +## Prerequisites + +- An Azure subscription and permission to deploy subscription-scoped templates, create the resource group, and manage its Front Door and monitoring resources. Use a scoped deployment role. If you use **Contributor** for this one-time provisioning task, limit the assignment's scope and duration, for example with [Privileged Identity Management](~/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-resource-roles-assign-roles.md). +- Completion of [Configure an app for Embedded native authentication](how-to-native-authentication-configure-app.md). +- A custom domain verified in your external tenant and associated with a custom URL domain. Complete the tenant-configuration steps in [Enable custom URL domains](~/external-id/customers/how-to-custom-url-domain.md), and record the tenant GUID. +- Permission to manage the custom domain's DNS `CNAME` and `TXT` records. +- Git and [Azure Developer CLI](/azure/developer/azure-developer-cli/install-azd). + +The deployment creates a Front Door profile, endpoint, origin group, service origin, custom domain with a managed certificate, rule set, and Log Analytics workspace. Review [Front Door pricing](https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/frontdoor/) and monitoring costs. Standard is the sample default; Premium is also supported by its module. Neither tier selection adds a firewall policy to this template. + +## Get the template + +Use the [template revision](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ms-identity-extid-cors-proxy-frontdoor/tree/d0111daba8c2674eab3c9819691c66caa3a96d63). This procedure creates a new profile. If the domain already uses Front Door, apply the equivalent API route and rule changes in that profile's infrastructure. Don't create a competing domain association or replace working DNS. + +1. Get the source: + + ```powershell + git clone https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ms-identity-extid-cors-proxy-frontdoor.git + Set-Location .\ms-identity-extid-cors-proxy-frontdoor + git checkout d0111daba8c2674eab3c9819691c66caa3a96d63 + ``` + +1. Initialize an Azure Developer CLI environment: + + ```powershell + azd init + ``` + + + +## Configure the custom-domain API route + +The pinned template outputs an `onmicrosoft.com` tenant path and matches `/*`. Change the API route and output to use your tenant GUID while keeping the documented service-origin configuration behind the custom domain. + +1. In `infra\main.bicep`, add: + + ```bicep + @description('Directory tenant ID, a GUID, for the custom authentication domain.') + param tenantId string + ``` + +1. In that file's `frontDoor` module parameters, add `tenantId: tenantId`. Keep `customDomain` as your tenant-verified authentication host. The module's existing `originUrl` remains the tenant's platform service host; it isn't an application-facing API authority. +1. In the `frontDoor` module declaration, add `dependsOn: [logAnalytics]` alongside `name`, `scope`, and `params`. Its diagnostic setting uses the workspace created by the `logAnalytics` module. +1. To select a tier explicitly, add `frontDoorSkuName: 'Standard_AzureFrontDoor'` or `frontDoorSkuName: 'Premium_AzureFrontDoor'` to the same module parameters. The module defaults to Standard when this value is omitted. +1. Replace the `CORS_PROXY_ENDPOINT` output with: + + ```bicep + output CORS_PROXY_ENDPOINT string = 'https://${customDomain}/${tenantId}' + ``` + +1. In `infra\modules\frontdoor.bicep`, add `param tenantId string`. Replace the `frontDoorRoute` resource's `patternsToMatch` and `supportedProtocols`, and disable its HTTP redirect: + + ```bicep + patternsToMatch: [ + '/${tenantId}/api/v2.0/*' + '/${tenantId}/oauth2/v2.0/authorize-challenge' + '/${tenantId}/oauth2/v2.0/token' + ] + supportedProtocols: [ + 'Https' + ] + httpsRedirect: 'Disabled' + ``` + +1. Keep `forwardingProtocol: 'HttpsOnly'`, `linkToDefaultDomain: 'Disabled'`, and the custom-domain association. Don't add an origin path or URL rewrite: the service receives the original tenant-GUID path and query. +1. In `frontDoorOrigin.properties`, set `enforceCertificateNameCheck: true`. Keep `hostName` and `originHostHeader` set to the template's `originUrl`, as required by the [custom URL domain configuration](~/external-id/customers/how-to-custom-url-domain.md). Don't point this origin back to the same custom domain's Front Door endpoint. +1. Leave `cacheConfiguration` absent from the route and don't add a caching rule override. [Omitting this object disables route caching](/azure/templates/microsoft.cdn/profiles/afdendpoints/routes). Front Door proxies non-`GET` requests rather than caching them, but the explicit disabled configuration also covers other responses on the API route. +1. In the same file's `audit` resource, set `enabled: false` for `FrontdoorAccessLog`. Keep metrics enabled. Access logs can record full authentication URLs; don't enable them without a reviewed data-handling policy. + +These are API-only routes. Keep hosted browser sign-in, fallback, and callback routing separate if your application uses those experiences. Don't widen this CORS route to `/*` to make an unrelated browser redirect work. + + + +## Configure the CORS and header rules + +The service returns empty HTTP `200` native preflight before parsing or credential mutation, without an additional feature flag. Front Door supplies `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`. Replace the sample's unrestricted requested-method and requested-header reflection with explicit values. + +1. Replace `infra\modules\frontdoor-rules-cors.bicep` with the following module: + + ```bicep + param frontDoorProfileName string + param corsAllowedOrigin string + + var requestHeadersToRemove = [ + 'Proxy-Authorization' + ] + var responseHeadersToRemove = [ + 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' + 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials' + 'Location' + ] + var requestHeaderActions = [for header in requestHeadersToRemove: { + name: 'ModifyRequestHeader' + parameters: { + headerAction: 'Delete' + headerName: header + value: '' + typeName: 'DeliveryRuleHeaderActionParameters' + } + }] + var responseHeaderActions = [for header in responseHeadersToRemove: { + name: 'ModifyResponseHeader' + parameters: { + headerAction: 'Delete' + headerName: header + value: '' + typeName: 'DeliveryRuleHeaderActionParameters' + } + }] + + resource frontDoorProfile 'Microsoft.Cdn/profiles@2024-09-01' existing = { + name: frontDoorProfileName + } + resource frontDoorRuleSet 'Microsoft.Cdn/profiles/ruleSets@2024-09-01' = { + name: 'CORSRuleSet' + parent: frontDoorProfile + } + resource requestBoundary 'Microsoft.Cdn/profiles/ruleSets/rules@2024-09-01' = { + name: 'RequestBoundary' + parent: frontDoorRuleSet + properties: { + order: 1 + conditions: [] + matchProcessingBehavior: 'Continue' + actions: requestHeaderActions + } + } + resource responseBoundary 'Microsoft.Cdn/profiles/ruleSets/rules@2024-09-01' = { + name: 'ResponseBoundary' + parent: frontDoorRuleSet + properties: { + order: 2 + conditions: [] + matchProcessingBehavior: 'Continue' + actions: concat(responseHeaderActions, [ + { + name: 'ModifyResponseHeader' + parameters: { + headerAction: 'Overwrite' + headerName: 'Cache-Control' + value: 'no-store' + typeName: 'DeliveryRuleHeaderActionParameters' + } + } + ]) + } + } + resource corsProxyRule 'Microsoft.Cdn/profiles/ruleSets/rules@2024-09-01' = { + name: 'CORSRule' + parent: frontDoorRuleSet + properties: { + order: 3 + conditions: [ + { + name: 'RequestHeader' + parameters: { + operator: 'Equal' + selector: 'Origin' + matchValues: [corsAllowedOrigin] + typeName: 'DeliveryRuleRequestHeaderConditionParameters' + } + } + { + name: 'RequestMethod' + parameters: { + operator: 'Equal' + matchValues: ['POST', 'PUT', 'OPTIONS'] + typeName: 'DeliveryRuleRequestMethodConditionParameters' + } + } + ] + actions: [ + { + name: 'ModifyResponseHeader' + parameters: { + headerAction: 'Overwrite' + headerName: 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' + value: corsAllowedOrigin + typeName: 'DeliveryRuleHeaderActionParameters' + } + } + { + name: 'ModifyResponseHeader' + parameters: { + headerAction: 'Overwrite' + headerName: 'Access-Control-Allow-Methods' + value: 'POST, PUT' + typeName: 'DeliveryRuleHeaderActionParameters' + } + } + { + name: 'ModifyResponseHeader' + parameters: { + headerAction: 'Overwrite' + headerName: 'Access-Control-Allow-Headers' + value: 'Content-Type, Accept, client-request-id, x-client-sku, x-client-ver, x-client-os, x-client-cpu, x-client-current-telemetry, x-client-last-telemetry' + typeName: 'DeliveryRuleHeaderActionParameters' + } + } + { + name: 'ModifyResponseHeader' + parameters: { + headerAction: 'Overwrite' + headerName: 'Access-Control-Expose-Headers' + value: 'Retry-After, client-request-id, x-ms-request-id, x-ms-clitelem' + typeName: 'DeliveryRuleHeaderActionParameters' + } + } + ] + } + } + + output frontDoorRuleSetId string = frontDoorRuleSet.id + ``` + +1. Set `corsAllowedOrigin` to one exact browser origin, including its scheme and any nondefault port. For additional origins, add separate exact-match rules with unique names and orders after the two boundary rules. Don't replace the value with `*` or an unchecked request-header variable. +1. Review any application-specific API header before adding its exact name to the allowed-header value. Don't enable browser credential sharing. Keep the existing route association with `corsRules.outputs.frontDoorRuleSetId`. + +The request rule removes `Proxy-Authorization` so client credentials for the edge aren't forwarded to the service. It forwards `Authorization` unchanged. The response rule removes upstream CORS grants and redirect locations, and adds `Cache-Control: no-store`. The final rule grants the configured browser origin access, including on service errors. An unexpected upstream redirect retains its status but has no `Location` for a browser to follow; handle it as an API failure without replaying credentials. + +Cookie handling is separate from CORS. This recipe passes `Cookie` and `Set-Cookie` through. To make the route cookie-free, add `Cookie` to `requestHeadersToRemove` and `Set-Cookie` to `responseHeadersToRemove`, after confirming that your application and service don't rely on them. + +These rules define browser CORS permission, not caller authentication. An unapproved browser origin gets no allowed-origin header, but CORS doesn't block all requests from reaching the service. Non-browser callers can supply an `Origin` header, and the service still validates operation methods. This configuration doesn't establish an unbypassable abuse-protection boundary. + + + +## Deploy Azure Front Door + +Supply the tenant and DNS values, then connect the verified custom domain to this endpoint. + +1. Replace `infra\main.parameters.json` with: + + ```json + { + "$schema": "https://schema.management.azure.com/schemas/2019-04-01/deploymentParameters.json#", + "contentVersion": "1.0.0.0", + "parameters": { + "environmentName": { "value": "${AZURE_ENV_NAME}" }, + "location": { "value": "${AZURE_LOCATION}" }, + "corsAllowedOrigin": { "value": "${CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN}" }, + "tenantSubdomain": { "value": "${TENANT_SUBDOMAIN}" }, + "customDomain": { "value": "${CUSTOM_DOMAIN}" }, + "tenantId": { "value": "${EXTERNAL_TENANT_ID}" } + } + } + ``` + +1. Set the values for your deployment. `CUSTOM_DOMAIN` is a host name, not a full URL. `EXTERNAL_TENANT_ID` is the external tenant GUID, not necessarily the tenant used for your Azure subscription. + + ```powershell + azd env set CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN "https://app.contoso.com" + azd env set TENANT_SUBDOMAIN "contoso-external" + azd env set CUSTOM_DOMAIN "login.contoso.com" + azd env set EXTERNAL_TENANT_ID "aaaabbbb-0000-cccc-1111-dddd2222eeee" + azd auth login + azd up + ``` + +1. Select the subscription and location when prompted. Read the deployment outputs: + + ```powershell + azd env get-values + ``` + +1. Create the custom domain's `CNAME` record pointing to `FRONTDOOR_ENDPOINT`. Use `CUSTOM_DOMAIN_DNS_TXT_DOMAIN`, `CUSTOM_DOMAIN_DNS_TXT_NAME`, and `CUSTOM_DOMAIN_DNS_TXT_VALUE` for the domain-validation `TXT` record, before `CUSTOM_DOMAIN_DNS_EXPIRY`. +1. In the Azure portal, open the Front Door profile's **Domains** page. Confirm domain validation, endpoint and route association, and the managed certificate are ready before sending authentication traffic. Use the actual DNS zone's relative record name if your DNS provider expects it. +1. Configure the application with the adapted `CORS_PROXY_ENDPOINT`, such as `https://login.contoso.com/`. For this edge deployment, the service authority and browser transport prefix have the same value: use it for `auth.authority` and `customAuth.authApiProxyUrl`, and add the custom domain host to `auth.knownAuthorities`. + +Don't use `FRONTDOOR_ENDPOINT`, the managed service-origin host, or the old `onmicrosoft.com` path as the application's service authority. The JavaScript SDK retains absolute HAL URLs: valid links already use the custom domain and receive its CORS policy. `authApiProxyUrl` doesn't rewrite them. + +For a custom client, validate absolute and relative service-returned links against the custom domain and tenant-GUID prefix. Preserve the remaining path, query, method IDs, and current continuation token. For an SDK client, verify that its requests stay on this custom-domain route and check how it validates returned links. + +## Validate the deployed proxy + +Check preflight and actual responses on the custom domain, not the default Front Door hostname. + +1. Send a credential-free preflight probe: + + ```powershell + $authority = "https://login.contoso.com/aaaabbbb-0000-cccc-1111-dddd2222eeee" + $origin = "https://app.contoso.com" + curl.exe --include --request OPTIONS "$authority/api/v2.0/signin/start" --header "Origin: $origin" --header "Access-Control-Request-Method: POST" --header "Access-Control-Request-Headers: content-type,client-request-id" + ``` + + Expect the service's empty HTTP `200` response with the edge's exact allowed origin, allowed methods and headers, and no credentials header. A generic HTML error page with HTTP `200` isn't a successful preflight. + +1. Repeat with an unapproved origin and confirm that no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` remains. An unsupported requested method or header must not receive the browser's required CORS permission. +1. In browser developer tools, check JSON `POST`, password-update `PUT`, form-encoded authorization and token exchange, returned-link routing, and the journeys your app implements, including any polling. +1. Confirm that non-success service statuses, error bodies, and `Retry-After` reach the client. Check that authentication responses, including errors, aren't cached, and that no API redirect is followed. +1. Check that the default endpoint and unrelated tenant paths don't match this API route. The route and CORS checks validate this path, not every service access path. + +## Operate the proxy safely + +Use the [shared proxy contract](concept-native-authentication-cors.md#proxy-contract) when reviewing changes to this deployment. + +1. Monitor availability, request volume, latency, throttling, and errors with metrics. Keep credentials, tokens, full authentication URLs, and bodies out of diagnostics, and limit access and retention for any reviewed logs. +1. Keep the allowed origins, headers, route patterns, disabled caching, and TLS configuration in the infrastructure source. Review changes and have a previous working configuration available for rollback. Don't automatically retry ambiguous credential or password-update requests. + +## Clean up resources + +Remove only the environment created for this proxy when you no longer need it. + +1. Switch the application away from this transport. Remove or restore this deployment's DNS records before deleting the endpoint, so you don't leave a dangling `CNAME`. Keep any tenant domain-verification records that are still required. +1. From this sample checkout and Azure Developer CLI environment, run: + + ```powershell + azd down + ``` + +1. Review the deletion prompt and remove only this environment's resources. Keep your tenant, app registration, and any preexisting Front Door profile or custom-domain resources. + +## Related content + +- [Embedded native authentication CORS concepts](concept-native-authentication-cors.md). +- [Azure Front Door Standard/Premium CORS](/azure/frontdoor/standard-premium/troubleshoot-cross-origin-resources). +- [Azure Front Door caching](/azure/frontdoor/front-door-caching).

newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/identity-platform/quickstart-native-authentication.md b/docs/identity-platform/quickstart-native-authentication.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..d213905f567 --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/identity-platform/quickstart-native-authentication.md @@ -0,0 +1,98 @@ +--- +title: "Quickstart: Sign in with Embedded native authentication" +description: Configure the React Next.js sample for Embedded native authentication with the JavaScript SDK and CORS at a tenant-verified custom-domain edge. +ms.topic: quickstart +ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1030 +ms.date: 11/13/2026 +ai-usage: ai-generated +#customer intent: As an application developer, I want to run an Embedded native authentication sample so that I can verify sign-in with my application configuration. +--- + +# Quickstart: Sign in with embedded native authentication + +[!INCLUDE [applies-to-external-only](../external-id/includes/applies-to-external-only.md)] + +[!INCLUDE [applies-to-authentication-native](../external-id/includes/applies-to-authentication-native.md)] + +In this quickstart, you configure a React Next.js sample for Embedded native authentication with Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL) for JavaScript 5.29.0. The email-and-password journey uses a tenant-verified custom domain with Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) at the edge. + +[!INCLUDE [native-authentication-public-preview](~/external-id/includes/native-authentication-public-preview.md)] + +## Prerequisites + +- An external tenant and a public client application configured for Embedded native authentication. Complete [Configure an application](how-to-native-authentication-configure-app.md). +- A tenant-verified custom domain, the application ID, and the directory tenant GUID. +- CORS at the custom-domain edge configured for the sample's browser origin, `http://localhost:3000`. Apply the [shared proxy contract](concept-native-authentication-cors.md#proxy-contract) for origins, preflight, SDK headers, and success and error responses. +- A customer account with email and password. If tenant policy requires multifactor authentication (MFA), prepare an enabled email or SMS factor for this sample journey. +- Node.js 20.9.0 or later, npm, Git, and a code editor. +- Port 3000 available for the application. + +## Get the sample + +The sample has a unified launcher for V1 and V2. Use the pinned revision and SDK version below to follow this quickstart: + +1. Clone the repository, check out the sample revision, and open its React Next.js application: + + ```bash + git clone https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ms-identity-ciam-native-javascript-samples + cd ms-identity-ciam-native-javascript-samples + git checkout --detach 49c4e250a1e6eb97e2b813e9fce6670c996a2808 + cd typescript/native-auth/react-nextjs-sample + ``` + +1. Install the exact SDK version with the sample dependencies: + + ```bash + npm install --save-exact "@azure/msal-browser@5.29.0" + ``` + + + +## Configure the application + +Use `https:///` for both the service authority and the SDK API transport base in this edge route. Keep opaque absolute HAL links for that authority unchanged. Don't add a client secret to browser configuration. + +1. Open `src/config/auth-config.ts`. +1. Replace `Enter_the_Application_Id_Here` with the application ID. +1. Replace the complete `auth.authority` value with `https:///`, substituting your verified hostname and tenant GUID. +1. Add `auth.knownAuthorities` as an array containing the verified hostname, without a scheme or path. +1. Set the required `customAuth.authApiProxyUrl` string to the same full `https:///` authority. Include the tenant GUID in both SDK URL settings. +1. Save the configuration file. The V2 sample uses the SDK's default scopes without custom claims. MFA requirements come from your tenant policy, not from selecting V2. + +## Run the sample + +Run the application from the sample directory. This custom-domain edge configuration doesn't use the sample's local CORS proxy: + +1. Start the application: + + ```bash + npm run dev + ``` + +1. Open `http://localhost:3000` in a browser and select **V2**. Keep the application process running while you test. + +## Sign in the test customer + +Use the sample's unified launcher to test only methods enabled for the current transaction. + +1. Enter the test customer's email address and select **Sign In**. +1. If the service offers multiple first-factor methods, select the password method. Enter the password when requested and select **Sign In**. +1. If the service requests MFA, select a returned email or SMS method and enter its verification code. +1. Confirm that the sample reports completed sign-in. Don't expose tokens in screenshots, logs, or support output. + +Email one-time passcode sign-in uses a customer account and user flow configured for that method. This quickstart follows the email-and-password journey. + +## Clean up the session + +End the local test without deleting shared tenant configuration. + +Signing out of the sample doesn't terminate other application or browser sessions. + +1. Sign out of the sample and clear the account-related application UI. +1. Stop the application process in its terminal. + +## Related content + +- [SDK compatibility and migration from V1](how-to-migrate-native-authentication-v1-v2.md#sdk-compatibility). +- [The Native Authentication API reference](reference-native-authentication.md). +- [Browser CORS and edge requirements](concept-native-authentication-cors.md#proxy-contract).
