diff --git a/docs/identity-platform/reference-native-authentication-api-v1.md b/docs/identity-platform/reference-native-authentication-api-v1.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..d60b22d4d40 --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/identity-platform/reference-native-authentication-api-v1.md @@ -0,0 +1,2208 @@ +--- +title: Microsoft Entra External ID Native Authentication API V1 reference +description: Use the Native Authentication API V1 to integrate existing customer-facing apps with sign-up and sign-in in Microsoft Entra External ID. +manager: dougeby +ms.service: identity-platform +ms.subservice: external +ms.topic: reference +ms.date: 11/13/2026 +ms.custom: sfi-ropc-nochange, sfi-image-nochange, msecd-doc-authoring-1030 +#Customer intent: As an identity developer, I want to integrate customer-facing apps with the Native Authentication API so that customers can sign in to an external tenant. +ai-usage: ai-assisted +author: adamstoffel +ms.author: adamstoffel +--- + +# Native Authentication API V1 reference + +[!INCLUDE [applies-to-external-only](../external-id/includes/applies-to-external-only.md)] + +[!INCLUDE [applies-to-authentication-native](../external-id/includes/applies-to-authentication-native.md)] + +This reference documents the V1 contract for existing integrations. For library-specific interfaces, use the [SDK references](#sdk-references). + +With [Embedded native authentication](concept-native-authentication.md), your application presents the authentication interface. You control its layout and interactions while Microsoft Entra External ID validates authentication requests. + +[!INCLUDE [native-auth-api-common-description](./includes/native-auth-api/native-auth-api-common-description-v1.md)] + +The Native Authentication API supports sign-up and sign-in for two authentication flows: + +- Email with password, which supports sign-up and sign-in with an email and password, and self-service password reset (SSPR). + - Users who sign in with an email address and password can also [sign in with a username and password](../external-id/customers/how-to-sign-in-alias.md). + +- Email one-time passcode, which supports sign-up and sign-in with email one-time passcode. + +## Browser CORS requirements + +[!INCLUDE [native-auth-api-cors-note](./includes/native-auth-api/native-auth-api-cors-note-v1.md)] + +## SDK references + +Use the library reference that matches your installed package. The linked documentation can also describe newer SDK interfaces; this article defines the V1 HTTP contract. + +- **Android:** [MSAL Android library](https://github.com/AzureAD/microsoft-authentication-library-for-android) and [`INativeAuthPublicClientApplication` interface](https://github.com/AzureAD/microsoft-authentication-library-for-android/blob/dev/msal/src/main/java/com/microsoft/identity/nativeauth/INativeAuthPublicClientApplication.kt). +- **iOS and macOS:** [MSAL iOS/macOS library](https://github.com/AzureAD/microsoft-authentication-library-for-objc) and [SDK API reference](https://azuread.github.io/microsoft-authentication-library-for-objc/). +- **JavaScript:** [MSAL JavaScript library](https://github.com/AzureAD/microsoft-authentication-library-for-js) and [SDK API reference](/javascript/api/overview/msal-overview?view=msal-js-latest&preserve-view=true). + +## Prerequisites + +1. A Microsoft Entra external tenant. If you don't already have one, [create an external tenant](../external-id/customers/how-to-create-external-tenant-portal.md). + +1. If you haven't already done so, [Register an application in the Microsoft Entra admin center](quickstart-register-app.md). Make sure to: + + * Record the **Application (client) ID** and **Directory (tenant) ID** for later use. + * [Grant admin consent](quickstart-register-app.md#grant-admin-consent-external-tenants-only) to the application. + * [Enable public client and native authentication flows](#enable-public-client-and-native-authentication-flows). + +1. If you haven't already done so, [Create a user flow in the Microsoft Entra admin center](../external-id/customers/how-to-user-flow-sign-up-sign-in-customers.md#to-add-a-new-user-flow). When you create the user flow, take note of the user attributes you configure as required as these attributes are the ones that Microsoft Entra expects your app to submit. + +1. [Associate your app registration with the user flow](../external-id/customers/how-to-user-flow-add-application.md). + +1. For sign-in flow, [register a customer user](../external-id/customers/how-to-manage-customer-accounts.md#create-a-customer-account), which you use to test the flow. Alternatively, you can get this test user after you run the sign-up flow. + +1. For SSPR flow, [enable self-service password reset](../external-id/customers/how-to-enable-password-reset-customers.md) for customer users in the external tenant. SSPR is available for customer users who use email with password authentication method. + +1. If you want to allow users who sign in with an email address and password to also sign in with a username and password, use the steps in [Sign in with an alias or username](../external-id/customers/how-to-sign-in-alias.md) article: + 1. [Enable username in sign-in](../external-id/customers/how-to-sign-in-alias.md#enable-username-in-sign-in-identifier-policy). + 1. [Create users with username in the admin center](../external-id/customers/how-to-sign-in-alias.md#create-and-update-users-with-username) or [update existing users by adding a username](../external-id/customers/how-to-sign-in-alias.md#create-and-update-users-with-username). Alternatively, you can also [automate user creation and updating in your app by using the Microsoft Graph API](../external-id/customers/how-to-sign-in-alias.md#create-and-update-users-with-username). + +1. To enforce multifactor authentication (MFA) for your customers, use the steps in [Add multifactor authentication (MFA) to an app](../external-id/customers/how-to-multifactor-authentication-customers.md) to add MFA to your sign-in flow. Native authentication supports email one-time passcode and SMS as a second factor for MFA. + +## Continuation token + +[!INCLUDE [entra-external-id-continuation-token](./includes/native-auth-api/continuation-token.md)] + +## V1 challenge types and capabilities + +V1 clients advertise authentication methods through `challenge_type` and additional UI and flow support through `capabilities`. + +[!INCLUDE [native-auth-challenge-type-v1](includes/native-auth-api/native-auth-challenge-type.md)] + +| Authentication method | Sign-up | Sign-in | Self-service password reset | +| --- | --- | --- | --- | +| Email with password | `oob password redirect` | `oob password redirect` | `oob redirect` | +| Email one-time passcode | `oob redirect` | `oob redirect` | Not applicable. | + +Direct API clients include `redirect` when declaring challenge types. The V1 Android, iOS, and JavaScript SDKs include it automatically. + +| Capability | Meaning | +| --- | --- | +| `mfa_required` | The client can handle inline MFA, including the `/introspect`, `/challenge`, and `/token` sequence and the corresponding UI. This includes authentication-context-driven MFA when the tenant policy requires it. | +| `registration_required` | The client can call the strong authentication method registration APIs and display registration UI. | + +An unsupported challenge type or capability makes the request invalid. If the client omits a required challenge type, the service requires web fallback. If the client omits an MFA or registration capability, the flow can proceed only when that capability isn't required by the service; otherwise, web fallback is required. + +V1 web fallback switches to browser-delegated authentication. For example, an email-with-password sign-up flow needs both `oob` and `password`. An app that advertises only `oob` uses browser fallback for that flow. Use the [SDK references](#sdk-references) for platform error checks and interactive library entry points. Browser fallback starts a separate authentication attempt rather than resuming native progress. + +### Enable public client and native authentication flows + +For an existing V1 application registration that you're authorized to manage: + +Use application ownership or delegated [application-management permissions](~/identity/role-based-access-control/delegate-app-roles.md) for the registration. Authentication settings don't require a tenant-wide administrator assignment solely for this task; consent and policy changes have separate permission requirements. + +1. Open the application registration in the Microsoft Entra admin center. +1. Under **Manage**, select **Authentication**. +1. Under **Advanced settings**, set **Enable the following mobile and desktop flows** and **Enable native authentication** to **Yes**. +1. Select **Save**. + +### V1 username sign-in + +[!INCLUDE [enable-username-signin-v1](includes/native-auth-api/enable-username-signin.md)] + +## API reference for sign-up + +To complete a user sign-up flow for either authentication method, your app interacts with four endpoints, `/signup/v1.0/start`, `/signup/v1.0/challenge`, `/signup/v1.0/continue`, and `/token`. + +### API endpoints for sign-up + +| Endpoint | Description | +| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | +| `/signup/v1.0/start` | This endpoint starts the sign-up flow. You pass valid application ID, new username, and [challenge type](#sign-up-challenge-types), then you get back a new continuation token. If you don't have your tenant subdomain, [learn how to read your tenant details](../external-id/customers/how-to-create-external-tenant-portal.md#get-the-external-tenant-details). | +| `continuation_token` | Yes | [Continuation token](#continuation-token) that Microsoft Entra returned in the previous request. | +| `client_id` | Yes | The Application (client) ID of the app you registered in the Microsoft Entra admin center. | + +#### Success response + +Example: + +```http +HTTP/1.1 200 OK +Content-Type: application/json +``` + +```json +{ + "status": "succeeded", + "continuation_token":"czZCaGRSa3F0..." +} +``` + +| Property | Description | +| ---------------------- | ------------------------ | +| `status` | The status of the reset password request. If the status is *succeeded*, the app can use the continuation token that Microsoft Entra returns to request for security tokens via the `oauth2/v2.0/token` endpoint as explained in [Request for security tokens](#step-3-request-for-security-tokens). This means that after a user successfully resets their password, you can directly sign them into your app without initiating a new sign-in flow. | + +Here are the possible statuses that Microsoft Entra returns (possible values of the `status` parameter): + +| Error value | Description | +| ---------------------- | ------------------------ | +| `succeeded` | Password reset completed successfully. | +| `failed` | Password reset failed. The app can resubmit the new password by making another request to the `/resetpassword/v1.0/submit` endpoint. | +| `not_started` | Password reset hasn't started. The app can check the status again later. | +| `in_progress` | Password reset is in progress. The app can check the status again later. | + +#### Error response + +Example: + +```http +HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request +Content-Type: application/json +``` + +```json +{ + "error": "expired_token", + "error_description": "AADSTS901007: The continuation_token is expired.\r\nTrace ID: 0000aaaa-11bb-cccc-dd22-eeeeee333333\r\nCorrelation ID: aaaa0000-bb11-2222-33cc-444444dddddd\r\nTimestamp: yyyy-...", + "error_codes": [ + 552003 + ], + "timestamp": "yyyy-mm-dd 10:15:00Z", + "trace_id": "0000aaaa-11bb-cccc-dd22-eeeeee333333", + "correlation_id": "aaaa0000-bb11-2222-33cc-444444dddddd" +} +``` + +| Property | Description | +| ---------------------- | ------------------------ | +| `error` | An error code string that can be used to classify types of errors, and to react to errors. | +| `error_description` | A specific error message that can help you to identify the cause of an authentication error. | +| `error_codes` | A list of Microsoft Entra-specific error codes that can help you to diagnose errors. | +| `timestamp` | The time when the error occurred. | +| `trace_id` | A unique identifier for the request that can help you to diagnose errors. | +| `correlation_id` | A unique identifier for the request that can help in diagnostics across components. | + +Here are the possible errors you can encounter (possible values of the `error` property): + +| Error value | Description | +| ---------------------- | ------------------------ | +| `invalid_request` | Request parameter validation failed such as validation of *continuation token* failed. | +| `expired_token` | The *continuation token* is expired. | + +### Automatically sign in after password reset + +If the user needs to sign in after a successful password reset. diff --git a/docs/identity-platform/reference-native-authentication-password-reset.md b/docs/identity-platform/reference-native-authentication-password-reset.md
new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..320e18dd87e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/identity-platform/reference-native-authentication-password-reset.md
@@ -0,0 +1,266 @@
+---
+title: Native authentication password reset API reference
+description: Verify customer recovery credentials, update a password, poll completion, and acquire tokens with the Native Authentication API.
+author: adamstoffel
+ms.author: adamstoffel
+ms.service: identity-platform
+ms.subservice: external
+ms.topic: reference
+ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1030
+ms.date: 11/13/2026
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+#customer intent: As an application developer, I want the password reset operations so that customers can recover access without bypassing authentication policies.
+---
+
+# Native authentication password reset API reference
+
+[!INCLUDE [applies-to-external-only](../external-id/includes/applies-to-external-only.md)]
+
+[!INCLUDE [applies-to-authentication-native](../external-id/includes/applies-to-authentication-native.md)]
+
+Password reset verifies a customer's recovery method, accepts a replacement password, and polls an asynchronous update. Email and SMS one-time passcode (OTP) methods support recovery. Multifactor authentication (MFA) and Conditional Access requirements can apply after the reset and before authorization completes.
+
+For existing V1 integrations, use the [V1 API reference](reference-native-authentication-api-v1.md).
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+[!INCLUDE [native-authentication-public-preview](../external-id/includes/native-authentication-public-preview.md)]
+
+- An [application configured for native authentication](how-to-native-authentication-configure-app.md).
+- Password reset enabled for the tenant and customer, with a usable recovery method. See [Enable self-service password reset](../external-id/customers/how-to-enable-password-reset-customers.md).
+- The delegated permissions and consent required for a target API, if you request an API scope.
+
+The examples use a [tenant-verified custom-domain authority](reference-native-authentication.md#operations-and-authority). `custom_domain` is the authentication domain and `tenant` is the tenant GUID.
+
+Passwordless email-OTP accounts don't have a password to reset.
+
+## Start password reset
+
+The diagram shows a standalone recovery sequence using email one-time passcode verification. Inline recovery instead uses the password method's `recover` link within the active sign-in transaction.
+
+:::image type="complex" source="media/native-authentication-v2/native-password-reset-sequence.svg" alt-text="Sequence diagram of password recovery, passcode verification, password update, optional polling, and authorization-code exchange." lightbox="media/native-authentication-v2/native-password-reset-sequence.svg":::
+   The application starts authorization and follows the returned password-reset link with the customer's identifier and current token.
+
+   The application challenges an offered email recovery method, collects the delivered passcode, and verifies it. When requested, the user supplies a replacement password and the application follows the returned update link.
+
+   The application polls only while the current action is `poll` and completes any remaining authentication requirements. It then resumes authorization when allowed and exchanges the authorization code for tokens.
+:::image-end:::
+
+[Start authorization](reference-native-authentication.md#start-authorization) and follow the returned reset-password link (`resetPassword` or `reset_password`). Don't call sign-in discovery first:
+
+```http
+POST https://{custom_domain}/{tenant}/api/v2.0/resetpassword/start
+Content-Type: application/json
+Accept: application/hal+json
+```
+
+```json
+{
+  "username": "user@contoso.com",
+  "continuationToken": "******"
+}
+```
+
+Send the customer's identifier in `username` and the current authorization token in `continuationToken`. The example uses an email address. A response can advertise an email recovery method:
+
+```json
+{
+  "state": "interactionRequired",
+  "action": "challenge",
+  "continuationToken": "******",
+  "_links": {
+    "self": {
+      "href": "/{tenant}/api/v2.0/resetpassword/start"
+    }
+  },
+  "_embedded": {
+    "methods": [
+      {
+        "id": "{email_method_id}",
+        "type": "email",
+        "hint": "j****n@c****o",
+        "_links": {
+          "challenge": {
+            "href": "/{tenant}/api/v2.0/auth/methods/email/{email_method_id}/challenge"
+          },
+          "verify": {
+            "href": "/{tenant}/api/v2.0/auth/methods/email/{email_method_id}/verify"
+          }
+        }
+      }
+    ]
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Select a returned email or SMS recovery method through user choice or application flow logic. The example shows email; for SMS, follow the returned SMS method's links without rewriting the example URL. Use the masked hint where the interface needs a destination label.
+
+### Inline recovery during sign-in
+
+Offer inline recovery only when a password method in the current sign-in response advertises a `recover` link. Follow that link using the current sign-in continuation token. Don't start another authorization request or resubmit the username or password.
+
+```http
+POST https://{custom_domain}/{tenant}/api/v2.0/auth/methods/password/{password_method_id}/recover
+Content-Type: application/json
+Accept: application/hal+json
+```
+
+```json
+{
+  "continuationToken": "******"
+}
+```
+
+Both entry points use the recovery method, challenge, verification, password-update, and polling operations returned by the service.
+
+## Challenge and verify the recovery method
+
+Post to the selected method's `challenge` link:
+
+```json
+{
+  "continuationToken": "******"
+}
+```
+
+Use JSON and `Accept: application/hal+json`. The [shared challenge operation](reference-native-authentication.md#challenge-or-resend) returns the current method type, masked `hint`, `codeLength`, and `verify` and optional `resend` links.
+
+Post the entered passcode to the returned `verify` link:
+
+```json
+{
+  "otp": "{one_time_passcode}",
+  "continuationToken": "******"
+}
+```
+
+Use the newest token for each request. For another code, use the current `resend` link and service limits, not an earlier challenge URL/token pair.
+
+A successful verification can return the password method:
+
+```json
+{
+  "state": "interactionRequired",
+  "action": "update",
+  "id": "{password_method_id}",
+  "type": "password",
+  "continuationToken": "******",
+  "_links": {
+    "update": {
+      "href": "/{tenant}/api/v2.0/auth/methods/password/{password_method_id}"
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Use the password method ID from the returned `update` link, not the email or SMS recovery method ID. Inline recovery can retain the password method ID from the parent sign-in.
+
+## Update a password
+
+Submit the replacement password with `PUT`, not `POST`:
+
+```http
+PUT https://{custom_domain}/{tenant}/api/v2.0/auth/methods/password/{password_method_id}
+Content-Type: application/json
+Accept: application/hal+json
+```
+
+```json
+{
+  "newPassword": "{new_password}",
+  "continuationToken": "******"
+}
+```
+
+| Property | Type | Required | Description |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| **`continuationToken`** | String. | Yes. | Current token requesting password update. |
+| **`newPassword`** | String. | Yes. | Replacement password. Password confirmation is local to your interface, not an additional request field. |
+
+The service can return:
+
+```json
+{
+  "state": "interactionRequired",
+  "action": "poll",
+  "pollInterval": "2",
+  "id": "{password_method_id}",
+  "type": "password",
+  "continuationToken": "******",
+  "_links": {
+    "poll": {
+      "href": "/{tenant}/api/v2.0/auth/methods/password/{password_method_id}/pollUpdate"
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+This indicates an asynchronous update, not final authorization. Don't submit the password again while waiting or automatically repeat the update after an ambiguous network failure.
+
+## Poll password update
+
+Follow the latest `poll` link:
+
+```http
+POST https://{custom_domain}/{tenant}/api/v2.0/auth/methods/password/{password_method_id}/pollUpdate
+Content-Type: application/json
+Accept: application/hal+json
+```
+
+```json
+{
+  "continuationToken": "******"
+}
+```
+
+While the update is in progress, the service returns `interactionRequired` with `action: poll`, an updated token, and a `poll` link. Replace the prior response before the next poll.
+
+When included, `pollInterval` is a string containing the interval in seconds. Use the current response's interval for the next request, and honor server retry guidance. The example `"2"` isn't a fixed service interval. Stop polling when the action changes or an error is returned, and handle any later authentication required by policy.
+
+A continuation response is:
+
+```json
+{
+  "state": "continue",
+  "continuationToken": "******",
+  "_links": {
+    "continue": {
+      "href": "/{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/authorize-challenge"
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+## Complete policy requirements and acquire tokens
+
+Password reset doesn't bypass MFA or Conditional Access. If another challenge is returned, complete it using the shared method operations. Token exchange follows completion of the remaining policy steps and authorization continuation.
+
+After `state: continue`, [resume authorization](reference-native-authentication.md#resume-authorization) using the latest token and [exchange the code](reference-native-authentication.md#exchange-the-authorization-code). The requested scopes and claims remain those established at the beginning of the transaction.
+
+## Outcomes and errors
+
+Use the [shared error handling](reference-native-authentication.md#errors). The recovery contract describes these outcomes:
+
+| Condition | Outcome and client handling |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Unknown username** | Recovery doesn't start. Use a generic customer-facing message. |
+| **Incorrect email or SMS passcode** | HTTP `400 invalidGrant` with `innerError.code: invalidOneTimeCode`. Let the user correct the code using the usable current state or an advertised resend. |
+| **Missing passcode** | HTTP `400 invalidRequest`. Correct the missing input. |
+| **Resend** | A new passcode is sent through the returned `resend` link. |
+| **Expired password-update token** | HTTP `400 expiredToken` with `innerError.code: expiredContinuationToken`. Restart authorization. |
+| **Weak or common replacement password** | HTTP `400 invalidRequest` with an applicable inner error such as `passwordTooWeak` or `passwordTooCommon`. Collect a compliant password. |
+| **Update in progress** | Follow the latest polling response and server retry guidance. |
+| **Poll fails password policy** | HTTP `400 invalidRequest` with an inner error such as `passwordTooCommon` or `passwordBannedByPolicy`. Handle the error rather than polling indefinitely. |
+| **Account locked or disabled during polling** | HTTP `403 forbidden` with `innerError.code: accountLocked`. Stop the recovery operation. |
+| **Password update job fails** | HTTP `500 serverError`. Show a clear failure without automatically repeating the password update. |
+| **Completed recovery** | Handle any remaining policy actions, resume authorization, and request tokens. |
+
+This table describes specific outcomes, not an exhaustive error catalog. Password update acceptance, polling completion, and token issuance are separate boundaries.
+
+Don't log recovery passcodes, replacement passwords, or transaction tokens. Record only safe diagnostic IDs, timestamps, and HTTP status. Don't automatically replay verification or password updates.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Native Authentication API reference](reference-native-authentication.md).
+- [Sign-in API reference](reference-native-authentication-sign-in.md).
+- [Configure an application](how-to-native-authentication-configure-app.md).

@@ -0,0 +1,180 @@
+---
+title: Native authentication sign-in API reference
+description: Discover sign-in methods, verify passwords and email passcodes, and handle policy-driven challenges with the Native Authentication API.
+author: adamstoffel
+ms.author: adamstoffel
+ms.service: identity-platform
+ms.subservice: external
+ms.topic: reference
+ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1030
+ms.date: 11/13/2026
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+#customer intent: As an application developer, I want the sign-in operations so that I can discover methods, verify credentials, and acquire tokens.
+---
+
+# Native authentication sign-in API reference
+
+[!INCLUDE [applies-to-external-only](../external-id/includes/applies-to-external-only.md)]
+
+[!INCLUDE [applies-to-authentication-native](../external-id/includes/applies-to-authentication-native.md)]
+
+Sign-in discovers the methods allowed for a customer's identifier and completes the required credential checks. Email-with-password and email one-time passcode (OTP) first-factor sign-in use the same response-driven model. The application selects allowed operations from the response through user choice or application flow logic, then satisfies the remaining authentication requirements before resuming authorization.
+
+For existing V1 integrations, use the [V1 API reference](reference-native-authentication-api-v1.md).
+
+The examples use a [tenant-verified custom-domain authority](reference-native-authentication.md#operations-and-authority). `custom_domain` is the authentication domain and `tenant` is the tenant GUID.
+
+## Start sign-in discovery
+
+[!INCLUDE [native-authentication-public-preview](../external-id/includes/native-authentication-public-preview.md)]
+
+The diagram shows one possible sign-in sequence. Policy requirements can add, repeat, or reorder actions; always follow the current response.
+
+:::image type="complex" source="media/native-authentication-v2/native-sign-in-sequence.svg" alt-text="Sequence diagram of native sign-in, credential verification, additional policy interactions, and authorization-code exchange." lightbox="media/native-authentication-v2/native-sign-in-sequence.svg":::
+   The application starts authorization, follows the returned sign-in link, and submits the user's identifier to discover available methods.
+
+   The application challenges an offered method and verifies the requested password or passcode. Email passcode delivery occurs when required. Additional policy interactions can require more verification or method registration.
+
+   Only when the current response permits continuation does the application resume authorization and exchange the resulting authorization code for tokens.
+:::image-end:::
+
+[Start authorization](reference-native-authentication.md#start-authorization), then follow the returned `sign_in` link. Send the OAuth response's `continuation_token` value as `continuationToken`:
+
+```http
+POST https://{custom_domain}/{tenant}/api/v2.0/signin/start
+Content-Type: application/json
+Accept: application/hal+json
+```
+
+```json
+{
+  "continuationToken": "******",
+  "username": "user@contoso.com"
+}
+```
+
+| Property | Type | Required | Description |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| **`continuationToken`** | String. | Yes. | Token from the current authorization challenge. |
+| **`username`** | String. | Yes. | Sign-in identifier accepted by tenant policy. This example uses email. |
+
+A password method-selection response can be:
+
+```json
+{
+  "continuationToken": "******",
+  "state": "interactionRequired",
+  "action": "challenge",
+  "_embedded": {
+    "methods": [
+      {
+        "id": "{password_method_id}",
+        "type": "password",
+        "_links": {
+          "challenge": {
+            "href": "/{tenant}/api/v2.0/auth/methods/password/{password_method_id}/challenge"
+          },
+          "verify": {
+            "href": "/{tenant}/api/v2.0/auth/methods/password/{password_method_id}/verify"
+          }
+        }
+      }
+    ]
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Email-OTP sign-in returns an email method with its own `id`, masked `hint`, and allowed links. Your app can present returned choices or select an available method through application flow logic. Not every account offers both password and email OTP. Use generic discovery failures and protect account-existence information.
+
+## Challenge the selected method
+
+Follow the method's `challenge` link with `POST` and the latest continuation token:
+
+```json
+{
+  "continuationToken": "******"
+}
+```
+
+The [shared challenge contract](reference-native-authentication.md#challenge-or-resend) defines headers, response fields, and resend behavior.
+
+| Returned method | Interaction |
+| --- | --- |
+| **`password`** | No code is sent. Collect the password when the response requests `verify`. |
+| **`email`** | Collect the delivered passcode. Use the returned masked `hint` and `codeLength`. |
+| **`sms`** | When advertised for a required factor, collect the SMS passcode using its own hint, length, and links. |
+
+Use `resend` only when the service advertises it and the customer requests another code. Don't resend automatically after a delivery delay.
+
+## Verify the credential
+
+Follow the current `verify` link using `POST`. Use JSON, `Accept: application/hal+json`, and one of these bodies.
+
+Password:
+
+```json
+{
+  "continuationToken": "******",
+  "password": "******"
+}
+```
+
+Email or SMS one-time passcode:
+
+```json
+{
+  "continuationToken": "******",
+  "otp": "{one_time_passcode}"
+}
+```
+
+Use the credential field for the returned method type. Don't submit a password in `otp` or a passcode in `password`. Don't automatically replay verification after an ambiguous network failure.
+
+## Complete additional policy requirements
+
+A successful verification can return another `interactionRequired` response with `action: challenge` and `_embedded.methods`. Select an advertised method and repeat challenge and verification with the new token and links.
+
+Multifactor authentication (MFA) uses the same shared credential operations and supports email and SMS one-time passcodes as second factors. MFA through system policies is supported. Select a method from those returned for the required factor. The SMS example describes a second-factor interaction.
+
+If the next response requires `enroll` or `activate`, use the [inline registration contract](reference-native-authentication.md#authentication-method-enrollment). Email-with-password accounts can register an offered email or SMS factor. Email-OTP first-factor accounts can't reuse email as their second factor; use an offered alternative such as SMS.
+
+If a required interaction isn't supported by your client, or the service returns `state: redirect`, stop native requests and offer a separately configured browser sign-in or a clear failure.
+
+## Resume authorization and acquire tokens
+
+When policy requirements are satisfied, a response can return:
+
+```json
+{
+  "continuationToken": "******",
+  "state": "continue",
+  "_links": {
+    "continue": {
+      "href": "/{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/authorize-challenge"
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Post the token as form-encoded `continuation_token` to the returned link. Then [exchange the authorization code](reference-native-authentication.md#exchange-the-authorization-code) for tokens. Neither a challenge response nor a successful verification response substitutes for that exchange.
+
+## Errors
+
+Use the [shared error envelope](reference-native-authentication.md#errors) with these sign-in conditions:
+
+| Condition | Status or error | Handling |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| **Missing username or token** | `400` | Correct the request. |
+| **Incorrect email or SMS passcode** | `400 invalidGrant`, with `innerError.code: invalidOneTimeCode` | Let the user correct the code using the usable current state or an advertised resend. |
+| **Missing passcode** | `400 invalidRequest` | Correct the missing input. |
+| **Invalid transaction state** | `400` with the native error envelope | Restart instead of replaying an earlier token. |
+| **Throttling** | `429` | Stop automatic retries and honor server guidance. |
+| **Unsupported native interaction** | `state: redirect`, or OAuth `invalid_grant` with `web_redirect_required` | Stop native requests. A separate browser sign-in restarts authentication. |
+
+For other credential, discovery, or delivery failures, handle the actual status and stable error codes without exposing account-existence details. This table isn't an exhaustive error catalog. Preserve only safe request IDs, correlation IDs, timestamps, and status information, not credentials or whole response bodies.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [SDK sign-in quickstart](quickstart-native-authentication.md).
+- [Native Authentication API reference](reference-native-authentication.md).
+- [Password reset API reference](reference-native-authentication-password-reset.md).

+#customer intent: As an application developer, I want the sign-up operations so that I can collect required attributes and complete verification.
+---
+
+# Native authentication sign-up API reference
+
+[!INCLUDE [applies-to-external-only](../external-id/includes/applies-to-external-only.md)]
+
+[!INCLUDE [applies-to-authentication-native](../external-id/includes/applies-to-authentication-native.md)]
+
+This reference describes sign-up through server-driven attribute collection. Email-with-password and email one-time passcode sign-up use the same operations and message shapes. For these email methods, the user flow associated with the application selects the sign-up method; the client doesn't select it in the start request.
+
+The examples show email-based sign-up. For existing V1 integrations, use the [V1 API reference](reference-native-authentication-api-v1.md).
+
+The examples use a [tenant-verified custom-domain authority](reference-native-authentication.md#operations-and-authority). `custom_domain` is the authentication domain and `tenant` is the tenant GUID.
+
+## Start sign-up
+
+[!INCLUDE [native-authentication-public-preview](../external-id/includes/native-authentication-public-preview.md)]
+
+The diagram shows a response-driven sign-up sequence. The user flow determines the sign-up method, and the current response determines which attributes and interactions are required.
+
+:::image type="complex" source="media/native-authentication-v2/native-sign-up-sequence.svg" alt-text="Sequence diagram of native sign-up with response-defined attribute collection, verification, and authorization-code exchange." lightbox="media/native-authentication-v2/native-sign-up-sequence.svg":::
+   The application starts authorization and follows the returned sign-up link. The service returns the current action and requested attribute descriptors.
+
+   While interaction is required, the application either collects and submits the requested attributes or handles the returned challenge, verification, enrollment, or activation operation. Each response replaces the previous action, links, and continuation token.
+
+   Submitting email can send a passcode and return a verification action without a separate challenge request. Password collection applies only when required by the configured sign-up method.
+
+   At `state: continue`, the application resumes authorization and exchanges the resulting authorization code for tokens.
+:::image-end:::
+
+[Start authorization](reference-native-authentication.md#start-authorization), then follow its `sign_up` link with the returned token:
+
+```http
+POST https://{custom_domain}/{tenant}/api/v2.0/signup/start
+Content-Type: application/json
+Accept: application/hal+json
+```
+
+```json
+{
+  "continuationToken": "******"
+}
+```
+
+`continuationToken` is a required string. The start response can request email:
+
+```json
+{
+  "continuationToken": "******",
+  "state": "interactionRequired",
+  "action": "collectAttributes",
+  "attributes": [
+    {
+      "attributeId": "email",
+      "inputType": "text",
+      "hidden": false,
+      "required": true,
+      "canChange": true,
+      "label": "Email"
+    }
+  ],
+  "_links": {
+    "submitAttributes": {
+      "href": "/{tenant}/api/v2.0/signup/submitattributes"
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Labels, requiredness, and validation metadata come from policy. Use those requirements within your application's interface and collection logic.
+
+## Submit attributes
+
+Follow `_links.submitAttributes.href`. Collection can occur more than once:
+
+```http
+POST https://{custom_domain}/{tenant}/api/v2.0/signup/submitattributes
+Content-Type: application/json
+Accept: application/hal+json
+```
+
+```json
+{
+  "continuationToken": "******",
+  "attributes": {
+    "email": "user@contoso.com"
+  }
+}
+```
+
+| Property | Type | Required | Description |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| **`continuationToken`** | String. | Yes. | Latest sign-up token. |
+| **`attributes`** | Object of string values. | Yes. | Values keyed by the exact returned `attributeId` values. |
+
+All required values must be supplied before sign-up completes. Optional values can be omitted. Missing required values can produce a validation error or another `collectAttributes` response.
+
+For email-with-password sign-up, submit a password when requested. For example, a collection round that requests password and profile fields can accept:
+
+```json
+{
+  "continuationToken": "******",
+  "attributes": {
+    "email": "user@contoso.com",
+    "password": "******",
+    "givenName": "Example",
+    "surname": "User"
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Submit fields according to the user flow's returned descriptors. Email one-time passcode sign-up creates a passwordless account that signs in with an email passcode.
+
+### Collection order
+
+The service can request email first, collect several attributes together, or return to attribute collection after verification. Submit attributes requested by the latest response rather than predicting the sequence from the values submitted.
+
+Your app can organize collection according to its flow logic and the available descriptors. See [Collection order and email verification](concept-native-authentication-user-attributes.md#collection-order-and-email-verification). Each response determines the available next operations.
+
+## Interpret attribute and page descriptors
+
+Each response describes the current form. The following fields define an attribute:
+
+| Field | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| **`attributeId`** | Submission key. |
+| **`inputType`** | Input control type, such as `text`, `password`, `boolean`, `date`, or `checkboxMultiSelect`. |
+| **`required`** | Whether a value must be supplied. |
+| **`hidden`** | Whether the field is hidden. |
+| **`canChange`** | Editability information, when included. |
+| **`label`** | Optional display label. |
+| **`initialValue`** | Optional prepopulated value. |
+| **`validation.validationRegEx`** | Optional validation pattern. |
+| **`options`** | Optional choices with `label` and `value` properties. |
+| **`confirmationInput`** | Optional confirmation behavior, such as `retype`, `reveal`, or `none`. |
+
+Don't require a `pages` member. The current `attributes` array defines the fields and requirements; page-grouping metadata, if returned, is additional presentation information. Input control types don't change the string-valued submission object. See [User attribute concepts](concept-native-authentication-user-attributes.md).
+
+## Verify email
+
+When attribute submission requires email verification, it sends the passcode and returns:
+
+```json
+{
+  "continuationToken": "******",
+  "state": "interactionRequired",
+  "action": "verify",
+  "id": "{email_method_id}",
+  "type": "email",
+  "hint": "u***@contoso.com",
+  "codeLength": 8,
+  "_links": {
+    "verify": {
+      "href": "/{tenant}/api/v2.0/auth/methods/email/{email_method_id}/verify"
+    },
+    "resend": {
+      "href": "/{tenant}/api/v2.0/auth/methods/email/{email_method_id}/challenge"
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+The service has already sent the passcode; proceed directly to verification. Use the returned length and masked hint. Post to `verify`:
+
+```http
+POST https://{custom_domain}/{tenant}/api/v2.0/auth/methods/email/{email_method_id}/verify
+Content-Type: application/json
+Accept: application/hal+json
+```
+
+```json
+{
+  "continuationToken": "******",
+  "otp": "{one_time_passcode}"
+}
+```
+
+To request another code, post only the latest `continuationToken` to the current `resend` link, subject to service limits.
+
+Verification can return more attribute collection:
+
+```json
+{
+  "continuationToken": "******",
+  "state": "interactionRequired",
+  "action": "collectAttributes",
+  "attributes": [
+    {
+      "attributeId": "givenName",
+      "inputType": "text",
+      "hidden": false,
+      "required": true,
+      "canChange": true,
+      "label": "First name"
+    }
+  ],
+  "_links": {
+    "submitAttributes": {
+      "href": "/{tenant}/api/v2.0/signup/submitattributes"
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Submit the requested values and continue handling the next response.
+
+## Complete policy requirements and authorization
+
+After account creation and any required verification, complete any multifactor authentication (MFA) and Conditional Access requirements before resuming authorization.
+
+If the response advertises another method challenge, use the [shared challenge and verification operations](reference-native-authentication.md#challenge-or-resend). Method registration is distinct from verifying a sign-up email. See [Method discovery and registration](concept-native-authentication-flow.md#method-discovery-isnt-method-registration) for the enrollment contract.
+
+When the service returns `state: continue`, follow `_links.continue`, [resume authorization](reference-native-authentication.md#resume-authorization), and exchange the code. This acquires tokens without starting an unrelated sign-in transaction.
+
+## Errors and lifecycle
+
+Use the [shared error envelope](reference-native-authentication.md#errors). Structured validation entries can contain `code`, `message`, `attributeIds`, `suggestions`, and optional `recovery`.
+
+| Condition | Status or behavior | Handling |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| **Invalid continuation token** | `400` | Restart the flow. |
+| **Missing or invalid attribute** | `400` or another `collectAttributes` response | Present field-level feedback and submit corrected values. |
+| **User already exists** | `400 invalidRequest` | Offer generic sign-in or recovery guidance without unnecessarily disclosing account existence. |
+| **Password policy violation** | `400` | Collect a compliant password. |
+| **Incorrect email passcode** | `400 invalidGrant` with `innerError.code: invalidOneTimeCode` | Let the user correct the code using the usable current state or an advertised resend. |
+| **Missing passcode** | `400 invalidRequest` | Correct the missing input. |
+| **Throttling** | `429` | Honor server retry guidance. |
+| **Unsupported native interaction** | `state: redirect` | Stop native requests and offer the configured browser path or a clear failure. |
+
+Handle other failures through their actual status and stable error codes. Don't treat an expired transaction as a recoverable incorrect-code entry.
+
+Attribute submission isn't idempotent after user creation. Don't replay successful submissions, log sensitive attribute values, or treat client-side validation as authoritative.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Native Authentication API reference](reference-native-authentication.md).
+- [Native authentication user attributes](concept-native-authentication-user-attributes.md).
+- [Sign-in API reference](reference-native-authentication-sign-in.md).

Follow service-controlled attempt and resend limits. + +## Verify a credential + +Post to the current `verify` link. For a password method: + +```http +POST https://{custom_domain}/{tenant}/api/v2.0/auth/methods/password/{id}/verify +Content-Type: application/json +Accept: application/hal+json +``` + +```json +{ + "continuationToken": "******", + "password": "******" +} +``` + +For an email or SMS method: + +```http +POST https://{custom_domain}/{tenant}/api/v2.0/auth/methods/{methodType}/{id}/verify +Content-Type: application/json +Accept: application/hal+json +``` + +```json +{ + "continuationToken": "******", + "otp": "{one_time_passcode}" +} +``` + +Verification can return another challenge, attribute collection, a password update, or continuation. Handle the returned action. Verification isn't idempotent; don't retry automatically after an ambiguous network failure. + +## Authentication-method enrollment + +Sign-up or sign-in can require inline registration through `action: enroll`, followed by `action: activate`. Enrollment is separate from collecting profile attributes or verifying an existing credential. + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> Enrollment is separate from authentication with a registered method. Use only enrollment methods advertised for the current transaction; don't infer an enrollment operation from a credential challenge. + +### Select and enroll a method + +Select a supported method from `_embedded.methods` and follow its `_links.enroll` URL. + +| Method | Advertisement | Required JSON fields | +| --- | --- | --- | +| **Phone SMS** | `type: phone`, with `sms` in `channels`. | `continuationToken`, `phoneNumber` including country code, and `channel: sms`. | +| **Email** | `type: email`. | `continuationToken` and `email`. Don't send a `channel`. | + +Phone enrollment uses `type: phone`, not the `sms` type used by existing SMS challenge methods. The example phone enrollment URL is `/{tenant}/api/v2.0/auth/methods/phone`; the email URL is `/{tenant}/api/v2.0/auth/methods/email`. Use `POST` with JSON and follow the advertised URL rather than constructing one. + +For phone SMS enrollment, the body is: + +```json +{ + "continuationToken": "******", + "phoneNumber": "+1 2025550123", + "channel": "sms" +} +``` + +For email enrollment, the body is: + +```json +{ + "continuationToken": "******", + "email": "user@contoso.com" +} +``` + +The service sends a passcode and returns `action: activate`, a new continuation token, and an `activate` link. Display the returned masked `hint` and `codeLength` when present. Email and SMS can use different code lengths. + +A phone activation response can be: + +```json +{ + "continuationToken": "******", + "state": "interactionRequired", + "action": "activate", + "id": "{phone_method_id}", + "type": "phone", + "channel": "sms", + "hint": "***0123", + "codeLength": 6, + "_links": { + "activate": { + "href": "/{tenant}/api/v2.0/auth/methods/phone/{phone_method_id}/activate" + }, + "resend": { + "href": "/{tenant}/api/v2.0/auth/methods/phone" + } + } +} +``` + +Use the fields and links from the actual response; email uses its own method type, code length, and links. + +### Activate or resend + +Send a JSON `POST` to the current `activate` link with the latest `continuationToken` and the user's code in `otp`. Phone examples use `/{tenant}/api/v2.0/auth/methods/phone/{phone_method_id}/activate`; email uses its own advertised link. Don't submit activation codes to a credential's `verify` link. + +```json +{ + "continuationToken": "******", + "otp": "{one_time_passcode}" +} +``` + +If the activation response advertises `resend`, send a JSON `POST` containing only the latest `continuationToken` to that link. The link can point back to enrollment. Don't retain or resend the contact details; the token carries the enrollment context. + +```json +{ + "continuationToken": "******" +} +``` + +Replace the active token, links, hint, and code length after each response. Continue handling returned actions after activation; only `state: continue` permits resuming authorization. Registration can itself satisfy MFA, so a separate credential challenge isn't always required. + +For `invalidGrant` with `innerError.code: invalidOneTimeCode`, keep the current activation token and advertised links. Let the user correct the code or request a resend. Don't automatically replay enrollment or activation after an ambiguous connection failure. + +## Errors + +OAuth errors use fields such as `error`, `error_description`, `trace_id`, and `correlation_id`. Native authentication failures use a nested envelope. For example, an incorrect email verification code can return HTTP `400` with: + +```json +{ + "error": { + "code": "invalidGrant", + "message": "AADSTS50181: Unable to validate the otp.", + "timestamp": "2026-08-28T17:30:00Z", + "traceId": "0000aaaa-11bb-cccc-dd22-eeeeee333333", + "correlationId": "aaaa0000-bb11-2222-33cc-444444dddddd", + "innerError": { + "code": "invalidOneTimeCode" + } + } +} +``` + +Use stable codes for handling rather than localized messages. Attribute validation can return `error.innerError.code: attributeValidationError` with `details` entries containing `code`, `message`, and `attributeIds`, plus optional `suggestions` or `recovery`. Check HTTP status and content type before parsing; don't render an unexpected HTML error body in the app. + +| Condition | Status or error | Handling | +| --- | --- | --- | +| **Invalid OAuth parameter** | `400 invalid_request` | Correct the request; don't retry unchanged. | +| **Invalid or expired code** | `400 invalid_grant` | Restart authorization. | +| **Invalid application** | `400 invalid_client` | Correct app configuration. | +| **Invalid or ungranted scope** | `400 invalid_scope` | Check requested scopes and consent. | +| **Authentication required** | `401 InsufficientAuthorization` | Follow an enabled journey link. | +| **Invalid continuation token/state** | `400 invalidRequest` | Restart the applicable flow. | +| **Expired password-update token** | `400 expiredToken` with `innerError.code: expiredContinuationToken` | Restart authorization. | +| **Missing verification code** | `400 invalidRequest` | Correct the missing input. | +| **Incorrect email or SMS verification code** | `400 invalidGrant` with `innerError.code: invalidOneTimeCode` | Let the user correct the code using the usable current verification state or follow an advertised resend link. Don't resubmit automatically. | +| **Incorrect activation code** | `400 invalidGrant` with `innerError.code: invalidOneTimeCode` | Keep the current activation token and advertised links. Let the user correct the code or use an advertised resend action. Don't resubmit automatically. | +| **Browser interaction required** | `invalid_grant` with `web_redirect_required` | Stop native requests and use the configured interactive recovery path. Don't forward the continuation token to an arbitrary URL. | +| **Native transaction can't continue** | Native body `{"state":"redirect"}` | Stop native requests. A separate browser sign-in doesn't preserve native progress. | +| **Throttling** | `429` | Honor `Retry-After` and server guidance. | + +Network and service failures can use other response formats. Treat an unexpected content type as an explicit failure. The table describes specific common cases, not an exhaustive error catalog for every operation. + +## Security and diagnostics + +Use HTTPS for every upstream request. Keep passwords, passcodes, continuation tokens, codes, and issued tokens out of URLs, logs, telemetry, exceptions, screenshots, and support attachments. Don't cache authentication responses or share transaction state across users. + +Reject unexpected authorities and redirects rather than forwarding secrets. Don't automatically retry credential verification, account-creation submissions, or password updates after an ambiguous failure. + +Display only masked hints supplied by the service. Use generic discovery failures so messages and method presentation don't unnecessarily disclose account existence. + +Retain safe diagnostics: HTTP status, operation category, `client-request-id`, service trace/correlation IDs, and timestamp. OAuth names use underscores; Native authentication error names use camel case. Extract these diagnostic fields without retaining full request or response bodies. + +## Custom authentication extensions + +Event configuration and contracts are specific to each extension and journey. Your app continues to select allowed operations from service responses when an extension participates in the flow. + +Native event coverage includes `OnOtpSend` for email and `OnTokenIssuanceStart`. `OnAttributeCollectionStart` and `OnAttributeCollectionSubmit` aren't supported for Embedded native authentication or Bring Your Own UX. See [Custom authentication extensions](../external-id/customers/concept-custom-extensions.md) for event-specific behavior. This event set doesn't establish password-migration hooks, password-update synchronization, or arbitrary context propagation. + +## Related content + +- [SDK sign-in quickstart](quickstart-native-authentication.md). +- [Sign-up API reference](reference-native-authentication-sign-up.md). +- [Password reset API reference](reference-native-authentication-password-reset.md).

+---
+title: Data collection for dynamic permissions
+description: Learn what Snowflake data Microsoft Entra ID Governance dynamic permissions collects, including identity, access, configuration, and activity metadata.
+ms.topic: reference
+ms.date: 11/16/2026
+ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1032
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+# Customer intent: As an administrator, I want to understand what data is collected from supported applications so that I can evaluate the data requirements for permission remediation.
+---
+
+# Data collection for dynamic permissions
+
+This reference describes data read by Microsoft Entra ID Governance dynamic permissions for permission remediation from the Snowflake application. This information is leveraged by Microsoft Entra for analyzing non-human identities and ensuring least privilege.
+
+[!INCLUDE [Dynamic permissions licensing](~/includes/licensing-dynamic-permissions.md)]
+
+## Permissions required for dynamic permissions
+
+Dynamic permissions relies on the effective privileges of the connection identity in each supported application to:
+
+- **Detect excessive access:** Read the identity, role, permission, and activity metadata needed to evaluate agent access.
+- **Remediate excessive access:** Revoke or adjust supported role assignments to right-size access, or disable supported identities.
+- **Assign task-scoped permissions:** Grant and revoke supported access for an approved task.
+
+The required privileges and supported operations depend on the application.
+
+## Snowflake
+
+When Microsoft Entra is integrated with Snowflake for dynamic permissions, then Microsoft Entra reads Snowflake metadata about users, roles, permissions, objects, security configuration, and activity. Collection depends on the connector's privileges, Snowflake visibility rules, and the features available in your account.
+
+
+### Identity and configuration data
+
+The following table summarizes the forms of metadata which may be collected.
+
+| Category | Data collected |
+| --- | --- |
+| Users | User identifiers, names, email addresses, user types, account status, timestamps, session defaults, ownership, comments, and authentication-configuration indicators. |
+| Roles and grants | Account, database, application, and instance roles; role properties; privilege grants; user and role assignments; role hierarchies; and grants to Snowflake Native Apps. Grant details include the privilege, object, recipient, grant option, grantor role, and timestamps. |
+| Future grants | Definitions of privileges to apply automatically to new objects, including the recipient role, object type, and database or schema scope. These aren't grants on existing objects. |
+| Objects and account information | Inventory and properties of database and data objects, compute resources, processing objects, functions, procedures, AI objects, applications, and security objects. Metadata can include names, identifiers, owners, comments, timestamps, object definitions, and service endpoint details. Account context includes organization, account, region, and Snowflake version. |
+| Security configuration | Security integration properties exposed by Snowflake, including integration type and enabled status; the account setting for blocking privileged roles in External OAuth; and network and authentication policy inventory. Collection doesn't include every network or authentication policy's full definition. |
+| Selected tags | Selected sensitivity, classification, criticality, environment, certification, privacy, and semantic tags. Collected data includes tag values and direct object or column associations, not every tag value or inherited association. |
+
+User authentication indicators describe whether credentials or authentication methods are configured. They aren't password, private-key, or token values.
+
+Role and grant records describe assignments and hierarchies, not a precomputed list of every user's effective privileges.
+
+### Activity data
+
+The default activity lookback is 90 days. This window applies to activity queries, not all metadata collection.
+
+| Activity source | Data collected |
+| --- | --- |
+| [Login history](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/account-usage/login_history) | The latest successful login per identified user within the collection window, rather than all login attempts. Details include event time, user name, client IP address, client type, authentication factors, and connection information. |
+| [Query history](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/account-usage/query_history) | Aggregated query activity by user, role, query type, execution status, errors, and warehouse. Summaries include query counts and first and last occurrence times. Both successful and unsuccessful activity can be represented. Executed SQL text isn't selected. |
+| [Access history](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/account-usage/access_history) | Aggregated activity for directly referenced objects, underlying objects, and modified objects. Details include users, object identifiers and types, query counts, latest activity time, and accessed or modified column names. |
+
+Access history collection doesn't include every field in the source view. Collected column names aren't a complete inventory of every column in every table.
+
+### Data boundaries and limitations
+
+This collection doesn't query business-data rows from Snowflake customer-defined tables or select executed SQL text from query history.
+

+
+# Manage dynamic permissions settings for a catalog
+
+As an Identity Governance Administrator, you can enable or disable dynamic permissions remediation for a catalog in Microsoft Entra ID Governance. This article describes how to change the **Permission remediation** setting in the Microsoft Entra admin center.
+
+For more information about dynamic permissions and its permission remediation capabilities, see [What is dynamic permissions?](dynamic-permissions-overview.md).
+
+Permission remediation is available for specific resources in a catalog. If you're getting started, see [Tutorial: Mitigate permission risk of agents in Snowflake with Microsoft Entra dynamic permissions](tutorial-dynamic-permissions-prevent-excessive-permissions.md).
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+[!INCLUDE [Dynamic permissions licensing](~/includes/licensing-dynamic-permissions.md)]
+
+## Enable dynamic permissions remediation for a catalog
+
+[!INCLUDE [Dynamic permissions reporting phase](~/includes/dynamic-permissions-reporting-phase.md)]
+
+To enable permission remediation for a catalog, complete the following steps:
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least an [Identity Governance Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#identity-governance-administrator).
+1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Dynamic permissions (preview)**.
+1. Select **Resources**, and then select **Enable dynamic permissions**.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/dynamic-permissions-manage-catalog-settings/enable-dynamic-permissions.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Dynamic permissions Resources page with the Enable dynamic permissions button highlighted." lightbox="media/dynamic-permissions-manage-catalog-settings/enable-dynamic-permissions.png" border="true":::
+
+1. Select the catalog for which you want to enable permission remediation.
+1. Confirm the catalog has the correct resources, and set **Permission remediation** to **Enabled**.
+1. Select **Enable dynamic permissions**.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/dynamic-permissions-manage-catalog-settings/confirm-enable-dynamic-permissions.png" alt-text="Screenshot of permission remediation enabled for a catalog with the final Enable dynamic permissions button highlighted." lightbox="media/dynamic-permissions-manage-catalog-settings/confirm-enable-dynamic-permissions.png" border="true":::
+
+## Disable dynamic permissions remediation for a catalog
+
+To disable permission remediation for a catalog, complete the following steps:
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least an [Identity Governance Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#identity-governance-administrator).
+1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Entitlement management**.
+1. Select **Catalogs**.
+1. Select the catalog for which you want to disable dynamic permissions capabilities.
+1. Select **Edit**.
+1. Change **Permission remediation** from **Enabled** to **Disabled**.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/dynamic-permissions-manage-catalog-settings/disable-permission-remediation.png" alt-text="Screenshot of catalog settings with the Permission remediation setting highlighted in the Disabled state." lightbox="media/dynamic-permissions-manage-catalog-settings/disable-permission-remediation.png" border="true":::
+
+1. Select **Save**.

diff --git a/docs/id-governance/dynamic-permissions-manage-separation-duties.md b/docs/id-governance/dynamic-permissions-manage-separation-duties.md

@@ -0,0 +1,109 @@
+---
+title: Manage separation of duties for dynamic permissions
+description: Learn how to import, update, enable, disable, and delete separation of duties rules for dynamic permissions in Microsoft Entra ID Governance.
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/14/2026
+ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1032
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+#customer intent: As an administrator, I want to manage separation of duties rules for dynamic permissions so that I can define incompatible roles and conflicts.
+---
+
+# Manage separation of duties for dynamic permissions
+
+As an Identity Governance Administrator, you can manage separation of duties rules for dynamic permissions in Microsoft Entra ID Governance.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> With separation of duties in the dynamic permissions preview, organizations can define rules using the authorization models and constructs of their applications and resources. These preview capabilities are separate from the generally available [separation of duties capabilities for access packages](entitlement-management-access-package-incompatible.md) in entitlement management.
+
+This article explains how to import, update, enable, disable, and delete rules, and where to view the impacted agent non-human identities.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+[!INCLUDE [Dynamic permissions licensing](~/includes/licensing-dynamic-permissions.md)]
+
+Have a resource already set up that supports separation of duties. If you're getting started, see [Tutorial: Mitigate permission risk of agents in Snowflake with Microsoft Entra dynamic permissions](tutorial-dynamic-permissions-prevent-excessive-permissions.md).
+
+## View separation of duties rule details
+
+To view the details of a separation of duties rule, follow these steps:
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least an [Identity Governance Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#identity-governance-administrator).
+1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Dynamic permissions (preview)** > **Separation of duties**.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/dynamic-permissions-manage-separation-duties/view-separation-of-duties-rules.png" alt-text="Screenshot of two separation of duties rules for a catalog, showing their descriptions, resources, and enabled status." lightbox="media/dynamic-permissions-manage-separation-duties/view-separation-of-duties-rules.png" border="true":::
+
+1. Select the name of the rule.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/dynamic-permissions-manage-separation-duties/view-separation-of-duties-rule-details.png" alt-text="Screenshot of a separation of duties rule showing its Object ID and the two sets of conflicting Snowflake account roles." lightbox="media/dynamic-permissions-manage-separation-duties/view-separation-of-duties-rule-details.png" border="true":::
+
+## Import separation of duties rules
+
+To import separation of duties rules from a CSV file, follow these steps:
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least an [Identity Governance Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#identity-governance-administrator).
+1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Dynamic permissions (preview)** > **Separation of duties**.
+1. Select **Import rules**.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/dynamic-permissions-manage-separation-duties/import-separation-of-duties-rules.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Separation of duties page with Import rules highlighted to add rules to the selected catalog." lightbox="media/dynamic-permissions-manage-separation-duties/import-separation-of-duties-rules.png" border="true":::
+
+1. Select **Download template** to get the CSV template.
+1. Update the CSV template with your separation of duties rules. For Snowflake examples, see [CSV examples for Snowflake](#csv-examples-for-snowflake).
+1. Select **Choose file**, and then select the CSV file to upload it.
+1. Confirm the import message, which summarizes how many rules will be created or updated. If validation reports errors, correct the CSV file and upload it again.
+1. Select **Review and import**.
+1. Confirm the list of rules to be imported.
+1. Select **Import**.
+1. Review the import results. If all rules were imported successfully, select **Return to rules**.
+
+### CSV examples for Snowflake
+
+The examples define two rules for illustrative custom Snowflake account roles. Replace the resource identifier and role names with values from your environment.
+
+- `PermissionSet1` and `PermissionSet2`: Use the exact names of the Snowflake account roles that an identity must not hold together.
+- `ResourceOriginId`: Use the resource's `originId` returned by the Microsoft Graph [List resources API](/graph/api/accesspackagecatalog-list-resources?tabs=http), not its `id`. Alternatively, use the exact display name of the resource in the catalog.
+- `Status`: Use `active` to enable the rule or `inactive` to disable it.
+- `incompatiblePermissionSetId`: Leave this value empty to create a rule. To update an existing rule, use its **Object ID**. To find this value, select the rule name on the **Separation of duties** page to open the rule details.
+
+The following CSV uses a resource origin ID to create an enabled finance rule and a disabled masking rule:
+
+```csv
+Name,Description,ResourceOriginId,PermissionSet1,PermissionSet2,Status,incompatiblePermissionSetId
+"Separate finance data changes and auditing","Prevent the same identity from modifying finance data and independently auditing that data.","a0a0a0a0-bbbb-cccc-dddd-e1e1e1e1e1e1","FINANCE_DATA_WRITER","FINANCE_AUDITOR","active",""
+"Separate masking administration and sensitive data access","Prevent the same identity from managing masking policies and reading the sensitive data those policies protect.","a0a0a0a0-bbbb-cccc-dddd-e1e1e1e1e1e1","MASKING_POLICY_ADMIN","SENSITIVE_DATA_READER","inactive",""
+```
+
+Alternatively, the following CSV defines the same rules using the resource's exact display name in the catalog:
+
+```csv
+Name,Description,ResourceOriginId,PermissionSet1,PermissionSet2,Status,incompatiblePermissionSetId
+"Separate finance data changes and auditing","Prevent the same identity from modifying finance data and independently auditing that data.","Snowflake for Microsoft Entra ID","FINANCE_DATA_WRITER","FINANCE_AUDITOR","active",""
+"Separate masking administration and sensitive data access","Prevent the same identity from managing masking policies and reading the sensitive data those policies protect.","Snowflake for Microsoft Entra ID","MASKING_POLICY_ADMIN","SENSITIVE_DATA_READER","inactive",""
+```
+
+## Update separation of duties rules
+
+To change which roles a separation of duties rule declares incompatible, use [Import separation of duties rules](#import-separation-of-duties-rules). Set `incompatiblePermissionSetId` in the CSV file to the rule's **Object ID**, shown when you select the rule name to view its details.
+
+To update a rule's name, description, or enabled status, follow these steps:
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least an [Identity Governance Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#identity-governance-administrator).
+1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Dynamic permissions (preview)** > **Separation of duties**.
+1. Select the name of the rule you want to update.
+1. Select **Edit**.
+1. Update the name, description, or enabled status.
+1. Select **Next**.
+1. Select **Review and save**.
+1. Select **Save changes**.
+
+## Enable, disable, or delete separation of duties rules
+
+To enable, disable, or delete separation of duties rules, follow these steps:
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least an [Identity Governance Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#identity-governance-administrator).
+1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Dynamic permissions (preview)** > **Separation of duties**.
+1. Select the checkbox for the rule you want to enable, disable, or delete.
+1. Select **Enable selected**, **Disable selected**, or **Delete selected**.
+
+## View separation of duties conflicts
+
+When identities hold permissions that conflict with enabled separation of duties rules, the conflicts appear in **Detections**. For more information, see [view detections and remediations (Preview)](dynamic-permissions-review-detections-remediations.md).

newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/id-governance/dynamic-permissions-overview.md b/docs/id-governance/dynamic-permissions-overview.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..489f030e177 --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/id-governance/dynamic-permissions-overview.md @@ -0,0 +1,75 @@ +--- +title: What is Dynamic permissions? (Preview) +description: Learn how Microsoft Entra manages permissions for AI agents. +author: markwahl-msft +ms.author: mwahl +ms.service: entra-id-governance +ms.topic: overview +ms.date: 11/16/2026 +ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1032 +ms.reviewer: markwahl-msft +ai-usage: ai-assisted +--- + + +# What is Dynamic permissions? (Preview) + +Microsoft Entra Dynamic permissions are new identity governance capabilities that help organizations ensure least privilege for permissions assigned to identities in their applications. + +While many organizations already have a zero trust model for employees interacting with applications, agents make zero trust principles even more important. When an agent is assisting an employee, the agent should not automatically inherit all the standing access rights of the employee using it. It should begin with no authority and receive only what it needs for the approved task, for only as long as the task requires. Similarly, autonomous agents with their own identities need to have only the required permissions for their tasks, and not be assigned permissions which could be misused. + +In the Dynamic permissions approach, organization-wide policies sets the outer boundary guardrails for agents, preventing agents from having permissions it should not have. Permissions are then further scoped to the task, made time-bound, and contracted or removed as the task changes or completes. The permissions assigned to an employee does not change, but an agent may receive its own identity with its own permissions scoped to the task. This new capability is augmented by dynamic agent risk and dynamic conditional access. + +A new identity governance preview detects excessive permissions that have been assigned to autonomous AI agent non-human identities in business applications. + +## Prerequisites + +Dynamic permissions builds upon features in Microsoft Entra, including provisioning account discovery, and entitlement management, with connections to applications to discover identities, evaluate their access, and perform supported remediation. + +[!INCLUDE [licensing-dynamic-permissions](../includes/licensing-dynamic-permissions.md)] + +## Detection and remediation of overprivileged agent identities (Preview) + +An agent's access isn't limited to the platform where it runs. Dynamic permissions focuses on how agents are represented in the applications and resources they access, and what those identities are allowed to do. + +### Where agents run and what they access + +Agent platforms and resource applications provide different perspectives on an agent: + +| Perspective | What it describes | +| --- | --- | +| Agent platform | Where an agent runs and its runtime context. | +| Applications and resources | The systems and data an agent accesses through identities, roles, permissions, and other authorization constructs. | + +[Connected platforms in Microsoft Agent 365](/microsoft-agent-365/admin/connected-platforms) focuses on discovering and managing agents from supported agent platforms. Dynamic permissions complements that platform perspective with a deeper understanding of the identities and access represented in important business applications and resources. + +An agent can run on one platform and access resources in another application. Understanding its roles and permissions in that resource application helps you identify excessive access, regardless of where the agent runs. + +![Diagram of agent access to a target resource, agent platform registration with Agent 365, and connections to Microsoft Entra.](media/agent-id-governance-overview/agent-and-target.png) + +### Agent identity coverage in the preview + +The preview supports agent identities in Snowflake. For supported identity types, connection requirements, and setup instructions, see [Tutorial: Mitigate permission risk of agents in Snowflake with Microsoft Entra dynamic permissions](tutorial-dynamic-permissions-prevent-excessive-permissions.md). + +### Input for excessive access + +The preview starts with two checks: ensuring that agents do not have excessive **privilege level** and are not subject to **separation of duties conflicts**. Together, they help you identify agents with powerful permissions and combinations of access that violate your organization's rules. + +- **Privilege level:** Dynamic permissions introduces a canonical privilege-classification model that maps application-specific permissions and roles to **Low**, **Medium**, **High**, or **Critical**. This creates a consistent way to understand authority across different authorization models without replacing them. Classification reflects what a permission or role allows, independently of the resource's sensitivity or business criticality. During preview, dynamic permissions flags agents with permissions or roles classified as **Critical**, such as authority to take ownership, grant access, or change security controls. For details, see [Privilege levels for dynamic permissions](dynamic-permissions-privilege-levels.md). +- **Separation of duties conflicts:** Organizations can define incompatible access using the authorization models and constructs of their applications and resources. For example, a rule can identify a conflict between roles that let an identity modify financial data and independently audit that data. This evaluates combinations of access that shouldn't be held together, rather than only the authority of each role individually. For details, see [Manage separation of duties for dynamic permissions](dynamic-permissions-manage-separation-duties.md). + +The separation of duties preview is separate from the generally available [separation of duties capabilities for access packages](entitlement-management-access-package-incompatible.md). Those capabilities check incompatible access package assignments and group memberships when users request access packages. Dynamic permissions adds rules expressed in the connected application's own authorization model. + + + +## Task-scoped permission assignment based on intent + +A separate preview enables task-scoped permission assignment so agents can dynamically request permissions for a specific task, based on the task's intent. This approach was demonstrated at Microsoft Ignite and described in the Microsoft Security blog, [Agents are your newest insiders. Security must move at their speed.](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/10/19/agents-are-your-newest-insiders-security-must-move-at-their-speed/). + +The same input used to assess excessive access, starting with privilege level and separation of duties conflicts, inform task-scoped permission requests. Organizational policy sets the boundaries. Within those boundaries, an agent receives only the permissions needed for an approved task, for only as long as needed. Permissions can be reduced or removed as the task changes or completes. + +Interested customers and ISVs are invited to partner with Microsoft to preview task-scoped permission assignment. To request participation in that preview, [sign up for dynamic permissions updates](https://aka.ms/DynamicPermissionsPreview). + +## Related content + +- [Governing agent identities](agent-id-governance-overview.md)
