+# Privilege levels for dynamic permissions
+
+Microsoft Entra ID Governance dynamic permissions uses a canonical privilege-classification model to categorize permissions and roles into four levels: **Low**, **Medium**, **High**, and **Critical**.
+
+Applications and resources express access differently, using their own permissions, roles, and authorization constructs. The canonical model maps those application-specific constructs to a common set of privilege levels. This gives organizations a consistent way to understand and assess privilege across supported Microsoft and non-Microsoft applications and resources, without replacing their native authorization models.
+
+The model is designed to scale across applications and resource types. Privilege level reflects the intrinsic authority a permission or role grants, independently of the sensitivity or business criticality of the application or resource. It describes what the permission allows an identity to do, not how sensitive the target resource or its data is.
+
+For example, a permission classified as **Critical** because it allows granting access to others or changing security controls remains **Critical** in a test subscription containing only test data. The lower sensitivity of that environment doesn't reduce the permission's intrinsic authority.
+
+The permission classification level alone isn't a complete assessment of the risk that access poses in a particular environment. Privilege level is one of multiple inputs that dynamic permissions uses alongside others, such as resource sensitivity.
+
+During preview, dynamic permissions flags AI agents that have permissions or roles categorized as **Critical**. This reference lists the Snowflake permissions and roles currently classified as **Critical**.
+
+Microsoft continually reassesses and updates privilege-level classifications. The classifications in this reference were last refreshed on **2026-11-12**.
+
+[!INCLUDE [Dynamic permissions licensing](~/includes/licensing-dynamic-permissions.md)]
+
+## How privilege levels are determined
+
+Microsoft evaluates the documented capabilities of each permission or role and applies reviewed classification rules to the authority those capabilities provide. The following table summarizes typical capabilities at each level.
+
+| Privilege level | Typical authority |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Low** | View metadata about resources, without reading their content or changing them. |
+| **Medium** | Read content, use services or functions, perform limited operations, create objects within a bounded scope, or view broader metadata. |
+| **High** | Modify existing resources, run automation, control broader operations, or perform destructive lifecycle actions. |
+| **Critical** | Own resources, grant access to others, control credentials, change security policies or boundaries, control an organization, or execute code with the permissions of its owner. |
+
+If a permission provides capabilities at multiple levels, the highest applicable level determines its classification. For roles, dynamic permissions evaluates their permissions and capabilities, along with relevant role hierarchies and inheritance relationships, to determine the overall privilege level.
+
+These descriptions explain the classification model across all four levels. The application-specific reference in this article currently lists only Snowflake permissions and roles classified as **Critical** during preview.

+---
+title: View detections and remediations (Preview)
+description: Learn how to see the dynamic permissions detection results and remediation details for non-human identities in catalog resources in Microsoft Entra ID Governance.
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/14/2026
+ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1032
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+#customer intent: As an administrator, I want to see the dynamic permissions detection results and remediation details so that I can understand planned remediation actions and remediation status for identities in catalog resources.
+---
+
+# View detections and remediations (Preview)
+
+As an Identity Governance Administrator, you can see results of dynamic permission detection of non-human identities across resources in a catalog in Microsoft Entra ID Governance. You can then select an identity to view more detection details, including the planned remediation action and remediation status.
+
+This feature focuses on overpermissioned non-human identities. For viewing the discovered users and groups in applications, see [Discover identities in target applications with account discovery](../identity/app-provisioning/how-to-account-discovery.md).
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+### Licensing
+
+[!INCLUDE [Dynamic permissions licensing](~/includes/licensing-dynamic-permissions.md)]
+
+### Resource setup
+
+Before viewing detections, you will need to 
+
+ * Have one or more resource in the catalog already set up for permission remediation.
+ * Optionally, configured [separation of duties rules for non-human identities](dynamic-permissions-manage-separation-duties.md).
+
+If you're getting started, see [Tutorial: Mitigate permission risk of agents in Snowflake with Microsoft Entra dynamic permissions](tutorial-dynamic-permissions-prevent-excessive-permissions.md).
+
+## View detections and remediations
+
+To see detections and remediation details for the resources in a catalog, follow these steps:
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least an [Identity Governance Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#identity-governance-administrator).
+1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Dynamic permissions (preview)**.
+1. Select **Detections**.
+1. Select a catalog which has the desired resources:
+
+    - If you're visiting **Detections** for the first time, select a catalog when prompted.
+    - If you've already selected a catalog and want to see the detections from another catalog, select **Change catalog**, and then select the other catalog.
+
+1. The detections are shown for each identity in a resource impacted by a rule. Select an identity to view the detection details, including the planned remediation action and remediation status, if configured.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/dynamic-permissions-review-detections-remediations/view-detections.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Detections page showing an identity's risk categories, resource, and remediation status." lightbox="media/dynamic-permissions-review-detections-remediations/view-detections-expanded.png" border="true":::

+description: Learn how to prepare Snowflake, configure dynamic permissions for a catalog, and view the resulting permission rule detections for AI agents in Microsoft Entra ID Governance.

+---
+
+# Tutorial: Mitigate permission risk of agents in Snowflake with Microsoft Entra dynamic permissions
+
+Microsoft Entra ID Governance dynamic permissions helps organizations ensure least privilege for permissions assigned to identities in their applications. During preview, it evaluates privilege levels and separation of duties conflicts to identify agents with powerful permissions and combinations of access that violate your organization's rules.
+
+In this tutorial, you connect Snowflake, enable permission remediation for a catalog, and review detections and planned remediation actions for Snowflake agent identities. For more information, see [What is dynamic permissions?](dynamic-permissions-overview.md).
+
+During preview, dynamic permissions assesses excessive access for Snowflake users with `TYPE = SERVICE_AGENT`. For more information, see the user `TYPE` property in [Snowflake's CREATE USER reference](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/sql/create-user#optional-object-properties-objectproperties).
+
+In this tutorial, you:
+
+> [!div class="checklist"]
+> - Prepare your Snowflake account for discovery.
+> - Enable dynamic permissions remediation for a catalog.
+> - Add Snowflake to the catalog and configure permission remediation.
+> - Start recurring discovery to refresh Snowflake identity and permission data.
+> - See the resulting detections and remediation details.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A Snowflake account. Microsoft recommends piloting dynamic permissions with a non-production Snowflake account during preview.
+- Access to a Snowflake user with the `ACCOUNTADMIN` role.
+- A catalog in Microsoft Entra ID Governance. If you don't have one, [create a catalog](entitlement-management-catalog-create.md).
+- A **Snowflake** enterprise application added from the Microsoft Entra application gallery. Use the gallery application, not a custom non-gallery application.
+    - Be an owner of the existing application, or [add a new Snowflake gallery application](../identity/saas-apps/snowflake-tutorial.md#add-snowflake-from-the-gallery) as at least a [Cloud Application Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#cloud-application-administrator).
+- Access to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least an [Identity Governance Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#identity-governance-administrator).
+
+Typically, you'll use a Snowflake application already integrated with Microsoft Entra ID for single sign-on (SSO) and System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) provisioning. However, neither integration is required for this tutorial. You can add a new Snowflake gallery application without configuring SSO or SCIM. For integration guidance, see [Configure single sign-on for Snowflake](../identity/saas-apps/snowflake-tutorial.md) and [Configure automatic user provisioning for Snowflake](../identity/saas-apps/snowflake-provisioning-tutorial.md).
+
+[!INCLUDE [Dynamic permissions licensing](~/includes/licensing-dynamic-permissions.md)]
+
+## Prepare your Snowflake account for discovery
+
+To analyze permissions for AI agents in Snowflake, Microsoft Entra uses a dedicated service user separate from the Snowflake SCIM security integration. The dedicated service user currently authenticates with a Programmatic Access Token (PAT).
+
+Microsoft recommends piloting dynamic permissions with a non-production Snowflake account during preview.
+
+[!INCLUDE [snowflake-prepare-discovery-identity-governance](~/includes/snowflake-prepare-discovery-identity-governance.md)]
+
+## Add an overpermissioned test agent (optional)
+
+To validate permission remediation, you can add an overpermissioned test agent in your Snowflake test account.
+
+> [!WARNING]
+> This example grants the test agent the `ACCOUNTADMIN` role. Run it only in a non-production Snowflake test account.
+
+1. Sign in to your Snowflake account as a user with the `ACCOUNTADMIN` role.
+1. Run the following SQL commands:
+
+    ```sql
+    USE ROLE ACCOUNTADMIN;
+
+    CREATE USER MY_SERVICE_AGENT
+      TYPE = SERVICE_AGENT;
+
+    GRANT ROLE ACCOUNTADMIN TO USER MY_SERVICE_AGENT;
+
+    SHOW GRANTS TO USER MY_SERVICE_AGENT;
+    ```
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> After completing this tutorial, remove the `MY_SERVICE_AGENT` test user from your Snowflake test account.
+
+## Enable dynamic permissions remediation for a catalog
+
+Enable permission remediation for the catalog you'll use in this tutorial.
+
+Enabling permission remediation for a catalog automatically enables it for all supported resources in that catalog, provided connectivity to those resources is established. Currently, only Snowflake is supported.
+
+[!INCLUDE [Dynamic permissions reporting phase](~/includes/dynamic-permissions-reporting-phase.md)]
+
+1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least an Identity Governance Administrator.
+1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Dynamic permissions (preview)**.
+1. Select **Resources**, and then select **Enable dynamic permissions**.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/dynamic-permissions-manage-catalog-settings/enable-dynamic-permissions.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Dynamic permissions Resources page with the Enable dynamic permissions button highlighted." lightbox="media/dynamic-permissions-manage-catalog-settings/enable-dynamic-permissions.png" border="true":::
+
+1. Select the catalog for which you want to enable permission remediation.
+1. Confirm the information, and set **Permission remediation** to **Enabled**.
+1. Select **Enable dynamic permissions**.
+
+## Add Snowflake to the catalog
+
+Continue with the catalog you selected in the previous section. If the Snowflake application isn't already part of that catalog, follow these steps to add it.
+
+1. On the **Resources** page in **Dynamic permissions (preview)**, select **Add resources**.
+1. Select **+Applications**.
+1. In the picker, search for your Snowflake application and select it.
+1. Select **Select** to complete the picker.
+1. Select **Add**.
+
+## Configure permission remediation for Snowflake
+
+Configure the discovery connection and enable permission remediation for the Snowflake application in your catalog. The following steps apply when **Discovery connection** shows **Not configured**.
+
+For details about the data collected from Snowflake, see [Data collection for dynamic permissions](dynamic-permissions-data-collection.md).
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> If you already provided the discovery and identity governance connectivity information through the enterprise application and provisioning pages, enabling permission remediation for the catalog is sufficient. You don't need to explicitly enable permission remediation for Snowflake.
+
+1. On the **Resources** page in **Dynamic permissions (preview)**, select the checkbox next to your Snowflake application. Don't select the application name.
+1. Select **Configure permission remediation** at the top of the page.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/tutorial-dynamic-permissions-prevent-excessive-permissions/configure-snowflake-permission-remediation.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the selected Snowflake resource with the Configure permission remediation action highlighted." lightbox="media/tutorial-dynamic-permissions-prevent-excessive-permissions/configure-snowflake-permission-remediation.png" border="true":::
+
+1. Under **Discovery connection**, select **Configure**.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/tutorial-dynamic-permissions-prevent-excessive-permissions/configure-discovery-connection-action.png" alt-text="Screenshot of permission remediation prerequisites with Configure highlighted beside the unconfigured discovery connection." lightbox="media/tutorial-dynamic-permissions-prevent-excessive-permissions/configure-discovery-connection-action.png" border="true":::
+
+1. Enter the following connection information:
+
+    - Your Snowflake tenant URL in the format `https://<organization-name>-<account-name>.snowflakecomputing.com`. In Snowsight, open **View account details** and copy **Account/Server URL**. For details, see [Find your Snowflake account identifier](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/admin-account-identifier#finding-the-organization-and-account-name-for-an-account).
+    - The API token generated when you prepared your Snowflake account for discovery.
+    - The same Snowflake warehouse you specified in the script in [Prepare your Snowflake account for discovery](#prepare-your-snowflake-account-for-discovery).
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/tutorial-dynamic-permissions-prevent-excessive-permissions/configure-snowflake-discovery-connection.png" alt-text="Screenshot of Snowflake discovery and identity governance connectivity settings with Tenant URL, API token, and Warehouse fields." lightbox="media/tutorial-dynamic-permissions-prevent-excessive-permissions/configure-snowflake-discovery-connection.png" border="true":::
+
+1. Select **Save**.
+1. Select **X** to close the connection configuration window and return to **Configure permission remediation**.
+1. Select **Next**.
+1. Select **Enable permission remediation**.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> Microsoft is partnering with Snowflake to move both the discovery connection and the SCIM connection between Snowflake and Microsoft Entra to workload identity-based authentication in a future update.
+
+## Start recurring discovery
+
+After configuring permission remediation, return to the **Resources** page in **Dynamic permissions (preview)** to start recurring discovery for your Snowflake application.
+
+1. Select the name of the Snowflake resource in your catalog to open its enterprise application page.
+1. Select **Provisioning**.
+1. Select **Discover identities**.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/tutorial-dynamic-permissions-prevent-excessive-permissions/discover-snowflake-identities.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Snowflake enterprise application with Discover identities highlighted in the left navigation and toolbar." lightbox="media/tutorial-dynamic-permissions-prevent-excessive-permissions/discover-snowflake-identities.png" border="true":::
+
+1. On the **Discover identities** page, select **Discover identities** to start discovery.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> Discovery starts immediately and then runs every 24 hours to refresh the data. The time needed to complete discovery depends on the number of identities and the amount of relevant data in the Snowflake application.
+
+## Add separation of duties rules for Snowflake (optional)
+
+If you want to add separation of duties rules for Snowflake, follow [Import separation of duties rules](dynamic-permissions-manage-separation-duties.md#import-separation-of-duties-rules). Then return to this tutorial to see the resulting detections and remediations.
+
+## View detections and remediations
+
+You can see the resulting detected non-human identities which triggered a rule for the catalog's resources, including planned remediation actions and remediation status for those identities.
+
+1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least an Identity Governance Administrator.
+1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Dynamic permissions (preview)**.
+1. Select **Detections**.
+1. Select the catalog you used in this tutorial. If another catalog is already selected, select **Change catalog**, and then select your catalog.
+1. The detections are shown for an identity in a resource. Select an identity to view the detection details, including the planned remediation action and remediation status.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/dynamic-permissions-review-detections-remediations/view-detections.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Detections page showing an identity's risk categories, resource, and remediation status." lightbox="media/dynamic-permissions-review-detections-remediations/view-detections-expanded.png" border="true":::

englishSummary.headline: New tutorial for dynamic permissions in Snowflake
englishSummary.summary: Microsoft added guidance for preparing Snowflake, enabling catalog remediation, running recurring discovery, and reviewing detections for users with TYPE = SERVICE_AGENT. Snowflake is currently the supported resource.
englishSummary.adminImpact: Administrators can use the tutorial to identify excessive permissions and planned remediation for Snowflake AI agents. Preview testing should use a non-production account; any test agent should be removed afterward.

+---
+title: Onboard users with identity verification (Preview)
+description: Configure identity verification onboarding workflows, choose an inline or TAP registration path, and review device and guest-account constraints.
+author: rogulati

+#customer intent: As an identity administrator, I want to configure identity verification during user onboarding so that users verify their identity before registering credentials through a supported flow.
+---
+
+# Onboard users with identity verification (Preview)
+
+Use Lifecycle Workflows in Microsoft Entra ID Governance to initiate identity verification before onboarding and configure credential registration when users start. This guide covers pre-hire and new-hire identity-verification templates, inline passkey registration, and a Temporary Access Pass (TAP) alternative with recommended Conditional Access protection.
+
+The identity-verification and passkey-registration walkthrough uses employee onboarding as its example. Guest onboarding is covered separately through the existing TAP flow; TAP support doesn't enable passkey registration for guest accounts.
+
+Before you start, review the roles, policies, and pilot-account settings in [Prerequisites](#prerequisites).
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+[!INCLUDE [Microsoft Entra ID Governance license](../includes/entra-entra-governance-license.md)]
+
+- At least the [Lifecycle Workflows Administrator](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#lifecycle-workflows-administrator) role to create and manage the workflows.
+- An [ID verification profile](~/verified-id/how-to-create-id-verification-profile.md) with purpose set to `all` or `onboarding`, and the provider configuration required for your verification journey.
+- Pilot user accounts with a populated `otherMails` attribute containing an email address each user can access. The employee example also uses `employeeHireDate` and a rule-based workflow scope.
+- Microsoft Authenticator version 6.2610.7075 or later for Android, or version 6.8.58 or later for iOS, installed on pilot users' devices.
+- A configured [passkey profile](~/identity/authentication/how-to-authentication-passkeys-fido2.md) for the pilot users. Review its **Enforce attestation** setting before choosing the registration path.
+- For manager verification-status emails, a populated manager relationship and a mailbox for the manager.
+- For the TAP alternative, an enabled [TAP authentication methods policy](~/identity/authentication/howto-authentication-temporary-access-pass.md#enable-the-temporary-access-pass-policy), eligible users in scope, and the [TAP task prerequisites](lifecycle-workflow-tasks.md#generate-temporary-access-pass-and-send-via-email-to-users-manager). Creating a TAP doesn't make an account eligible to use it.
+- If you configure the recommended Conditional Access registration policy, at least the [Conditional Access Administrator](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#conditional-access-administrator) role.
+- For the recommended Conditional Access-protected registration, an ID verification profile that targets the new-hire pilot group. Review profile priority if multiple profiles apply. Complete the [Verified ID and FaceCheck setup](~/verified-id/how-to-create-id-verification-profile.md#prerequisites) before testing that registration journey.
+- For identity-verification status and history review, confirm that tenant-wide **Collect identity verification history** is enabled. Creating an ID verification profile enables collection automatically. See [Identity verification collection prerequisites](~/identity/authentication/concept-authentication-verified-id.md#prerequisites).
+
+Before testing onboarding, review [Configure an onboarding and recovery policy](~/identity/conditional-access/policy-require-identity-verification.md#configure-an-onboarding-and-recovery-policy). The combined **Account onboarding and recovery** user action protects both bootstrap journeys. It is separate from the **Register security information** policy used for the TAP alternative in this guide.
+
+Review the [global onboarding and recovery exclusion](~/identity/conditional-access/policy-require-identity-verification.md#enable-the-global-onboarding-and-recovery-exclusion-preview) with your Conditional Access policy owner. This tenant-wide setting excludes the combined user action from **All resources** policies. Policies targeting the user action still apply, and ordinary application access remains subject to resource-access policies. Configure and test the intended user-action policy rather than using the exclusion as a replacement for protecting onboarding.
+
+## Check guest-account eligibility
+
+Lifecycle Workflows supports [member and guest accounts](workflows-faqs.md#can-i-create-custom-workflows-for-guests), but authentication-method eligibility is separate from workflow support. Keep the guest TAP flow separate from the employee passkey-registration walkthrough. Selecting **User** and **otherMails** as email delivery settings doesn't change TAP eligibility.
+
+1. Determine whether the guest account is internal or external. For the account-type distinctions, see [B2B guest user properties](~/external-id/user-properties.md).
+1. Review the [TAP guest-access requirements](~/identity/authentication/howto-authentication-temporary-access-pass.md#guest-access).
+
+    | Account type | TAP boundary |
+    |--------------|--------------|
+    | **Internal guest** | An internal guest can be issued a TAP, subject to the authentication methods policy. If you use the Lifecycle Workflows TAP task, its task prerequisites also apply. |
+    | **External guest** | You can't issue a TAP to the external guest account in the resource tenant. A TAP issued by the user's home tenant can support sign-in under the documented home-tenant and cross-tenant trust conditions. This isn't the resource-tenant TAP task described in this guide. |
+
+1. Use the existing [TAP setup and sign-in guidance](~/identity/authentication/howto-authentication-temporary-access-pass.md) for eligible internal guests. Don't apply the employee passkey-registration walkthrough to guest accounts. [Passkey (FIDO2) registration isn't supported for internal or external guests](~/identity/authentication/how-to-authentication-passkeys-fido2.md#guest-users), and the current preview doesn't add an exception.
+
+The procedures below don't define a guest-specific Verified ID presentation journey.
+
+## Choose a Day 1 registration path
+
+Choose the registration path before creating the new-hire workflow. Day 0 refers to the pre-hire verification phase; Day 1 refers to credential registration when the user starts. These passkey-registration paths don't apply to guest accounts.
+
+1. Review the user's device context and applicable passkey profile.
+1. Select the path that matches the configuration.
+
+    | Configuration | Registration path |
+    |---------------|-------------------|
+    | **A configuration that supports inline registration** | Use **Select verification for Verified ID presentation (Preview)** to present the Verified ID with FaceCheck and complete inline passkey registration. |
+    | **iOS with Enforce attestation enabled** | Inline passkey registration through the presentation task isn't supported. Use the TAP alternative. Conditional Access protection for registration is recommended. |
+    | **Android work-profile passkey registration** | The inline task doesn't register a passkey in the work profile. Use the TAP alternative in the required work-profile context. Conditional Access protection for registration is recommended. |
+    | **A user with an existing strong authentication method** | The onboarding flow redirects to the standard My Sign-ins registration experience instead of inline registration. Don't remove existing authentication methods to force the inline experience. |
+
+1. For the TAP alternative, check TAP task eligibility separately. The existing task documentation lists restrictions on other authentication methods, previous sign-ins, and Microsoft Entra role assignments; TAP isn't a general workaround for those restrictions.
+
+On Android, the user receives the Verified ID in Microsoft Authenticator in the personal profile. The inline presentation task uses that Verified ID with FaceCheck and registers the passkey in the personal profile, not the work profile. This limitation doesn't mean that identity verification or every Android onboarding flow is unsupported.
+
+Using TAP doesn't bypass passkey policy requirements. Keep the required attestation policy in place and use a registration method that satisfies it.
+
+The following diagram summarizes the employee journey and its assurance outcomes. Conditional Access protection is recommended, not required, for using TAP. In the TAP path, completing the recommended CA-protected verification and passkey registration establishes the verified user state, verification event, and high-assurance passkey that TAP alone doesn't establish.
+
+:::image type="complex" source="media/how-to-onboard-users-with-identity-verification/employee-identity-verification-diagram.png" alt-text="Diagram of employee onboarding showing user identity-verification and passkey credential-assurance stamps for inline and TAP paths." lightbox="media/how-to-onboard-users-with-identity-verification/employee-identity-verification-diagram.png":::
+The shared pre-hire phase sends a verification invitation to the user's `otherMails` address. The user completes an email one-time passcode (OTP) check and identity verification, then receives a Verified ID in Microsoft Authenticator.
+
+On Day 1, eligible employees follow one of two registration paths. In the inline path, the user opens a presentation invitation protected by email OTP, presents the Verified ID with FaceCheck, and registers a passkey. Completing this flow stamps the user's identity-verification attribute as verified, records the identity-verification event, and establishes High credential assurance for the new passkey. In the TAP path, the user receives a TAP by email and signs in to start security-information registration.
+
+The TAP path shows recommended Conditional Access protection for **Register security information** with the **Require identity verification** grant control. Completing the required Verified ID presentation with FaceCheck and passkey registration stamps the user's identity-verification state as verified, records the identity-verification event, and establishes High credential assurance for the new passkey. A dashed route shows registration without that recommended policy; TAP alone doesn't establish those outcomes. The dashed route isn't a way to skip an enforced policy.
+
+All routes end with an administrator reviewing the user's identity-verification state and events and the registered passkey's credential assurance and provenance. Lifecycle Workflows uses its explicitly selected profile. Conditional Access resolves the user's profile through group membership and profile priority. All paths remain subject to device, account, and passkey-policy eligibility. Guest TAP access follows separate guidance.
+:::image-end:::
+
+## Configure pre-hire identity verification
+
+Configure the pre-hire workflow for the employee example. This verification stage is used before either Day 1 registration path.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> In the current release, `otherMails` is the only supported and recommended recipient email property for the two identity-verification link tasks. Other custom extension attributes can appear in the picker, but email one-time passcode (OTP) protection isn't supported for them. This link-protection statement doesn't establish OTP protection for the TAP email.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a Lifecycle Workflows Administrator.
+1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Lifecycle workflows** > **Create a workflow**.
+1. Select **Pre-hire identity verification initiation (Preview)**.
+1. On **Basics**, enter the workflow details and review **Trigger type**. The template's default timing is seven days before `employeeHireDate`; see [Lifecycle Workflows templates](lifecycle-workflow-templates.md) for customization options.
+1. On **Configure scope**, define the rule for the intended users. Department values shown in screenshots are examples, not required scope settings.
+1. On **Select identity verification profile**, select the profile from **Verified ID Profile**. Its purpose must be `all` or `onboarding`.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/create-lifecycle-workflow/select-identity-verification-profile.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the identity verification profile selection page, with the Verified ID Profile dropdown and a link to create a profile." lightbox="media/create-lifecycle-workflow/select-identity-verification-profile.png":::
+
+1. On **Review tasks**, review **Select verification profile for identity verification (Preview)** and **Send manager verification status email (Preview)**.
+1. Open the identity-verification task. Set **To recipient** to **User** and **To recipient email address property** to **otherMails**. Select or change the verification profile at the workflow level, not in the task pane.
+1. Review the workflow and create it with the scheduling checkbox cleared for the pilot. For the complete wizard procedure, see [Create a lifecycle workflow](create-lifecycle-workflow.md#create-a-lifecycle-workflow-by-using-a-template-in-the-microsoft-entra-admin-center).
+
+The user opens the invitation sent to their `otherMails` address, completes the email OTP check to access the verification link, and completes the configured verification journey to receive a Verified ID in Microsoft Authenticator.
+
+## Configure new-hire inline registration
+
+Use this path only when the device, account, and passkey profile support inline registration.
+
+1. Create a workflow from **New Hire employee onboarding with identity verification (Preview)**.
+1. Configure the workflow details and intended scope. The template defaults to running on `employeeHireDate`; see [Lifecycle Workflows templates](lifecycle-workflow-templates.md).
+1. On **Select identity verification profile**, select the profile used for the onboarding verification journey.
+1. On **Review tasks**, review the default task order: **Enable User Account**, **Select verification for Verified ID presentation (Preview)**, and **Send manager verification status email (Preview)**.
+1. Open **Select verification for Verified ID presentation (Preview)**. Set **To recipient** to **User** and **To recipient email address property** to **otherMails**.
+1. Review and create the workflow with the scheduling checkbox cleared for the pilot.
+
+The user opens the protected presentation link, presents their Verified ID with FaceCheck, and follows the inline passkey-registration experience. For iOS attestation or Android work-profile constraints, use the alternative below instead.
+
+On successful completion of the inline flow, Microsoft Entra ID stamps the user's identity-verification attribute as `verified` and records the identity-verification event. The new passkey has identity-verified provenance and **High** credential assurance. Review all three outcomes after registration; the user-level state and events are separate from the credential-level assurance. For the shared definitions, see [Identity verification status and history](~/identity/authentication/concept-authentication-methods-manage.md#identity-verification-status-and-history) and [Credential assurance classification](~/identity/authentication/concept-authentication-passkeys-fido2.md#credential-assurance-classification-preview).
+
+## Configure TAP with identity-verification-protected registration
+
+For the employee walkthrough, use the existing TAP task instead of the Day 1 inline presentation task for eligible accounts that need the alternative path. Retain the pre-hire identity-verification workflow. This is a passkey-registration alternative, not the guest TAP access flow.
+
+The recommended TAP onboarding configuration uses a Conditional Access policy with **Require identity verification** to protect security-information registration. This policy isn't required to use TAP. However, TAP issuance or sign-in alone doesn't stamp the user's identity-verification state or establish the new passkey's high-assurance credential stamp.
+
+### Require identity verification for security-information registration
+
+To configure the recommended protection, create this policy before sending the pilot user's TAP. The policy isn't a prerequisite for issuing or emailing a TAP.
+
+Conditional Access doesn't prompt you to select an ID verification profile in the policy. It selects the user's targeted profile based on group membership and profile priority. This selection is separate from the profile explicitly selected in the Lifecycle Workflows wizard.
+
+1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least a Conditional Access Administrator.
+1. Browse to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > **Policies**, and create a policy for the pilot users. Keep your organization's approved emergency access exclusions.
+1. Under **Target resources**, select **User actions** and **Register security information**.
+1. Under **Grant**, select **Require identity verification**. With this policy configured, registration requires presentation of the user's Verified ID with FaceCheck. If you combine grant controls, don't provide an alternative that allows registration without identity verification.
+1. Apply the policy to the pilot before testing the registration journey. A report-only policy doesn't enforce identity verification.
+
+For the registration user action and policy structure, see [Protect security info registration with Conditional Access](~/identity/conditional-access/policy-all-users-security-info-registration.md). That article's existing example isn't the identity-verification policy described here.
+
+### Configure the Day 1 TAP task
+
+Change the registration task, not the pre-hire verification stage.
+
+1. In the new-hire workflow's **Review tasks**, remove **Select verification for Verified ID presentation (Preview)** for this alternative path.
+1. Add the existing [Generate Temporary Access Pass and send via email to user's manager](lifecycle-workflow-tasks.md#generate-temporary-access-pass-and-send-via-email-to-users-manager) task. Its settings pane can display **Generate TAP and Send Email**; despite the catalog name, the recipient is configurable.
+1. In the TAP task, set **To recipient** to **User** and **To recipient email address property** to **otherMails**. Confirm that the user's address is populated and accessible.
+1. Update **Task description** to reflect delivery to the user, for example, "Generate a Temporary Access Pass and email it to the user."
+1. For the default TAP email body, confirm that the user's `manager` relationship is populated. Alternatively, provide a custom body under **Email Customization** to remove this default-body manager requirement. The manager's `mail` attribute isn't required for delivery to `otherMails`.
+1. Set **Activation duration** and **One time use** within the tenant's TAP policy. Check the hire-date start time and TAP lifetime so that the code is valid when registration starts.
+1. Review the remaining new-hire tasks, including account enablement and the manager notification, and create the workflow with the scheduling checkbox cleared for the pilot.
+
+The user signs in with the TAP and starts standard security-information registration. If the recommended Conditional Access policy is configured, it requires the user to present the previously issued Verified ID with FaceCheck before completing credential registration. Completing this verification and passkey-registration journey stamps the user's identity-verification state as `verified`, records the identity-verification event, and establishes **High** credential assurance with identity-verified provenance for the new passkey. Adding a policy without completing the user journey doesn't establish these outcomes; issuing, emailing, or signing in with a TAP alone doesn't establish them either.
+
+For Android work-profile registration, complete credential registration in the intended work-profile context rather than using the personal-profile inline link.
+
+## Verify the onboarding journey
+
+Check workflow execution and user completion separately before expanding beyond the pilot. Keep the pilot workflows enabled (`isEnabled` is `true`) with scheduling disabled (`isSchedulingEnabled` is `false`). Disabling scheduling doesn't prevent on-demand runs; disabling the workflow itself does.
+
+1. [Run the pre-hire workflow on-demand](on-demand-workflow.md) for the pilot user.
+1. Confirm that the user can access the invitation through email OTP, complete verification, and receive the Verified ID.
+1. Run the selected Day 1 workflow on-demand and check [workflow and task status](check-status-workflow.md).
+1. Complete the selected registration path as the pilot user. Confirm that the passkey is registered in the intended device/profile context. If you configured the recommended Conditional Access policy for the TAP alternative, confirm that it resolves the intended ID verification profile through group targeting and priority and requires Verified ID presentation with FaceCheck.
+1. [Review the assurance stamps](#review-the-assurance-stamps) for the user and the newly registered passkey separately from the workflow's task status. Successful task execution or email delivery alone doesn't confirm these outcomes.
+1. Enable scheduling only after validating the intended user scope and onboarding journey.
+
+The three Preview identity-verification tasks are available in Microsoft Graph `/beta`, not `/v1.0`. Workflow configuration in this guide uses the Microsoft Entra admin center; the assurance review below also includes a Microsoft Graph beta query. For workflow API guidance, see [Create a lifecycle workflow by using Microsoft Graph](create-lifecycle-workflow.md#create-a-lifecycle-workflow-by-using-microsoft-graph).
+
+### Review the assurance stamps
+
+Review the user's current identity-verification state, verification events, and the new passkey's credential assurance separately. A `verified` user-level state doesn't establish the assurance of every credential on the account. The passkey's displayed **Credential assurance** classification is **High**, **Medium**, or **Low**, not a second user-level `verified` status.
+
+Before reviewing these outcomes, confirm the following reporting prerequisites:
+
+- **Licensing:** Confirm entitlement to identity-verification status, history, and credential-provenance reporting in [Identity verification licensing](~/fundamentals/licensing.md#identity-verification). A Lifecycle Workflows license alone doesn't establish entitlement to these reports.
+- **Collection:** Confirm that tenant-wide **Collect identity verification history** is enabled. Creating an ID verification profile enables collection automatically. See [Identity verification collection prerequisites](~/identity/authentication/concept-authentication-verified-id.md#prerequisites).
+- **Read access:** To review the user's **Identity verification** page, use an account assigned the [Security Reader](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#security-reader) role. Separately, confirm permission to read the user's passkey details. For the Graph review, also confirm the application's [permissions to read the user's FIDO2 methods](/graph/api/fido2authenticationmethod-list?view=graph-rest-beta&preserve-view=true#permissions). Don't assume the Lifecycle Workflows Administrator role grants these reporting or Graph permissions.
+
+These checks establish whether you can view the outcomes; they don't establish that verification or registration succeeded. This read-only review doesn't require permissions to overwrite identity-verification events or credential provenance. An unavailable view isn't evidence that verification failed.
+
+1. In the Microsoft Entra admin center, open the pilot user's **Identity verification** page. Review the current status and the verification event for the completed Day 1 journey. This page is separate from **Authentication methods**. See [Identity verification status and history](~/identity/authentication/concept-authentication-methods-manage.md#identity-verification-status-and-history).
+1. On the user's **Authentication methods** page, open the passkey registered during this pilot. Review its **Credential assurance** classification and [credential provenance](~/identity/authentication/concept-authentication-passkeys-fido2.md#credential-provenance).
+1. In Microsoft Graph Explorer, sign in to the same pilot tenant with the [permissions to read the user's FIDO2 methods](/graph/api/fido2authenticationmethod-list?view=graph-rest-beta&preserve-view=true#permissions). Run this preview query, replacing `{userObjectId}` with the pilot user's object ID:
+
+    ```http
+    GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/users/{userObjectId}/authentication/fido2methods?$select=provenance
+    ```
+
+1. Confirm that the newly registered method includes `provenance`. Check the credential's assurance outcome, not just the presence of that property. If you collect review evidence, redact the response and retain the request ID.
+1. Compare the user state, verification event, and credential assurance with the expected outcome for the completed journey:
+
+    | Completed journey | User identity-verification state | Identity-verification event | New passkey credential assurance |
+    |-------------------|----------------------------------|-----------------------------|----------------------------------|
+    | Inline Verified ID presentation with FaceCheck and passkey registration | Stamped as `verified`. | Recorded for the completed verification. | **High**, with identity-verified provenance. |
+    | TAP sign-in followed by CA-required Verified ID presentation with FaceCheck and passkey registration | Stamped as `verified`. | Recorded for the completed verification. | **High**, with identity-verified provenance. |
+    | TAP-only registration without the recommended identity-verification policy | TAP alone doesn't establish this stamp. | TAP alone isn't an identity-verification event. | TAP alone doesn't establish a high-assurance stamp. |
+
+The TAP-only row describes what TAP establishes, not the user's existing verification state or the assurance of other passkeys. If an expected stamp is missing, don't treat workflow success or email delivery as confirmation of high-assurance onboarding.
+
+For the shared reporting model and investigation guidance, see [Identity verification reporting](~/identity/authentication/howto-authentication-methods-activity.md#identity-verification-reporting). Registering a new passkey in an identity-verified journey is distinct from using an existing passkey with identity verification; see [Credential assurance classification](~/identity/authentication/concept-authentication-passkeys-fido2.md#credential-assurance-classification-preview).
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Lifecycle Workflows templates](lifecycle-workflow-templates.md)
+- [Lifecycle workflow tasks](lifecycle-workflow-tasks.md)
+- [Configure Temporary Access Pass](~/identity/authentication/howto-authentication-temporary-access-pass.md)

englishSummary.headline: Identity-verification onboarding workflows are documented
englishSummary.summary: A new guide explains how Lifecycle Workflows can initiate identity verification during employee onboarding, with inline passkey registration or a Temporary Access Pass (TAP). It also documents prerequisites, Conditional Access considerations, and guest-account limitations.
englishSummary.adminImpact: Administrators can plan pilot deployments with the required roles, profiles, policies, app versions, and separate guest TAP handling.

+++ b/docs/identity/conditional-access/policy-require-identity-verification.md
@@ -0,0 +1,276 @@
+---
+title: Conditional Access Identity Verification
+description: Configure and test Conditional Access identity verification policies for resource access, onboarding, account recovery, and risk-based scenarios.
+author: tilarso
+ms.author: tilarso
+ms.service: entra-id
+ms.subservice: conditional-access
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/11/2026
+ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-108
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+#customer intent: As an administrator, I want to configure identity verification policies so that users complete the appropriate verification journey without weakening resource protection.
+---
+
+# Require identity verification with Conditional Access
+
+Use Conditional Access to require identity verification for protected resource access or to add security to onboarding and account recovery. Choose the policy's scenario, configure an eligible verification profile, and test the user journey and policy outcome before rollout.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+Prepare the following before configuring a pilot:
+
+- A test environment with the identity verification control and intended target available.
+- The applicable [identity verification licenses](../../fundamentals/licensing.md#identity-verification).
+- An eligible [identity verification profile](../authentication/concept-authentication-verified-id.md#create-and-manage-identity-verification-profiles), with the provider or issuer setup required for your scenario.
+- To review users' verification status and history, enable [verification data collection](../authentication/concept-authentication-verified-id.md#prerequisites).
+
+    > [!NOTE]
+    > Creating an identity verification profile automatically enables **Collect identity verification history**; otherwise, enable it in the authentication methods policy under **Verified ID** > **Configure** > **Data collection**.
+
+- For onboarding or recovery, a configured [Lifecycle Workflows onboarding journey](../../id-governance/tutorial-onboard-custom-workflow-portal.md) or [account recovery journey](../authentication/how-to-account-recovery-enable.md). A Conditional Access policy doesn't replace that setup.
+- Approved pilot users, selected resources or actions, a support owner, and a recorded policy baseline and rollback plan.
+- Working emergency access accounts excluded from the pilot, following [Manage emergency access accounts](../role-based-access-control/security-emergency-access.md).
+- For journeys that use Microsoft Authenticator, meet the requirements in [Enable passkeys in Microsoft Authenticator](../authentication/how-to-enable-authenticator-passkey.md). If the journey includes passkey registration, also complete the platform-specific passkey-provider setup.
+
+
+## Choose the scenario and target
+
+Use the scenario to select the policy boundary:
+
+| Scenario | Policy intent | Configuration guidance |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Resource access | Require verification after initial authentication for a protected resource. | [Configure a resource-access policy](#configure-a-resource-access-policy). |
+| Onboarding and recovery | Protect the bootstrap journey before the user has established or restored credentials. | [Configure an onboarding and recovery policy](#configure-an-onboarding-and-recovery-policy). |
+| Risk-based verification | Require verification when a supported user-risk or sign-in-risk condition applies. | [Configure a risk-based policy](#configure-a-risk-based-policy). |
+
+1. Identify the protected resources or journey and the pilot users who need it.
+1. Check [credential and profile eligibility](../authentication/concept-authentication-verified-id.md#credential-support-by-scenario). A profile or credential accepted for one scenario isn't necessarily eligible for another.
+1. Review all applicable policies, including policies targeting all resources. Identify requirements users can't satisfy before onboarding or recovery completes.
+1. Record inclusions, exclusions, and other applicable grant and session controls. Use only combinations supported for the selected target.
+
+For resource-access policies, identity verification follows initial authentication and precedes additional MFA or authentication-strength requirements. That ordering doesn't establish support for authentication strength in onboarding and recovery policies.
+
+## Configure a resource-access policy
+
+Start with a small pilot scope.
+
+1. Select the approved pilot users and test resources. Record inclusions and exclusions, including emergency access.
+1. Confirm the profile is eligible for resource-access verification and assigned to the intended users.
+1. Configure **Require identity verification** for the selected resource scope. Don't substitute **Require risk remediation**, which has separate behavior.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/policy-require-identity-verification/require-identity-verification-grant-control.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Conditional Access Grant pane with Grant access selected and Require identity verification checked." lightbox="media/policy-require-identity-verification/require-identity-verification-grant-control.png":::
+
+1. Under **Conditions** > **Client apps**, set **Configure** to **Yes** and select only **Browser** and **Mobile apps and desktop clients**. Don't leave the policy targeting all client app types.
+1. Review the effective policy set. Confirm other policies don't prevent completion of the verification or supported inline issuance journey.
+1. Use [report-only mode](concept-conditional-access-report-only.md) for initial impact evaluation where supported. Keep the policy out of production enforcement until the pilot review is complete.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> New Conditional Access policies apply to all client app types by default, including legacy clients. Legacy client types aren't supported for identity verification step-up, and including them can cause the flow to fail. Explicitly configure the [client apps condition](concept-conditional-access-conditions.md#client-apps) before testing the policy.
+
+
+When testing, check whether existing verification satisfies the policy and when a new challenge is required. Don't infer verification reuse, freshness, expiration, or revocation behavior from credential issuance alone.
+
+### Link to Windows compatibility
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> Identity verification step-up and recovery aren't currently supported when initiated from a mobile app while Link to Windows is the active broker on the device. Support for both features is planned in Link to Windows version **1.26111.xxx**, starting **November 30**. Update Link to Windows to that version when it becomes available.
+
+### Android work-profile compatibility during preview
+
+Before enabling identity verification step-up for Android users whose Conditional Access policies also use **Require device to be marked as compliant**, identify whether work-profile enrollment uses Android Management API (AM API) or Enterprise Mobility Management API (EMM API).
+
+During AM API work-profile setup, users can be required to sign in before work apps are installed. Verified ID presentation can't complete in that setup context, which can block enrollment when both policies apply. Don't apply the identity verification step-up policy to AM API work-profile setup flows during preview. Retain the required device protection.
+
+| Work-profile enrollment | Identity verification step-up with a device-compliance requirement | Deployment guidance |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Android Management API (AM API) | This combination isn't supported during preview. | Don't enable the identity verification step-up policy for this group of users. |
+| Enterprise Mobility Management API (EMM API) | Supported when prerequisites are met. | Use Intune to deploy Microsoft Authenticator and a supported browser into the work profile before enabling the identity verification step-up policy. Users might be unable to complete verification if either app is unavailable. |
+
+This restriction doesn't mean that onboarding and recovery are unsupported for Android Management API (AM API) users. Configure those journeys to issue a Temporary Access Pass (TAP) at completion instead of requiring passkey setup. A device-bound passkey created in the personal profile can't currently be used from the work profile. See [Enable passkeys in Microsoft Authenticator](../authentication/how-to-enable-authenticator-passkey.md).
+
+The TAP guidance addresses passkey registration, not the step-up block during work-profile setup. The global onboarding and recovery exclusion doesn't establish support for this resource-access step-up combination.
+
+<!-- TODO: Confirm how administrators identify Android Management API (AM API) versus Enterprise Mobility Management API (EMM API) enrollment, and supported work-profile browsers and versions before publication. -->
+
+## Configure an onboarding and recovery policy
+
+Use the **Account onboarding and recovery** user action to protect bootstrap separately from ordinary resource access. Identity-verified onboarding and account recovery require identity verification regardless of whether a Conditional Access policy requires it.
+
+1. Identify whether the pilot covers onboarding, recovery, or both. Confirm the available action scope; don't assume the combined action supports independent assignments for each journey.
+1. Record the pilot group, emergency access exclusions, and approved handling of noninteractive accounts.
+1. Under **Target resources**, select **User actions**, then select **Account onboarding and recovery**, as shown in the following screenshot.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/policy-require-identity-verification/account-setup-recovery-user-action.png" alt-text="Screenshot of Conditional Access target resources with User actions selected and Account onboarding and recovery checked. A callout requires the identity verification grant control and an identity verification profile." lightbox="media/policy-require-identity-verification/account-setup-recovery-user-action.png":::
+
+1. Under **Conditions** > **Client apps**, set **Configure** to **Yes**, explicitly select **Browser** and **Mobile apps and desktop clients**, and select **Done**.
+1. Configure the intended verification journey and eligible profile. Recovery requires identity verification; scoping the policy isn't a replacement for recovery setup.
+1. Review the prerequisites in [Enable passkeys in Microsoft Authenticator](../authentication/how-to-enable-authenticator-passkey.md). For users enrolled through Android Management API (AM API), configure TAP issuance at completion instead of requiring passkey setup.
+1. Review the [control limitations](#review-control-limitations). Don't require unsupported controls for this action.
+1. Review applicable resource policies together with the action policy. To exclude the onboarding and recovery action from **All resources** policies, review and approve the tenant-wide impact, then [enable the global exclusion](#enable-the-global-onboarding-and-recovery-exclusion-preview). Policies targeting the user action still apply.
+1. Save the configuration and rollback record before conducting an enforcement test.
+
+The action boundary isn't a general-purpose access bypass. After onboarding or recovery, ordinary resource-access policies still protect application access. Don't exempt users from those policies merely to make bootstrap work.
+
+Before enabling onboarding or account recovery, review the applicable Conditional Access policies and test each intended journey with a small group of users. Successful identity verification alone doesn't confirm that credential registration or recovery can complete. If a saved policy blocks the journey, review the Conditional Access results in the sign-in logs to identify the blocking policy.
+
+## Enable the global onboarding and recovery exclusion (preview)
+
+Without this exclusion, policies targeting **All resources** also apply to onboarding and account recovery events. Those policies can prevent users from establishing or restoring credentials. Enabling the exclusion removes the **Account onboarding and recovery** user action from **All resources** policies; policies that directly target the user action still apply.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> This setting affects all policies targeting **All resources**, not just the policy used in your pilot. Review and approve the tenant-wide impact before changing it. Configure and test the intended user-action policy rather than treating the exclusion as a replacement for protecting onboarding and recovery.
+
+### Review the excluded apps and permissions
+
+The global exclusion covers the following client-to-resource requests and explicit scopes or permissions for onboarding and account recovery. Review both the client app and resource app when assessing the exclusion's impact.
+
+| Client app | Resource app | Scopes or permissions |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| My Sign-Ins (`19db86c3-b2b9-44cc-b339-36da233a3be2`) | Microsoft Graph (`00000003-0000-0000-c000-000000000000`) | `AuditLog.Read.All`, `Directory.Read.All`, `email`, `openid`, `Policy.Read.All`, `profile`, `User.Read`, `UserAuthenticationMethod.Read`, `UserAuthenticationMethod.ReadWrite`, `AgentIdentity.Read.All`, `CrossTenantInformation.ReadBasic.All`, `User.RevokeSessions.All`, `offline_access`, `Organization.Read.All`, `OrganizationalBranding.Read.All`. |
+| My Sign-Ins (`19db86c3-b2b9-44cc-b339-36da233a3be2`) | My Sign-Ins (`19db86c3-b2b9-44cc-b339-36da233a3be2`) | `UserAuthenticationMethod.Read`, `AuditLog.Read.All`, `Directory.Read.All`, `Policy.Read.All`, `User.Read`, `UserAuthenticationMethod.ReadWrite`, `AgentIdentity.Read.All`, `CrossTenantInformation.ReadBasic.All`, `User.RevokeSessions.All`, `Organization.Read.All`, `OrganizationalBranding.Read.All`. |
+| Azure ESTS Service (`00000001-0000-0000-c000-000000000000`) | Microsoft Graph (`00000003-0000-0000-c000-000000000000`) | `UserAuthMethod-TAP.ReadWrite`. |
+
+This table lists explicit scopes and permissions, not every request covered by the exclusion. It doesn't mean that all requests to Microsoft Graph or My Sign-Ins are excluded. The setting is a Conditional Access exclusion, not a grant of the listed API permissions.
+
+This global user-action exclusion is separate from excluding a resource in an individual policy. For background on how resource exclusions affect scope evaluation, see [Improved enforcement for All resources policies with resource exclusions](concept-enforcement-resource-exclusions.md). Don't use that article's baseline-scope list as the scope of the onboarding and recovery exclusion.
+
+### Enable and validate the exclusion
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) with an account permitted to manage Conditional Access settings.
+1. Browse to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > **Settings (Preview)**.
+1. Under **Global exclusions**, enable the **Account onboarding and recovery (Preview)** exclusion.
+1. Verify that the row's **Policy state** shows **Enabled**.
+
+:::image type="content" source="media/policy-require-identity-verification/global-account-setup-recovery-exclusion.png" alt-text="Screenshot of Conditional Access Settings (Preview), showing the Account onboarding and recovery global exclusion with Policy state Enabled." lightbox="media/policy-require-identity-verification/global-account-setup-recovery-exclusion.png":::
+
+The settings page labels the exclusion **Account onboarding and recovery (Preview)**. It applies to the **Account onboarding and recovery** user action used in policy targeting.
+
+After enabling the exclusion, test onboarding and recovery with approved pilot users. Review Conditional Access results in the sign-in logs to confirm that:
+
+- **All resources** policies no longer apply to the onboarding and recovery user action.
+- Policies targeting the user action still apply, including when a user fails to meet their requirements.
+- Ordinary application access after onboarding or recovery remains subject to applicable resource-access policies.
+
+Record the exclusion's previous state in your rollback plan. If you disable the exclusion, **All resources** policies again apply to onboarding and recovery events.
+
+## Review control limitations
+
+Policies targeting the onboarding and recovery user action don't support the full set of controls available for ordinary resource access. The following controls aren't supported for these journeys:
+
+- **Terms of use**.
+- **Require authentication strength**.
+
+Most other Microsoft Entra-specific controls also aren't supported for this action. Don't assume a control is supported because you can configure it in a policy. These examples aren't a complete compatibility matrix.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> There's no current plan or timeline to add support for these controls. Don't design onboarding or recovery policies that depend on them.
+
+For recovery, unsupported conditions or controls can block the journey or leave intended requirements unenforced. Test the applicable policies and resulting enforcement, not just whether the user can finish recovery.
+
+These limitations apply to onboarding and recovery user-action policies. They don't remove support for these controls in ordinary resource-access policies.
+
+### Troubleshoot onboarding and recovery policy configuration errors
+
+The following validation errors can occur when you create or update a Conditional Access policy for the Account recovery user action. A policy-save error is different from a saved policy blocking a user's recovery attempt. Don't assume that an error for the Account recovery action establishes the same restriction for an ordinary resource-access policy.
+
+| Error | Message | What to check |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| 1329 | Account recovery user action only supports 'browser' and 'mobileAppsAndDesktopClients' client app types. | Explicitly configure the **Client apps** condition and select **Browser** and **Mobile apps and desktop clients** for the Account recovery user action. Don't leave this condition unconfigured. Confirm that you can save the policy before rollout. |
+| 1248 | GPS based named locations are not supported for account recovery user action condition. | Check whether the named location uses GPS coordinates or IP addresses. If the location is IP-based but the same error appears, contact support with the policy validation details. The error alone doesn't establish that IP-based location exclusions are unsupported. |
+
+Don't disable unrelated policies or broadly exclude users to work around a validation error. Review the intended recovery scope with your policy owner before changing the configuration.
+
+<!-- TODO: Conditional Access SME: confirm these validation messages and remaining restrictions for the target release. Validate the GPS restriction and investigate error 1248 with IP-based named-location exclusions before documenting a supported exclusion procedure or workaround. -->
+
+## Configure a risk-based policy
+
+Use **Require Identity Verification (preview)** with a supported **User risk** or **Sign-in risk** condition. Successful verification remediates the risk targeted by the triggering policy: user risk or sign-in risk. Failed verification doesn't remediate risk.
+
+Risk-based Conditional Access policies currently don't apply to onboarding actions.
+
+1. Choose the risk condition and users for the pilot. Keep user-risk and sign-in-risk conditions in separate policies.
+1. [Create an identity verification profile](../authentication/concept-authentication-verified-id.md#create-and-manage-identity-verification-profiles) with **Profile purpose** set to **All** or **Verification**, a credential type eligible for the risk scenario, and scope that includes the pilot users. For tenant-issued credentials, select **Verification**. Don't use an **Onboarding**- or **Recovery**-purpose profile for this resource-access policy.
+1. Configure the verification requirement and review the effective policy set.
+1. Define separate success criteria for completed verification, the access decision, and the applicable risk outcome.
+1. Test the supported remediation journey with approved pilot users before expanding scope.
+
+**Require risk remediation** remains a distinct adaptive control. Selecting it doesn't automatically require identity verification. Don't copy its session revocation, password-change, or reauthentication behavior into an identity verification policy.
+
+See [Identity Protection policies](../../id-protection/concept-identity-protection-policies.md) and [Configure risk policies](../../id-protection/howto-identity-protection-configure-risk-policies.md) for the product-owned remediation guidance.
+
+## Test verification and credential issuance
+
+Report-only mode evaluates which policies could apply without enforcing them or triggering identity verification. Conduct a separately approved enforcement test with the pilot scope.
+
+1. Test a user who already has an eligible credential and a user who doesn't.
+1. Complete credential presentation and verification, then check the protected resource's access decision.
+1. Where supported, use **Get Verified ID** on the challenge to test inline issuance and presentation of the resulting credential.
+1. Test cancellation, timeout, provider failure, missing credentials, and retry. Confirm these outcomes don't grant access protected by an unsatisfied requirement.
+1. Review how the user returns to or restarts the original access attempt. Don't assume issuance guarantees automatic return or access.
+1. Review policy results and verification evidence independently. For risk-based policies, also inspect the relevant risk record.
+
+### Validate inline issuance separately
+
+Presentation uses a credential the user holds; issuance gives the user a credential. Successful issuance alone doesn't satisfy the originating verification challenge.
+
+- **Tenant-issued custom Verified ID:** The challenge redirects to the tenant-configured issuance site.
+- **Third-party identity verification:** The challenge uses the inline integration pattern also used by onboarding and recovery.
+- **Verified Employee:** Inline issuance is deferred. Employee ID presentation eligibility doesn't establish support for inline issuance or risk remediation.
+
+Conditional Access step-up uses inline issuance rather than My Account as its issuance surface. My Account self-service issuance is a separate task. Don't add broad My Account or dependency exclusions to work around an issuance loop.
+
+<!-- TODO: Confirm credential eligibility, secure issuance redirects, supported clients, cancellation/retry behavior, and exact return/restart instructions. -->
+
+### Test onboarding and recovery enforcement
+
+Identity-verified onboarding and account recovery always require identity verification, independently of Conditional Access policy requirements. A report-only policy doesn't trigger that verification; the onboarding or recovery journey does.
+
+[Report-only mode](concept-conditional-access-report-only.md) excludes policies in the user-action scope from evaluation. Don't rely on it to validate this action unless support is confirmed in your environment.
+
+1. Evaluate ordinary resource-policy impact in report-only mode where supported.
+1. Use an approved, isolated enforcement pilot for action policies when report-only isn't supported. Missing results aren't a passing test.
+1. Test onboarding with a user who hasn't established the credentials required for ordinary access.
+1. Test recovery with a user who can't use existing credentials. Check that unrelated resource requirements don't prevent entry.
+1. For Android users enrolled through Android Management API (AM API), verify that onboarding and recovery complete with TAP issuance rather than requiring passkey setup. For an Enterprise Mobility Management API (EMM API) step-up pilot with a device-compliance requirement, verify that Authenticator and a supported browser are available in the work profile.
+1. Test failed verification, cancellation, and retry, then test application access after each successful journey.
+1. Verify that normal resource policies and emergency access remain effective.
+
+Review the [recovery setup guide](../authentication/how-to-account-recovery-enable.md) and validate device and registration support for your pilot; don't apply recovery platform behavior to onboarding without checking its own requirements.
+
+## Review evidence and resolve failures
+
+Use policy results, verification records, and the journey stage to narrow the investigation. During preview, credential provenance is recorded only for passkey credentials; provenance reporting doesn't provide credential-provenance policy enforcement.
+
+| Symptom | Next check |
+| --- | --- |
+| Verification isn't offered. | Check policy scope, profile eligibility and assignment, and whether the policy is only in report-only mode. |
+| Sign-in fails with `AADSTS10020005: No valid VidProfile data found for the tenant.` | Check whether a valid identity verification profile is available to the user for onboarding, recovery, or step-up. See [Troubleshoot an unavailable identity verification profile](../authentication/concept-authentication-verified-id.md#troubleshoot-an-unavailable-identity-verification-profile). |
+| Identity verification step-up fails with the default client-app selection. | Under **Conditions** > **Client apps**, select only **Browser** and **Mobile apps and desktop clients**. Legacy client types aren't supported for this step-up flow. |
+| Identity verification step-up can't complete on an Android device with a work profile. | Check [Android work-profile compatibility](#android-work-profile-compatibility-during-preview). The step-up and managed-device policy combination isn't supported for Android Management API (AM API) enrollment during preview. For Enterprise Mobility Management API (EMM API) enrollment, verify that both Authenticator and a supported browser are deployed in the work profile. |
+| Issuance returns to another challenge or requests authentication again. | Check the approved issuer and return-path contract. Don't assume this proves verification failure. |
+| Verification completes but access fails. | Review other applicable policies and the verification outcome separately. |
+| Onboarding or recovery can't start. | Check whether **All resources** policies are preventing bootstrap and review the [global onboarding and recovery exclusion](#enable-the-global-onboarding-and-recovery-exclusion-preview). Policies targeting the user action still apply when the exclusion is enabled. Don't remove all-resource protection wholesale. |
+| Recovery completes but an expected requirement isn't enforced. | Review the [control limitations](#review-control-limitations) and all applicable policies. Completion isn't proof that every configured requirement was enforced. |
+| Report-only has no action result. | Check evaluation scope. An absent result isn't evidence of successful enforcement. |
+| Verification succeeds but risk remains. | Continue the [risk investigation](../../id-protection/howto-identity-protection-investigate-risk.md). Don't dismiss risk merely to make a pilot pass. |
+| The user can't complete verification. | Use the approved support path; don't collect raw identity documents or biometric material in a support ticket. |
+
+Review [Conditional Access insights and reporting](howto-conditional-access-insights-reporting.md), [sign-in log details](../monitoring-health/concept-sign-in-log-activity-details.md), and [audit activities](../monitoring-health/reference-audit-activities.md) for product-owned evidence guidance. Use [authentication methods activity](../authentication/howto-authentication-methods-activity.md) to review account verification evidence and [passkeys (FIDO2)](../authentication/concept-authentication-passkeys-fido2.md) for credential-level evidence.
+
+For possible journey events and their scenario markers, see [Verified ID audit activities](../monitoring-health/reference-audit-activities.md#verified-id). A `Verified ID verification completed` event doesn't establish a Conditional Access grant or risk remediation. Review the sign-in and risk records separately.
+
+<!-- TODO: Validate released audit/sign-in fields and event availability, profile/extension failure evidence, concurrent-session behavior, verification reuse, and expected remediation timing. Don't infer risk-state values from verification completion. -->
+
+## Roll out or restore the pilot
+
+Expand only after supported targeting, verification and issuance outcomes, remediation outcomes where applicable, resource protection, failure handling, and emergency access tests pass. Keep exclusions scoped, documented, and approved.
+
+If testing fails, restore the recorded policy configuration and stop expansion. Remove pilot-only assignments or exclusions after testing while retaining approved emergency access. Don't weaken unrelated production policies as a recovery workaround.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [High assurance overview](../../verified-id/high-assurance.md).
+- [Conditional Access grant controls](concept-conditional-access-grant.md).
+- [Conditional Access target resources and user actions](concept-conditional-access-cloud-apps.md).
+- [Protect security information registration](policy-all-users-security-info-registration.md).
