+++ b/docs/verified-id/high-assurance.md
@@ -0,0 +1,92 @@
+---
+title: Microsoft Entra High Assurance
+description: Plan Microsoft Entra high assurance scenarios for identity-verified onboarding, resource access, risk remediation, and account recovery.
+author: tilarso
+ms.author: tilarso
+contributors: rogulati
+ms.topic: concept-article
+ms.date: 11/10/2026
+ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-108
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+#customer intent: As an identity architect, I want to understand high assurance scenarios so that I can choose the supported Microsoft Entra capabilities for onboarding, access, and recovery.
+---
+
+# Microsoft Entra high assurance overview
+
+Microsoft Entra high assurance is a scenario across Microsoft Entra products that connects identity verification with supported onboarding, credential registration, protected access, risk remediation, and account recovery. It helps you ensure the right person is accessing the intended account across the lifecycle of the user, including capabilities to record and review verification history along with details on how a credential was registered.
+
+This overview describes the preview scope and connects you to the product-owned configuration guides. Identity verification supports these journeys; it isn't itself an authentication method or a replacement for sign-in, MFA, or self-service password reset.
+
+## Supported journeys
+
+Use the journey to choose its configuration and policy owner.
+
+| Journey | Purpose | Product-owned guidance |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Identity-verified onboarding | Verify the new hire before credential bootstrap, with Lifecycle Workflows orchestration. | [Onboard users with identity verification](../id-governance/how-to-onboard-users-with-identity-verification.md). |
+| Verification for resource access | Require identity verification after initial authentication for a protected resource or action. | [Conditional Access identity verification policy](../identity/conditional-access/policy-require-identity-verification.md#configure-a-resource-access-policy). |
+| Risk remediation | Require verification when a supported user-risk or sign-in-risk condition applies. | [Identity verification for risk](../id-protection/concept-identity-protection-policies.md#identity-verification-for-risk). |
+| Account recovery | Verify account ownership when existing authentication methods are unavailable, then register replacement credentials. | [Account recovery overview](../identity/authentication/concept-account-recovery-overview.md). |
+
+Onboarding and recovery establish or restore credentials. They aren't substitutes for ordinary resource-access policies. Conditional Access can add security to those flows through the onboarding and recovery action.
+
+## Shared verification profiles
+
+An identity verification profile connects the scenario to its provider, accepted credential, account-validation configuration, and user scope. Configure shared profiles before the workflow or policy that uses them.
+
+The [identity verification profile overview](../identity/authentication/concept-authentication-verified-id.md) is the authoritative home for profile setup and the [credential/scenario matrix](../identity/authentication/concept-authentication-verified-id.md#credential-support-by-scenario). Link to that matrix when planning a journey rather than maintaining separate eligibility tables.
+
+Creating a profile automatically enables tenant-wide collection of users' identity verification history. Review the profile article's [collection prerequisites](../identity/authentication/concept-authentication-verified-id.md#prerequisites) before reviewing status and history.
+
+## Verification and credential registration
+
+To establish a high-assurance passkey, complete identity verification as part of a supported credential-registration journey. The passkey's recorded provenance connects the new registration to the verified identity and records its credential assurance classification.
+
+Use [credential provenance and assurance classification](../identity/authentication/concept-authentication-passkeys-fido2.md#credential-assurance-classification-preview) to understand the individual passkey's **Low**, **Medium**, or **High** assurance. Use [identity verification status and history](../identity/authentication/concept-authentication-methods-manage.md#identity-verification-status-and-history) to review the account-level verification evidence. During preview, credential assurance classification and provenance are available only for passkeys.
+
+New passkeys registered through supported identity-verified onboarding, recovery, or other registration journeys have **High** assurance when their chain of trust is intact. An existing passkey used with identity verification has **Medium** assurance. Expiration or invalidation of supporting identity verification lowers affected **High** and **Medium** passkeys to **Low**. Successful reverification restores their previous level without requiring new registration for a previously **High** passkey. These changes affect only passkeys whose provenance relies on that verification. See the [credential assurance lifecycle](../identity/authentication/concept-authentication-passkeys-fido2.md#credential-assurance-lifecycle) for the differences between these journeys and changes to trust.
+
+Credential issuance gives a user a credential. Presentation uses an existing credential to satisfy a verification request. Successful issuance alone doesn't establish that the user completed the originating challenge or gained access.
+
+For protected resource access, verification follows initial authentication and precedes additional MFA or authentication-strength requirements. A user who needs a credential uses the supported inline issuance path from the verification challenge.
+
+Successful recovery records verification history on the user's account. When a user registers a passkey during recovery, provenance is recorded on that credential. Administrators use verification status and history to understand how a passkey was established and should be trusted.
+
+During preview, credential provenance is recorded only for passkey credentials. Reporting doesn't provide credential-provenance policy enforcement or establish that every credential on a verified account has the same provenance. See [user verification status and history](../identity/authentication/concept-authentication-methods-manage.md#identity-verification-status-and-history), [passkey credential provenance](../identity/authentication/concept-authentication-passkeys-fido2.md#credential-provenance), and [identity verification reporting](../identity/authentication/howto-authentication-methods-activity.md#identity-verification-reporting) for the product-owned evidence guidance.
+
+## Preview limitations
+
+Plan each scenario against its supported configuration:
+
+- **Cloud availability:** During preview, high assurance scenarios are available only in the Microsoft public cloud. National and sovereign clouds aren't supported.
+- **Credential eligibility:** Use the shared profile matrix. Employee ID presentation support doesn't establish support for Employee ID inline issuance or risk remediation.
+- **Authenticator and Android work profiles:** Review [Authenticator preview prerequisites](../identity/authentication/how-to-enable-authenticator-passkey.md#identity-verified-onboarding-and-recovery-during-preview) before onboarding or recovery. Android Management API (AM API) users should complete those journeys with TAP issuance rather than being required to set up a passkey. For identity verification step-up with a device-compliance requirement, review the [Android Management API (AM API) and Enterprise Mobility Management API (EMM API) compatibility guidance](../identity/conditional-access/policy-require-identity-verification.md#android-work-profile-compatibility-during-preview).
+- **Onboarding and recovery policies:** Terms of use, authentication strength, and most other Microsoft Entra-specific controls aren't supported for this user action. There's no current plan or timeline to add support. These limitations don't remove support in ordinary resource-access policies. See [control limitations](../identity/conditional-access/policy-require-identity-verification.md#review-control-limitations).
+- **Recovery registration:** When passkey attestation is required, TAP-free registration is supported only on Android. iOS continues to receive a Temporary Access Pass (TAP), even with issuance turned off. Review [account recovery setup](../identity/authentication/how-to-account-recovery-enable.md); don't assume recovery platform behavior also applies to onboarding.
+- **Risk outcomes:** Successful identity verification remediates user risk or sign-in risk, depending on the risk condition in the triggering policy. Failed verification doesn't remediate risk. Risk-based Conditional Access policies currently don't apply to onboarding actions. Review verification completion, the access decision, and the risk record separately. **Require risk remediation** is a distinct adaptive control.
+- **Evaluation:** Report-only mode evaluates which policies could apply without triggering identity verification. Identity-verified onboarding and account recovery still require identity verification independently of Conditional Access policy requirements. Use the [CA walkthrough](../identity/conditional-access/policy-require-identity-verification.md) to plan testing.
+
+<!-- TODO: Confirm tenant rollout, supported clients, final roles, portal labels, and released telemetry before publication. This overview doesn't establish GA or universal tenant availability. -->
+
+## Deployment sequence
+
+Build the shared foundation before enabling individual journeys:
+
+- **Profiles and eligibility:** Configure the provider or issuer, account-validation rules, profile purpose, and user scope using the profile guide.
+- **Product configuration:** Prepare Lifecycle Workflows, recovery settings, or risk policy configuration for the selected journey.
+- **Policy boundaries:** Configure the applicable Conditional Access policy. Review bootstrap conflicts, exclusions, emergency access, and control limitations together.
+- **Pilot validation:** Test successful and unsuccessful verification, issuance, registration, access, and remediation outcomes as applicable. Record support and rollback paths before expanding scope.
+- **Operations:** Review product-owned workflow history, sign-in records, [Verified ID audit activities](../identity/monitoring-health/reference-audit-activities.md#verified-id), and user verification evidence. Keep identity documents and biometric material out of troubleshooting tickets.
+
+## Licensing
+
+Requirements vary by capability. Use [identity verification licensing](../fundamentals/licensing.md#identity-verification) and the licensing prerequisites in each product guide rather than assuming one scenario's entitlement covers every journey.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Identity verification profiles](../identity/authentication/concept-authentication-verified-id.md).
+- [Conditional Access identity verification policy](../identity/conditional-access/policy-require-identity-verification.md).
+- [Lifecycle Workflows onboarding](../id-governance/tutorial-onboard-custom-workflow-portal.md).
+- [Account recovery setup](../identity/authentication/how-to-account-recovery-enable.md).
+- [Risk remediation](../id-protection/howto-identity-protection-remediate-unblock.md).
+- [Microsoft Entra audit activities](../identity/monitoring-health/reference-audit-activities.md).

The steps below apply to profiles that map first-name and last-name claims. For other directory mappings, check the corresponding user properties instead. If the profile uses only a custom authentication extension, validate readiness against the extension's requirements rather than this name-field checklist. + +1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a [User Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#user-administrator). +1. Go to **Entra ID** > **Users** > **All users**, and select a user in the recovery profile's scope. +1. Select **Edit properties**. +1. Confirm that **First name** and **Last name** are filled in and match the user's government-issued identification. Correct blank or inaccurate properties before enabling recovery for that user, and save any changes. +1. Repeat for the users who will participate in your initial rollout. + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> For first-name and last-name directory matching, the display name isn't used. Check **First name** and **Last name** against the profile's account-validation rules. Configured custom authentication extensions can provide additional validation or replace directory matching. + + + +## Move a profile from evaluation to production + +After evaluation confirms that verification works for your users, update the profile to enable the full journey: + +1. Go to **Verified ID** > **ID verification profiles** > **Profiles** and open the profile. +1. Review its user groups, verification method, claim matching, and any custom extension configuration. +1. Before switching modes, confirm that the selected journey is configured: + + - For account recovery, enable the tenant's Account recovery policy and choose the actions after recovery. + - For verification at sign-in, configure and save the required Conditional Access policy. + - For onboarding, complete the onboarding configuration separately from profile creation. + +1. Open **Profile mode** and select **Production**. +1. Review the updated configuration and save the profile. Return to **Profiles** and confirm that **Mode** shows **Production**. +1. Validate the complete journey with a small group of users before expanding the profile's scope. + +> [!CAUTION] +> Review the users in scope before switching to **Production**. Confirm that only the intended users can participate in the verification journey. + + + +For a recovery profile, Production mode alone doesn't enable the tenant's Account recovery policy. Configure tenant enablement, Temporary Access Pass (TAP) issuance, and stale-credential cleanup in Account recovery settings. + +## Related content + +- [Configure account recovery settings](../identity/authentication/how-to-account-recovery-enable.md). +- [Verified ID identity verification overview](../identity/authentication/concept-authentication-verified-id.md). +- [Explore identity verification partners](idv-partners.md).

diff --git a/docs/verified-id/how-to-get-verified-id-my-account.md b/docs/verified-id/how-to-get-verified-id-my-account.md
new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..24abf35c039
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/verified-id/how-to-get-verified-id-my-account.md
@@ -0,0 +1,87 @@
+---
+title: Get Microsoft Entra Verified ID from My Account
+description: Get Microsoft Entra Verified ID credentials from My Account through existing VerifiedEmployee issuance or targeted ID verification profiles.
+author: rogulati
+ms.author: rogulati
+ms.service: entra-verified-id
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 10/30/2026
+ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1026
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+#customer intent: As a user, I want to get a Verified ID available to my account so that I can present the credential my organization requests.
+---
+
+# Get your Microsoft Entra Verified ID from My Account
+
+Use My Account to get Microsoft Entra Verified ID credentials that your organization makes available to you. This article explains which configuration controls each issuance path and how to get a credential in Microsoft Authenticator. Before you begin, review the account and Microsoft Authenticator requirements in Prerequisites.
+
+My Account keeps the existing issuance flow for the tenant-issued `VerifiedEmployee` credential. For other tenant-issued credential types and identity verification provider Verified IDs, availability depends on ID verification profile configuration and user targeting.
+
+My Account self-service issuance starts when you sign in and choose to get a credential. It isn't the My Access access-package request flow or inline issuance during a protected sign-in journey.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- An account that can sign in to [My Account](https://myaccount.microsoft.com).
+- For `VerifiedEmployee`, access through your organization's existing My Account issuance settings.
+- For other tenant-issued credentials or identity verification provider Verified IDs, an ID verification profile that enables self-service issuance and targets your account.
+- Microsoft Authenticator to receive the credential.
+- Access to the provider's or your organization's issuance site, when that credential uses an external issuance journey.
+
+For administrator setup, prepare Microsoft Entra Verified ID and the applicable issuer or provider configuration. The [tenant setup guide](verifiable-credentials-configure-tenant-quick.md) describes existing workplace credential issuance. Use [Create an ID verification profile](how-to-create-id-verification-profile.md) for profile-based configuration.
+
+Review the [identity verification licensing requirements](../fundamentals/licensing.md#identity-verification) for your intended scenario. Base Verified ID issuance and integrated onboarding or recovery have separate entitlement requirements; getting a credential in My Account doesn't establish eligibility for those integrated journeys.
+
+## Make credentials available for self-service issuance
+
+Administrator configuration controls which credentials My Account offers. `VerifiedEmployee` is a tenant-issued credential, but its discovery and issuance continue to use the existing My Account configuration. Other tenant-issued credential types and identity verification provider Verified IDs use ID verification profiles.
+
+For the profile-based paths, a provider subscription or credential configuration alone isn't enough. The profile must enable self-service issuance and target the signed-in user.
+
+1. Identify the credential you want to offer and its issuance route. Use the table below to select the corresponding configuration.
+1. Configure the applicable issuance route:
+
+    - For `VerifiedEmployee`, use the existing My Account issuance and group controls in [Quick Microsoft Entra Verified ID setup](verifiable-credentials-configure-tenant-quick.md#myaccount-available-now-to-simplify-issuance-of-workplace-credentials). This path doesn't move to ID verification profile targeting.
+    - For a tenant-issued credential whose type isn't `VerifiedEmployee`, configure an ID verification profile with the **Tenant issued credentials** verification method. Select the credential type and configure the issuance URL for your organization's portal.
+    - For an identity verification provider Verified ID, configure an ID verification profile with the **Identity Verification Provider** verification method. Configure the provider through Microsoft Security Store and select it in the profile.
+
+1. For both profile-based paths, enable self-service issuance in the profile and configure the user groups in scope. See [Create an ID verification profile](how-to-create-id-verification-profile.md) for the shared profile setup. Review your organization's issuance destination before making it available to users.
+1. Test with an eligible account and an account outside the configured scope. Check the credential offered and the destination reached, not just whether the My Account tile appears.
+
+| Credential offered | Configuration used by My Account | Issuance experience |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Tenant-issued credential with type `VerifiedEmployee`. | Existing My Account issuance settings and group controls. | Continue the existing issuance flow and scan the QR code with Microsoft Authenticator. |
+| Tenant-issued credential with a type other than `VerifiedEmployee`. | An ID verification profile using **Tenant issued credentials**, with self-service issuance enabled, an issuance URL, and the user in scope. | Continue to your organization's configured issuance portal to get the credential. |
+| Identity verification provider Verified ID. | An ID verification profile using **Identity Verification Provider**, with the provider configured, self-service issuance enabled, and the user in scope. | Open the provider's issuance journey in a new browser tab and receive the provider-issued Verified ID in Microsoft Authenticator. |
+
+## Get a credential from My Account
+
+My Account shows the credentials available to you. A choice of credential isn't a guarantee that another scenario accepts it.
+
+1. Sign in to [My Account](https://myaccount.microsoft.com) with the account your organization uses for this credential.
+1. Select **Get my Verified ID**.
+1. If more than one credential is offered, select the credential your organization asked you to get. When there's one eligible credential, continue directly to its issuance flow.
+1. Complete the applicable issuance path:
+
+    - For the tenant-issued `VerifiedEmployee` credential, scan the displayed QR code with Microsoft Authenticator and complete the existing issuance flow.
+    - For a tenant-issued credential whose type isn't `VerifiedEmployee`, follow your organization's issuance portal instructions. The destination comes from the ID verification profile, and the portal handles issuance.
+    - For an identity verification provider Verified ID, follow the provider's instructions in the new browser tab, then complete the credential receipt flow in Microsoft Authenticator.
+
+1. Check that the credential is available in Microsoft Authenticator. When another journey requests a credential, present the credential that journey accepts.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> Getting a Verified ID through My Account doesn't complete an identity verification request in another service. If a service asks you to present a Verified ID, follow that service's instructions.
+
+## Troubleshoot getting a Verified ID
+
+| Symptom | Check |
+| --- | --- |
+| The expected provider Verified ID or non-`VerifiedEmployee` tenant-issued credential isn't offered. | Ask your administrator to check the ID verification profile's credential or provider configuration, self-service issuance setting, and user targeting. |
+| A `VerifiedEmployee` credential isn't offered. | Ask your administrator to check the existing My Account issuance settings and group controls, not ID verification profile targeting. |
+| Issuance starts but the provider doesn't complete it. | Contact your administrator for help with the provider's issuance experience. |
+| Your organization's portal doesn't issue the expected tenant-issued credential. | Contact the portal owner; the portal controls that issuance journey. |
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Plan a verification solution and choose the credential scenario](plan-verification-solution.md).
+- [Configure your tenant for Microsoft Entra Verified ID](verifiable-credentials-configure-tenant-quick.md).
+- [Configure Verified ID requirements for an access package](../id-governance/entitlement-management-verified-id-settings.md).

newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/app-roles-activate.md b/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/app-roles-activate.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..62fc4912f25 --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/app-roles-activate.md @@ -0,0 +1,113 @@ +--- +title: Activate app roles in PIM (preview) +description: Learn how to activate and deactivate app roles, view request status, and cancel pending requests in Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management. +ms.topic: how-to +ms.date: 10/29/2026 +ms.custom: pim, msecd-doc-authoring-1031 +ai-usage: ai-generated +# Customer intent: As a user with eligible app role assignments, I want to activate and deactivate my roles and manage activation requests so that I can use application permissions when I need them. +--- +# Activate app roles in Privileged Identity Management (preview) + +Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) for app roles is in preview. Follow the steps in this article to activate an eligible app role, view or cancel a pending request, and deactivate a role when you finish your work. + +## Prerequisites + +- A Microsoft Entra ID Governance license. +- An eligible app role assignment, either assigned directly or through a group. For information about assignments, see [Assign app roles in PIM](app-roles-assign.md). + +## Activate a role + +When you need to take on an app role, you can request activation by using the **My roles** navigation option in PIM. The [app role's settings](app-roles-settings.md) determine the requirements for activation. + +If your eligibility comes from a group's eligible app role assignment, you activate the role for yourself. Your activation doesn't activate the role for the whole group or its other members. + +1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com). + +1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Privileged Identity Management** > **App Roles (Preview)**, and select the application. + +1. Select **My roles** > **Eligible assignments**, and review the list of app roles that you're eligible to activate. + +1. Select **Activate** for the eligible assignment you want to activate. + +1. Depending on the application's role settings, you might be asked to provide multifactor authentication or another form of credential. Follow the instructions to complete the required verification. + +1. On the **Activate** tab, select **Custom activation start time** if you need to schedule activation. Enter **Start time** and select the time zone. + +1. Set **Duration (hours)** using the slider or numeric field, within the maximum configured for the role. + +1. Depending on the application's role settings, justification for activation might be required. If needed, provide the justification in **Reason (max 500 characters)**. + +1. Select **Activate** to submit the request. + +1. Review the request status. + + The **Status** tab shows progress through request processing, validation, and completion. Wait for the stages to finish. The status panel indicates that the PIM page refreshes automatically after completion. + +If the [role requires approval](app-roles-approval-workflow.md) to activate, use **Pending requests** to view the status of your request while it awaits review. The request list shows **Pending approval** for a request awaiting a decision. + +After activation, select **My roles** > **Active assignments** to review your active app roles. An activated assignment shows **Activated** in the **State** column and its **End time**. + +Before using the activated role in the application, the application must obtain a new token. Follow the application's sign-in instructions if another sign-in is needed, and then perform the tasks that require the role. The PIM page's automatic refresh doesn't replace token acquisition by the application. + +## View the status of your requests + +You can view the status of your pending activation requests. Check the status when your requests require another person's approval. + +1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com). + +1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Privileged Identity Management** > **App Roles (Preview)**, and select the application. + +1. Select **Pending requests**. + +1. Review the list of requests, including the reason and status for each request. + +To review your assignments rather than pending requests, select **My roles**. Use the **Eligible assignments**, **Active assignments**, and **Expired assignments** tabs to view the corresponding assignments for the application. + +## Cancel a pending request + +If you no longer need to activate a role that requires approval, you can cancel the pending request. + +1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com). + +1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Privileged Identity Management** > **App Roles (Preview)**, and select the application. + +1. Select **Pending requests**. + +1. For the request that you want to cancel, select **Cancel**. + +To activate the role after canceling the pending request, submit a new activation request. + +## Deactivate a role + +If you no longer need an activated app role assignment, you can deactivate it before the activation expires. + + + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> Deactivation or expiration doesn't automatically invalidate already-issued tokens or existing application sessions. Application access can persist according to token lifetime and the application's session and authorization behavior. Ending an activation in PIM isn't a guarantee of immediate access removal in the application. + +1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com). + +1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Privileged Identity Management** > **App Roles (Preview)**, and select the application. + +1. Select **My roles** > **Active assignments**. + +1. Find the assignment with **State** set to **Activated** that you want to deactivate, and select **Deactivate**. + +1. In the **Deactivate** panel, review **Resource name**, **Role**, **Scope**, **Member**, **Start time**, and **End time** to confirm the activation. + +1. Select **Deactivate** to submit the request, or **Cancel** to close the panel without submitting. + + > [!NOTE] + > If PIM reports **Deactivate role failed** because the active duration is too short and the minimum required is five minutes, wait until the activation has been active for at least five minutes before retrying. A failed deactivation doesn't end the activation. + +1. Review the result, and then check **Active assignments** to verify that the activation has ended. If PIM reports a failure, don't treat the request as a completed deactivation. + +Deactivation ends the activation, not your eligible assignment. You can request activation again while your eligible assignment remains valid. + +## Next steps + +- [Approve or deny app role requests in PIM](app-roles-approval-workflow.md). +- [Configure app role settings in PIM](app-roles-settings.md). +- [Learn about PIM for app roles (preview)](concept-pim-for-app-roles.md).

newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/app-roles-approval-workflow.md b/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/app-roles-approval-workflow.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..bb535e02e9f --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/app-roles-approval-workflow.md @@ -0,0 +1,96 @@ +--- +title: Approve or deny app role requests in PIM (preview) +description: Learn how to view, approve, and deny app role activation and assignment renewal or extension requests in Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management. +ms.topic: how-to +ms.date: 10/29/2026 +ms.custom: pim, msecd-doc-authoring-1031 +ai-usage: ai-generated +# Customer intent: As an app role approver, I want to review and approve or deny requests so that users receive appropriate application access. +--- +# Approve or deny app role requests in PIM (preview) + +Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) for app roles is in preview. Follow the steps in this article to approve or deny requests for app role activation and assignment renewal or extension. + + + +## Overview + +Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) enables you to configure app roles so that they require approval for activation, and choose users or groups from your Microsoft Entra organization as delegated approvers. Configure delegated approvers in the application's [role settings](app-roles-settings.md). + +For activation requests, being designated as an approver in the app role's settings is sufficient to approve or deny requests. You don't need an additional administrative role. + +For assignment extension and renewal requests, you must own the target service principal or have one of the administrative roles listed in [Permissions for app role assignments](app-roles-assign.md#permissions) to approve or deny requests. + +For the requester's workflow, see [Activate app roles in PIM](app-roles-activate.md) and [Extend or renew app role assignments in PIM](app-roles-renew-extend.md). + +## View pending requests + +You can view requests pending your approval in Privileged Identity Management. + +1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com). + +1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Privileged Identity Management** > **App Roles (Preview)**, and select the application. + +1. Select **Approve requests**. + + In **Requests for role activations**, you see the activation requests pending your approval. **Requests to renew or extend role assignments** lists assignment extension and renewal requests. + +1. Select **Refresh** in a request section to update its list. + +If you can't find a request, check that you've selected the correct application and refresh both request sections. + +## Approve requests + +Follow these steps to approve a pending activation request. + +1. In **Requests for role activations**, find and select the checkbox for the request that you want to approve. Select **Approve** to open the decision panel. + + Review **Request details**, including the role, requestor, resource, reason, and start and end times. + +1. Enter your business justification in the required box showing **Enter the reason**. + + If the box is empty, the panel displays **Required fields are missing or invalid**, and **Submit** is unavailable. + +1. Select **Submit** to approve the request. + + PIM shows **Approving** while processing the decision and **Request(s) approved successfully.** when approval succeeds. + +1. After submitting the decision, select **Refresh** in **Requests for role activations** to check that the approved request is no longer listed. + +1. To check the resulting PIM assignment state, open **Assignments** > **Active assignments** and check for **Activated** in the **State** column for the user's app role. + +An approval decision isn't confirmation that the application has started granting access. For activation status and the application-access considerations, see [Activate app roles in PIM](app-roles-activate.md). + +## Deny requests + +If a request doesn't meet your organization's access requirements, deny it and provide the business justification. + +The following steps describe an activation request in **Requests for role activations**. + +1. On the application's **Approve requests** page, select the checkbox for the request in **Requests for role activations**, and then select **Deny**. + +1. In **Denying request(s)**, review **Request details** to confirm the request. + +1. Enter your business justification in the required box showing **Enter the reason**. + +1. Select **Submit** to deny the request. + +1. Select **Refresh** in the request section to review the list after your decision. + +## Workflow notifications + +Here's some information about workflow notifications: + +- Approvers are notified by email when a request for a role is pending their review. Email notifications include a direct link to the request, where the approver can approve or deny. +- Requests are resolved by the first approver who approves or denies. +- When an approver responds to the request, all approvers are notified of the action. +- Resource administrators are notified when an approved user becomes active in their role. + +> [!NOTE] +> A resource administrator who believes that an approved user shouldn't be active can remove the active role assignment in Privileged Identity Management. Although resource administrators aren't notified of pending requests unless they're an approver, they can view and cancel pending requests for all users by viewing pending requests in Privileged Identity Management. + + +## Next steps + +- [Configure app role settings in PIM](app-roles-settings.md). +- [Extend or renew app role assignments in PIM](app-roles-renew-extend.md).

newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/app-roles-assign.md b/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/app-roles-assign.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..3de6204e637 --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/app-roles-assign.md @@ -0,0 +1,124 @@ +--- +title: Assign app roles in PIM (preview) +description: Learn how to assign eligible and active app roles and update or remove assignments in Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management. +ms.topic: how-to +ms.date: 11/16/2026 +ms.custom: pim, msecd-doc-authoring-1031 +ai-usage: ai-generated +#customer intent: As an administrator, I want to assign and maintain eligible and active app roles so that assignees have access when they need it. +--- +# Assign app roles in Privileged Identity Management (preview) + +With Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM), you can create eligible and active app role assignments. PIM for app roles is in preview. This article shows you how to create, update, and remove app role assignments. + + + +## Role assignment conditions + +With Microsoft Entra PIM, assignees must activate an eligible app role assignment before they can use the role. The app role's settings control activation requirements and assignment duration. + +App role assignments support the following assignees: + +- **Eligible** assignments support users, groups, agents, and agent identities. +- **Active** assignments support users, groups, and workload identities. + +You can create permanent or time-bound assignments, subject to the app role's settings. + +PIM for app roles (preview) requires E7 licenses. + +> [!NOTE] +> Agents and agent identities can receive eligible app role assignments in preview. Each agent or agent identity requires an E7 license. Existing assignment-management permissions remain unchanged. + +To create, update, or remove app role assignments in Microsoft Entra PIM, you must be an owner of the target service principal or have one of the following roles: + +- **Directory Writers**. +- **Hybrid Identity Administrator**. +- **Identity Governance Administrator**. +- **Privileged Role Administrator**. +- **User Administrator**. +- **Application Administrator**. +- **Cloud Application Administrator**. +- **CSP Partner Admin Agent**. + +## Assign a role + +Follow these steps to create an eligible or active app role assignment. Before adding an assignment, review the role's [activation and assignment settings](app-roles-settings.md). + +The application must already define the app role you want to assign. You can manage any enterprise application with app roles, including Microsoft and third-party applications. The application's registration doesn't have to be owned by your tenant. For background, see [PIM for app roles (preview)](concept-pim-for-app-roles.md). + +1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com). + +1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Privileged Identity Management** > **App Roles (Preview)**. + +1. Select the application you want to manage. Use the application and object IDs in the application list to identify the intended application. + +1. Under **Manage**, select **Roles** to see the list of app roles and their active and eligible assignment counts. + +1. Select **Add assignments**. + + You can also start from the application's **Assignments** page. + +1. On the **Membership** tab, review **Resource** to confirm the application. Under **Select role**, select the app role you want to assign. + + **Resource type** identifies the application as a service principal. It doesn't identify the type of assignee. + +1. Under **Select member(s)**, select **No member selected** to open **Select a member or group**. + +1. Use **Search** to find the target identity. Select the checkbox for the identity, and then select **Select**. + +1. Select **Next** to continue to the **Setting** tab. Under **Assignment type**, select **Eligible** or **Active**. Privileged Identity Management provides two distinct assignment types: + + - *Eligible* assignments require the assignee to activate the role before using it. Depending on the role settings, activation might require additional actions such as multifactor authentication (MFA), a business justification, or approval from designated approvers. + - *Active* assignments don't require the assignee to activate the role before using it. + +1. Configure the assignment duration: + + - For a permanent eligible assignment, use **Permanently eligible**. + - For a permanent active assignment, use **Permanently assigned**. + - For a time-bound assignment, clear the corresponding permanent option and set **Assignment starts** and **Assignment ends**. + +1. If you're creating an active assignment and the role settings require justification, enter the reason in **Enter justification**. + +1. Review the role, assignee, assignment type, and schedule, and select **Assign**. + +1. Return to the role's **Eligible assignments** or **Active assignments** tab to verify the new assignment. + +For information about activating an eligible assignment, see [Activate app roles in PIM (preview)](app-roles-activate.md). + +## Update or remove an existing role assignment + +Follow these steps to update or remove an existing role assignment. + +1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com). + +1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Privileged Identity Management** > **App Roles (Preview)**. + +1. Select the application you want to manage. + +1. Under **Manage**, select **Assignments**. + +1. Use **Eligible assignments** and **Active assignments** to review existing assignments for the selected application. Use **Expired assignments** to review expired assignments. + + To review assignments for a single role instead, select **Roles**, and then select the role. + +1. Find the eligible direct-user assignment you want to update or remove. + +1. Select the action for the assignment: + + - To change the assignment, select **Update** to open **Membership settings**. Review **Assignment details** to confirm the application, role, and member. Update **Permanently eligible** or **Assignment ends** as needed, and then select **Save**. + + The panel also shows an **Assignment type** dropdown. + + PIM displays an **Updating role grant** notification while processing the update, followed by **Update role assignment request queued**. The queued notification acknowledges the request; it doesn't confirm that the assignment has finished updating. + + - To remove the assignment, select **Remove**. In the **Remove** confirmation, check the member and role, and select **Yes** to proceed or **No** to cancel. + +1. Return to the assignment list and verify the result of your change. For an update, check that the assignment reflects the requested values rather than relying only on the queued notification. + +The eligible direct-user assignment list also provides an **Extend** action. For information about extending or renewing an assignment, see [Extend or renew app role assignments in PIM (preview)](app-roles-renew-extend.md). + +## Next steps + +- [Configure app role settings in PIM (preview)](app-roles-settings.md). +- [Activate app roles in PIM (preview)](app-roles-activate.md). +- [Approve or deny app role requests in PIM (preview)](app-roles-approval-workflow.md).

newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/app-roles-audit.md b/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/app-roles-audit.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..e2112904df2 --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/app-roles-audit.md @@ -0,0 +1,66 @@ +--- +title: View app role audit history in PIM (preview) +description: Learn how to view application-level and personal app role audit history in Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management during preview. +ms.topic: how-to +ms.date: 10/29/2026 +ms.custom: pim, msecd-doc-authoring-1031 +ai-usage: ai-generated +#Customer Intent: As an administrator or assignee, I want to view app role audit history so that I can investigate assignment changes and review my role activity. +--- + +# View app role audit history in Privileged Identity Management (preview) + +Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) for app roles is in preview. Use resource and personal audit history to investigate app role assignment changes, activation activity, and role-setting changes. + + + +## Prerequisites + +PIM for app roles (preview) requires Microsoft Entra ID Governance licenses. + +To view **Resource audit**, you must own the target service principal or have one of the administrative roles listed in [Role assignment conditions](app-roles-assign.md#permissions). + +## View resource audit history + +Use **Resource audit** to investigate the app role activity recorded for the selected application. + +1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com). +1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Privileged Identity Management** > **App Roles (Preview)**. +1. Select the application you want to view audit history for. +1. Expand **Activity**, and then select **Resource audit**. +1. Use **Time span**, **Audit type**, **Original requestor**, and **Subject type** to narrow the results. +1. Use **Search by requestor, resource, primary target or subject** to find relevant entries. +1. Review the **Time**, **Requestor**, **Action**, **Resource name**, **Primary target**, **Subject**, and **Status** columns. +1. Select an entry to open **Audit details**. Use **Refresh** to reload the audit view. + +**Audit details** includes **Date**, **Requestor**, **Action**, **Resource**, **Scope**, **Primary target**, **Subject**, **Type**, **Reason**, **Ticket system**, **Ticket number**, **Status**, **Status Reason**, and **Correlation ID**. Some fields can be empty or show a dash for a particular event. + +## View my audit + +Use **My audit** to review app role activity associated with your account for the selected application. + +1. Select **Start** to begin the export. + + + +## Next steps + +- [Assign app roles in PIM (preview)](app-roles-assign.md). +- [Activate app roles in PIM (preview)](app-roles-activate.md).

newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/app-roles-renew-extend.md b/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/app-roles-renew-extend.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..e002439acd1 --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/app-roles-renew-extend.md @@ -0,0 +1,161 @@ +--- +title: Extend or renew app role assignments in PIM (preview) +description: Learn how to extend or renew time-bound app role assignments in Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) during preview. +ms.topic: how-to +ms.date: 10/29/2026 +ms.custom: pim, msecd-doc-authoring-1031 +ai-usage: ai-generated +#Customer Intent: As an administrator or assignee, I want to extend or renew time-bound app role assignments so that I can maintain necessary access. +--- + +# Extend or renew app role assignments in Privileged Identity Management (preview) + +Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) for app roles is in preview. This article describes how to request, approve, or administer an extension or renewal of a time-bound app role assignment. + + + +## Prerequisites + +PIM for app roles (preview) requires Microsoft Entra ID Governance licenses. + +## Navigate to the PIM section for the desired application + +Use the following entry point for the procedures in this article: + +1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com). +1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Privileged Identity Management** > **App Roles (Preview)**. +1. Select the application whose role assignments you want to extend or renew. + +## Who can extend and renew? + +The assignee can request to extend role assignments that are about to expire and request to renew role assignments that are already expired. Only users with permissions to manage these assignments can complete an extension or renewal on behalf of an assignee. + +To initiate an extension or renewal on behalf of an assignee, you need one of the administrative roles listed in [Permissions for app role assignments](app-roles-assign.md#permissions), or you must own the target service principal. + +## When are notifications sent? + +In the common PIM workflow, email notifications help affected users and administrators maintain appropriate access as assignments approach expiration. Administrators receive notifications when an assignee requests to extend or renew an expiring or expired role. When an administrator resolves the request, notifications report the approval or denial. + + +App-role notification recipients, schedules, and message contents haven't been verified. Use **Pending requests** to check your request status, or **Approve requests** to review requests, rather than depending on an email notification. + +## Extend role assignments + +Extend an assignment before it expires. The following steps outline the process for requesting, resolving, or administering an extension of a role assignment. + +Extending an eligible assignment changes its assignment period; it doesn't replace [activating the role](app-roles-activate.md). For background on eligible and active app role assignments, see [PIM for app roles (preview)](concept-pim-for-app-roles.md). + +### Self-extend expiring assignments + +Users with a time-bound eligible app role assignment can request an extension from **My roles** > **Eligible assignments** when **Extend** is available. The following steps describe that eligible-assignment workflow. + + +1. On the application's **My roles** page, select **Eligible assignments**. +1. Find the role assignment that you want to extend. +1. Select **Extend** to open **Extend role assignment**. +1. Review **Assignment details**, including the application, role, assignee type, member, and start and end times. +1. Enter the business justification in the required **Reason** box. +1. Select **Extend** to submit the request. + +PIM displays **Request to Extend role assignment is submitted** after submission. This notification confirms submission, not approval or a changed assignment end time. + +Go to **Pending requests** to view the status of your request or to cancel it. To cancel a pending request, find the request and select **Cancel**. + +### Extension approval + +Administrators can approve or deny requests by going to the Privileged Identity Management administration experience and selecting **Approve requests**. For app roles, this page separates **Requests to renew or extend role assignments** from **Requests for role activations**. + +When approving an extension request, an approver can change the assignment's start date and time, end date and time, and assignment type. + + + +1. On the application's **Approve requests** page, locate **Requests to renew or extend role assignments**. +1. Find the extension request. Select **Refresh** to update the list if needed. +1. Select **Approve** or **Deny** for the request. +1. Review the original assignment and the reason for the request. When approving, adjust the start and end dates and times and assignment type as needed. +1. Complete any required decision fields, and submit the approval or denial. + +For the related approval workflow, see [Approve or deny app role requests in PIM (preview)](app-roles-approval-workflow.md). + +### Admin initiated extension + +If a user assigned to a role doesn't request an extension for the role assignment, an administrator with the required app-role permissions can extend an assignment on behalf of the user. + +To extend a role assignment, browse to the application's assignment view in Privileged Identity Management. Find the assignment that requires an extension, and then select **Extend** in the action column. + +The following steps describe extending a time-bound eligible assignment. + +1. On the application's **Assignments** page, select **Eligible assignments**. +1. Find the assignment that requires an extension, and then select **Extend**. +1. In **Membership settings**, review **Assignment details** to confirm the application, role, and member. +1. Set **Assignment ends** to the new end date and time. If the role settings allow it and permanent eligibility is appropriate, select **Permanently eligible** instead. + + + +1. Select **Save**. +1. Review the notification. PIM shows **Extending role grant** followed by **Extend role assignment request queued**. +1. Return to **Assignments** and check **End time** to verify the result. A queued notification doesn't confirm that the extension has finished processing. + + + +## Renew role assignments + +Renew an assignment after it expires. The following steps describe self-service renewal, approval, and administrator-initiated renewal. + +### Self-renew + +Use **My roles** > **Expired assignments** to find your expired role assignments and request renewal. + +1. On the application's **My roles** page, select **Expired assignments**. +1. Review the **Assignment type** filter to check which assignments the list shows. + + + +1. Find the expired assignment that you want to renew. +1. Select **Renew** to open the request form. +1. If the role requires a renewal reason, enter the reason for the request. Otherwise, skip this step. +1. Select **Renew** to submit the renewal request for approval. + + + +When a reason is required, include context that helps the approver decide whether to approve or deny the request. + + +After submitting the request, open **Pending requests** to view its status. To cancel a pending request, find the request and select **Cancel**. + +### Admin approves + +Administrators can access renewal requests by opening **Approve requests** for the application and using **Requests to renew or extend role assignments**. + +When approving a renewal request, an approver can change the assignment's start date and time, end date and time, and assignment type. + + + +1. On the application's **Approve requests** page, locate **Requests to renew or extend role assignments**. +1. Find the renewal request. Select **Refresh** to update the list if needed. +1. Select **Approve** or **Deny** for the request. +1. Review the original assignment and the reason for the request. When approving, adjust the start and end dates and times and assignment type as needed. +1. Complete any required decision fields, and submit the approval or denial. + +### Admin renew + +Administrators can use the application's **Assignments** > **Expired assignments** view to locate expired role assignments. An administrator with the required permissions can renew an assignment on behalf of the assignee. The following steps describe an expired eligible assignment. + + + +1. On the application's **Assignments** page, select **Expired assignments**. +1. Review the **Assignment type** filter to check which assignments the list shows. +1. Find the expired assignment that you want to renew. +1. Select **Renew** to open **Membership settings**. +1. Review **Assignment details** to confirm the application, role, and member. +1. Set **Assignment starts** to the new start date and time. Set **Assignment ends** for a time-bound assignment, or select **Permanently eligible** if the role settings allow it and permanent eligibility is appropriate. +1. Select **Save**. +1. Review the notification. PIM shows **Renewing role grant** followed by **Renew role assignment request queued**. +1. Return to **Assignments** and verify that the assignment reflects the renewal. A queued notification acknowledges the request; it doesn't confirm that renewal has finished processing. + + + +## Next steps + +- [Approve or deny app role requests in PIM (preview)](app-roles-approval-workflow.md). +- [Configure app role settings in PIM (preview)](app-roles-settings.md).

newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/app-roles-settings.md b/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/app-roles-settings.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..f8fa5c54a20 --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/app-roles-settings.md @@ -0,0 +1,182 @@ +--- +title: Configure app role settings in PIM (preview) +description: Learn how to configure activation, assignment, approval, and notification settings for app roles in Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management. +ms.topic: how-to +ms.date: 10/29/2026 +ms.custom: pim, msecd-doc-authoring-1031 +ai-usage: ai-generated +#customer intent: As an administrator, I want to configure app role settings so that eligible and active assignments follow my organization's access requirements. +--- +# Configure app role settings in Privileged Identity Management (preview) + + + +In Privileged Identity Management (PIM) in Microsoft Entra ID, which is part of Microsoft Entra, role settings define role assignment properties. These properties include multifactor authentication and approval requirements for activation, assignment maximum duration, and notification settings. This article shows you how to configure role settings and set up the approval workflow to specify who can approve or deny requests to elevate privilege. + +## Prerequisites + +To modify app role settings, you need PIM AdminReadWrite permissions. The `microsoft.directory/servicePrincipals/appRoleAssignedTo/update` permission grants this access. Each of the administrative roles listed in [Role assignment conditions](app-roles-assign.md#permissions) provides the required permission. + +PIM role settings are also known as PIM policies. + +## Open role settings + +To open the settings for an app role: + +1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com). + +1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Privileged Identity Management** > **App Roles (Preview)**. + +1. Select the application for which you want to configure role settings. Use the application and object IDs in the application list to identify the intended application. + +1. Under **Manage**, select **Settings**. View the list of roles and the **Modified**, **Last updated**, and **Last updated by** columns. + +1. Select the role that you want to configure to open **Role setting details**. + +1. Review the current role settings. + +1. Select **Edit** to update role settings. + +1. Configure the **Activation**, **Assignment**, and **Notification** tabs as described in [Role settings](#role-settings). Use the tab names or the **Next: Assignment**, **Next: Notification**, **Prev: Activation**, and **Prev: Assignment** buttons to move between sections. + +1. Select **Update** to save your changes. + +1. Review the notification. PIM shows **Updating role settings** while processing the change and **Role setting update succeeded** when it succeeds. + +1. Return to **Settings** and reopen the role to confirm that **Role setting details** reflects your changes. The **Settings** list also shows **Modified**, **Last updated**, and **Last updated by**. + + + +## Role settings + +For background on eligible and active app role assignments, see [PIM for app roles (preview)](concept-pim-for-app-roles.md). + + + +### Activation maximum duration + +On the **Activation** tab, use the **Activation maximum duration (hours)** slider or numeric field to set the maximum activation duration. This duration concerns activation of an eligible assignment, rather than the lifetime of the eligible assignment itself. + + + +### On activation, require multifactor authentication + +You can require users who are eligible for a role to prove who they are by using multifactor authentication (MFA) before they can activate. On the **Activation** tab, **On activation, require** offers **None**, **Azure MFA**, and **Microsoft Entra Conditional Access authentication context**. + +Select **Azure MFA** to configure the MFA requirement. The authentication-context option is also present, but its additional configuration isn't shown in the supplied editor views. + + + +### Require justification on activation + +On the **Activation** tab, select **Require justification on activation** to require users to enter a business justification when they activate an eligible assignment. + + + +### Require ticket information on activation + +On the **Activation** tab, select **Require ticket information on activation** to require users to enter ticket information when they activate an eligible assignment. + + + +### Require approval to activate + +You can require approval for activation of an eligible assignment. On the **Activation** tab: + +1. Select **Require approval to activate**. +1. Open **Select approver(s)**. +1. In **Select a member**, use **Search** or the **All**, **Users**, and **Groups** tabs to find the intended approvers. +1. Select the checkboxes for the intended entries, and then select **Select**. +1. Review **Selected approvers**. Use **Remove** to remove an entry you don't want. + + + +The **Activation** tab also includes **Require pre-approval custom extension to activate (Preview)** and **Require post-approval custom extension to activate (Preview)**. + + + +To learn more about approvals, see [Approve or deny app role requests in PIM (preview)](app-roles-approval-workflow.md). + +### Assignment duration + +When you configure settings for a role, you can choose assignment duration options for each assignment type: *eligible* and *active*. + +On the **Assignment** tab, configure the permanent-assignment checkboxes and the corresponding expire-after dropdowns. The expiry dropdowns are disabled in the supplied configuration while permanent assignments are allowed. + +You can choose from these eligible assignment duration settings. + +| Setting | Description | +| --- | --- | +| **Allow permanent eligible assignment** | Allows eligible assignments without an end date. | +| **Expire eligible assignments after** | Sets the expiration period for eligible assignments. | + +You can also choose from these active assignment duration settings. + +| Setting | Description | +| --- | --- | +| **Allow permanent active assignment** | Allows active assignments without an end date. | +| **Expire active assignments after** | Sets the expiration period for active assignments. | + + + +Permanent eligibility doesn't remove the need to activate the role before use. Review the activation settings separately from the assignment duration settings. + +For information about creating assignments, see [Assign app roles in PIM (preview)](app-roles-assign.md). For information about changing an assignment's end date, see [Extend or renew app role assignments in PIM (preview)](app-roles-renew-extend.md). + +### Require multifactor authentication on active assignment + +You can require users who are eligible for a role to prove who they are by using the multifactor authentication feature in Microsoft Entra ID before they can activate. Multifactor authentication helps safeguard access to data and applications. It provides another layer of security by using a second form of authentication. + +Users might not be prompted for multifactor authentication if they authenticated with strong credentials or provided multifactor authentication earlier in this session. + +If your goal is to ensure that users must provide authentication during activation, you can use [On activation, require Microsoft Entra Conditional Access authentication context](pim-how-to-change-default-settings.md#on-activation-require-azure-ad-conditional-access-authentication-context) together with [Authentication Strengths](~/identity/authentication/concept-authentication-strengths.md). These options require users to authenticate during activation by using methods different from the one they used to sign in to the machine. + +For example, if users sign in to the machine by using Windows Hello for Business, you can use **On activation, require Microsoft Entra Conditional Access authentication context** and **Authentication Strengths** to require users to do passwordless sign-in with Microsoft Authenticator when they activate the role. + +After the user provides passwordless sign-in with Microsoft Authenticator once in this example, they can do their next activation in this session without another authentication. Passwordless sign-in with Microsoft Authenticator is already part of their token. + +Enable the multifactor authentication feature of Microsoft Entra ID for all users. For more information, see [Plan a Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication deployment](~/identity/authentication/howto-mfa-getstarted.md). + +### Require justification on active assignment + +You can require the person creating an active (as opposed to eligible) assignment to enter a business justification. + +When justification is required, the assignment creator enters it in **Enter justification** on the assignment wizard's **Setting** tab. The form shows required-field validation if the justification is missing. + +On the **Assignment** tab, use **Require justification on active assignment** to configure this requirement. + +### Notifications + +Privileged Identity Management enables granular control over who receives notifications and which notifications they receive. The app-role notification summary includes eligible assignment, active assignment, and activation rows, with default recipients, additional recipients, and a critical-emails-only option. + +On the **Notification** tab, configure each notification's **Default recipients**, **Additional recipients**, and **Critical emails only** controls. Notifications are grouped into eligible assignments, active assignments, and eligible-member activations. + +For rows that accept additional recipients, enter email addresses separated by semicolons. + +The editor shows these recipient categories: + +| Notification group | Notification | Recipient category shown | +| --- | --- | --- | +| Eligible or active assignments | Role assignment alert | Admin. | +| Eligible or active assignments | Notification to the assigned user (assignee) | Assignee. | +| Eligible or active assignments | Request to approve a role assignment renewal/extension | Approver. | +| Eligible-member activation | Role activation alert | Admin. | +| Eligible-member activation | Notification to activated user (requestor) | Requestor. | +| Eligible-member activation | Request to approve an activation | Approver. | + +Use the controls as follows: + +- **Turn off an email**: Clear its default-recipient checkbox and remove any editable additional recipients. +- **Limit emails to specified email addresses**: For a row that accepts additional recipients, clear its default-recipient checkbox and enter the intended addresses. +- **Send emails to both default recipients and additional recipients**: Keep the default-recipient checkbox selected and add the intended addresses. +- **Critical emails only**: Select this checkbox to limit the notification to critical emails. + +For **Request to approve an activation**, the additional-recipient field is disabled and states **Only designated approvers can receive this email**. Configure those recipients through **Select approver(s)** on the **Activation** tab, not by adding arbitrary email addresses. + + + +## Next steps + +- [Assign app roles in PIM (preview)](app-roles-assign.md). +- [Activate app roles in PIM (preview)](app-roles-activate.md). +- [Approve or deny app role requests in PIM (preview)](app-roles-approval-workflow.md).

diff --git a/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/concept-pim-for-app-roles.md b/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/concept-pim-for-app-roles.md

@@ -0,0 +1,80 @@
+---
+title: Privileged Identity Management for app roles (preview)
+description: Learn how Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) for app roles provides eligible assignments and just-in-time activation.
+ms.topic: concept-article
+ms.date: 11/16/2026
+ms.custom: pim, msecd-doc-authoring-1031
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+#Customer Intent: As an application administrator, I want to understand PIM for app roles so that I can provide just-in-time access to application-defined roles.
+---
+# Privileged Identity Management (PIM) for app roles (preview)
+
+Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) for app roles lets you manage eligible and active assignments to application-defined roles. PIM for app roles is in preview.
+
+## Overview
+
+App roles let an application owner define roles that an application uses to make authorization decisions. With PIM for app roles, administrators can create eligible app role assignments instead of active assignments. Assignees activate an eligible assignment when they need to use the role and deactivate it when they finish.
+
+With PIM for app roles, you can use policies similar to those in PIM for Microsoft Entra roles and PIM for Azure resources. You can require approval for app role activation, enforce multifactor authentication (MFA), require justification, and limit maximum activation time.
+
+PIM for app roles (preview) requires E7 licenses.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> Agents and agent identities can receive eligible app role assignments in preview. Each agent or agent identity requires an E7 license. Existing assignment-management permissions remain unchanged.
+
+## What is PIM for app roles?
+
+PIM for app roles is part of Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management, alongside PIM for Microsoft Entra roles, PIM for Azure resources, and PIM for Groups. It applies PIM assignment and activation policies to the roles defined by an application.
+
+With PIM for app roles, you can use policies similar to the ones you use in the other PIM providers: require approval for activation, require authentication, require justification, and limit maximum activation time. You can also configure assignment duration and notifications for each app role.
+
+PIM manages access to existing app roles. The application continues to define what each role allows an assignee to do.
+
+For information about defining roles, see [Add app roles to your application and receive them in the token](~/identity-platform/howto-add-app-roles-in-apps.md).
+
+## Eligible and active app role assignments
+
+The assignment type determines whether an assignee needs to activate an app role before using it:
+
+- **Eligible**: A role assignment that requires an assignee to perform one or more actions to use the role. If an assignee is eligible for a role, they can activate the role when they need it.
+- **Active**: A role assignment that doesn't require an assignee to activate the role through PIM before using it.
+
+An eligible assignee activates the app role for a limited duration, subject to the role settings. Depending on those settings, activation can require authentication, a business justification, ticket information, or approval from a designated approver.
+
+The assignment settings control whether eligible and active assignments can be permanent or must expire. Extending or renewing an assignment changes the period of the assignment; activating a role lets an eligible assignee use it.
+
+During preview, users, groups, agents, and agent identities can receive eligible app role assignments.
+
+Users, groups, and workload identities can receive active app role assignments through PIM.
+
+When a group has an eligible app role assignment, each eligible group member activates the app role for themselves. Activation applies to the requesting user, not to the group as a whole or its other members.
+
+
+
+## App roles and role claims
+
+App roles are defined on an application registration representing a service, app, or API. Applications can use the `roles` claim in a token to make authorization decisions.
+
+Depending on the scenario, app roles appear in different tokens issued for the application. For an application that signs in users, role claims are included in the ID token. When an application calls an API, role claims are included in the access token for that API.
+
+PIM provides the assignment and activation lifecycle. The application uses role claims to authorize access to its functionality.
+
+After activation completes, the application must obtain a new token to receive the activated app role. Whether you need to sign in again depends on the application.
+
+Deactivation or expiration doesn't automatically invalidate already-issued tokens or existing application sessions. Application access can persist according to token lifetime and the application's session and authorization behavior.
+
+## Manage the app role lifecycle
+
+Use the app-role task guides to manage each part of the lifecycle:
+
+- [Assign app roles in PIM (preview)](app-roles-assign.md).
+- [Activate and deactivate app roles in PIM (preview)](app-roles-activate.md).
