newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-connect-virtual-machine-my-access.md b/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-connect-virtual-machine-my-access.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..87fd8164f33 --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-connect-virtual-machine-my-access.md @@ -0,0 +1,128 @@ +--- +title: Connect to an Azure Virtual Machine from the My Access portal +description: Use the My Access portal to view Azure Virtual Machine access, activate eligible roles, and connect with Microsoft Entra ID authentication. +author: tamimsangrar +ms.author: tamimsangrar +ms.topic: how-to +ms.date: 11/17/2026 +ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1032 +ai-usage: ai-generated +#customer intent: As a user with access to an Azure Virtual Machine, I want to activate the access I need and connect from the My Access portal so that I can complete my task. +--- + +# Connect to an Azure Virtual Machine in the My Access portal (Preview) + + + + + +Use the My Access portal to view your access to an Azure Virtual Machine, activate eligible role assignments when required, and connect to the Virtual Machine with Microsoft Entra ID authentication. An eligible role assignment lets you request temporary role access for your signed-in identity. + +## Prerequisites + +Before you begin, confirm your access and ask the resource administrator to verify the connection setup. + +### Your access + +- Microsoft Entra ID Governance licensing is required for **Resource Connections**. See [Microsoft Entra ID Governance licensing fundamentals](~/id-governance/licensing-fundamentals.md). +- You need an active or eligible **Virtual Machine Administrator Login** or **Virtual Machine User Login** role assignment for Microsoft Entra sign-in to the virtual machine. An Owner or Contributor **role assignment** alone will not grant the user the ability to sign-in. +- For Azure Bastion, you need read access to the virtual machine, its network interface, and the Bastion resource. You also need read access to the target virtual machine's virtual network when Bastion is deployed in a peered virtual network. Existing active role assignments can provide some of this access within their scopes. Ask your administrator to provide the required access where it is missing, for example through the **Reader** role. If this access isn't already active, you need existing eligible role assignments that cover the required resources and permissions. +- Use a client that meets the [Windows](~/identity/devices/howto-vm-sign-in-azure-ad-windows.md) or [Linux](~/identity/devices/howto-vm-sign-in-azure-ad-linux.md) sign-in requirements. Windows virtual machine connectivity doesn't support guest accounts. + +### Administrator-managed setup + +- The Azure Virtual Machine must be configured for Microsoft Entra sign-in. The resource administrator can follow the setup procedures for [Windows](~/identity/devices/howto-vm-sign-in-azure-ad-windows.md) or [Linux](~/identity/devices/howto-vm-sign-in-azure-ad-linux.md) virtual machines. For Azure Arc-enabled servers, this preview supports only Linux. +- For Azure Bastion connections, a Bastion host must have network connectivity to the virtual machine. Use [Deploy Azure Bastion](/azure/bastion/quickstart-host-portal) for deployment and [Microsoft Entra ID authentication with Azure Bastion](/azure/bastion/bastion-entra-id-authentication) for authentication setup and required resource access. +- An administrator manages the active or eligible role assignments. For role assignment setup, see [Assign Azure resource roles in PIM](pim-resource-roles-assign-roles.md). + + + +## Find your Azure Virtual Machine + +In the [My Access portal](../my-access-portal-overview.md), locate the virtual machine you want to connect to and view its role assignments. Eligible role assignments need to be activated before you can use their permissions. If the role assignments you need are already active, you don't need to activate them again. + +1. Sign in to the [My Access portal](https://myaccess.microsoft.com) in the tenant where you have access. +1. Under **My Access**, select [**Resource Connections**](https://aka.ms/pim/resource-connections). +1. Select **Virtual Machine** to view Azure Virtual Machines, or **Azure Arc VM** for supported Azure Arc-enabled Linux servers. +1. Find the resource and view its active and eligible role assignments. Select the resource name to view its details. To view it in the Azure portal, select **Open in Azure** from the resource details. + +:::image type="content" source="media/pim-connect-virtual-machine-my-access/my-access-resource-connections.png" alt-text="Screenshot of My Access Resource Connections showing eligible role assignments and the Activate action for a virtual machine." lightbox="media/pim-connect-virtual-machine-my-access/my-access-resource-connections.png"::: + +## Activate the access you need + +If you already have active access and **Connect** is available, continue to [Connect to the Azure Virtual Machine](#connect-to-the-vm). Otherwise, request role activation for the roles you need. + +Dependent resources are resources used for the connection, such as the Azure Bastion host and the virtual machine's network interface. An existing eligible role assignment can cover dependent resources when it grants the required permissions at a scope that includes those resources. You don't need a separate eligible role assignment on every dependency. You can optionally select a lower-privileged role when the eligible role's policy allows it. + +For example, if the virtual machine, network interface, Bastion host, and relevant virtual network are in the same resource group, the following eligible role assignments can provide the required access after activation: + +| Existing eligible role assignment | Role assignment scope | Access after activation | +| --- | --- | --- | +| **Reader** | The resource group containing the resources. | Reader access to the virtual machine, network interface, Bastion host, and virtual network in that resource group. | +| **Virtual Machine User Login** | The virtual machine. | Microsoft Entra sign-in to the virtual machine as a regular user. | + +Confirm the roles and scopes offered in the role activation dialog for your connection. + +1. Select **Activate** at the Azure subscription, resource group, or resource scope where you need access. The scope you select is the activation scope. +1. In the role-selection dialog, select **Activate** for the eligible role assignment you need. + + :::image type="content" source="media/pim-connect-virtual-machine-my-access/resource-connection-role-selection.png" alt-text="Screenshot of available virtual machine sign-in role assignments and their Activate actions." lightbox="media/pim-connect-virtual-machine-my-access/resource-connection-role-selection.png"::: + +1. Under **Choose a connection path**, select an available path, such as **Azure Bastion**. Review **Role assignments to activate**, including access to dependent resources such as the Azure Bastion host or network interface. + + The roles shown depend on your existing eligibility. Review the roles and resources listed before you submit the request. + + :::image type="content" source="media/pim-connect-virtual-machine-my-access/resource-connection-activation.png" alt-text="Screenshot of a connection path, dependent-resource role assignments, and the Activate access action." lightbox="media/pim-connect-virtual-machine-my-access/resource-connection-activation.png"::: + +1. Review the **Duration** and enter a **Justification** for your task. +1. Optional: If **Allow least-privilege role activation** is enabled on the policy for the role you're eligible for, use **Change settings** in the activation dialog to select an available lower-privileged role. The eligible role's policy governs approval, authentication, justification, and activation maximum duration. +1. Complete the role activation requirements shown and select **Activate access**. Requirements depend on each eligible role's policy and can include approval or Conditional Access. +1. Select **Refresh** to check the request status. If the request is pending approval, wait for approval. Continue when access is **Active** and **Connect** is available. + +:::image type="content" source="media/pim-connect-virtual-machine-my-access/resource-connection-active-access.png" alt-text="Screenshot of a virtual machine with an active role assignment and the Connect action available." lightbox="media/pim-connect-virtual-machine-my-access/resource-connection-active-access.png"::: + + + +## Connect to the Azure Virtual Machine + +Use a connection method offered for the selected resource. The available options depend on the resource configuration. + +If your organization requires a recording, check [Azure Bastion recording support and limitations](azure-pim-resource-rbac.md#azure-bastion-recording-support) before selecting a method. Microsoft Entra ID RDP in the Azure portal and native-client connections don't support Bastion graphical session recording. + +1. Select **Connect** for the Azure Virtual Machine or supported Azure Arc-enabled Linux server. +1. In the connection dialog, choose an available method: + + - For Azure Bastion in-browser access, select **Azure Bastion** under **Choose a connection path**. Select **Browser** under **Choose a connection option**, and then select **Connect**. + - For Azure Cloud Shell, select the offered Cloud Shell connection option. + - For a native RDP or SSH connection, follow the instructions in the connection dialog. Use the applicable [Windows](~/identity/devices/howto-vm-sign-in-azure-ad-windows.md) or [Linux](~/identity/devices/howto-vm-sign-in-azure-ad-linux.md) guide for client requirements. + +1. Complete the connection instructions and sign in with your Microsoft Entra ID credentials. + +:::image type="content" source="media/pim-connect-virtual-machine-my-access/resource-connection-bastion-browser.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Azure Bastion connection path, Browser connection option, and Connect action." lightbox="media/pim-connect-virtual-machine-my-access/resource-connection-bastion-browser.png"::: + +## Troubleshoot access and connection + +Use the following checks when you can't connect. An administrator handles role assignment or activation issues. A resource administrator handles virtual machine and Bastion setup. + +| Symptom | Next action | +| --- | --- | +| The virtual machine isn't listed. | Confirm that you're signed in to the tenant where you have access. Ask the administrator to verify your role assignment and its scope, and the resource administrator to verify the connection setup. | +| The required role assignment isn't listed for activation. | Ask the administrator to check whether you have an eligible role assignment with the required permissions and scope. My Access activation doesn't create eligibility. | +| Activation is pending approval. | Wait for approval before using the role. If you no longer need the request, [cancel it in My Access](pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles.md?pivots=my-access#view-and-cancel-a-pending-request-in-my-access). | +| **Connect** is unavailable after activation. | Select **Refresh** and check the activation status in [**Resource Connections**](https://aka.ms/pim/resource-connections). If the request is pending approval, wait for approval. If the status is **Active** but **Connect** is still unavailable, ask your administrator to check the access and setup requirements in [Prerequisites](#prerequisites). | +| Sign-in fails after you start the connection. | Use the [Windows sign-in troubleshooting guide](~/identity/devices/howto-vm-sign-in-azure-ad-windows.md#troubleshoot-sign-in-problems) or [Linux sign-in troubleshooting guide](~/identity/devices/howto-vm-sign-in-azure-ad-linux.md#troubleshoot-sign-in-issues), with help from the resource administrator for configuration checks. | + +## Finish your work + +When you're finished, end your Azure Virtual Machine or Azure Arc-enabled server session and deactivate temporary access that you no longer need. + +1. Sign out of the Azure Virtual Machine or Azure Arc-enabled server session. +1. In the [My Access portal](../my-access-portal-overview.md), review the active role assignment and select **Deactivate** where available. + +Role deactivation removes the active role assignment. It isn't a procedure for disconnecting an existing Azure Virtual Machine or Azure Arc-enabled server session. For administrator session management in PIM, see [Monitor and disconnect Azure Bastion sessions](pim-manage-bastion-sessions.md). For session management on the Azure Bastion resource, see [Monitor active sessions](/azure/bastion/session-monitoring). + +## Related content + +- [Activate Azure resource roles in PIM](pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles.md). +- [Connect to Azure Virtual Machines using Microsoft Entra ID authentication with Azure Bastion](/azure/bastion/bastion-entra-id-authentication). +- [Monitor Azure Bastion](/azure/bastion/monitor-bastion).

newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-how-to-activate-role.md b/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-how-to-activate-role.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..b8176e23e97 --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-how-to-activate-role.md @@ -0,0 +1,326 @@ +--- +title: Activate Microsoft Entra roles in PIM +description: Learn how to activate eligible Microsoft Entra roles with Privileged Identity Management (PIM) to perform administrative tasks when needed. +ms.author: tamimsangrar +ms.reviewer: ilyal +ms.date: 11/17/2026 +ms.topic: how-to +ai-usage: ai-assisted +ms.custom: + - sfi-ga-nochange + - sfi-image-nochange + - msecd-doc-authoring-1032 +zone_pivot_groups: pim-entra-role-activation-methods +#customer intent: As a user with eligible Microsoft Entra role assignments, I want to activate my roles so that I can perform administrative tasks when needed. +--- + +# Activate a Microsoft Entra role in PIM + +Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) simplifies how enterprises manage privileged access to resources in Microsoft Entra ID and other Microsoft online services like Microsoft 365 or Microsoft Intune. + +If you have an *eligible* administrative role assignment, *activate* it when you need to perform privileged actions. For example, a user who manages Exchange Online might be eligible for Exchange Online Administrator rather than have permanent Global Administrator access. + +Choose the method you will use to activate your Microsoft Entra role assignment. + + + +>[!IMPORTANT] +>When a role is activated, Microsoft Entra PIM temporarily adds active assignment for the role. Microsoft Entra PIM creates active assignment (assigns user to a role) within seconds. When deactivation (manual or through activation time expiration) happens, Microsoft Entra PIM removes the active assignment within seconds as well. +> +>Application may provide access based on the role the user has. In some situations, application access may not immediately reflect the fact that user got role assigned or removed. If application previously cached the fact that user does not have a role – when user tries to access application again, access may not be provided. Similarly, if application previously cached the fact that user has a role – when role is deactivated, user may still get access. Specific situation depends on the application’s architecture. For some applications, signing out and signing back in may help get access added or removed. + +>[!IMPORTANT] +>If you activate an administrative role while signed in to Microsoft Teams on a mobile device, Teams sends a notification saying "Open Teams to continue receiving notifications for *<email address>*", or "*<email address>* needs to sign in to see notifications". Open Teams to continue receiving notifications. + +::: zone pivot="entra-admin-center" + + + +## Activate a role in the Microsoft Entra admin center + +When you need to assume a Microsoft Entra role, you can request activation by opening **My roles** in Privileged Identity Management. + +>[!NOTE] +> You can use the Azure mobile app on iOS or Android to activate eligible Microsoft Entra and Azure resource role assignments, request renewals, and check pending requests. See [Activate PIM roles using the Azure mobile app](pim-how-to-activate-role.md?pivots=azure-mobile-app#activate-pim-roles-using-the-azure-mobile-app). + +1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as a user who has an eligible role assignment. + +1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Privileged Identity Management** > **My roles**. For information about how to add the Privileged Identity Management tile to your dashboard, see [Start using Privileged Identity Management](pim-getting-started.md). + +1. Select **Microsoft Entra roles** to see a list of your eligible Microsoft Entra roles. + + ![Screenshot of the My roles page showing roles you can activate.](./media/pim-how-to-activate-role/my-roles.png) + +1. In the **Microsoft Entra roles** list, find the role you want to activate. + + ![Screenshot of the Microsoft Entra roles list showing eligible roles.](./media/pim-how-to-activate-role/activate-link.png) + +1. Select **Activate** to open the Activate pane. + + ![Screenshot of Microsoft Entra role activation details showing duration and scope.](./media/pim-how-to-activate-role/activate-page.png) + +1. Select **Additional verification required** and follow the instructions to provide security verification. You are required to authenticate only once per session. + + ![Screenshot of the security verification screen for role activation.](./media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/resources-mfa-enter-code.png) + +1. After multifactor authentication, select **Activate before proceeding**. + + ![Screenshot of the identity verification prompt before role activation.](./media/pim-how-to-activate-role/activate-role-mfa-banner.png) + +1. If you want to specify a reduced scope, select **Scope** to open the filter pane. On the filter pane, you can specify the Microsoft Entra resources that you need access to. It's a best practice to request access to the fewest resources that you need. + +1. If necessary, specify a custom activation start time. The Microsoft Entra role would be activated after the selected time. + +1. In the **Reason** box, enter the reason for the activation request. + +1. Select **Activate**. + + If the [role requires approval](pim-approval-workflow.md) to activate, a notification appears in the upper right corner of your browser informing you the request is pending approval. + + ![Screenshot of the notification that a role activation request is pending approval.](./media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/resources-my-roles-activate-notification.png) + +## View the status of activation requests + +You can view the status of your pending requests to activate. + +1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a [Privileged Role Administrator](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#privileged-role-administrator). + +1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Privileged Identity Management** > **My requests**. + +1. When you select **My requests** you see a list of your Microsoft Entra role and Azure resource role requests. + + :::image type="content" source="./media/pim-how-to-activate-role/my-requests-page.png" alt-text="Screenshot of My requests - Microsoft Entra ID page showing your pending requests" lightbox="./media/pim-how-to-activate-role/my-requests-page.png"::: + +1. Scroll to the right to view the **Request Status** column. + + + +## Cancel a pending request in the Microsoft Entra admin center + +If you don't require activation of a role that requires approval, you can cancel a pending request at any time. + +1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a [Privileged Role Administrator](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#privileged-role-administrator). + +1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Privileged Identity Management** > **My requests**. + +1. For the role that you want to cancel, select the **Cancel** link. + + When you select Cancel, the request is canceled. To activate the role again, you have to submit a new request for activation. + + ![Screenshot of the My requests list with the Cancel action highlighted.](./media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/resources-my-requests-cancel.png) + +::: zone-end + +::: zone pivot="my-access" + + + + + +## Activate a Microsoft Entra role in My Access portal (Preview) + +Use [**Roles**](https://aka.ms/pim/roles) under **My Access** in the [My Access portal](../my-access-portal-overview.md) to activate an eligible Microsoft Entra role assignment. + +Microsoft Entra role assignment activation through the My Access portal is in preview. View the status of your activation requests and your role assignments under **My Microsoft Entra roles**. + + :::image type="content" source="./media/pim-how-to-activate-role/mobile-app-select-part-3.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the mobile app showing the user's role status." lightbox="./media/pim-how-to-activate-role/mobile-app-select-part-3.png"::: + +::: zone-end + +## Deactivate a role assignment + +When a role assignment is activated, you see a **Deactivate** option in the portal for the role assignment. Also, you can't deactivate a role assignment within five minutes after activation. + +To deactivate your active role assignment by using Microsoft Graph, create a role assignment schedule request with `action` set to `selfDeactivate`. For the request format and permissions, see [Create roleAssignmentScheduleRequests](/graph/api/rbacapplication-post-roleassignmentschedulerequests). + +## Related content + +- [View audit history for Microsoft Entra roles](pim-how-to-use-audit-log.md)

newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-how-to-enable-pim-only-mode.md b/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-how-to-enable-pim-only-mode.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..5501edc6008 --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-how-to-enable-pim-only-mode.md @@ -0,0 +1,133 @@ +--- +title: Configure PIM-only mode for Azure (preview) +description: Configure PIM-only mode for an Azure subscription to help enforce PIM role assignment settings. Review audit events and configure exceptions before enforcement. +ms.topic: how-to +ms.date: 11/02/2026 +ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1030 +ai-usage: ai-assisted +#customer intent: As an IT administrator, I want to configure PIM-only mode for an Azure subscription so that PIM role assignment settings apply when administrators manage access. +--- + +# Configure PIM-only mode for Azure (preview) + +PIM-only mode for Azure (preview) helps ensure that your organization's Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) role assignment settings apply when you manage Azure role assignments. You can manage role assignments in both **Privileged Identity Management** and **Access control (IAM)**. + +Use this guide to configure PIM-only mode for an Azure subscription. Start in **Audit** mode to review role assignment operations that would be blocked, configure any necessary exceptions, and then switch to **Deny** mode. + +Existing role assignments continue to function. + +## Prerequisites + +- To read and assign Azure Policy and manage policy exemptions, you need the **Resource Policy Contributor** or **Owner** role at Azure subscription scope. +- To manage PIM role settings for the Azure subscription, you need the **Owner** or **User Access Administrator** role at Azure subscription scope. + +## Assign the policy in Audit mode + +Start in **Audit** mode to identify role assignment operations that would be blocked in **Deny** mode. Review those operations to determine whether they can follow PIM role assignment settings or need an exception. The policy's default effect is **Audit**. Keep this setting for the initial rollout to review operations before enforcing restrictions. + +Both **Privileged Identity Management** and **Access control (IAM)** support role assignment management. The following table shows how **Deny** mode restricts specific operations at Azure subscription scope. Each action requires appropriate permissions. + +| Action in the admin interface | Without PIM-only mode | With PIM-only mode (Deny) | +| --- | --- | --- | +| Manage eligible or active assignments in **Privileged Identity Management**. | Available. | Available. | +| Manage eligible assignments in **Access control (IAM)**. | Available. | Available. | +| Manage active assignments in **Access control (IAM)**. | Available. | Blocked; exceptions don't apply. | + +> [!WARNING] +> Before enforcing PIM-only mode, ensure that you have an emergency recovery option if your usual administrative access becomes unavailable. Configure emergency access accounts with **permanent active Global Administrator role assignments** in Microsoft Entra ID, as described in [Manage emergency access accounts in Microsoft Entra ID](~/identity/role-based-access-control/security-emergency-access.md). +> +> Microsoft Entra Global Administrators can use [Elevate access](/azure/role-based-access-control/elevate-access-global-admin) to obtain permissions to manage access to Azure resources. In an emergency, an administrator with the required permissions can also [delete the policy assignment through Azure Policy](/azure/governance/policy/assign-policy-portal#clean-up-resources). + +1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com). + +1. Browse to **ID Governance** > **Privileged Identity Management** > **Azure resources**. From the **Subscriptions** dropdown, select the Azure subscription where you want to configure PIM-only mode. + + :::image type="content" source="media/pim-resource-roles-configure-role-settings/resources-list.png" alt-text="Screenshot that shows the list of Azure resources discovered in Privileged Identity Management." lightbox="media/pim-resource-roles-configure-role-settings/resources-list.png"::: + +1. Select **Assignment Policies**, and then select **+ Assign policy**. + +1. On the **Basics** tab, review the **Scope** and any **Exclusions**. Confirm that **Policy definition** is **Azure role assignment management should be restricted to Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management**. Keep **Policy enforcement** set to **Enabled**. + + :::image type="content" source="media/pim-resource-roles-configure-role-settings/pim-only-mode-policy-basics.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Assign policy Basics tab with Assignment Policies selected in the left navigation." lightbox="media/pim-resource-roles-configure-role-settings/pim-only-mode-policy-basics.png"::: + +1. On the **Parameters** tab, clear **Only show parameters that need input or review**, and confirm that **Effect** is set to **Audit**. + + :::image type="content" source="media/pim-resource-roles-configure-role-settings/pim-only-mode-policy-parameters.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Assign policy Parameters tab with Effect set to Audit and exception parameters visible." lightbox="media/pim-resource-roles-configure-role-settings/pim-only-mode-policy-parameters.png"::: + +1. Leave the exception parameters at their default empty lists unless you have a specific scenario that requires an exception to PIM-only mode: + + - **Exempted Role Definition IDs:** Exempt assignments for the listed role definition IDs from PIM-only mode restrictions. + - **Exempt Requestor Types:** Select the principal types from the dropdown for identities allowed to make assignments without PIM-only mode restrictions. + - **Exempt Assignee Types:** Select the principal types from the dropdown for identities allowed to receive role assignments without PIM-only mode restrictions. + - **Excluded Requestors:** Allow the listed requester object IDs to create active assignments without PIM-only mode restrictions. For example, to allow an application to create these assignments, add its object ID to this list. + + These parameters allow exceptions based on the role or identities involved. To exempt a scope instead, use an Azure Policy exemption as described in Review activity logs and configure exemptions. Parameter-based exceptions don't allow active assignment creation through **Access control (IAM)**. + +1. On **Review + create**, review the settings, and then select **Create**. + +The policy assignment appears on the **Assignment Policies** page. In **Audit** mode, noncompliant attempts to create or update assignments are allowed and recorded as audit events in the Azure Activity Log. + +:::image type="content" source="media/pim-resource-roles-configure-role-settings/pim-only-mode-policy-assignments.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Assignment Policies page showing the created policy assignment and its View activity logs link." lightbox="media/pim-resource-roles-configure-role-settings/pim-only-mode-policy-assignments.png"::: + +For more information about policy assignment options, see [Create a policy assignment in the Azure portal](/azure/governance/policy/assign-policy-portal). + + + +## Review activity logs and configure exemptions + +Use the Azure Activity Log to review role assignment operations before switching to **Deny**. Start from the **Assignment Policies** page in PIM and open the activity logs for the policy assignment. + +1. On **Assignment Policies**, select **View activity logs** next to the policy assignment to open its activity logs. +1. Review audit events for noncompliant attempts to create or update role assignments. For each operation, determine whether it can follow PIM role assignment settings or requires an exception. +1. If a scope requires an Azure Policy exemption, select the policy assignment, and then select **Create exemption**. +1. Specify the **Scope**, **Exemption name**, **Exemption category**, **Expiration**, and **Description**. In the description, record the business justification and owner. + + :::image type="content" source="media/pim-resource-roles-configure-role-settings/pim-only-mode-create-exemption.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Create exemption page showing scope, exemption name, category, expiration, and description fields." lightbox="media/pim-resource-roles-configure-role-settings/pim-only-mode-create-exemption.png"::: + +1. Select **Review + create**, review the details, and then create the exemption. + +Azure Policy exemptions support expiration dates and exemption categories. Review exemptions at least quarterly, and use the narrowest scope and shortest expiration that meets the need. + +For more information about exemption scopes, categories, and expiration, see [Azure Policy exemption structure](/azure/governance/policy/concepts/exemption-structure). + + + +## Switch to Deny mode + +After you review audit events and configure any necessary exceptions, use the **Deny** effect to help enforce PIM role assignment settings unless an exception applies. Tell administrators who work in the affected scope that they can manage assignments in both **Privileged Identity Management** and **Access control (IAM)**, subject to the **Deny** mode restrictions. + +1. Return to **Privileged Identity Management** > **Azure resources**, and select the scope. +1. Under **Manage**, select **Assignment Policies**, and then select the policy assignment. +1. Select **View assignment**, and edit the assignment. +1. On the **Parameters** tab, clear **Only show parameters that need input or review**, and change **Effect** from **Audit** to **Deny**. +1. Save the assignment. + +Active assignment creation through **Access control (IAM)** is blocked in **Deny** mode and can't be exempted. Each policy assignment is independent, so you can use **Deny** on one scope while continuing to audit another. + +## API and automation behavior + +If you use Azure CLI, PowerShell, scripts, or applications to manage assignments, their behavior depends on the API they call and any applicable policy exceptions. These tools aren't categorically blocked. + +PIM-only mode uses Azure Policy to audit or block role assignment management through APIs other than PIM APIs. Both **Privileged Identity Management** and **Access control (IAM)** support role assignment management; the restriction depends on the API used for the operation, not just the interface. **Privileged Identity Management** and eligible assignment creation through **Access control (IAM)** use PIM APIs. Active assignment creation through **Access control (IAM)** doesn't use PIM APIs. + +| API used to manage assignments | Without PIM-only mode | With PIM-only mode (Deny) | +| --- | --- | --- | +| PIM APIs. | Available with appropriate permissions. | Available with appropriate permissions. | +| Non-PIM APIs. | Available with appropriate permissions. | Blocked unless a configured exception applies for the client. | + + + + + +## Scope and preview limitations + +PIM-only mode for Azure doesn't govern Microsoft Entra directory roles or the Groups resource provider. Consider these limitations when you review activity logs and plan exceptions: + +- **Supported scope:** You can configure PIM-only mode at Azure subscription scope. Management group scope isn't supported in the preview. +- **Activity logs:** Use audit and deny events in the Azure Activity Log to identify noncompliant attempts to create or update role assignments. + + + +## Related content + +- [Configure Azure resource role settings in PIM](pim-resource-roles-configure-role-settings.md).

newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-manage-bastion-sessions.md b/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-manage-bastion-sessions.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..367f6e95192 --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-manage-bastion-sessions.md @@ -0,0 +1,51 @@ +--- +title: Monitor and disconnect Azure Bastion sessions in PIM +description: Learn how to find active Azure Bastion sessions in Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management and disconnect a selected session. +author: tamimsangrar +ms.author: tamimsangrar +ms.topic: how-to +ms.date: 11/17/2026 +ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1032 +ai-usage: ai-generated +#customer intent: As an administrator, I want to find and disconnect active Azure Bastion sessions so that I can manage privileged sessions in the selected Azure scope. +--- + +# Monitor and disconnect Azure Bastion sessions in PIM (Preview) + + + +Use Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) to find active Azure Bastion sessions in an Azure subscription or resource group and disconnect a selected session. + +Session Management in PIM is in preview and supports RDP and SSH sessions. + +## Prerequisites + +- Microsoft Entra ID Governance licensing is required for Session Management. See [Microsoft Entra ID Governance licensing fundamentals](../licensing-fundamentals.md). +- A deployed Azure Bastion host and an active session in the scope you want to manage. For deployment, see [Deploy Azure Bastion](/azure/bastion/quickstart-host-portal). +- The **Network Contributor** role on the resource group containing the Azure Bastion host, for viewing and disconnecting sessions. + +## Find and disconnect a session + +Find the session before you disconnect it so that you act on the intended user and Azure Virtual Machine. + +1. Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com). +1. Open **Privileged Identity Management**, select **Azure resources**, and select the Azure subscription or resource group you want to manage. +1. Under **Activity**, select **Session Management (Preview)**. +1. Search for the user, Azure Virtual Machine, Bastion host, protocol, or IP address. + + :::image type="content" source="media/pim-manage-bastion-sessions/session-management-active-session.png" alt-text="Screenshot of Session Management with an active SSH session selected and the Disconnect action available." lightbox="media/pim-manage-bastion-sessions/session-management-active-session.png"::: + +1. Select the session, and then select **Disconnect**. + + In the confirmation dialog, select **Disconnect** to confirm, or **Cancel** to keep the session connected. + + After a successful disconnection, the session automatically disappears from the list. + +1. Optional: Select **Refresh** to reload the session list. Use **Load more** to scan additional hosts. + +Selecting **Disconnect** ends the selected Azure Bastion connection without deactivating the user’s role assignments. The user can reconnect if they still meet the connection requirements. For more information, see [Azure Bastion session monitoring and management](/azure/bastion/session-monitoring). + +## Related content + +- [Connect to an Azure Virtual Machine from My Access](pim-connect-virtual-machine-my-access.md). +- [View activity and audit history for Azure resource roles](azure-pim-resource-rbac.md).

newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles.md b/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..ec0edbb071b --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles.md @@ -0,0 +1,408 @@ +--- +title: Activate Azure resource roles in PIM +description: Learn how to activate eligible Azure resource roles with Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) to manage Azure resources. +ms.author: tamimsangrar +ms.date: 11/16/2026 +ms.topic: how-to +ai-usage: ai-assisted +ms.custom: + - pim + - sfi-image-nochange + - msecd-doc-authoring-1031 +zone_pivot_groups: pim-azure-role-activation-portals +#customer intent: As a user with eligible Azure resource role assignments, I want to activate my roles so that I can manage Azure subscriptions and resources when needed. +--- + +# Activate my Azure resource roles in Privileged Identity Management + +Use Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) to allow eligible role members for Azure resources to schedule activation for a future date and time. They can also select a specific activation duration within the maximum (configured by administrators). + +This article is for members who need to activate their Azure resource role in Privileged Identity Management. + +> [!NOTE] +> Agents and agent identities can receive and activate eligible Azure resource role assignments in preview. Each agent or agent identity requires an E7 license. See [agent preview requirements](pim-resource-roles-assign-roles.md#eligible-assignments-for-agents-preview). For activation, see [Agent identity API activation (preview)](pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles.md?pivots=api#activate-an-agent-identity-with-azure-resource-manager-api-preview). + +Choose the method you will use to activate your Azure role assignment. + +>[!IMPORTANT] +>When a role is activated, Microsoft Entra PIM temporarily adds active assignment for the role. Microsoft Entra PIM creates active assignment (assigns user to a role) within seconds. When deactivation (manual or through activation time expiration) happens, Microsoft Entra PIM removes the active assignment within seconds as well. +> +>Application may provide access based on the role the user has. In some situations, application access may not immediately reflect the fact that user got role assigned or removed. If application previously cached the fact that user does not have a role – when user tries to access application again, access may not be provided. Similarly, if application previously cached the fact that user has a role – when role is deactivated, user may still get access. Specific situation depends on the application’s architecture. For some applications, signing out and signing back in may help get access added or removed. + +::: zone pivot="entra-admin-center" + + + +## Activate a role in the Microsoft Entra admin center + +When you need to take on an Azure resource role, you can request activation by using the **My roles** navigation option in Privileged Identity Management. + +>[!NOTE] +> PIM is now available in the Azure mobile app (iOS | Android) for Microsoft Entra ID and Azure resource roles. Easily activate eligible assignments, request renewals for ones that are expiring, or check the status of pending requests. [Activate roles with the Azure mobile app](pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles.md?pivots=azure-mobile-app#activate-pim-roles-using-the-azure-mobile-app) + +1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com). + +1. Browse to **Identity Governance** > **Privileged Identity Management** > **My roles**. + + [![Screenshot of my roles page showing roles you can activate.](./media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/resources-my-roles.png)](./media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/resources-my-roles.png#lightbox) + +1. Select **Azure resources** to see a list of your eligible Azure resource roles. + + ![Screenshot of my roles - Azure resource roles page.](./media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/resources-my-roles-azure-resources.png) + +1. In the **Azure resource roles** list, find the role you want to activate. + + [![Screenshot of azure resource roles - My eligible roles list.](./media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/resources-my-roles-activate.png)](./media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/resources-my-roles-activate.png#lightbox) + +1. Select **Activate** to open the Activate page. + + ![Screenshot of the opened Activate pane with scope, start time, duration, and reason.](./media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/azure-role-eligible-activate.png) + +1. If your role requires multifactor authentication, select **Verify your identity before proceeding**. You only have to authenticate once per session. + +1. Select **Verify my identity** and follow the instructions to provide additional security verification. + + ![Screenshot of screen to provide security verification such as a PIN code.](./media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/resources-mfa-enter-code.png) + +1. It's a best practice to only request access to the resources you need. If you want to specify a reduced scope. + + 1. Go to the **Scope** tab. + 1. Click **Select scope** to select the scope. + + :::image type="content" source="./media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/activate-billing-reader-select-scope.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Scope tab in the Activate - Billing Reader pane, showing the 'Select scope' button and a management group listed under Selected resources. This helps users identify where to click to begin scoping their activation request."::: + + 1. Use the dropdown provided to scope the search to a specific resource. + 1. The reduced scoped resources are shown in **Selected resources** before activation and should be selected from the grid provided. The dropdown selection does not define the reduced scope. + + :::image type="content" source="./media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/active-billing-reader-set-scope.png" alt-text="Screenshot showing the process of setting the scope for activation, with a management group selected in the grid. This image demonstrates how to confirm the correct resource is selected before proceeding with activation."::: + + >[!NOTE] + >If your eligibility is at the management group level, the dropdown will show all direct child resources (management group and subscription). You can select either a management group or subscription from the grid shown, or further scope down the search by selecting the appropriate management group or subscription. + + ![Screenshot of activate - Resource filter pane to specify scope.](./media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/resources-my-roles-resource-filter.png) + +1. If necessary, specify a custom activation start time. The member would be activated after the selected time. + +1. In the **Reason** box, enter the reason for the activation request. + +1. Optional: If your administrator enabled [Allow least-privilege role activation](pim-resource-roles-configure-role-settings.md#allow-least-privilege-role-activation) on the policy for your eligible role, select the **Role** tab. In the **Role** dropdown, choose an available lower-privileged role whose permissions are sufficient for your task. + + The eligible role's policy governs approval, authentication, justification, and activation maximum duration, including selection of a lower-privileged role. + + :::image type="content" source="media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/entra-manual-role-selection.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Role tab in the Microsoft Entra admin center activation pane, showing the Role dropdown for manual role selection." lightbox="media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/entra-manual-role-selection.png"::: + +1. Optional: To request a Microsoft Security Copilot recommendation, select the **Activate** tab and review the task description in the **Reason** box. Select **Copilot can recommend a lower-privileged role**. + + This option requires **Allow least-privilege role activation** to be enabled and access to Microsoft Security Copilot in your tenant. A default Security Copilot workspace must be available for the Microsoft Entra integration, and you must have access to it. Recommendations consume security compute units (SCUs). You can select a role manually without Copilot when **Allow least-privilege role activation** is enabled. + + :::image type="content" source="media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/entra-copilot-request.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Activate tab with the Reason box and the Copilot can recommend a lower-privileged role button." lightbox="media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/entra-copilot-request.png"::: + + Review the recommended role and its suitability for your task. To use it, select **Switch to the recommended role**. Copilot doesn't create eligible role assignments or activate a role on your behalf. The eligible role's policy requirements still apply. + + :::image type="content" source="media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/entra-copilot-recommendation.png" alt-text="Screenshot of a Copilot role recommendation with the Switch to the recommended role button and a separate Activate button." lightbox="media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/entra-copilot-recommendation.png"::: + +1. Select **Activate**. + + >[!NOTE] + >If the [role requires approval](pim-resource-roles-approval-workflow.md) to activate, a notification will appear in the upper right corner of your browser informing you the request is pending approval. + +::: zone-end + +::: zone pivot="azure-portal" + + + +## Activate a role in the Azure portal + +Privileged Identity Management role activation is integrated into the Billing and Access Control (AD) extensions within the Azure portal. Shortcuts to Subscriptions (billing) and Access Control (AD) allow you to activate PIM roles directly from these blades. + +From the Subscriptions blade, select “View eligible subscriptions” in the horizontal command menu to check your eligible, active, and expired assignments. From there, you can activate an eligible assignment in the same pane. + + ![Screenshot of view eligible subscriptions on the Subscriptions page.](./media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/view-subscriptions-1.png) + + ![Screenshot of view eligible subscriptions on the Cost Management: Integration Service page.](./media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/view-subscriptions-2.png) + +In Access control (IAM) for a resource, you can now select “View my access” to see your currently active and eligible role assignments and activate directly. + + ![Screenshot of current role assignments on the Measurement page.](./media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/view-my-access.png) + +By integrating PIM capabilities into different Azure portal blades, this new feature allows you to gain temporary access to view or edit subscriptions and resources more easily. + +::: zone-end + +::: zone pivot="entra-admin-center" + +## View the status of your requests + +You can view the status of your pending requests to activate. + +1. Open Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management. + +1. Select **My requests** to see a list of your Microsoft Entra role and Azure resource role requests. + + [![Screenshot of my requests - Azure resource page showing your pending requests.](./media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/resources-my-requests.png)](./media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/resources-my-requests.png#lightbox) + +1. Scroll to the right to view the **Request Status** column. + +## Cancel a pending request + +If you don't require activation of a role that requires approval, you can cancel a pending request at any time. + +1. Open Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management. + +1. Select **My requests**. + +1. For the role that you want to cancel, select the **Cancel** link. + + When you select Cancel, the request will be canceled. To activate the role again, you will have to submit a new request for activation. + + ![Screenshot of my request list with Cancel action highlighted.](./media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/resources-my-requests-cancel.png) + +::: zone-end + +::: zone pivot="my-access" + + + + + + + +## Activate an Azure resource role in My Access portal (Preview) + +Use [**Roles**](https://aka.ms/pim/roles) under **My Access** in the [My Access portal](../my-access-portal-overview.md) to activate an eligible Azure resource role assignment. + +Azure resource role assignment activation through the My Access portal is in preview. Activation uses an existing eligible role assignment to give your signed-in identity temporary access. + +1. Sign in to the [My Access portal](https://myaccess.microsoft.com) in the tenant where you have an eligible role assignment. + +1. Under **My Access**, select [**Roles**](https://aka.ms/pim/roles), and then select **Azure Roles**. + +1. Find the role assignments and select **Activate**. + + :::image type="content" source="media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/my-access-azure-roles.png" alt-text="Screenshot of My Access Azure roles showing eligible role assignments and their Activate actions." lightbox="media/pim-resource-roles-activate-your-roles/my-access-azure-roles.png"::: + +1. @@ -0,0 +1,75 @@
+---
+title: Secure Enterprise Browser Overview (Preview)
+description: Learn how secure enterprise browser combines Microsoft Edge and Global Secure Access for private web apps and protected internet and Microsoft 365 browsing.
+ms.topic: concept-article
+ms.date: 11/13/2026
+ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1026
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+ms.author: alexpav
+# Customer intent: As an IT administrator, I want to understand secure enterprise browser capabilities so that I can plan browser-only access for employees and protect browsing on company-owned kiosks and VDI devices.
+---
+
+# Secure enterprise browser overview (preview)
+
+Secure enterprise browser integrates Microsoft Edge with Global Secure Access (GSA) for browser-based access to private web applications. It also protects internet and Microsoft 365 traffic without installing the Global Secure Access client. Microsoft Entra Conditional Access steers users to sign in to Microsoft Edge using their work account. Edge Management Service (EMS) delivers the GSA policy to Edge. Edge uses the traffic forwarding policy calculated from your Global Secure Access traffic forwarding profiles.
+
+This article explains the supported scenarios, how traffic forwarding works, and the limitations of the preview. The preview supports Microsoft Edge on Windows and macOS.
+
+## Browser-only access scenarios
+
+You can use secure enterprise browser when you want to allow access to private web applications and when you want to protect user's browsing activities using Global Secure Access policies, without deploying the GSA client software or requiring a managed device.
+
+- **Limited browser-only access for your users with Entra ID work accounts.** Give employees access to selected private web applications through Edge, rather than deploying a client for access from other applications. Use Global Secure Access traffic forwarding profiles and application assignments to define the resources available to those users.
+- **Company-owned kiosks.** Protect internet access on Windows kiosks where employees use Edge with their work accounts.
+- **Virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI).** Provide employees with access to private web applications and protect their internet access in Edge on Windows VDI devices without installing the Global Secure Access client.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> These scenarios require users to sign in to Edge with a work account in your tenant. Business-to-business (B2B) guest accounts aren't supported because users can't sign in to Edge with a B2B guest account.
+
+## Traffic forwarding and policy
+
+Global Secure Access calculates the user's traffic forwarding policy from traffic forwarding profiles, just as it does for the Global Secure Access client. Edge retrieves that policy and uses it to forward browser traffic to the service.
+
+There are three configuration elements for secure enterprise browser connectivity:
+
+- **Global Secure Access Microsoft Edge Configuration** determines which traffic types are enabled for Edge and which forwarding profiles and rules apply to the user. Here, you can selectively enable Internet Access (which includes Microsoft 365), Private Access, or both.
+- **Global Secure Access Traffic Forwarding Configuration** determines the resulting traffic forwarding policy for the signed-in user.
+- **Edge Management Experience (EMX) policy** enables the integration in Edge - it instructs Edge to follow the traffic forwarding policy for the signed-in user.
+
+For background on profile configuration, see [Global Secure Access traffic forwarding profiles](concept-traffic-forwarding.md).
+
+## Supported traffic profiles
+
+You can enable Internet Access and Private Access for Microsoft Edge independently. Microsoft 365 traffic is enabled together with Internet Access in the browser enablement configuration.
+
+| Traffic profile | Preview support |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Internet** | Supported. Global Secure Access applies Microsoft Entra Internet Access policies, including Transport Layer Security (TLS) inspection and bypass policies. |
+| **Microsoft 365** | Supported. Enabled together with Internet Access for Edge. The Microsoft traffic forwarding profile determines how Microsoft 365 traffic is forwarded. No TLS inspection, no web filtering policies. |
+| **Private Access** | Supported for private web applications configured by fully qualified domain name (FQDN). |
+| **Microsoft Entra** | Not supported. |
+
+Global Secure Access delivers TLS inspection certificate trust automatically to Edge. You don't need to deploy the TLS inspection certificate to user's devices or to Microsoft Edge profiles. You still configure the certificate and TLS inspection policies in Global Secure Access.
+
+## Preview requirements and limitations
+
+Plan your deployment around these preview boundaries:
+
+- **Platforms:** Microsoft Edge on Windows and macOS.
+- **Global Secure Access client coexistence:** On Windows, running the Global Secure Access client while Microsoft Edge is configured for Global Secure Access is supported. On macOS, this coexistence isn't supported. Enabling the client while Edge is configured for Global Secure Access results in unexpected mutual TLS (mTLS) certificate prompts presented to the user.
+- **Minimum Edge version:** 157.0.4341.46.
+- **Browser configuration:** EMS policy is the only supported configuration method. Intune app policies aren't supported for enabling this integration in the preview.
+- **Identity:** Users sign in to Edge with a work account in the tenant configured for Global Secure Access. B2B guest accounts aren't supported.
+- **Microsoft Entra ID traffic:** The Microsoft Entra traffic profile isn't supported. Compliant network checks and universal tenant restrictions for Microsoft Entra ID aren't supported by this preview.
+- **Private name resolution:** Private DNS isn't supported. Configure private web applications by FQDN rather than relying on IP-only application definitions to provide private name resolution.
+
+## Next step
+
+> [!div class="nextstepaction"]
+> [Configure Global Secure Access secure enterprise browser settings](how-to-configure-global-secure-access-browser-settings.md)
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Global Secure Access traffic forwarding profiles](concept-traffic-forwarding.md)
+- [Explicit Forward Proxy overview](concept-explicit-forward-proxy.md)
+- [Global Secure Access traffic logs](how-to-view-traffic-logs.md)

@@ -0,0 +1,101 @@
+---
+title: Configure Global Secure Access Browser Settings (Preview)
+description: Configure Global Secure Access secure enterprise browser settings and traffic forwarding for native Microsoft Edge integration on Windows and macOS.
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/13/2026
+ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1026
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+ms.author: alexpav
+# Customer intent: As an IT administrator, I want to configure Global Secure Access secure enterprise browser settings so that employees can use protected browsing and private web applications on Windows and macOS.
+---
+
+# Configure Global Secure Access secure enterprise browser settings (preview)
+
+Configure secure enterprise browser with Microsoft Edge and Global Secure Access to give employees browser-only access to private web applications. You can also protect internet and Microsoft 365 browsing. This configuration supports company-owned Windows kiosks and virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI) devices without installing the Global Secure Access client.
+
+Enable the traffic types for secure enterprise browser using the Entra admin center, and then use the Microsoft 365 Admin center to configure an Edge Management Service (EMS) policy. This preview supports Windows and macOS.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A tenant onboarded to Global Secure Access. See [Access Global Secure Access in the admin center](quickstart-access-admin-center.md).
+- The **Global Secure Access Administrator** role to configure Global Secure Access.
+- The **Application Administrator** role to assign users to traffic forwarding profiles and to configure Private Access enterprise applications and connector groups.
+- Licenses for the Global Secure Access capabilities you plan to use. See [Global Secure Access licensing](overview-what-is-global-secure-access.md#licensing-overview).
+- The [Edge Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#edge-administrator) role, the least-privileged role to configure and assign the Edge policy in the M365 admin center.
+- Microsoft Edge for Windows or macOS, version **157.0.4341.46** or newer.
+- Work accounts in your tenant for the employees who use the feature. Business-to-business (B2B) guest accounts aren't supported because users can't sign in to Edge with those accounts.
+- For Private Access, private web applications configured by fully qualified domain name (FQDN) and the associated private network connectors. See [Configure per-app access](how-to-configure-per-app-access.md).
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> EMS is the only supported method to enable this integration in Edge for the preview. Intune app policies aren't supported for this configuration.
+
+On Windows, the Global Secure Access client can run while Microsoft Edge is configured for Global Secure Access.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> On macOS, running the Global Secure Access client while Edge is configured for Global Secure Access isn't supported and results in certificate prompts. Keep the client disabled while using the Edge integration on macOS.
+
+## Configure traffic forwarding in Global Secure Access
+
+Global Secure Access calculates the user's traffic forwarding policy from traffic forwarding profiles, just as it does for the Global Secure Access client. Configure these profiles for your intended users before testing Edge.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as a **Global Secure Access Administrator**.
+1. Go to **Global Secure Access** > **Connect** > **Traffic forwarding**.
+1. Configure the profiles for the traffic types you want to forward:
+
+    - For internet and Microsoft 365 browsing, configure the [Internet traffic profile](how-to-manage-internet-access-profile.md) and the [Microsoft traffic profile](how-to-manage-microsoft-profile.md).
+    - For private web applications, configure a [Private Access traffic forwarding profile](how-to-manage-private-access-profile.md) and the applications employees need.
+
+1. [Assign the profiles to the intended users](how-to-manage-users-groups-assignment.md). Confirm that the users who receive the Edge policy are included in the applicable Global Secure Access profile assignments.
+
+The Edge policy enables the browser integration. It doesn't define a separate set of traffic forwarding rules.
+
+## Enable browser access in the Global Secure Access portal
+
+Choose which traffic types Edge can forward to Global Secure Access. Internet Access and Microsoft 365 share a browser enablement control; Private Access is enabled separately.
+
+1. In the Microsoft Entra admin center, go to **Global Secure Access** > **Connect** > **Explicit forward proxy**.
+1. Turn on **Global Secure Access with Microsoft Edge**.
+1. Under **Settings**, select the traffic types required for your deployment:
+
+    - **Internet Access with Microsoft Edge**. Select this option for both internet and Microsoft 365 traffic. There isn't a separate Microsoft 365 browser enablement option.
+    - **Private Access with Microsoft Edge**. Select this option for private web applications.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/howto-secure-enterprise-browser/enable-browser-access.png" alt-text="Screenshot of Global Secure Access with Microsoft Edge enabled, with Internet Access and Private Access selected." lightbox="media/howto-secure-enterprise-browser/enable-browser-access.png":::
+
+1. Configure the Edge policy in the M365 admin center.
+
+Enabling Internet Access for Edge also enables Microsoft 365 support in the browser configuration. Continue to manage the forwarding rules and user assignments for each traffic profile in Global Secure Access.
+
+## Configure the Edge policy
+
+Use the M365 admin center to enable the Edge integration for the users who need browser-based access. Global Secure Access portal enablement and the EMS policy are both required.
+
+Follow [Configure Global Secure Access policy in Microsoft Edge secure enterprise browser settings](how-to-configure-global-secure-access-edge-policy.md) to create and assign the cloud policy, set **Enable secure network access (preview)** to **Enabled**, and save your changes.
+
+Global Secure Access delivers Transport Layer Security (TLS) inspection certificate trust automatically to Edge. No separate manual certificate deployment to Edge is required for this integration. For Internet Access, configure the certificate and [TLS inspection policies](how-to-transport-layer-security.md) in Global Secure Access. Automatic trust delivery to Edge doesn't replace that service configuration or establish device-wide certificate trust.
+
+## Validate browser access
+
+Test from an employee account included in both the Edge policy assignment and the applicable Global Secure Access traffic forwarding profiles.
+
+1. On a Windows or macOS device, open the supported version of Edge and sign in to a work profile with the employee's account.
+1. Open `edge://policy` and confirm that the policy configured in EMS appears with the intended value.
+1. Browse to destinations covered by your enabled profiles:
+
+    - An internet destination covered by your Internet Access policy.
+    - A Microsoft 365 destination covered by your Microsoft traffic profile, if enabled.
+    - A private web application using its FQDN, if Private Access is enabled.
+
+1. In the Microsoft Entra admin center, go to **Global Secure Access** > **Monitor** > **Traffic logs**.
+1. Select **Transactions** and filter **Device Category** to **Secure enterprise browser**.
+1. Review the corresponding transactions. Compare the traffic type, destination, and access decision with your configured policies.
+
+The Microsoft Entra traffic profile isn't supported in this preview. Don't use compliant network checks or tenant restrictions v2 policies for Microsoft Entra ID to validate this integration. Private DNS is also unsupported.
+
+If access fails or traffic doesn't match your policy, use [Troubleshoot secure enterprise browser](troubleshoot-secure-enterprise-browser.md) to check assignments, effective Edge policies, and traffic logs.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Secure enterprise browser overview](concept-secure-enterprise-browser.md)
+- [Assign users to traffic forwarding profiles](how-to-manage-users-groups-assignment.md)
+- [Use Global Secure Access traffic logs](how-to-view-traffic-logs.md)

+---
+title: Configure Global Secure Access Policy in Microsoft Edge (Preview)
+description: Configure the Global Secure Access policy in Microsoft Edge secure enterprise browser settings and assign it to employee work profiles on Windows and macOS.
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/13/2026
+ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1026

+ms.author: alexpav
+#customer intent: As an Edge administrator, I want to configure and assign the Global Secure Access policy in Microsoft Edge secure enterprise browser settings so that employees can use secure enterprise browser in their work profiles.
+---
+
+# Configure Global Secure Access policy in Microsoft Edge secure enterprise browser settings (preview)
+
+Configure a Microsoft Edge policy in Edge Management Experience (EMX) to enable secure enterprise browser for your employees. Create and assign a cloud policy to enable secure network access for Edge on Windows and macOS. Before you begin, configure Global Secure Access for browser access and confirm your Edge Administrator role assignment. For the full requirements, see [Prerequisites](#prerequisites).
+
+The Edge policy enables the browser integration. Global Secure Access traffic forwarding profiles determine the traffic forwarding rules that apply to each user.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Global Secure Access traffic forwarding and browser enablement configured for your deployment. Complete the [Global Secure Access configuration steps](how-to-configure-global-secure-access-browser-settings.md#configure-traffic-forwarding-in-global-secure-access) before configuring Edge.
+- An account with an active [Edge Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#edge-administrator) role, the least-privileged role for this task.
+- Microsoft Edge for Windows or macOS, version **157.0.4341.46** or newer.
+- Employee work accounts in your Global Secure Access tenant. Business-to-business (B2B) guest accounts aren't supported.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> On Windows, the Global Secure Access client can run while Edge is configured for Global Secure Access. On macOS, this coexistence isn't supported and results in certificate prompts. Keep the client disabled while using the Edge integration on macOS.
+
+## Create and assign the Edge policy
+
+Create a cloud policy and choose the employees who receive it. You configure the secure network access setting after creating the policy.
+
+1. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, open the [Microsoft Edge policy creation page](https://admin.cloud.microsoft/#/Edge/PolicyConfiguration/id/CreateConfiguration). Sign in with your Edge Administrator account.
+1. On **Basics**, enter a **Name** for the policy, such as *Global Secure Access Settings*, and a **Description**.
+1. Under **Platforms**, select **Windows 10+**, **macOS 11+**, or both for your deployment. Set **Policy type** to **Cloud**.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/how-to-configure-edge-policy-global-secure-access/create-policy.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the policy Basics page with a name, description, Windows and macOS platforms, and Cloud policy type." lightbox="media/how-to-configure-edge-policy-global-secure-access/create-policy.png":::
+
+1. Skip to **Assignments**. Select **Add all users** to apply the policy to all users in your tenant. Alternatively, use **Select group** to target a specific security group.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/how-to-configure-edge-policy-global-secure-access/assign-policy.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Assignments page showing the All users assignment and the controls for selecting a group or adding all users." lightbox="media/how-to-configure-edge-policy-global-secure-access/assign-policy.png":::
+
+1. On **Finish**, review the policy name, platforms, and assignments. Select **Review and create**.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/how-to-configure-edge-policy-global-secure-access/review-policy.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Finish page showing the cloud policy configuration, user assignment, and Review and create button." lightbox="media/how-to-configure-edge-policy-global-secure-access/review-policy.png":::
+
+## Enable secure network access
+
+Open the policy you created to configure its security settings.
+
+1. On **Configuration policies**, select your new policy.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/how-to-configure-edge-policy-global-secure-access/select-policy.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Configuration policies list with the newly created Global Secure Access Settings cloud policy." lightbox="media/how-to-configure-edge-policy-global-secure-access/select-policy.png":::
+
+1. Select **Customization Settings** > **Security settings**.
+1. Under **Secure Network Access**, set **Enable secure network access (preview)** to **Enabled**.
+
+    :::image type="content" source="media/how-to-configure-edge-policy-global-secure-access/enable-secure-network-access.png" alt-text="Screenshot of Security settings with Enable secure network access set to Enabled and Save changes available." lightbox="media/how-to-configure-edge-policy-global-secure-access/enable-secure-network-access.png":::
+
+1. If your organization relies on universal tenant restrictions, you can also configure **Enable browser-based tenant restrictions**. Microsoft Entra traffic doesn't pass through the Global Secure Access network channel in Edge. Global Secure Access universal tenant restrictions aren't enforced for that traffic. The browser-based setting is separate from the Global Secure Access integration.
+1. Select **Save changes**.
+
+The configuration policy applies when assigned employees sign in to Edge with a work account from your organization.
+
+## Validate the policy
+
+Test with an employee account included in both the Edge policy assignment and the applicable Global Secure Access traffic forwarding profiles.
+
+1. Open Edge on a supported Windows or macOS device and sign in to a work profile with the employee's account.
+1. Open `edge://policy` and check the effective policy value and any reported errors.
+1. Complete [Validate browser access](how-to-configure-global-secure-access-browser-settings.md#validate-browser-access) to test destinations and confirm the corresponding Global Secure Access transactions.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Configure Global Secure Access secure enterprise browser settings](how-to-configure-global-secure-access-browser-settings.md)
+- [Secure enterprise browser overview](concept-secure-enterprise-browser.md)
+- [Troubleshoot secure enterprise browser](troubleshoot-secure-enterprise-browser.md)
