@@ -0,0 +1,209 @@
+---
+title: Troubleshoot Secure Enterprise Browser (Preview)
+description: Troubleshoot secure enterprise browser in Microsoft Edge and Global Secure Access by checking configuration, policy assignments, traffic logs, and network traces.
+ms.topic: troubleshooting-general
+ms.date: 11/13/2026
+ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1026
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+ms.author: alexpav
+#customer intent: As an IT administrator, I want to diagnose secure enterprise browser access and policy issues so that employees can use protected browsing and private web applications.
+---
+
+# Troubleshoot secure enterprise browser (preview)
+
+Use this article to diagnose secure enterprise browser access and policy issues in Microsoft Edge with Global Secure Access. Check browser sign-in, configuration in both admin centers, and traffic logs before collecting a network trace. The guidance covers internet, Microsoft 365, and private web application access on Windows and macOS. It also helps you investigate Transport Layer Security (TLS) inspection issues for Internet Access traffic.
+
+Before you begin, have access to the affected employee's work profile and the administrators who manage Global Secure Access and Edge policies.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A Windows or macOS device running Microsoft Edge, version **157.0.4341.46** or newer.
+- An employee work account in the tenant configured for Global Secure Access. Business-to-business (B2B) guest accounts aren't supported.
+- Access to review your [secure enterprise browser configuration](how-to-configure-global-secure-access-browser-settings.md), including traffic forwarding profiles and Edge Management Experience (EMX) policy assignments.
+- Access to Global Secure Access traffic logs and, for configuration changes, the required administrative roles. See [Global Secure Access traffic logs](how-to-view-traffic-logs.md).
+- For Private Access issues, access to the private application's configuration and its connector administrator.
+
+## Troubleshooting checklist
+
+Start with the affected work profile and one failing destination. Record the reproduction time, including the time zone, so you can correlate browser results with service logs.
+
+| Symptom | Start with |
+| --- | --- |
+| The Edge policy is missing or has an unexpected value. | [Check the EMX policy and effective Edge settings](#check-the-emx-policy-and-effective-edge-settings). |
+| Browsing works, but you can't find the expected Global Secure Access traffic. | [Check browser enablement and traffic forwarding](#check-browser-enablement-and-traffic-forwarding), then [review traffic logs](#review-traffic-logs-and-policy-decisions). |
+| Traffic is denied or an internet destination isn't inspected. | [Check Internet Access security and TLS inspection policies](#check-internet-access-security-and-tls-inspection-policies). |
+| A private web application fails while internet access works. | [Check the private application and connectors](#check-the-private-application-and-connectors). |
+| Edge displays a certificate error. | [Investigate certificate errors without manual Edge trust deployment](#investigate-certificate-errors-without-manual-edge-trust-deployment). |
+| Edge displays certificate prompts on macOS while the Global Secure Access client is enabled. | [Check Global Secure Access client coexistence](#check-global-secure-access-client-coexistence). |
+
+### Check the platform and signed-in work profile
+
+Confirm that you're testing a supported browser profile:
+
+1. Record the installed Edge version and confirm that the device runs Windows or macOS. The minimum supported preview version is **157.0.4341.46**.
+1. Check that the affected Edge profile is signed in with the employee's work account in your Global Secure Access tenant.
+1. Open `edge://signin-internals` to review browser sign-in status. Record any relevant errors rather than switching to a personal profile for the test.
+1. Confirm that the same employee is included in the applicable Global Secure Access and EMX assignments.
+
+For information about the browser diagnostic pages, see [Microsoft Edge sign-in and policy diagnostics](/deployedge/microsoft-edge-troubleshoot-enterprise-sync). Use the sign-in checks for this investigation, not the sync reset procedures.
+
+### Check Global Secure Access client coexistence
+
+Check whether the Global Secure Access client is enabled on the affected device:
+
+- **Windows:** Running the client while Microsoft Edge is configured for Global Secure Access is supported.
+- **macOS:** Running the client while Edge is configured for Global Secure Access isn't supported and results in certificate prompts. Disable the client while using the Edge integration, and retest the affected destination.
+
+### Check browser enablement and traffic forwarding
+
+Review both the browser enablement settings and the profiles that calculate the employee's forwarding policy:
+
+1. In the Microsoft Entra admin center, review the secure enterprise browser configuration described in [Enable browser access](how-to-configure-global-secure-access-browser-settings.md#enable-browser-access-in-the-global-secure-access-portal).
+1. Confirm that Internet Access and Microsoft 365 are enabled together if you want to forward those traffic types. Check Private Access separately.
+1. Go to **Global Secure Access** > **Connect** > **Traffic forwarding**.
+1. Review the enabled profiles, their user and group assignments, and the rules for the failing destination. Check whether a rule forwards or bypasses that destination.
+1. Compare the Global Secure Access assignments with the employees assigned the EMX policy.
+
+The EMX policy enables the integration; the forwarding rules come from Global Secure Access profiles, as they do for the Global Secure Access client. See [Traffic forwarding profiles](concept-traffic-forwarding.md) and [Assign users to traffic forwarding profiles](how-to-manage-users-groups-assignment.md).
+
+### Check the EMX policy and effective Edge settings
+
+Compare the intended cloud configuration with the policy Edge actually receives:
+
+1. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to **Settings** > **Microsoft Edge** > **Configuration policies**.
+1. Open the policy used for secure enterprise browser. Under **Customization Settings** > **Security settings**, confirm that **Enable secure network access (preview)** is set to **Enabled**. Review the assignments and confirm that the affected employee is in scope.
+1. Check for other assigned configuration policies that configure the same setting. Review their priorities rather than assuming the most recently edited policy wins.
+1. In the affected Edge work profile, open `edge://policy`. Check the integration policy's effective value, source, and any reported errors or conflicts.
+1. If you changed the policy, restart Edge and check the effective value again.
+
+EMX is the only supported configuration method for enabling this integration in the preview. Don't substitute an Intune app policy. For general cloud-policy assignment and priority behavior, see [Microsoft Edge management service](/deployedge/microsoft-edge-management-service).
+
+For the configuration steps, see [Configure Global Secure Access policy in Microsoft Edge secure enterprise browser settings](how-to-configure-global-secure-access-edge-policy.md).
+
+### Review traffic logs and policy decisions
+
+Correlate the failing browser request with Global Secure Access logs:
+
+1. Reproduce the issue once in the affected work profile. Record the time, destination, and browser error.
+1. In the Microsoft Entra admin center, go to **Global Secure Access** > **Monitor** > **Traffic logs**.
+1. Select **Transactions** and filter **Device Category** to **Secure enterprise browser**.
+1. Use **Add filter** and the time range to narrow the results to the affected user and destination.
+1. Review the matching transactions. Compare the traffic type and action, such as **Allowed** or **Denied**, with the intended forwarding and security policies.
+1. Open the matching details and record the **Connection ID** and **Transaction ID**, when available, for further investigation.
+
+See [Use Global Secure Access traffic logs](how-to-view-traffic-logs.md) for available filters and columns. A missing matching entry isn't enough to establish that forwarding failed; recheck the time range, filters, destination, and configuration.
+
+If the behavior changed after an administrator updated configuration, review **Global Secure Access** > **Monitor** > **Audit logs**. See [Access Global Secure Access audit logs](how-to-access-audit-logs.md).
+
+For authentication or Conditional Access failures, review the affected event under **Entra ID** > **Monitoring & health** > **Sign-in logs**. Use [Troubleshoot Microsoft Entra sign-in errors](../identity/monitoring-health/howto-troubleshoot-sign-in-errors.md) to investigate the reported failure.
+
+### Check Internet Access security and TLS inspection policies
+
+For an internet request that is denied or isn't inspected as expected, check the service policies:
+
+1. Go to **Global Secure Access** > **Secure** > **Security profiles**. Review the relevant profile and its linked policies.
+1. Check the web content filtering rules and the policy assignments that apply to the affected employee.
+1. Go to **Global Secure Access** > **Secure** > **TLS inspection policies**. Review the rules for the destination, including bypass rules and the **Default action**.
+1. Confirm that the intended TLS inspection policy is linked to the appropriate security profile and that the certificate authority is active and enabled.
+
+For configuration details, see [Web content filtering](how-to-configure-web-content-filtering.md) and [TLS inspection policies](how-to-transport-layer-security.md). Use those articles for service-side policy configuration, not their Global Secure Access client setup or manual device certificate-deployment procedures.
+
+Microsoft 365 traffic isn't subject to TLS inspection or web filtering policies in this preview. Use an Internet Access destination, not a Microsoft 365 destination, to test those protections.
+
+### Check the private application and connectors
+
+For a failing private web application, check its assignment, destination, and connector group:
+
+1. Go to **Global Secure Access** > **Applications** > **Enterprise applications**, and open the affected application.
+1. Review **Users and groups** to confirm that the employee is assigned access.
+1. Review **Network access properties**. Compare the configured fully qualified domain name (FQDN), port, and protocol with the failing request, and check the selected connector group.
+1. Go to **Global Secure Access** > **Connect** > **Connectors**. Check that the selected group has an active connector.
+1. Work with the connector administrator to check name resolution and connectivity from the connector server to the backend application.
+
+See [Configure per-app access](how-to-configure-per-app-access.md) and [Troubleshoot connectors](troubleshoot-connectors.md). Private DNS isn't supported in the browser preview; use FQDN-based private web application definitions.
+
+If the main page opens but sign-in or page resources fail, use the [DevTools Network tool](#inspect-failed-requests-with-devtools) to identify the failing destinations. Compare those destinations with your forwarding rules and private application segments.
+
+## Causes and solutions
+
+Use the checklist results to correct configuration problems. Retest the same destination with the same employee work profile after each change.
+
+### Correct a missing or conflicting Edge policy
+
+If the integration policy is missing or its effective value differs from the intended value, correct the EMX setting or assignment. Review competing configuration policies with the Edge administrator, restart Edge, and recheck `edge://policy`.
+
+Don't treat a saved Global Secure Access browser configuration as proof that Edge received its policy. Both Global Secure Access enablement and the EMX policy are required.
+
+### Correct forwarding or application scope
+
+If the employee or destination is outside the intended scope, correct the relevant traffic profile assignment or destination rule. For private applications, also check application assignment, the FQDN-based segment, and connector group connectivity.
+
+Internet Access and Microsoft 365 share a browser enablement control, but their forwarding profiles still determine which traffic is forwarded. Review both profiles when only one traffic type behaves as expected.
+
+If a logged denial matches an intended security rule, the denial isn't evidence of a forwarding failure. Review whether the rule meets your organization's access requirements before changing it.
+
+### Investigate certificate errors without manual Edge trust deployment
+
+Global Secure Access delivers TLS inspection certificate trust automatically to Edge. A separate manual certificate deployment to Edge isn't required for this integration.
+
+For certificate prompts on macOS, first [check Global Secure Access client coexistence](#check-global-secure-access-client-coexistence). An enabled client alongside Edge configured for Global Secure Access is an unsupported configuration that results in certificate prompts.
+
+If a certificate error persists, check the active Global Secure Access certificate, the inspection or bypass rule for the destination, and the effective browser policy. Record the exact error and the certificate issuer and validity information displayed by Edge. Collect a bounded network trace if the configuration checks don't explain the failure.
+
+Automatic delivery to Edge doesn't establish device-wide certificate trust. Don't change the operating system's certificate store or bypass the browser certificate warning as a substitute for diagnosing the integration.
+
+### Use a supported preview scenario
+
+If the test uses an unsupported scenario, change the test rather than the policy. The preview supports Windows and macOS with employee work accounts. The Microsoft Entra traffic profile, compliant network checks, and tenant restrictions v2 for Microsoft Entra ID aren't supported.
+
+Use Internet Access, Microsoft 365, or an FQDN-based private web application to validate the integration. Don't use a B2B guest account or private DNS functionality as a validation test.
+
+## Advanced troubleshooting and data collection
+
+If configuration and service logs don't explain the issue, collect browser evidence for one reproduction. Keep the browser profile, destination, and time consistent with your traffic-log investigation.
+
+### Inspect failed requests with DevTools
+
+Use the Network tool to identify which requests fail:
+
+1. Open the affected page in the employee's Edge work profile.
+1. Right-click the page, select **Inspect**, and open the **Network** tool.
+1. Select **Preserve log** if the issue involves navigation between pages.
+1. Refresh the page or reproduce the failing action. Record failed request destinations, status or error information, and timing.
+
+See [Microsoft Edge DevTools Network reference](/microsoft-edge/devtools/network/reference) for request details. Record only the headers needed for the investigation; request headers can contain credentials.
+
+### Capture an Edge network trace
+
+Use NetLog when you need browser network evidence beyond the page's request list.
+
+> [!WARNING]
+> Network captures can contain sensitive information. Don't select **Include raw bytes (will include cookies and credentials)** for routine collection. Share captures only through approved support channels, not public trace viewers.
+
+To capture one reproduction:
+
+1. Open `edge://net-export` in the affected Edge profile.
+1. Select **Start Logging to Disk**, and save the capture file.
+1. Keep the capture tab open. In another tab, reproduce the issue.
+1. Return to the capture tab and select **Stop Logging** promptly.
+1. Record the reproduction time and the matching Global Secure Access connection and transaction IDs with the capture.
+
+See [Capture network traffic with NetLog](/troubleshoot/entra/entra-id/app-integration/use-netlog-capture-network-traffic) for capture guidance.
+
+### Prepare information for support
+
+Provide the evidence needed to correlate the browser request with service-side processing:
+
+- The affected user's tenant and work profile, shared only through the authorized support case.
+- The operating system (Windows or macOS) and Edge versions, and the destination and action that reproduce the issue.
+- The exact error, reproduction time, and time zone.
+- The relevant EMX policy, assignment, and effective value from `edge://policy`.
+- The Global Secure Access browser enablement, traffic profiles, application assignments, and applicable security policies.
+- The matching traffic-log records, connection and transaction IDs, and relevant configuration changes from audit logs.
+- Browser sign-in diagnostics and a bounded network capture, if requested.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Secure enterprise browser overview](concept-secure-enterprise-browser.md)
+- [Configure Global Secure Access secure enterprise browser settings](how-to-configure-global-secure-access-browser-settings.md)
+- [Global Secure Access traffic logs](how-to-view-traffic-logs.md)

 ## Lifecycle workflow catch-up window
 
-By design, Lifecycle workflows provide a three day catch up window to help customers process users that could have been missed due to delays in HR user data updates. This means when the workflow engine evaluates users that meet the current execution conditions for the scheduled workflow, it includes users for whom the expected trigger date has already passed but wasn't more than three days past the original trigger date. Once the user is processed, it would only be considered again if there was a change for the user or workflows that allowed it to meet the execution conditions again.

-The following table shows examples of Lifecycle Workflows' catch-up window:
+New workflows that use the updated **Time based attribute** trigger don't have an automatic three-day catch-up window. Existing workflows aren't affected by this change and retain their current catch-up behavior.
 
+For new workflows that use **Equal to**, users are eligible only on the UTC calendar day that matches the configured offset. This matching day isn't an additional catch-up window. -|A [pre-hire template](lifecycle-workflow-templates.md#onboard-pre-hire-employee) workflow is scheduled to run for users 7 days before their **EmployeeHireDate**.    | A new user is provisioned by HR in Microsoft Entra ID with an **EmployeeHireDate** in 5 days.      |  The workflow runs for the new user as the date is within 3 days of the offset.      |

+To allow for delays in user data updates, configure **Between** or **Within** to match a period that meets your requirements. If the workflow or user account is configured after the intended processing time (e.g., due to a delay in the HR system), Lifecycle Workflows will still attempt to process the user—provided the necessary setup is completed within three days of the original processing time. This catch-up behavior doesn't apply when you select **Time based attribute V2 (Preview)** during public preview.
+> The **Time based attribute** trigger processes users whose date attribute meets the configured **Equal to**, **Between**, or **Within** comparison and whose accounts meet the scope rules. Configure the relevant trigger and scoping attributes before users need to meet the execution conditions. New workflows that use the updated trigger don't have an automatic three-day catch-up window. Existing workflows aren't affected by this change and retain their current catch-up behavior. To allow for delays in user data updates in new workflows, configure a relative time range with **Between** or **Within**. For details and examples, see [Time based attribute trigger](lifecycle-workflow-execution-conditions.md#time-based-attribute-trigger).
 
 To view a detailed guide on  customizing the schedule of a workflow, see: [Customize the schedule of workflows](customize-workflow-schedule.md).

+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+# Customer intent: As an IT admin, I want to understand the deprecated memberOf preview and find its replacement, so that I can move existing configurations to MemberOf Next.
 ---
 
-# Configure dynamic membership groups with the memberOf operator in the Entra Admin Center (preview)
-
-
-## Overview
-
-This feature preview in Microsoft Entra ID enables admins to create dynamic membership groups and administrative units that populate by adding members of other groups using the `memberOf` attribute. Apps that couldn't read group-based membership previously in Microsoft Entra ID can now read the entire membership of these new `memberOf` groups. Not only can these groups be used for apps but they can also be used for licensing assignments.
+# Deprecated memberOf preview for dynamic membership groups
 
 > [!IMPORTANT]
-> The public preview of the `memberOf` rule operator is ending. After **November 3, 2026**, dynamic membership groups, dynamic administrative units, and entitlement management auto-assignment policies that use the `memberOf` operator stop updating and remain in their last known state. This can lead to stale access and enforcement gaps, including outdated Teams and SharePoint access, Conditional Access targeting, group-based licensing, and access package assignments.
+> The earlier `memberOf` preview was deprecated in favor of **MemberOf Next**. The earlier preview ended on **November 3, 2026**. Dynamic membership groups, dynamic administrative units, and entitlement management auto-assignment policies that still used the earlier preview stopped updating and remained in their last known state.
 >
-> Before November 3, 2026, review all uses of the `memberOf` operator and remove or replace those configurations. See [Migrate before the preview ends](#migrate-before-the-preview-ends). This is a preview feature that isn't intended for production use; review the [Preview limitations](#preview-limitations). 
-
-
-The following diagram illustrates how you could create Dynamic-Group-A with members of Security-Group-X and Security-Group-Y. Members of the groups inside Security-Group-X and Security-Group-Y don't become members of Dynamic-Group-A.
+> For current capabilities, requirements, and setup instructions, see [Use MemberOf Next and Transitive Reports To in dynamic membership groups (preview)](groups-dynamic-rule-advanced.md). To move existing groups to MemberOf Next, see [Move existing MemberOf groups to MemberOf Next](groups-dynamic-rule-advanced.md#move-existing-memberof-groups-to-memberof-next).
 
-:::image type="content" source="./media/groups-dynamic-rule-member-of/member-of-diagram.png" alt-text="Diagram that shows how the memberOf attribute works.":::
+The earlier `memberOf` preview in Microsoft Entra ID enabled admins to create dynamic membership groups and administrative units that populated by adding members of other groups. Apps that couldn't read group-based membership previously could read the flattened membership of these `memberOf` groups. These groups could also be used for licensing assignments.
 
-With this preview, admins can configure dynamic membership groups with the `memberOf` attribute in the Azure portal, Microsoft Graph, and PowerShell. Security groups, Microsoft 365 groups, and groups that are synced from on-premises Active Directory can all be added as members of these dynamic membership groups. They can also all be added to a single group. For example, the dynamic group could be a security group, but you can use Microsoft 365 groups, security groups, and groups that are synced from on-premises to define its membership.
+The following diagram illustrates how the earlier preview populated Dynamic-Group-A with direct members of Security-Group-X and Security-Group-Y. Members of nested groups inside Security-Group-X and Security-Group-Y weren't included in Dynamic-Group-A.
 
-## Prerequisites
+:::image type="content" source="./media/groups-dynamic-rule-member-of/member-of-diagram.png" alt-text="Diagram that shows how the memberOf attribute worked in the deprecated preview.":::
 
-You must be at least a [User Administrator](/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference#user-administrator) to use the `memberOf` attribute to create a Microsoft Entra dynamic group. You must have a Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 license for the Microsoft Entra tenant.
+The earlier preview was available through the Azure portal, Microsoft Graph, and PowerShell. Source groups could be security groups, Microsoft 365 groups, or groups synced from on-premises Active Directory.
 
 ## Preview limitations
 
+The following limitations applied to the deprecated preview. For the limitations of its replacement, see [MemberOf Next and Transitive Reports To preview limitations](groups-dynamic-rule-advanced.md#preview-limitations).
 
-- This preview should only be used in test environments as it can affect dynamic group processing in the tenant. These limitations are being addressed, and updates will be provided when they're available.
-- Each Microsoft Entra tenant is limited to 500 dynamic groups using the `memberOf` attribute. The `memberOf` groups count toward the total dynamic group quota of 15,000.
-- Each dynamic group can have up to 50 member groups.
-- When you add members of security groups to `memberOf` dynamic membership groups, only direct members of the security group become members of the dynamic group.
-- You can't use one `memberOf` dynamic group to define the membership of another `memberOf` dynamic group. For example, Dynamic Group A, with members of group B and C in it, can't be a member of Dynamic Group D.
-- The `memberOf` attribute can't be used with other rules. For example, a rule that states dynamic group A should contain members of group B and also should contain only users located in Redmond will fail.
-- The dynamic group rule builder and validate feature can't be used for `memberOf` at this time.
-- The `memberOf` attribute can't be used with other operators. For example, you can't create a rule that states "Members Of group A can't be in Dynamic group B."
-- Users included in `memberOf` dynamic membership groups might cause a slower processing time for your tenant, if the tenant has a large number of groups or frequent dynamic membership groups updates.
-- Membership of a memberOf dynamic group doesn't automatically update when a child group is deleted. The affected users or devices remain members of the memberOf dynamic group until the rule is modified.
-
-
-- Only available in public cloud. 
-
-## Get started
-
-This feature is available in the Azure portal, Microsoft Graph, and PowerShell. However, the `memberOf` attribute isn’t currently supported in the rule builder UI. To use `memberOf` in the Azure portal, you must define the rule by using the rule editor (advanced syntax).
-
-### Create a memberOf dynamic group
-
-1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a [User Administrator](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#user-administrator).
-1. Browse to **Entra ID** > **Groups** > **All groups**.
-1. Select **New group**.
-1. Fill in group details. The group type can be **Security** or **Microsoft 365**, and the membership type can be set to **Dynamic User** or **Dynamic Device**.
-1. Select **Add dynamic query**.
-1. MemberOf isn't yet supported in the rule builder UI. Select **Edit** to write the rule in the **Rule syntax** box.
-    1. Example user rule: `user.memberof -any (group.objectId -in ['groupId'])`
-    1. Example device rule: `device.memberof -any (group.objectId -in ['groupId'])`  
-    
-    > [!NOTE]
-    > Replace `'groupId'` with the **object ID of the source group** whose members you want to include in the dynamic group.
-    >
-    > The two examples are alternatives:
-    >
-    > - Use the **user** rule when creating a **Dynamic user** group.
-    > - Use the **device** rule when creating a **Dynamic device** group.
-    >
-    > To include multiple source groups, specify multiple group object IDs. For example:
-    >
-    > ```text
-    > user.memberof -any (group.objectId -in ['<groupObjectId1>', '<groupObjectId2>'])
-    > ```
-
-1. Select **OK**.
-1. Select **Create group**.
-
-## Migrate before the preview ends
-
-As Microsoft continues to improve the scale and reliability of dynamic membership processing, the `memberOf` preview is ending. During preview, we observed that using `memberOf` can slow dynamic membership processing for all groups in a tenant. `memberOf` is a preview operator and isn't recommended for production use.
-
-We recognize the importance of the customer scenarios that `memberOf` addresses, and we're continuing to develop an alternative solution that meets these needs with the right level of scalability and reliability.
-In the interim, identify and replace every configuration that uses the `memberOf` operator before November 3, 2026. After that date, configurations that still use `memberOf` stop updating and stay in their last known state, which can leave access stale and enforcement gaps in place.
-
-**Dynamic membership groups**
-
-- Export dynamic membership groups from the Microsoft Entra admin center and identify rules that contain `memberOf`.
-- Replace `memberOf` with [supported rule operators](~/identity/users/groups-dynamic-rule-more-efficient.md), or convert the group to assigned membership.
-- Validate group membership after making changes. If the group is no longer needed, pause or delete it.
+- The earlier preview was intended only for test environments because it could affect dynamic group processing across the tenant.
+- Each Microsoft Entra tenant was limited to 500 dynamic groups that used the `memberOf` attribute. These groups counted toward the total dynamic group quota of 15,000.
+- Each dynamic group could reference up to 50 source groups.
+- Only direct members of source groups were included. Members of nested groups weren't included.
+- A `memberOf` dynamic group couldn't define the membership of another `memberOf` dynamic group.
+- The `memberOf` attribute couldn't be combined with other rules or operators.
+- The dynamic group rule builder and rule validation weren't supported for `memberOf`.
+- Large numbers of groups or frequent membership updates could slow dynamic membership processing for the tenant.
+- Membership didn't automatically update when a source group was deleted. Affected users or devices remained members until the rule was modified.
+- The earlier preview was available only in the public cloud.
 
-**Dynamic administrative units**
+## Move to MemberOf Next
 
-- Use Microsoft Graph PowerShell to identify [dynamic administrative units](~/identity/role-based-access-control/admin-units-members-dynamic.md) that use `memberOf` rules.
-- Replace `memberOf`-based rules with supported logic, or convert the administrative unit to assigned membership.
-- Validate both membership and administrative scope. If the administrative unit is no longer needed, delete it.
+MemberOf Next replaces the earlier preview with separate processing on a twice-daily schedule. It requires Microsoft Entra ID Governance and Standard priority. The name shown in the product and the rule syntax are unchanged.
 
-**Entitlement management auto-assignment policies**
+For migration requirements and instructions, see [Move existing MemberOf groups to MemberOf Next](groups-dynamic-rule-advanced.md#move-existing-memberof-groups-to-memberof-next). For current setup instructions and guidance for dynamic administrative units, see [Use MemberOf Next and Transitive Reports To in dynamic membership groups (preview)](groups-dynamic-rule-advanced.md).
 
-- Use Microsoft Graph PowerShell to identify [auto-assignment policies](~/id-governance/entitlement-management-access-package-auto-assignment-policy.md) that use `memberOf`.
-- Replace `memberOf`-based logic with supported attribute-based operators where possible. If no equivalent rule is available, plan an alternative assignment method before retirement.
-- Validate access package assignments after making changes.
+## Related content
 
+- [Use MemberOf Next and Transitive Reports To in dynamic membership groups (preview)](groups-dynamic-rule-advanced.md).
+- [Manage rules for dynamic membership groups in Microsoft Entra ID](groups-dynamic-membership.md).
+- [Understand and manage dynamic group processing in Microsoft Entra ID](manage-dynamic-group.md).

 A cloud-only identity refers to a user account that exists only in Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) and does not have a corresponding account in an on-premises Active Directory.
 
+Cloud-only identity scenarios include human users and agent users when the target workload supports them.
+
 ## Key features and benefits
 
 **Seamless hybrid authentication**: Microsoft Entra Kerberos allows users whose accounts reside in on-premises AD DS and are synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID to authenticate across cloud and on-premises resources. It reduces (and in some cases, eliminates) the need for direct connectivity to domain controllers.
@@ -44,21 +46,24 @@ For example, when a Microsoft Entra ID-joined Windows client accesses a file sha
 
 **Scalable group memberships**: Microsoft Entra Kerberos addresses traditional Kerberos limitations with large or dynamic group memberships to improve reliability and user experience. In scenarios that involve large groups of users, performance is optimized through automatic load distribution across all domain controllers (DCs) within a site. For deployments in Azure Virtual Desktop environments, we recommend ensuring that sufficient DCs are available and geographically close to the environment, to maintain responsiveness.
 
+For applications that use group SIDs in Kerberos service tickets, see [Configure optional group SID claims for Microsoft Entra Kerberos tickets](configure-optional-group-claims-kerberos.md).
+
 ## How Microsoft Entra Kerberos works
 
 In hybrid scenarios, Microsoft Entra Kerberos allows your Microsoft Entra ID tenant to operate as a dedicated Kerberos realm alongside your existing on-premises Active Directory realm. When a user signs in to a Windows device that's either Microsoft Entra ID joined or hybrid joined, the device authenticates with Microsoft Entra ID and receives a [Primary Refresh Token (PRT)](../devices/concept-primary-refresh-token.md).

+title: Governance policy templates

+description: Learn about governance policy templates and how to use them to enforce consistent governance across tenants in Microsoft Entra
+ms.topic: concept-article

+---
+
+# Governance policy templates
+
+Governance policy templates are a foundational component of the Tenant Governance service, which helps organizations secure Microsoft Entra tenants at scale. Before establishing a governance relationship between tenants, create a governance policy template that defines the relationship behavior. These templates are reusable across distinct governance relationships, enabling consistent and scalable management of cross-tenant access.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> Governance policy templates define cross-tenant access for governance relationships. They aren't [resource policy definitions](resource-policy-concepts.md), which use Rego to evaluate resource changes. Creating a governance policy template doesn't create a resource policy assignment.
+
+## How governance policy templates work
+
+A governance policy template serves as a blueprint for governance relationships. When you create a template, you define two key areas of access:
+
+- Cross-tenant delegated administration roles - Specify which Microsoft Entra built-in roles users from the governing tenant have in the governed tenant.
+
+- Multitenant applications - Select custom applications to create and manage across tenants.
+
+After you create a template, you can use it to establish multiple governance relationships with different governed tenants, ensuring consistent access policies across your organization.
+
+When you create a governance relationship, Tenant Governance captures and stores a policy snapshot with the relationship. This snapshot represents the roles and permissions that applied at the time you established or last updated the relationship.
+
+Updating a governance policy template doesn't automatically update relationships that you created using that template. This design ensures that the governed tenant always has the opportunity to review desired permission changes for the relationship. To apply permission updates to an active relationship, you must repeat the request and approval process.
+
+## Relationship lifetime (Preview)
+
+You can optionally set **Relationship lifetime** to a whole number from 1 to 730 days. The governed tenant reviews the lifetime with the permissions in the governance request. On acceptance, the relationship stores the approved lifetime and calculates its expiration.
+
+An unset lifetime creates a non-expiring relationship. Editing a template doesn't automatically change an active relationship's lifetime. To apply new terms, send a new **Initial** request using the same template ID and have the governed tenant approve it.
+
+Renewal uses the lifetime and permissions already stored in the relationship's policy snapshot, not a newer version of the template. See [Manage relationship expiration and renewal](how-to-manage-relationship-expiration.md).
+
+## Cross-tenant delegated administration configuration
+
+By selecting Microsoft Entra built-in roles and assigning them to a group in the governing tenant, you define which roles (and level of access) users in that group have in the governed tenant. With these roles, users can:
+
+- Sign in to the governed tenant using their governing tenant credentials.
+
+- Manage the governed tenant without needing a local or business-to-business (B2B) account in that tenant.
+
+Each group can have multiple role assignments, and each policy template can have multiple groups defined. When you create the governance relationship, Tenant Governance creates [granular delegated admin privileges (GDAP)](cross-tenant-delegated-administration.md) role assignments in the governed tenant.
+
+## Multitenant application configuration
+
+By selecting custom, multitenant applications in the policy template, you enable centralized application management. When you create the governance relationship, Tenant Governance creates a service principal with the same permissions in the governed tenant.
+
+This capability allows you to manage your custom, multitenant applications at scale from the central governing tenant. You don't need to go into every tenant individually to monitor and maintain least privileged app access.
+
+For example, assume you've built a custom line of business app called Contoso Resource Manager, responsible for monitoring, reporting, and automating resource configuration across your tenants. Use the governance relationship to set up a service principal instance of Contoso Resource Manager across your governed tenants, with the right provisioned permissions consented. When you need to add or remove permissions, do so through the governance relationship instead of making changes and consenting to permissions on a per-tenant basis.

+The default policy template is a special template used for secure tenant creation scenarios. When you create a new add-on tenant, Tenant Governance automatically establishes a governance relationship between the parent tenant and the add-on tenant using the default policy template. This setup ensures that new tenants immediately come under centralized tenant administration from the start.
+
+The default policy template has these characteristics:
+
+- **Unique identifier**: Instead of a GUID, the default policy template has an ID of "default."
+
+- **Configuration required**: You must configure the default policy template before you can use it.
+
+Relationships created automatically during add-on tenant creation are excluded from relationship expiration. Setting a lifetime on the default template doesn't by itself schedule expiration for those automatically created relationships.
+
+## Limitations
+
+The following limitations apply to governance policy templates:
+
+| Limit | Value |
+| --- | --- |
+| Maximum number of multitenant applications per template | 10 |
+| Maximum number of permissions per multitenant application | 100 |
+| Maximum number of role assignments per template | 10 |

+
+# Governance relationships
+
+A governance relationship establishes a directional connection between two Microsoft Entra tenants. One tenant (the *governing* tenant) governs another tenant (the *governed* tenant). These relationships enable organizations to securely manage multiple tenants at scale from a central location.
+
+Governance relationships enable four key scenarios:
+
+| Scenario | Description |
+| --- | --- |
+| Cross-tenant delegated administration | Use governance relationships to centralize **least-privileged administrative access** across multiple Microsoft Entra tenants. Administrators sign in using accounts from the governing tenant. This approach eliminates the need to create and manage local or B2B administrator accounts in every governed tenant. |
+| Multitenant application management | Manage custom, multitenant applications from the governing tenant. Administrators can monitor and maintain least-privileged application access across governed tenants without signing into each tenant individually. This approach reduces operational overhead and configuration drift. |
+| Tenant configuration management | If you configured cross-tenant delegated administration in your governance relationship, use this administrative access to ensure that the tenant meets your organization's security and compliance objectives on an ongoing basis. |
+| Secure tenant creation | When you create a new add-on tenant from an existing tenant, Tenant Governance automatically establishes a governance relationship between the parent tenant and the new tenant by using a default governance policy template. This step immediately brings newly created tenants under centralized administration and governance controls, reducing the risk of unmanaged or misconfigured tenants. |
+
+## Relationship handshake
+
+Any two Microsoft Entra tenants can create a new governance relationship through the three-step handshake. To create a new governance relationship, or update an existing one, administrators from both tenants must configure and agree on the roles and permissions that the governing tenant has over the governed tenant.
+
+1. The future governed tenant sends the future governing tenant a governance invitation.
+
+1. Upon receiving a governance invitation, the future governing tenant sends the future governed tenant a governance request (with a selected governance policy template).
+
+1. After the future governed tenant reviews and accepts the request, the tenants establish a governance relationship.
+
+Tenants that meet these criteria can skip the invitation step:
+
+- The future governing tenant identifies the future governed tenant as a related tenant through tenant discovery with a shared billing account.
+
+- Tenants in an active governance relationship can skip the invitation step to update their relationship or create a new one.
+
+## Relationship lifecycle
+
+A governance relationship moves through several states from creation to termination. The following sections describe the states for both requests and established relationships.
+
+### Request states
+
+Governance requests progress through these states:
+
+| State | Description |
+| --- | --- |
+| Pending | The governing tenant sent the request and awaits a response from the governed tenant. |
+| Accepted | The governed tenant accepted the request, creating a governance relationship. |
+| Rejected | The governed tenant rejected the request. |
+
+### Relationship states
+
+Governance relationships progress through these states:
+
+| State | Description |
+| --- | --- |
+| Active | The relationship is established and operational. |
+| Termination requested | The governing tenant has requested to terminate the relationship. |
+| Terminated | The relationship ended through termination or expiration. Tenant Governance removes access granted only through that relationship and preserves resources required by surviving relationships or unrelated grants. |
+
+### Expiration and renewal (Preview)
+
+You can optionally configure a relationship lifetime from 1 to 730 days in a governance policy template. The governed tenant reviews and approves that lifetime when accepting the governance request. Without a configured lifetime, the relationship doesn't expire automatically.
+
+The governing tenant can request renewal before expiration, and the governed tenant must approve it. Renewal preserves the relationship ID, permissions, and existing policy snapshot. The new expiration is the renewal acceptance time plus the lifetime stored in the active relationship.
+
+A pending renewal doesn't pause expiration. If renewal isn't approved before the deadline, Tenant Governance terminates the relationship and removes its exclusive access. An expiration warning isn't a separate relationship status.
+
+For setup, notifications, cleanup behavior, and the add-on tenant exception, see [Manage relationship expiration and renewal](how-to-manage-relationship-expiration.md).
+
+## Governance models
+
+When you set up governance relationships between a pair of tenants, note these supported models.
+
+| Supported? | Model type | Description |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| ✅ | One to many | A tenant can govern multiple tenants. |
+| ✅ | Many to one | Multiple tenants can govern a tenant. |
+| ✅ (Preview) | Multi-tier | A tenant can be governed by another tenant while governing downstream tenants. Each direct relationship requires independent approval and defines its own permissions. Access isn't inherited down the chain. |
+
+For example, if A governs B and B governs C, A doesn't automatically gain access to C. To administer C, A needs its own direct relationship with C, approved by C. Each relationship has an independent policy snapshot and lifecycle.
+
+For a walkthrough, see [Set up multi-tier governance relationships](how-to-set-up-multi-tier-governance.md).
+
+## Switch between governed tenants (Preview)
+
+The **Governed tenants** view under **Entra ID** > **Overview** > **Manage tenants** helps users find and switch to tenants available through active relationships and qualifying delegated-role group membership. Switching uses existing access; it doesn't grant new permissions or create B2B guest accounts.
+
+For prerequisites and instructions, see [Switch between governed tenants](how-to-switch-governed-tenants.md).
+

+

+- [Governance policy templates](governance-policy-templates.md)
+- [Cross-tenant delegated administration](cross-tenant-delegated-administration.md)

-# Terminate a governance relationship
-
-This article describes how to terminate a governance relationship between a governing tenant and a governed tenant. When you terminate a governance relationship, Tenant Governance deletes all relationship-related resources from the governed tenant, including granular delegated admin privileges (GDAP) role assignments, service principals, and their permissions.

-- You must have an active governance relationship between two tenants.
-
-- You need the **Tenant Governance Administrator** role.

-## Terminate a relationship: Governing tenant initiation

-### Initiate termination as the governing tenant

-
-1. Browse to **Tenant governance** > **Governed tenants**.
-
-1. Select the active governance relationship you want to terminate.
-
-1. Select **Terminate governance**.
-
-    The relationship status changes to **Termination requested**. Tenant Governance sends an email notification to the governed tenant about the termination request.
-
-1. Wait for the governed tenant to confirm the termination.
-
-    When the governed tenant confirms, Tenant Governance deletes all relationship-related resources from the governed tenant, and the relationship status changes to **Terminated**.

-
-1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a **Tenant Governance Administrator** in the governed tenant.
-
-1. Browse to **Tenant governance** > **Governing tenants**.
-
-1. Change the **Relationship status** filter to **Termination requested**.
-
-1. Select the tenant that requested termination.
-
-1. Select **Confirm termination**.
-
-    Tenant Governance deletes all relationship-related resources from the governed tenant, and the relationship status changes to **Terminated**. Tenant Governance sends an email notification to the governing tenant that termination is complete.
-
-## Directly terminate a relationship: Governed tenant
-As the governed tenant, directly terminate a governance relationship without requiring approval from the governing tenant.
-
-1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a **Tenant Governance Administrator** in the governed tenant.
-
-1. Browse to **Tenant governance** > **Governing tenants**.
-
-1. Select the tenant whose governance relationship you want to terminate.
-
-1. Select **Terminate governance**.
-
-1. Review the details of the relationship, then confirm termination.
-
-    Tenant Governance deletes all relationship-related resources from the governed tenant, and the relationship status changes to **Terminated**. Tenant Governance sends an email notification to the governing tenant that the relationship is terminated.

-## What happens when you terminate a governance relationship

-
-- **Cross-tenant access policy**: Tenant Governance removes the governing tenant as a partner from the partner-specific cross-tenant access configuration in the governed tenant.
-
-- **GDAP role assignments**: Tenant Governance removes cross-tenant role assignments that allowed users from the governing tenant to sign in to and manage the governed tenant.

+title: Terminate a governance relationship
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra ID Governance
+description: Learn how to terminate a governance relationship between tenants in Microsoft Entra Tenant Governance and understand what resources are removed
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/11/2026

+---
+
+<!-- source: How to terminate a governance relationship.docx -->
+
+# Terminate a governance relationship
+
+This article describes how to terminate a governance relationship between a governing tenant and a governed tenant. When you terminate a governance relationship, Tenant Governance removes access granted only through that relationship. Resources still required by another relationship, preexisting resources, and unrelated grants are preserved.
+
+Terminate a governance relationship in two ways, depending on whether the governing tenant or the governed tenant initiates the termination.
+
+| Initiated by | Process |
+| --- | --- |
+| Governing tenant | Sends a termination request to the governed tenant. The governed tenant must confirm to complete termination. |
+| Governed tenant | Directly terminates the relationship. The governing tenant doesn't need to take any action. |
+
+## Prerequisites
+- You must have an active governance relationship between two tenants.
+
+- You need the **Tenant Governance Administrator** role.
+
+## Terminate a relationship: Governing tenant initiation
+The governing tenant can request to terminate a governance relationship. This process requires confirmation from the governed tenant before Tenant Governance removes the relationship and its resources.
+
+### Initiate termination as the governing tenant
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a **Tenant Governance Administrator** in the governing tenant.
+
+1. Browse to **Tenant governance** > **Governed tenants**.
+
+1. Select the active governance relationship you want to terminate.
+
+1. Select **Terminate governance**.
+
+    The relationship status changes to **Termination requested**. Tenant Governance sends an email notification to the governed tenant about the termination request.
+
+1. Wait for the governed tenant to confirm the termination.
+
+    When the governed tenant confirms, Tenant Governance cleans up relationship-exclusive access in the governed tenant, and the relationship status changes to **Terminated**.
+
+### Confirm termination as the governed tenant
+When the governing tenant initiates termination, the governed tenant must confirm the request to complete the process.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a **Tenant Governance Administrator** in the governed tenant.
+
+1. Browse to **Tenant governance** > **Governing tenants**.
+
+1. Change the **Relationship status** filter to **Termination requested**.
+
+1. Select the tenant that requested termination.
+
+1. Select **Confirm termination**.
+
+    Tenant Governance cleans up relationship-exclusive access in the governed tenant, and the relationship status changes to **Terminated**. Tenant Governance sends an email notification to the governing tenant that termination is complete.
+
+## Directly terminate a relationship: Governed tenant
+As the governed tenant, directly terminate a governance relationship without requiring approval from the governing tenant.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a **Tenant Governance Administrator** in the governed tenant.
+
+1. Browse to **Tenant governance** > **Governing tenants**.
+
+1. Select the tenant whose governance relationship you want to terminate.
+
+1. Select **Terminate governance**.
+
+1. Review the details of the relationship, then confirm termination.
+
+    Tenant Governance cleans up relationship-exclusive access in the governed tenant, and the relationship status changes to **Terminated**. Tenant Governance sends an email notification to the governing tenant that the relationship is terminated.
+
+## What happens when you terminate a governance relationship
+When you terminate a governance relationship, Tenant Governance updates or deletes these resources from the governed tenant:
+
+- **Cross-tenant access policy**: Tenant Governance disables the service-provider setting when no other relationship for the same tenant pair still needs GDAP access. It preserves unrelated partner and B2B settings rather than deleting the entire partner policy.
+
+- **GDAP role assignments**: Tenant Governance removes assignments used only by the terminated relationship and preserves assignments required by surviving relationships. It doesn't remove the source group or its membership.
+
+- **Service principals and permissions**: Tenant Governance removes relationship-exclusive grants and injected applications that qualify for cleanup. It preserves shared or preexisting applications, surviving or unrelated grants, and the source application registration.
+
+After termination, users from the governing tenant can no longer sign in to the governed tenant with their governing tenant credentials through the governance relationship.
+
+Other active relationships or independently granted permissions can still provide access. Terminating one link in a multi-tier arrangement doesn't terminate the other links.
+
+Time-bound relationships can also end automatically through [expiration](how-to-manage-relationship-expiration.md). Automatic expiration doesn't require the manual confirmation workflow described in this article.
+
+## Related content
+- [Set up a governance relationship](how-to-set-up-governance-relationship.md)
+
+- [Update a governance relationship](how-to-update-governance-relationship.md)

+title: Update a governance relationship
+titleSuffix: Microsoft Entra ID Governance
+description: Learn how to update an existing governance relationship between a governing and governed tenant in Microsoft Entra Tenant Governance
+ms.topic: how-to

+# Update a governance relationship
+
+This article describes how to update an existing governance relationship between a governing tenant and a governed tenant. You might need to update a governance relationship to add or modify delegated administration roles or multitenant application configurations.
+
+## Prerequisites
+- You must have an active governance relationship between a governing tenant and a governed tenant.
+
+- You must have access to the governance policy template you used to create the existing relationship. If you deleted the policy template, you need to create a new relationship.
+
+- You need the **Tenant Governance Administrator** role.
+
+- Review license requirements for sending governance requests in [Microsoft Entra licensing](~/fundamentals/licensing.md#microsoft-entra-tenant-governance).
+
+## Update the governance policy template
+Before you can update a governance relationship, you must first modify the governance policy template you used to establish the existing relationship. When you update the template, its version number automatically increments by one.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a **Tenant Governance Administrator** in the governing tenant.
+
+1. Browse to **Tenant Governance** > **Templates**, and select the policy template you used to set up the relationship.
+
+1. Modify the template as needed. Update one or more of these configurations:
+
+    - **Delegated administration roles**: Add or change the Microsoft Entra built-in roles assigned to security groups in the governing tenant. These roles determine the access level that users in those groups have when they sign in to the governed tenant.
+
+    - **Multitenant application management**: Add or update custom, multitenant applications. When you update the relationship, Tenant Governance creates or updates a service principal with the corresponding permissions in the governed tenant.
+
+    - **Relationship lifetime (Preview)**: Add or change the lifetime for an active relationship. Use the same template ID in the new **Initial** request to update that relationship rather than create a separate one.
+
+1. Save the updated governance policy template. The version number of the template increments by one.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> Updating the governance policy template doesn't automatically update the governance relationship. The tenant admins must complete the governance request and approval process described in the sections that follow for the policy template changes to take effect.
+
+Renewing a time-bound relationship is different from updating its terms. **Request renewal** preserves the existing policy snapshot and lifetime; it doesn't apply template edits. See [Manage relationship expiration and renewal](how-to-manage-relationship-expiration.md).
+
+## Send a new governance request with the updated template
+After updating the governance policy template, send a new governance request from the governing tenant to the governed tenant using the updated template.
+
+1. In the governing tenant, create a new governance request.
+
+1. Select the governed tenant that has the existing relationship you want to update.
+
+1. Select the updated governance policy template.
+
+1. Submit the governance request. The governed tenant receives an email notification about the new governance request.
+
+## Accept the governance request
+An admin in the governed tenant must accept the governance request to complete the update.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a **Tenant Governance Administrator** in the governed tenant.
+
+1. Browse to **Tenant Governance** > **Received requests**.
+
+1. Review the updated governance request, including the changes in the policy template.
+
+1. Accept the governance request. The system updates the existing governance relationship with the new policy template configuration. The governing tenant receives an email confirming the accepted request and the updated governance relationship.
+
+When the governed tenant accepts the governance request, these changes take effect:
+
+- Tenant Governance updates the policy snapshot of the existing governance relationship to reflect the latest version of the policy template.
+
+- If you updated delegated administration roles, Tenant Governance updates the GDAP role assignments in the governed tenant accordingly.
+
+- If you updated multitenant application management, Tenant Governance updates the corresponding service principal and its permissions in the governed tenant.
+
+- If you updated the relationship lifetime, Tenant Governance updates the existing relationship's policy snapshot and expiration after acceptance.
+
+## Related content
+- [Set up a governance relationship](how-to-set-up-governance-relationship.md)
+
+- [Terminate a governance relationship](how-to-terminate-governance-relationship.md)
+
+- [Governance policy templates](governance-policy-templates.md)

+This workflow helps you provision a fleet of separately managed agents: it creates a multi-instance blueprint, configures its credentials and scopes, creates a blueprint principal, and provisions child identities. The skill described here isn't the single-instance or local public-client setup procedure.
 
-This AI-guided setup automates this entire workflow by using an AI coding agent (such as GitHub Copilot in VS Code) to execute the steps on your behalf. Instead of navigating between multiple documentation pages and running commands manually, you provide the AI agent with a single instruction file and it walks you through the process interactively. This instruction file is available as a Skill and can be accessed in more than one way.
+An AI coding assistant, such as GitHub Copilot in VS Code, can use a skill to help execute the provisioning steps. You remain responsible for reviewing proposed changes, arranging administrator approvals, and checking the results. Skill behavior depends on its version and the assistant; its completion summary isn't evidence of runtime authorization.
 
 ## Benefits
 
-The AI-guided setup offers several advantages over the manual workflow:
+The assistant can help assemble provisioning commands, suggest names, and explain error responses. Before allowing changes:
 
-- **Single entry point**: One instruction file replaces the need to navigate between multiple documentation pages. The AI agent follows the steps in order and handles transitions automatically.
-- **Automated prerequisite validation**: The AI agent validates that you have the correct Microsoft Entra roles, that the required tools and Graph modules are installed, and that required permissions are configured with admin consent before making any API calls.
-- **Smart defaults and auto-detection**: The AI agent queries your tenant for existing user information and resource details, then uses those values as suggestions when collecting configuration inputs.
-- **Derived naming conventions**: You provide a single display name for your agent, and the AI agent derives all related resource names (blueprint, blueprint principal, agent identities, identifier URIs) using consistent patterns.
-- **Inline error handling**: When a command fails, the AI agent analyzes the error, suggests a fix, and retries rather than requiring you to search through troubleshooting documentation. -- **Idempotent operations**: The AI agent checks whether resources already exist before creating them, making it safe to rerun the setup if a previous attempt was interrupted.

-#customer-intent: As a developer or identity architect, I want to understand the OAuth 2.0 authentication protocols and token flows for agents, so that I can implement secure authentication patterns for Agent identity blueprints and Agent Identities in my applications.
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+
+#customer-intent: As a developer or identity architect, I want to choose the right authentication protocol for my agent's hosting model and access requirements.
 ---
- 
-# Authentication protocols in agents
- 
-Agents use OAuth 2.0 protocols with specialized token exchange patterns enabled by Federated Identity Credentials (FIC). All agent auth flows involve multi-stage token exchanges where the agent identity blueprint impersonates the agent identity to perform operations. This article explains the authentication protocols and token flows used by agents. It covers delegation scenarios, autonomous operations, and federated identity credential patterns. Microsoft recommends that you use our SDKs like [Microsoft Entra ID Auth SDK (sidecar)](https://aka.ms/entra/sdk/agentid) since implementing these protocol steps isn't easy.
- 
-All agent entities are confidential clients that can also serve as APIs for On-Behalf-Of scenarios. Interactive flows aren't supported for any agent entity type, ensuring that all authentication occurs through programmatic token exchanges rather than user interaction flows.
- 
+
+# Choose an authentication protocol for an agent
+
+The right authentication protocol depends on where the agent runs and whose identity it uses to access a resource. Start with these questions:
+
+1. Does the agent run on a user's device or in a hosted service?
+1. Does the agent act for a signed-in user, as itself, or as a dedicated agent user account?
+1. If it acts for a signed-in user, does the agent initiate sign-in or receive a user access token from another application?
+
+Use Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL) or another supported authentication library instead of constructing protocol requests directly.
+
 [!INCLUDE [Use Microsoft SDKs](./includes/use-microsoft-libraries.md)]
- 
-## Prerequisites
- 
-If you aren't familiar already, go through the following protocol docs.
- 
+
+## Choose a protocol
+
+| Use case | Recommended protocol | Access type | Client type |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| A local agent runs on an endpoint device and signs in the user | Authorization code flow with Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) | Delegated | Public |
+| A hosted agent receives a user access token from a client application and calls another service for that user | On-Behalf-Of (OBO) flow | Delegated | Confidential |
+| A hosted agent runs without a user and accesses resources as itself | Client credentials flow; blueprint impersonation for multi-instance Agent IDs | Application | Confidential |
+| An autonomous agent needs a mailbox or another resource available only to a user | Agent's user account impersonation | Delegated permissions assigned to the agent's user account | Confidential |
+
+If more than one row applies, use a separate token acquisition path for each operating mode. For example, a hosted agent might use OBO for requests initiated by a user and app-only access for scheduled work that doesn't have user context.
+
+The blueprint's [instance mode](agent-blueprint.md#instance-modes-preview) also affects token acquisition. A single-instance Agent ID (preview) uses the shared blueprint client ID directly for authorization code, refresh, client credentials, and OBO requests. It doesn't acquire an intermediate blueprint impersonation token. Single-instance mode isn't limited to local or public clients. For an overview and links to the consent and SDK walkthroughs, see [Authentication for a single-instance agent identity](authenticate-single-instance-agent.md). To start with a platform-specific walkthrough, see [Choose an integration path for an agent](choose-agent-integration-path.md).
+
+## Local agent that signs in a user
+
+Choose the authorization code flow with PKCE when the agent:
+
+- Runs on a desktop, mobile device, or other endpoint.
+- Can open a browser for interactive sign-in.
+- Accesses protected services for the signed-in user.
+- Can't securely store a client secret, certificate, or federated identity credential.
+
+The local agent is a public client. It sends the user to the Microsoft identity platform `/authorize` endpoint, receives an authorization code at its registered redirect URI, and redeems the code by using a PKCE verifier. It doesn't present a client credential.
+
+A registered public-client Agent ID must use [single-instance mode](agent-blueprint.md#instance-modes-preview). Every installation uses the same client ID; don't create an Agent ID for each device. A local agent can alternatively use a [Client ID Metadata Document (CIMD)](client-id-metadata-documents.md) URL as its client ID.
+
+Don't use this flow for a hosted agent that receives a user access token from another application. Use OBO instead.
+
+For implementation and protocol details, see:
+
+- [Authenticate a local agent with Microsoft Entra ID](authenticate-local-agent.md)
+- [OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant](agent-authorization-code-oauth-flow.md)
+- [Microsoft identity platform and OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow](/entra/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-auth-code-flow)
+- [Public client and confidential client applications](/entra/identity-platform/msal-client-applications)
+
+## Hosted agent that acts for a signed-in user
+
+Choose the OBO flow when:
+
+- A client application signs in the user.
+- The client calls the hosted agent or its API with a user access token.
+- The agent must call a downstream API with the user's identity and delegated permissions.
+
+The hosted agent is a confidential client. It doesn't start another interactive sign-in. Instead, it exchanges the incoming user access token for a token to the downstream resource. The incoming token must be intended for the agent's blueprint; don't relay a token issued for another resource.
+
+For a multi-instance Agent ID, configure the required delegated permissions as inheritable permissions on the blueprint and obtain administrator consent.
+
+Don't use OBO when no signed-in user initiated the operation. Use app-only access for autonomous work.
+
+For implementation and protocol details, see:
+
+- [Agent OAuth flows: On behalf of flow](agent-on-behalf-of-oauth-flow.md)
 - [Microsoft identity platform and OAuth 2.0 On-Behalf-Of flow](/entra/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-on-behalf-of-flow)
-- [Microsoft identity platform and the OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow](/entra/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-client-creds-grant-flow)
- 
-## Supported grant types
- 
-The following are the supported grant types for agent applications.
- 
-### Agent identity blueprint
- 
-Agent identity blueprints support `client_credentials` enabling secure token acquisition for impersonation scenarios. The `jwt-bearer` grant type facilitates token exchanges in [On-Behalf Of scenarios](/entra/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-on-behalf-of-flow), allowing for delegation patterns. `refresh_token` grants enable background operations with user context, supporting long-running processes that maintain user authorization.
- 
-### Agent identity
- 
-Agent identities use `client_credentials` for app-only autonomous operations, enabling independent functionality without user context, and impersonation for a user agent identity. The `jwt-bearer` grant type supports both [client credential flow](/entra/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-client-creds-grant-flow) and  [On-Behalf Of (OBO) flow](/entra/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-on-behalf-of-flow) providing flexibility in delegation patterns.`refresh_token` grants facilitate background user-delegated operations, allowing agent identities to maintain user context across extended operations.
- 
-### Unsupported flows
-
-- The agent application model explicitly excludes certain authentication patterns to maintain security boundaries. Agents aren't supported for interactive (`/authorize`) flows, ensuring all authentication occurs programmatically.
-- Public client capabilities aren't available, requiring all agents to operate as confidential clients.
-- A web redirect URI can be configured on a blueprint for consent flows only (`response_type=none`), but can't be used for interactive token acquisition. Full redirect URI functionality is configured on the client application.
-
-## Core protocol patterns
- 
-Agents can operate in three primary modes:
- 
-- Agents operating on behalf of regular users in Microsoft Entra ID (interactive agents). This is a regular on-behalf-of flow.
-- Agents operating on their own behalf using service principals created for agents (autonomous).
-- Agents operating on their own behalf using user principals created specifically for that agent (for instance agents having their own mailbox).
+- [Configure inheritable permissions for agent identity blueprints](configure-inheritable-permissions-blueprints.md)
+
+## Hosted agent that acts as itself
+
+Choose the client credentials flow with Agent ID impersonation when the agent:
+
+- Runs in a hosted service that can protect a credential.
+- Performs scheduled, event-driven, or other autonomous work.
+- Accesses a resource as the Agent ID rather than as a user.
+
+For a multi-instance Agent ID, the blueprint first authenticates and obtains a token-exchange token for its child Agent ID. The Agent ID then uses that token as a client assertion in the client credentials flow. A single-instance Agent ID instead authenticates directly with the shared client ID and a credential on the blueprint. The resource token contains application permissions granted by an administrator and identifies the Agent ID as the actor.
+
+Use a managed identity and federated identity credential when the hosting environment supports them. Avoid client secrets.
 
 [!INCLUDE [Managed identities support](./includes/managed-identities-preferred.md)]
 
 [!INCLUDE [Dont use secrets](./includes/do-not-use-secrets.md)]
- 
-## Oauth protocols
- 
-There are three agent oauth flows:
- 
-:::image type="content" source="media/agent-oauth-protocols/agent-flows.png" alt-text="Diagram showing the illustration of oauth flow for agents." lightbox="media/agent-oauth-protocols/agent-flows.png":::
- 
-- [Agent on-behalf of flow](./agent-on-behalf-of-oauth-flow.md): Agents operating on behalf of regular users (interactive agents).
-- [Autonomous app flow](./agent-autonomous-app-oauth-flow.md): App-only operations enable agent identities to act autonomously without user context.
-- [Agent's user account flow](./agent-user-oauth-flow.md): Agents operating on their own behalf using user principals created specifically for agents.
+
+Don't use application permissions when the resource should apply a signed-in user's permissions or consent. Use authorization code with PKCE or OBO instead.
+
+For implementation and protocol details, see:
+
+- [Agent autonomous app OAuth flow](agent-autonomous-app-oauth-flow.md)
+- [Microsoft identity platform and the OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow](/entra/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-client-creds-grant-flow)
+- [Workload identity federation](/entra/workload-id/workload-identity-federation)
+
+## Autonomous agent that acts as a dedicated user
+
+Choose agent's user account impersonation only when an autonomous agent needs capabilities that are available to a user but not to an application identity. For example, an agent might need its own mailbox.
+
+An [agent's user account](agent-users.md) is a dedicated user identity for the agent, not the account of the person using the agent. The Agent ID impersonates this account through an agent-specific token exchange. Access is limited by the permissions assigned to the Agent ID and the agent's user account.
+
+Don't create an agent's user account only to run unattended work. If the resource supports application permissions, prefer app-only access so the workload doesn't depend on a user identity.
+
+For implementation details, see:
+
+- [Agent's user account impersonation protocol](agent-user-oauth-flow.md)
+- [Agent's user accounts](agent-users.md)
+
+## Related authentication concepts
+
+The following settings affect authentication but don't replace the protocol choice:
+
+- **Public or confidential client** describes whether the agent can securely hold a credential. For more information, see [Public client and confidential client applications](/entra/identity-platform/msal-client-applications).
+- **Managed identity, certificate, secret, or federated identity credential** describes how a confidential client proves its identity. Prefer managed identities and federated identity credentials when possible.
+- **CIMD or registered client ID** describes how a public client is identified. Both options can use authorization code flow with PKCE.
+- **Refresh token** lets a client obtain new access tokens without repeating the original authorization. It continues an existing delegated session; it isn't a separate operating model.
