diff --git a/docs/identity-platform/concept-native-authentication.md b/docs/identity-platform/concept-native-authentication.md index 64c93f26d52..48cd6c58ff3 100644 --- a/docs/identity-platform/concept-native-authentication.md +++ b/docs/identity-platform/concept-native-authentication.md @@ -1,90 +1,121 @@ --- -title: Native authentication -description: Learn how to set up native authentication in Microsoft Entra External ID. Customize the user interface for mobile and desktop apps, and provide a seamless sign-in experience. - +title: Embedded native authentication overview +description: Understand how Embedded native authentication gives your application control of the interface while Microsoft Entra External ID controls authentication. manager: dougeby -ms.service: identity-platform +ms.service: identity-platform ms.subservice: external -ms.topic: concept-article -#Customer intent: As a developer, devops, I want to learn more how to host the user interface (UI) within the client app by using native authentication so that I can take greater control over the UI and experience of my customer apps. -ms.date: 06/22/2026 +ms.topic: overview +ms.date: 11/13/2026 +ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1030 +ai-usage: ai-assisted +#customer intent: As an application developer, I want to understand Embedded native authentication so that I can choose and implement an application-managed authentication experience. +author: adamstoffel +ms.author: adamstoffel --- -# Native authentication in Microsoft Entra External ID + +# Native authentication overview [!INCLUDE [applies-to-external-only](../external-id/includes/applies-to-external-only.md)] -Microsoft Entra’s native authentication allows you to have full control over the design of your mobile and desktop application sign-in experience. Unlike browser-based solutions, native authentication allows you to create visually appealing, pixel-perfect authentication screens that seamlessly blend into your app's interface. With this approach, you can fully customize the user interface, including design elements, logo placement, and layout, ensuring a consistent and branded look. +[!INCLUDE [applies-to-authentication-native](../external-id/includes/applies-to-authentication-native.md)] + +Embedded native authentication is an authentication approach that lets your application present sign-up, sign-in, and password reset while Microsoft Entra External ID validates credentials and enforces authentication requirements. Your app controls the interface and handles the actions, available methods, and links returned by the Native Authentication API. + +## API version boundaries + +[!INCLUDE [native-authentication-public-preview](../external-id/includes/native-authentication-public-preview.md)] + +The primary references describe the response-driven Native Authentication API, with native routes such as `/api/v2.0`. Follow service-returned links without rewriting their versions or paths. The `/oauth2/v2.0` OAuth endpoint path is also used by V1 integrations. + +Existing V1 integrations can continue to use the [V1 API reference](reference-native-authentication-api-v1.md) and its [SDK library references](reference-native-authentication-api-v1.md#sdk-references). The legacy V1 guides and tutorials have been removed from this documentation. This documentation change doesn't announce retirement of V1 or its SDKs. See [SDK compatibility and migration](how-to-migrate-native-authentication-v1-v2.md#sdk-compatibility) for platform and package requirements. + + + +## Application-owned experience, service-controlled authentication + +With Embedded native authentication, a mobile, desktop, or single-page application (SPA) can present authentication within its own interface. Your application controls layout, interaction, and validation feedback. Microsoft Entra External ID validates credentials, enforces authentication requirements, and issues tokens. + +Tenant and Conditional Access policies and the application's user flow apply to Microsoft-hosted authentication, Embedded native authentication, and Bring Your Own UX (BYO UX). Presentation and integration responsibilities differ. With Embedded native authentication, your app handles the required interactions, such as a second-factor challenge after password verification or more attribute collection after email verification. + +Microsoft-hosted authentication presents pages on behalf of your app. Choose Embedded native authentication when your team needs control of the interface and can implement response handling and security responsibilities. See [Choose an authentication approach](../external-id/customers/concept-choose-authentication-approach.md) for the broader comparison. + +## Customer journeys + +The same authorization transaction surrounds each journey. Your app starts authorization, completes the returned authentication interactions, resumes authorization, and exchanges the authorization code for tokens. + +| Journey | Behavior | +| --- | --- | +| **Sign-up** | Create an email-with-password or passwordless email one-time passcode (OTP) account. Collect the attributes and complete the verification steps requested by the user flow. | +| **Sign-in** | Submit the customer's identifier and complete password or email one-time-passcode verification using an offered method. Username-with-password sign-in is also available for configured local accounts. | +| **Password reset** | Verify an offered email or SMS one-time passcode, submit a replacement password, and follow the password-update polling responses. Recovery can start before sign-in discovery or through a password method's `recover` link. | +| **Multifactor authentication (MFA) and inline registration** | Complete email or SMS verification when policy requires MFA. If registration is required, handle the returned `enroll` and `activate` operations. Email OTP first-factor accounts use a different second factor, such as SMS. | +| **Policy requirements after sign-up or password reset** | Continue handling required authentication, including MFA and Conditional Access, before requesting tokens. Completing account creation or a password update doesn't bypass policy. | -The standard app sign-in process, which relies on browser-delegated authentication, often results in a disruptive transition during authentication. Users are temporarily redirected to a system browser for authentication, only to be brought back to the app once the sign-in is complete. +Select journeys and methods from those available in the current transaction. Your application can present a choice or apply its flow logic within those options. -While browser-delegated authentication offers benefits such as reduced attack vectors and support for single sign-on (SSO), it offers limited UI customization options. +The Native Authentication API doesn't support federation, phone numbers as a first factor, time-based one-time passwords (TOTP), passkeys, push authentication, or external MFA methods. Later-operation step-up and using native-issued tokens with profile or credential-management APIs aren't supported. See the [method and integration matrices](../external-id/customers/concept-supported-features-customers.md#methods-and-journeys-by-approach) for the comparison with Microsoft-hosted authentication and BYO UX. -## When to use native authentication +For supported custom authentication extension events, see the [approach comparison](../external-id/customers/concept-supported-features-customers.md#custom-authentication-extension-applicability). For configuration, see [Custom authentication extensions](../external-id/customers/concept-custom-extensions.md). -When it comes to implementing authentication for mobile and desktop apps on External ID, you have two options: + -- Microsoft-hosted browser-delegated authentication. -- Fully custom SDK based native authentication. +## Integration responsibilities -The approach you choose depends on your app's specific requirements. While each app has unique authentication needs, there are some common considerations to keep in mind. Whether you choose native authentication or browser-delegated authentication, Microsoft Entra External ID supports both of them. +Use the configuration guide and API references for a direct integration, or use a documented JavaScript, Android, or Apple SDK. The [SDK quickstart](quickstart-native-authentication.md) configures a React Next.js sample. SDK entry points and supported continuation interfaces are specific to the package and platform. -For a side-by-side comparison of the two approaches, including feature availability, supported languages and frameworks, user experience, customization, and security trade-offs, see [Choose an authentication approach](/entra/external-id/customers/concept-choose-authentication-approach). +| Responsibility | What your application implements | +| --- | --- | +| **Response handling** | Use the latest `state`, `action`, and links to select an allowed operation through user choice or application flow logic. | +| **Method selection** | Select from the returned methods, use masked hints where needed, and follow the selected method's links. | +| **Attribute collection** | Collect values according to the returned field requirements and validation metadata. Don't require page-grouping metadata. | +| **Transaction continuity** | Keep the latest continuation token in memory and use it only with links from the same response. | +| **Authorization** | Request the needed scopes initially and exchange the final authorization code for tokens. | +| **Recovery** | Handle validation failures, throttling, expiration, unsupported interactions, and cancellation without replaying credentials automatically. A separately configured browser sign-in starts a new authentication attempt; it doesn't resume native progress. | -## How to enable native authentication +SPAs with Embedded native authentication and BYO UX websites need a proxy or edge cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) policy for cross-origin browser API calls. Android and iOS apps using native HTTP transports don't need CORS or a CORS proxy. See [Native authentication CORS concepts](concept-native-authentication-cors.md). -First, review the guidelines on [when to use native authentication](/entra/external-id/customers/concept-native-authentication#when-to-use-native-authentication). Then, have an internal discussion with your application's business owner, designer, and development team to determine if native authentication is necessary. +All service API calls in the current native authentication integration use a tenant-verified custom domain and the tenant GUID. Configure that authority before starting a journey; see [Configure the API authority](how-to-native-authentication-configure-app.md#configure-the-api-authority). -If your team determines that native authentication is necessary for your application, follow these steps to enable native authentication in the Microsoft Entra admin center: + -1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com). -1. Browse to **App registrations** and select the app registration for which you want to enable public client and native authentication flows. -1. Under **Manage**, select **Authentication**. -1. On the **Redirect URI configuration** tab, allow public client flows: - 1. For **Enable the following mobile and desktop flows** select **Yes**. - 1. For **Enable native authentication**, select **Yes**. -1. Select the **Save** button. +## Security boundaries -## Update your configuration code +Your application handles credentials, so protect passwords, one-time passcodes, continuation tokens, authorization codes, and issued tokens. Use HTTPS, don't log authentication bodies, and don't cache credential responses. Validate returned URL authorities before sending transaction data. -After enabling the native authentication APIs in the admin center, you still need to update your application's configuration code to support native authentication flows for Android or iOS/macOS. To do so, you need to add the challenge type field to your configuration. Challenge types are a list of values that the app uses to notify Microsoft Entra about the authentication method it supports. You can find more information about native authentication challenge types in [Native authentication challenge types](/entra/external-id/customers/concept-native-authentication-challenge-types). -If the configuration isn't updated to integrate native authentication components, the native authentication SDKs and APIs aren't usable. +Use client-side validation to help customers correct their input. The service validates authentication requests. -## Security considerations for native authentication + -Native authentication gives your development team full control over the authentication experience. With this control comes the responsibility to follow security best practices in your app's implementation, such as secure token handling and transport security (HTTPS). +## Session boundaries +Embedded native authentication supports single sign-on (SSO) for embedded webviews. A signed-in native app requests an access token for the web resource and includes it in the webview request's `Authorization` header. The resource validates the token and establishes a session, allowing access without another sign-in prompt. See [Authenticate an embedded webview from a native app](how-to-native-authentication-webview-sso.md). -## Single sign-on (SSO) +Signing out of your native app doesn't terminate other application or browser sessions. Clear each application's session separately when your sign-out experience requires it. -Native authentication supports single sign-on (SSO) for embedded web views. This allows users to sign in once through the native app's UI and then access web resources hosted in an embedded web view (for example, `WKWebView` on iOS or `WebView` on Android) without encountering a second login prompt. + + -The app achieves this by retrieving an access token using the Native Auth SDK or the [native authentication API](reference-native-authentication-api.md) and injecting it into the web view's HTTP request via the `Authorization` header. The web resource validates the token and establishes a session, providing a seamless transition from the native experience to web content. +## Existing V1 application configuration -For implementation steps, see [Implement single sign-on from native apps to embedded web views](how-to-native-authentication-webview-sso.md). +For existing V1 applications, [enable public client and native authentication flows](reference-native-authentication-api-v1.md#enable-public-client-and-native-authentication-flows), then update your platform configuration. The [V1 API reference](reference-native-authentication-api-v1.md#v1-challenge-types-and-capabilities) describes challenge types and capabilities. For a response-driven integration, follow [Configure an application](how-to-native-authentication-configure-app.md) to select and configure the V2 entry points. -> [!NOTE] -> Cross-app SSO through system browsers isn't supported with native authentication. +## Conditional Access and sign-in frequency -## How to use native authentication +Microsoft Entra External ID supports the Conditional Access [sign-in frequency (SIF)](../identity/conditional-access/concept-session-lifetime.md#user-sign-in-frequency) session control for both Microsoft-hosted and native authentication. -You can build apps that use native authentication by using our native authentication APIs or the Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL) SDK for Android, iOS, macOS, and web applications. Whenever possible, we recommend using MSAL to add native authentication to your apps. +For native authentication, when reauthentication is required by the policy, Microsoft Entra External ID prevents token issuance during refresh token grants (`grant_type=refresh_token`). Your app must handle the failed token refresh and prompt the user to sign in again before it can acquire new tokens. modifiedFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/identity-platform/how-to-native-authentication-webview-sso.md b/docs/identity-platform/how-to-native-authentication-webview-sso.md index e99122cc2df..72322358134 100644 --- a/docs/identity-platform/how-to-native-authentication-webview-sso.md +++ b/docs/identity-platform/how-to-native-authentication-webview-sso.md @@ -1,143 +1,127 @@ --- -title: Implement Single Sign-On from Native Apps to Embedded Web Views -description: Learn how to implement SSO between a native mobile app and a web resource in an embedded web view using Microsoft Entra External ID native authentication. -ms.service: identity-platform -ms.subservice: external +title: Authenticate an embedded webview from a native app +description: Use a resource access token to open an authenticated embedded webview and establish a web resource's own session with Microsoft Entra External ID. ms.topic: how-to -ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-105 -ms.date: 04/04/2026 +ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1030 +ms.date: 11/13/2026 ai-usage: ai-assisted - -#customer intent: As a mobile developer, I want to implement single sign-on between my native app and an embedded web view so that users can access web resources without encountering a second login prompt. +#customer intent: As a mobile developer, I want to implement single sign-on between my native app and an embedded webview so that users can access my web resource without a second sign-in prompt. --- -# Implement single sign-on from native apps to embedded web views +# Authenticate an embedded webview from a native app [!INCLUDE [applies-to-external-only](../external-id/includes/applies-to-external-only.md)] -When your mobile app includes web-based features like a profile update page or rewards dashboard, users expect a seamless single sign-on experience. They shouldn't encounter a second login prompt after already signing in through the native app. +[!INCLUDE [applies-to-authentication-native](../external-id/includes/applies-to-authentication-native.md)] -This article shows you how to implement single sign-on (SSO) between a native mobile application and a web resource hosted in an embedded web view (for example, `WKWebView` on iOS or `WebView` on Android). Unlike system browsers, embedded web views allow you to manipulate network requests before they're sent. This capability enables your app to inject the user's authentication state directly into request headers. +Use a resource access token to open an authenticated web page inside your native app. This guide connects a user signed in through Microsoft Entra External ID to an HTTPS web resource your team controls, such as your app's rewards page, without a second sign-in prompt. -The recommended flow works as follows: +You need a native app with a working sign-in flow and a web resource that can validate bearer tokens. This resource-token flow provides single sign-on (SSO) to that resource in the embedded webview. -1. The user signs in through the mobile app's native UI using the Native Auth SDK or the [native authentication API](reference-native-authentication-api.md). -1. Before loading the web view, the app retrieves a valid access token from the SDK or API. -1. The app loads the web view with a custom request that includes the access token in the `Authorization: Bearer ` header. -1. The web resource validates the token and grants access immediately. +[!INCLUDE [native-authentication-public-preview](~/external-id/includes/native-authentication-public-preview.md)] -The following diagram shows the interaction between the web resource, mobile app, SDK, and the identity service (ESTS): +The resource-token pattern for embedded webviews is generally available. It establishes a session for your web resource, independently of the Native Authentication API's support contract. -:::image type="content" source="./media/native-authentication/common/native-application-sign-in-with-web-view-authentication.png" alt-text="Sequence diagram showing the SSO flow where the mobile app signs in via SDK, receives tokens, and loads the web view with the access token in the Authorization header."::: + + ## Prerequisites -- A mobile app with native authentication configured using the Native Auth SDK or the [native authentication API](reference-native-authentication-api.md). If you're using the SDK and haven't set up your app yet, see [Prepare your Android app for native authentication](tutorial-native-authentication-prepare-android-app.md) or [Prepare your iOS/macOS app for native authentication](tutorial-native-authentication-prepare-ios-macos-app.md). -- A completed sign-in flow in your native app. For guidance, see [Sign in users in an Android mobile app](quickstart-native-authentication-android-sign-in.md) or [Sign in users in an iOS mobile app](quickstart-native-authentication-ios-sign-in.md). -- A web resource served over HTTPS (TLS). Don't send tokens over HTTP. -- A shared client identity (application ID) between the mobile app and the web resource. For details, see [Limitations and configuration requirements](#limitations-and-configuration-requirements). +- An app configured for Embedded native authentication in an external tenant. See [Configure an application](how-to-native-authentication-configure-app.md). +- A native app with a working sign-in flow. See the [sign-in reference](reference-native-authentication-sign-in.md). +- An HTTPS web resource with exposed delegated scopes and server-side token validation. See [Expose a web API](quickstart-configure-app-expose-web-apis.md#add-a-scope). +- Permission for the native app to request those scopes. See [Configure access to your web API](quickstart-configure-app-access-web-apis.md#add-permissions-to-access-your-web-api). +- An embedded webview that can send an `Authorization` header with its initial request. ## Sign in with native authentication -Complete the standard sign-in flow using the Native Auth SDK or the [native authentication API](reference-native-authentication-api.md). When sign-in succeeds using the SDK, it caches the access token, ID token, and refresh token securely. If you use the API directly, your app is responsible for securely storing the tokens it receives. - -For detailed sign-in implementation steps, see: - -- **Android**: [Sign in users in an Android (Kotlin) mobile app](tutorial-native-authentication-android-sign-in-sign-out.md) -- **iOS/macOS**: [Sign in users in an iOS (Swift) mobile app](tutorial-native-authentication-ios-macos-sign-in-sign-out.md) - -## Retrieve the access token - -When the user triggers the action to open the web view, ensure the app has a valid, unexpired access token before loading the web resource. - -If you use the Native Auth SDK, request a token silently. The SDK provides a `getAccessToken()` method that retrieves a valid token from the cache or silently refreshes it. For details on acquiring access tokens with specific scopes, see: - -- **Android**: [Acquire multiple access tokens](tutorial-native-authentication-android-sign-in-call-api.md) -- **iOS/macOS**: [Acquire multiple access tokens](tutorial-native-authentication-ios-sign-in-call-api.md) +Request access for the resource you intend to open, rather than reusing a token issued for a different API. -If you use the native authentication API directly, your app retrieves tokens through the API's `/oauth/v2.0/token` endpoint. For details, see [Native authentication API reference](reference-native-authentication-api.md). +1. Start authorization with the web resource's required scopes in the initial `scope` parameter. Request only the permissions needed for the page's operations. +1. Complete the sign-in actions returned by the service. Follow the returned links and use the latest continuation token for the active transaction. +1. When the service returns `state: continue`, follow `_links.continue` to resume authorization. +1. Exchange the returned authorization code for tokens. Use the response's `access_token` for the web resource, not the `id_token` or a continuation token. -Request the token with the exact scopes required by the web resource. For scope requirements, see [Limitations and configuration requirements](#limitations-and-configuration-requirements). +For the authorization and token request contracts, see the [Native Authentication API reference](reference-native-authentication.md). -## Load the web view with authentication - -There are two methods to pass the authentication state to the web view. The recommended approach uses authorization headers. A cookie-based fallback is available for legacy scenarios but is discouraged. +For existing V1 integrations, see the [V1 API reference](reference-native-authentication-api-v1.md) and its [SDK library references](reference-native-authentication-api-v1.md#sdk-references) for your platform. -### Option A: Use a bearer token via HTTP header (recommended) +The following diagram illustrates the resource-token flow with a V1 SDK: -Inject the access token directly into the `Authorization` header of the initial HTTP request used to load the web view. This is the most secure and robust method. +:::image type="content" source="./media/native-authentication/common/native-application-sign-in-with-web-view-authentication.png" alt-text="Sequence diagram showing an app signing in through an SDK and sending an access token in the embedded webview request."::: -This approach is preferred because it: - -- **Is stateless**: It doesn't rely on persistent cookies on the client side. -- **Isolates the token**: It strictly limits the token to this specific request flow. -- **Avoids web-based attack vectors**: It sidesteps common security issues associated with browser-managed sessions. +## Retrieve the access token -To load the web view with header-based authentication: +Before opening the webview, get a valid, unexpired access token for the resource. -1. Construct the URL for the web resource. Ensure it uses HTTPS. -1. Create a custom network request object. -1. Add the header `Authorization: Bearer ` to the request. -1. Load the request into the web view component (for example, `WKWebView` on iOS or `WebView` on Android). +1. Check the token response's expiration metadata rather than parsing the access token in the client. +1. If the app doesn't have a usable token for the required resource and scopes, complete authorization to obtain one before loading the page. +1. Keep the token in the native app's protected authentication state until you construct the request. Don't expose it in page scripts, diagnostics, or a URL. - +Access tokens are validated by the receiving resource, not by the native client. See [Access tokens](access-tokens.md). -### Option B: Use cookies (fallback only) +For V1 SDK token acquisition, use the platform's [SDK library reference](reference-native-authentication-api-v1.md#sdk-references). Request the scopes described in [Limitations and configuration requirements](#limitations-and-configuration-requirements). -If the target web resource can't handle header-based authentication (for example, certain legacy single-page applications), you can inject the token as a cookie. This approach is generally discouraged because of security risks. +## Load the web view with authentication -Injecting cookies into a web view entrusts the authentication state to a browser-managed mechanism. This makes the session "ambient" (automatically attached to requests), which exposes the app to standard web attack classes: +Send the token in the initial request to the intended web resource. This procedure establishes the web resource's session. -- **XSS (cross-site scripting)**: The session is vulnerable to hijacking if the web content is compromised. -- **CSRF (cross-site request forgery)**: There's a risk of unintended authenticated requests. -- **Session fixation**: An attacker might control the session state. -- **Compliance**: This approach conflicts with security best practices (for example, MASTG-KNOW-0018) regarding persisting sensitive state in web view cookie jars. + -> [!WARNING] -> The cookie-based approach is conditionally approved and generally discouraged. Use it only when the target web resource can't support header-based authentication. +1. Construct the HTTPS URL for your web resource without including the token in its path, query, or fragment. +1. Create the initial webview request with `Authorization: Bearer `, replacing `` with the access token for the web resource. +1. Load that request in the embedded webview. +1. Restrict bearer-token delivery to the intended resource. Don't forward the header to unrelated origins when handling navigation or redirects. -If you use the cookie-based approach, these requirements apply: + -- Use server-issued session cookies where possible. -- Avoid placing raw access tokens directly into cookies. -- Set cookies with the `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, and appropriate `SameSite` attributes. -- Enforce strict CSRF protection on the server side. +Use bearer authentication for the initial request and let the server issue the application session cookie after validation. Keep the raw access token in the native app's protected authentication state. ## Validate and persist the token on the backend -When the request reaches the web resource, the backend processes the token to establish the session. +The web resource validates the access token and authorizes the requested operation before creating a session. ### Validate the token -The web server intercepts incoming requests and verifies the token's signature and claims. For ASP.NET Core backends, use `Microsoft.Identity.Web` (MISE) to handle validation automatically. +Use the resource's token-validation middleware before returning protected content. -Ensure the token's audience (`aud`) claim matches the web API's identifier and the issuer (`iss`) claim matches the expected authority. +1. Validate the token's signature, issuer, and lifetime against the resource's trusted Microsoft Entra configuration. +1. Verify that the `aud` claim identifies the receiving resource. +1. Verify the delegated scopes required for the requested operation and the user's authorization to access the data. +1. Reject the request if validation or authorization fails. Don't create a session from an invalid token. - - +For the audience and permission checks, see [Validate access-token claims](claims-validation.md). ### Persist the session -The web view doesn't persist custom headers on subsequent navigation events (for example, when the user selects a link). To maintain the authenticated state after the initial request, the server issues a standard session cookie (`Set-Cookie`) upon successful validation of the initial bearer token. +Establish a server-managed session for subsequent webview navigation. + +1. After successful token validation, issue the web resource's session cookie through `Set-Cookie`. +1. Set `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, and the `SameSite` policy appropriate for the application's navigation. Apply server-side protection against cross-site request forgery for cookie-authenticated operations. +1. Use the session cookie for subsequent requests to that web resource. Don't store the raw access token in the cookie. + +## Verify access and sign-out + +Signing out of the native app doesn't terminate the web resource's session or other application and browser sessions. Clear each session through its own sign-out mechanism. -Configure the session cookie with the following attributes: +Test both resource authorization and the session that the webview retains. -- `HttpOnly` -- `Secure` -- An appropriate `SameSite` policy +1. Sign in to the native app and open the web resource. Confirm that the expected user's page opens without another sign-in prompt. +1. Navigate to another protected page in the same web resource. Confirm that its server-issued session cookie maintains the session. +1. Test an expired token, a token issued for a different resource, and a token without the required scope. Confirm that none establishes an authorized session. +1. Sign out and clear authentication state in both the native app and the web resource. Reopen the protected page and confirm that the old web session no longer grants access. +1. Check that application and server diagnostics exclude tokens, cookies, credentials, and personal data. ## Limitations and configuration requirements -To ensure the token issued to the mobile app is accepted by the web resource, keep the following configurations in mind: +The token's audience and permissions identify the web resource and authorized operations. The native client and resource can have separate app registrations. -- **Shared client identity**: The mobile app and web app should share the same client ID (application ID). If they have different IDs, the backend rejects the mobile app's token as an audience mismatch. -- **Scope alignment**: The mobile app requests the access token with the exact scopes required by the web resource (for example, `Profile.Read`, `Orders.Write`). +This integration requires control over the web resource's bearer-token validation and session creation. -> [!NOTE] -> This solution is tailored specifically for the web view scenario. A more generic solution that extends SSO capabilities to system browsers and other complex scenarios is planned for a future release. +The resulting cookie belongs to your web resource. It doesn't create a browser-wide Microsoft Entra session or enable profile or credential-management APIs. ## Related content -- [Native authentication in Microsoft Entra External ID](concept-native-authentication.md) -- [Native authentication web fallback](concept-native-authentication-web-fallback.md) -- [Native authentication API reference](reference-native-authentication-api.md) +- [Embedded native authentication overview](concept-native-authentication.md). +- [Embedded native authentication web fallback](concept-native-authentication-web-fallback.md). +- [The Native Authentication API reference](reference-native-authentication.md).

 So for example, if a new employee joins your organization and that employee has never been affiliated with your organization before, that employee requires a new digital identity, represented as a user account in Microsoft Entra ID. The creation of this account would fall into a "Joiner" process, which could be automated if there was a system of record such as Workday that could indicate when the new employee starts work. Later, if your organization has an employee move from say, Sales to Marketing, they would fall into a "Mover" process. Review guest eligibility separately before applying this employee journey to a guest account.
+
 ## Identity lifecycle management for guests
 
 Similar processes are also needed for additional identities, for partners, suppliers and other guests, to enable them to collaborate or have access to resources. Microsoft Entra entitlement management utilizes Microsoft Entra External ID business-to-business (B2B) to provide the lifecycle controls needed to collaborate with people outside your organization who require access to your organization's resources. With Microsoft Entra B2B, external users authenticate to their home directory or identity provider, but have a representation in your organization's directory. The representation in your organization's directory enables the user to be assigned access to your resources. Entitlement management enables individuals outside your organization to request access, creating a digital identity for them as needed. These digital identities are automatically removed when the user loses access.

 # Risk-based access policies
 
 Risk-based access control policies can be applied to protect organizations when a sign-in or user is detected to be at risk.
 
-![Diagram that shows a conceptual risk-based Conditional Access policy.](./media/concept-identity-protection-policies/risk-based-conditional-access-diagram.png)
+![Diagram of user, location, device, application, and risk signals informing Conditional Access decisions, including requiring identity verification.](./media/concept-identity-protection-policies/risk-based-conditional-access-diagram.png)
 
 Microsoft Entra Conditional Access offers two user-specific risk conditions powered by Microsoft Entra ID Protection signals: **[Sign-in risk](../identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-conditions.md#sign-in-risk)** and **[User risk](../identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-conditions.md#user-risk)**. Organizations can create risk-based Conditional Access policies by configuring these two risk conditions and choosing an access control method. During each sign-in, ID Protection sends the detected risk levels to Conditional Access, and the risk-based policies apply if the policy conditions are satisfied.
 
@@ -36,6 +39,7 @@ ID Protection analyzes signals about user accounts and calculates a risk score b
 1. Require risk remediation: ID Protection manages the appropriate remediation flow for all authentication methods.
 1. Require password change: ID Protection blocks access until user completes a secure password change.
 1. Block access: ID Protection blocks the user until risk is addressed.
+1. **Require Identity Verification (preview)**: Users complete identity verification to remediate risk in supported scenarios.
 
 Policies requiring either #1 or #2 forces end users to remediate their user risk and unblock themselves.
 
@@ -57,6 +61,27 @@ This control uses adaptive risk remediation to let you author a Conditional Acce
   - `AppId`: Public cloud = `93625bc8-bfe2-437a-97e0-3d0060024faa`, Azure for US Government = `00001111-aaaa-2222-bbbb-3333cccc4444`
   - `ResourceId`: `00000003-0000-0000-c000-000000000000`
 
+## Identity verification for risk
+
+The **Require Identity Verification (preview)** grant control lets users remediate risk by verifying their identity in supported scenarios. Use this control in a Conditional Access policy with a **User risk** or **Sign-in risk** condition to require identity verification when the detected risk matches the policy. Create separate policies for the two risk conditions.
+
+An eligible identity verification profile is a prerequisite for a policy that uses this grant control to work. Before configuring the policy, [create and configure an identity verification profile](../identity/authentication/concept-authentication-verified-id.md#create-and-manage-identity-verification-profiles) with **Profile purpose** set to **All** or **Verification** and a provider and credential type that support your risk scenario. For tenant-issued credentials, select **Verification**. Don't use an **Onboarding**- or **Recovery**-purpose profile for the risk-based resource-access policy.
+
+- **Policy configuration:** Select an identity verification profile and credential type that support the risk scenario, and apply the identity verification grant control to your risk-based policy.
+- **User experience:** When the policy applies, the user completes the required identity verification challenge. Microsoft Entra ID Protection can use the successful verification result to remediate the applicable risk.
+- **Remediation outcome:** Review the verification result, access decision, and relevant risk record separately to confirm the outcome for the scenario.
+
+Successful identity verification remediates user risk when the triggering policy uses a **User risk** condition, or sign-in risk when it uses a **Sign-in risk** condition. Failed verification doesn't remediate risk.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> **Require Identity Verification (preview)** is independent of the **Require risk remediation** control described earlier. **Require risk remediation** manages adaptive remediation based on the observed threat and authentication method; selecting it doesn't automatically require an identity verification challenge.
+
+Follow the existing guidance to [configure identity verification for risk](howto-identity-protection-configure-risk-policies.md#configure-identity-verification-for-risk), [complete the verification journey](concept-identity-protection-user-experience.md#identity-verification-for-risk), and [validate the remediation outcome](howto-identity-protection-remediate-unblock.md#validate-identity-verification-remediation). Review the risk targeted by the triggering policy; don't infer that every risk was cleared.
+
+For licensing specific to this integration, see [identity verification licensing](../fundamentals/licensing.md#identity-verification).
+
+:::image type="content" source="../identity/conditional-access/media/policy-require-identity-verification/require-identity-verification-grant-control.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Conditional Access Grant pane with Grant access selected and Require identity verification checked." lightbox="../identity/conditional-access/media/policy-require-identity-verification/require-identity-verification-grant-control.png":::
+
 ## Sign-in risk-based Conditional Access policy
 
 During each sign-in, ID Protection analyzes hundreds of signals in real-time and calculates a sign-in risk level that represents the probability that the given authentication request isn't authorized. This risk level then gets sent to Conditional Access, where the organization's configured policies are evaluated. Administrators can configure sign-in risk-based Conditional Access policies to enforce access controls based on sign-in risk, including requirements such as:
@@ -65,13 +90,14 @@ During each sign-in, ID Protection analyzes hundreds of signals in real-time and
 - Allow access
 - Require multifactor authentication
 - Require reauthentication (Sign-in frequency)
+- **Require Identity Verification (preview)**: Users complete identity verification to remediate risk in supported scenarios.
 
 If risks are detected on a sign-in, users can perform the required access control such as multifactor authentication to self-remediate and close the risky sign-in event to prevent unnecessary noise for administrators.
 
 ![Screenshot of a sign-in risk-based Conditional Access policy.](./media/concept-identity-protection-policies/sign-in-risk-policy.png)
 
 > [!NOTE] 
-> Users must have registered an authentication method that can satisfy Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication before triggering a sign-in risk policy.
+> If your sign-in risk policy requires multifactor authentication, users must have registered an authentication method that can satisfy that requirement before triggering the policy.

Successful recovery writes verification history to the user's account. For more information, see [User verification status and history](concept-authentication-methods-manage.md#identity-verification-status-and-history) and [Passkey credential provenance](concept-authentication-passkeys-fido2.md#credential-provenance). + +> [!NOTE] +> During preview, credential provenance is recorded only for passkey credentials. + +## Next step + +Account recovery takes about 5–10 minutes to set up. Start in Evaluation mode so you can validate the experience before enabling production recovery. -Account recovery takes about 5–10 minutes to set up. Start in Evaluation mode so you can validate the experience before enabling production recovery. To get started, see [Enable and configure account recovery in Microsoft Entra ID](how-to-account-recovery-enable.md). +> [!div class="nextstepaction"] +> [Enable and configure account recovery in Microsoft Entra ID](how-to-account-recovery-enable.md) ## Related content

Instead, Verified ID serves as the identity proofing layer for scenarios where a user's identity must be re-established — such as account recovery when all authentication methods are lost. -Identity verification profiles are the policy layer that controls which users can participate in Verified ID flows, which provider performs verification, and how identity claims are validated. Today, Verified ID profiles are used for account recovery — enabling users who lose all authentication methods to regain access through government-issued identity verification. The profile framework is designed to support additional identity verification scenarios in the future. +Identity verification profiles control which users can participate in these flows, which verification method is used, and how identity claims are validated. Profiles support account recovery, onboarding, and verification for access. + +## Prerequisites + +During preview, identity verification profiles and their integrated journeys are available only in the Microsoft public cloud, not in national or sovereign clouds. + +To view users' identity verification status and history, enable tenant-wide **Collect identity verification history** in the authentication methods policy under **Authentication methods** > **Verified ID** > **Configure** > **Data collection**. + +:::image type="content" source="media/concept-authentication-verified-id/collect-identity-verification-history.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Verified ID Configure tab with Collect identity verification history enabled under Data collection." lightbox="media/concept-authentication-verified-id/collect-identity-verification-history.png"::: + +> [!NOTE] +> Creating an identity verification profile automatically enables **Collect identity verification history** across your tenant. For the user-level views, see [Identity verification status and history](concept-authentication-methods-manage.md#identity-verification-status-and-history). + +To view a user's identity verification status and history, use at least the [Security Reader](../role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#security-reader) role. + +Before creating a profile: + +- Identify whether you need recovery, onboarding, or verification for access. +- For recovery, complete the Verified ID, Face Check, provider subscription, and account-matching preparation in [Enable and test account recovery](how-to-account-recovery-enable.md). +- Identify the users to include in your evaluation. +- Confirm that your tenant has access to shared profiles and that you have at least the [Authentication Policy Administrator](../role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#authentication-policy-administrator) role to manage them. +- Microsoft Entra ID P1 or an eligible higher license for identity verification profiles. Review the [identity verification licensing requirements](../../fundamentals/licensing.md#identity-verification) for your scenario. + + ## Identity verification profiles An identity verification profile is a configuration object that defines identity verification behavior for a group of users. Profiles specify: -- **Name and description** — A display name and description that identifies the profile's purpose. -- **State** — Whether the profile is enabled or disabled. +- **Name and description** — A display name and description that identify the profile. +- **Profile purpose** — The scenario the profile supports: **All**, **Verification**, **Onboarding**, or **Recovery**. See [Credential support by scenario](#credential-support-by-scenario). +- **Profile mode** — Whether the profile operates in **Evaluation** or **Production** mode. - **User group scope** — Which users the profile applies to, defined through group-based assignment. -- **Identity verification provider** — The third-party provider that performs identity proofing, identified by a verifier DID (Decentralized Identifier) — a unique cryptographic identifier for the verifier in the credential exchange. +- **Verification method** — The identity verification provider or supported tenant-issued credential used for the selected purpose. - **Face Check configuration** — Settings for Microsoft Entra Verified ID Face Check behavior during verification. - **Profile configuration** — The accepted credential issuer, how identity claims map to user properties, and the credential type for the exchange. -- **Usage configurations** — The scenarios the profile applies to, such as `recovery`. Additional scenarios may be supported in the future. - **Priority** — The processing order when a user matches multiple profiles. -### Automatic creation through account recovery +### Profile mode + +Use **Profile mode** to test identity verification or make it operational for the selected **Profile purpose**. + +| Mode | Behavior | +| --- | --- | +| **Evaluation** | The scenario can invoke identity verification, but verification doesn't complete the handoff to onboarding, account recovery, or resource access. | +| **Production** | Identity verification is fully operational for the selected profile purpose, enabling the handoff to the corresponding onboarding, account recovery, or resource-access journey. | + +Successful verification in **Evaluation** mode doesn't mean onboarding or recovery completed or access was granted. + +### Credential support by scenario + +Choose the purpose before selecting a verification method: **All**, **Verification**, **Onboarding**, or **Recovery**. Use this matrix to choose a credential for your scenario. Confirm release availability in your tenant before deployment. + +| Credential | All-purpose profile | Verification for access | Recovery | Onboarding | +| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | +| Employee ID | Not supported. | Supported. | Not supported. | Not supported. | +| Custom-issued Verified ID | Not supported. | Supported. | Not supported. | Not supported. | +| Third-party Verified ID from Security Marketplace | Supported. | Supported. | Required. | Required. | + +For recovery, keep the third-party provider and account-matching requirements. Don't substitute an employee credential or a custom-issued credential based only on the existence of a shared profile. + +For resource-access verification, including risk-based policies, set **Profile purpose** to **All** or **Verification**. **All** supports identity verification providers only. To use tenant-issued credentials, select **Verification**. **Onboarding** and **Recovery** purposes are for their respective bootstrap journeys. + + + + + + +## Create and manage identity verification profiles + +Create and manage profiles in the Microsoft Entra admin center under **Verified ID** > **ID verification profiles** > **Profiles**. On **Getting started**, review the setup checklist and select **Create your first identity verification profile**. If profiles already exist, select **Profiles** > **Create profile** instead. + +Enter a **Name** and **Description**, select **Profile purpose**, and choose **Profile mode**. The shared wizard also includes user groups, the verification method, account validation, optional custom claim validation, and self-service issuance settings. Review those settings before completing profile creation. + +For recovery, use your subscribed identity verification provider and check the user's **First name** and **Last name** against the claims returned by that provider. Review any custom claim-validation extension with its owner before using it. -Identity verification profiles are automatically created and configured when an [Authentication Administrator](/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference#authentication-administrator) sets up account recovery through the Microsoft Entra admin center (**Entra ID** > **Account recovery**). The Account Recovery setup wizard handles profile creation, provider configuration, user group scoping, and account validation rules. + + + +### User scope and profile selection + +Configure user scope in the shared-profile wizard. Use **Include** > **Select targets** > **Select groups** to start with an evaluation group. > [!IMPORTANT] -> Profiles created through account recovery don't require separate management in the authentication method policy settings. We recommend managing Verified ID assignment for recovery purposes through the Account Recovery setup wizard, which provides a guided experience for creating and configuring profiles. +> Exclusions apply globally across all identity verification profiles, not just the profile you're creating or editing. Groups excluded here are also reflected in the Verified ID authentication methods policy's **Exclude** settings. Don't use **Exclude** to remove a group from only one profile; use that profile's **Include** assignments to define its scope. + +These profile exclusions are separate from the [Conditional Access onboarding and recovery exclusion](../conditional-access/policy-require-identity-verification.md#enable-the-global-onboarding-and-recovery-exclusion-preview). -### Profile management in authentication method policy +Use multiple profiles for different user populations, verification providers, or pilot groups. When a user belongs to groups that match multiple profiles, the system evaluates profiles in priority order and applies the first matching profile. -The Verified ID authentication method policy provides visibility into profiles and user assignments. +Lower priority numbers are evaluated first: priority 1 precedes priority 5. Priority numbers are unique, so ties aren't possible. -[![Screenshot that shows the Verified ID authentication method policy page with the Enable toggle, Include and Exclude tabs, group assignment table, and profile dropdown.](media/how-to-account-recovery-enable/vid-auth-method-policy.png)](media/how-to-account-recovery-enable/vid-auth-method-policy.png#lightbox) +### Review self-service issuance -From the policy settings, administrators can: +Review whether to enable self-service issuance, the approved user scope, and the custom credential issuance destination before enabling the experience. My Account self-service issuance is separate from inline issuance during a protected journey. Don't assume that provider issuance destinations follow the same rules as custom credential destinations. -- **View profile details** — See the configuration, provider, state, and priority of each identity verification profile, including the account validation claims mapping and custom authentication extension settings. +### Keep recovery settings separate - [![Screenshot that shows the Identity Verification Profile details panel with profile mode, profile details, user group, identity verification provider, account validation claims table, and custom authentication extension.](media/how-to-account-recovery-enable/vid-profile-details.png)](media/how-to-account-recovery-enable/vid-profile-details.png#lightbox) +Profile creation is separate from enabling the tenant's Account recovery policy and choosing actions after recovery. Configure those settings under **Account recovery**, not in the shared profiles blade. Temporary Access Pass (TAP) issuance is on by default. TAP-free registration and stale-credential cleanup are preview choices. -- **Scope user groups** — Assign a group of users to a specific Verified ID profile, controlling which users can participate in the verified credential flow. -- **Create new assignments** — Add new group-to-profile assignments for users who need access to a specific identity verification profile. -- **Global exclusion** — Exclude specific groups from all identity verification profiles. Excluded users can't participate in any Verified ID-based flow, regardless of which profiles are configured. +For account recovery setup, see [Enable and configure account recovery](how-to-account-recovery-enable.md). Creating a profile alone doesn't establish that the TAP-free path is supported for your users. -> [!TIP] -> The authentication method policy view is useful for auditing profile assignments across the organization. For creating and configuring profiles, use the Account Recovery setup wizard. +### Test and manage the profile -### Multiple profiles +> [!NOTE] +> Changes to identity verification profiles can take 5-10 minutes to apply. After saving changes, allow time for them to take effect before testing the affected journey. -Organizations can create multiple identity verification profiles to support different user populations. For example: +Validate the profile before expanding your deployment: -- A profile for corporate employees using one identity verification provider with exact name matching -- A profile for frontline workers using a different provider with relaxed matching -- A profile for a pilot group testing a new provider before broad deployment +- Confirm that the intended profile appears with the expected purpose and verification method. +- Test with a user in the intended scope and confirm that the expected provider handles verification. +- For recovery, test account matching and confirm that evaluation doesn't restore account access. +- Check that an out-of-scope user doesn't receive the intended recovery offer, using the eligibility guidance in [the recovery user article](how-to-account-recovery-for-users.md). +- Review the Conditional Access scope for your scenario with the policy owner. +- Before enabling the profile for production users, set **Profile mode** to **Production** and test the complete journey for the selected **Profile purpose**. -When a user belongs to groups that match multiple profiles, the system evaluates profiles in priority order and applies the first matching profile. +### Troubleshoot an unavailable identity verification profile -## Usage scenarios +During onboarding, account recovery, or identity verification step-up, a user can receive the following sign-in error when no valid identity verification profile is available to them: -Each identity verification profile includes one or more usage configurations that define which scenarios the profile applies to. +`AADSTS10020005: No valid VidProfile data found for the tenant.` -### Account recovery +The message doesn't necessarily mean that the tenant has no profiles. Check whether a valid profile is available for the affected user and scenario: -Account recovery is the primary usage scenario for Verified ID profiles today. When a user loses all registered authentication methods — such as when a device is lost, stolen, or compromised — account recovery uses the Verified ID profile to determine: +- Confirm that the intended profile exists and supports the scenario and credential type. See [Credential support by scenario](#credential-support-by-scenario). +- Review the user's group assignments and applicable exclusions in the profile and Verified ID authentication method policy. +- Confirm that Verified ID is enabled for the intended users and review the saved profile configuration. -- Which identity verification provider verifies the user's identity -- How identity claims from the provider are matched against the user's Microsoft Entra ID profile -- Whether the profile operates in Evaluation mode (testing) or Production mode (full recovery) +After correcting the configuration, test the affected journey again with the user. The [global Conditional Access exclusion](../conditional-access/policy-require-identity-verification.md#enable-the-global-onboarding-and-recovery-exclusion-preview) doesn't supply a missing profile and isn't a workaround for this error. + +If you're an end user, contact your organization's support team with the error code, request ID, correlation ID, and timestamp from **Troubleshooting details**. Don't send identity documents, biometric images, or Temporary Access Pass values. Administrators can use those diagnostic details when escalating an unresolved error. + +## Usage scenarios + +A profile supplies identity verification. Each scenario also needs its own configuration. + +### Account recovery -For more information about configuring account recovery, see [Enable and configure account recovery in Microsoft Entra ID](how-to-account-recovery-enable.md). +Account recovery helps users who lose all registered authentication methods regain access through identity verification. For scenario setup, see [Enable and configure account recovery in Microsoft Entra ID](how-to-account-recovery-enable.md). > [!NOTE] > Identity verification providers are external services available through the Microsoft Security Store. Review your provider's privacy, data retention, and compliance policies before deploying a profile to production users. -## Profile properties +### Onboarding and verification for access + +| Scenario | Purpose | Where to start | +| --- | --- | --- | +| Integrated onboarding | Complete required identity verification before access and passkey bootstrap, with Lifecycle Workflows orchestration. | [Onboard users with identity verification](../../id-governance/how-to-onboard-users-with-identity-verification.md). | +| Verification for access | Require identity verification after initial authentication for a protected resource or action. | [High assurance overview](../../verified-id/high-assurance.md). | + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> When you use this profile for identity verification during resource access, configure the associated Conditional Access policy's **Conditions** > **Client apps** to select **Browser** and **Mobile apps and desktop clients**. The default configuration includes legacy client types that aren't supported for identity verification step-up and can cause the verification flow to fail. See [Configure a resource-access policy](../conditional-access/policy-require-identity-verification.md#configure-a-resource-access-policy). -The following properties define a Verified ID profile: +During preview, credential provenance is recorded only for passkey credentials. For more information, see [Passkey credential provenance](concept-authentication-passkeys-fido2.md#credential-provenance). -| Property | Description | -|---|---| -| **name** | Display name for the profile | -| **description** | Description of the profile's purpose | -| **state** | Whether the profile is `enabled` or `disabled` | -| **priority** | Processing order when multiple profiles match a user | -| **verifierDid** | The Decentralized Identifier (DID) representing the verifier in the credential exchange | -| **faceCheckConfiguration** | Settings for Entra Verified ID Face Check behavior | -| **verifiedIdProfileConfiguration** | The accepted issuer, claims binding, and credential type | -| **verifiedIdUsageConfigurations** | The scenarios the profile applies to (such as `recovery`) | -| **lastModifiedDateTime** | When the profile was last modified | +## Profile properties -For the full API reference, see [verifiedIdProfile resource type (beta)](/graph/api/resources/verifiedidprofile?view=graph-rest-beta&preserve-view=true). +For Microsoft Graph API properties and values, see [verifiedIdProfile resource type (beta)](/graph/api/resources/verifiedidprofile?view=graph-rest-beta&preserve-view=true). API property names, including `state`, aren't the profile creation controls described in this article. ## Face Check @@ -107,6 +185,20 @@ Verified ID profiles include Face Check configuration to verify proof of presenc Face Check requires a [Face Check license](/entra/verified-id/using-facecheck), available through Entra Suite or as a standalone license. +## Common questions + +Review profile deletion behavior and supported user-level overwrites. + +### How do I stop use of previously issued Verified IDs through a profile? + +Delete the associated identity verification profile to stop use through that profile. Review the profile's dependencies before deleting it. Don't delete and recreate profiles merely to change navigation. + +Deleting a profile doesn't mean deleting a credential from a user's wallet or revoking it with its issuer. Don't infer effects on unrelated verifiers, retained history, credential provenance, or existing sessions. + +### Can administrators overwrite identity verification events and credential provenance? + +Administrators can overwrite identity verification events and credential provenance. These operations are separate from the user completing identity verification and from deleting a shared profile. See [Manage identity verification for a user](concept-authentication-methods-manage.md#manage-identity-verification-for-a-user) and the [identity verification licensing requirements](../../fundamentals/licensing.md#identity-verification). + ## Related content - [Account recovery overview](concept-account-recovery-overview.md) @@ -114,3 +206,4 @@ Face Check requires a [Face Check license](/entra/verified-id/using-facecheck), - [Frequently asked questions about account recovery](self-service-account-recovery.yml) - [What is Microsoft Entra Verified ID?](/entra/verified-id/decentralized-identifier-overview) - [verifiedIdProfile resource type (beta)](/graph/api/resources/verifiedidprofile?view=graph-rest-beta&preserve-view=true) +- [Identity verification status and history](concept-authentication-methods-manage.md#identity-verification-status-and-history).
modifiedFiles.commitMessage: Publish Ignite 2026 High Assurance documentation release (#15002)

englishSummary.headline: Identity verification profiles now cover more scenarios
englishSummary.summary: The documentation expands profiles beyond account recovery to onboarding and access verification, and adds profile purposes, Evaluation/Production modes, supported methods, and prerequisites. It also documents public-cloud availability and automatic collection of verification history when a profile is created.
englishSummary.adminImpact: Admins evaluating profiles should review the required licensing, roles, cloud availability, and scenario-specific preparation.

Learn how to set up profiles and providers. +title: Configure account recovery settings in Microsoft Entra ID +description: Enable the Account recovery policy in Microsoft Entra ID and configure actions after recovery, including Temporary Access Pass issuance and stale credential cleanup. ms.reviewer: tilarso ms.service: entra-id ms.topic: how-to -ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-108, msecd-doc-authoring-1012 -ms.date: 04/29/2026 - -#customer intent: As an identity administrator, I want to enable and configure account recovery in Microsoft Entra ID so that users who lose all their authentication methods can securely recover their accounts through identity verification without contacting the help desk. - +ms.custom: sfi-ga-nochange, sfi-image-nochange, msecd-doc-authoring-108, msecd-doc-authoring-1012, msecd-doc-authoring-1026 +ms.date: 11/13/2026 +author: rogulati +ms.author: rogulati +ai-usage: ai-assisted +#customer intent: As an identity administrator, I want to enable account recovery and configure actions after recovery so that users can register replacement authentication methods after identity verification. --- -# Enable and configure account recovery in Microsoft Entra ID - -Account recovery is a Microsoft Entra ID feature that helps users regain access to their accounts when they lose all their authentication methods — such as when they lose a phone, hardware token, or their passkeys.  # Configure Temporary Access Pass to register passwordless authentication methods
 
-Passwordless authentication methods like a passkey (FIDO2) let users sign in securely without a password. Users can bootstrap passwordless methods in one of two ways:
+Passwordless authentication methods like a passkey (FIDO2) let users sign in securely without a password. Common ways to bootstrap passwordless methods include:
 
 - Use existing Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication methods 
 - Use a Temporary Access Pass 
 
 A Temporary Access Pass (TAP) is a time-limited passcode that can be configured for single use or multiple sign-ins. Users can sign in with a TAP to onboard other passwordless authentication methods. A TAP also makes recovery easier when a user loses or forgets a strong authentication method.
 
+> [!NOTE]
+> For identity-verified onboarding (preview), use Microsoft Entra Lifecycle Workflows to orchestrate identity verification before credential bootstrap. See the [high assurance onboarding overview](../../verified-id/high-assurance.md#supported-journeys) and [Create and manage identity verification profiles](concept-authentication-verified-id.md#create-and-manage-identity-verification-profiles). This journey requires separate configuration; issuing a TAP alone doesn't enable identity-verified onboarding.
+
 This article shows you how to enable and use a TAP using the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com). You can also perform these actions using REST APIs.

You can find more information about terms of use in [Microsoft Entra terms of use](terms-of-use.md).
 
+## Require identity verification
+
+The identity verification grant control requires users to verify their identity for protected access. Configure an eligible verification profile and apply the requirement to the supported resource or action scope in your tenant.
+
+Identity verification and credential provenance are distinct. An identity verification requirement doesn't, by itself, establish the provenance of the specific credential used at sign-in. During preview, credential provenance is recorded only for passkey credentials.
+
+
+Check [Identity verification licensing](../../fundamentals/licensing.md#identity-verification) for the requirements that apply to your scenario. License requirements for identity verification are separate from the existing generic authentication-strength guidance.
+
+Configure an eligible [identity verification profile](../authentication/concept-authentication-verified-id.md#create-and-manage-identity-verification-profiles), then follow the guide for your scenario:
+
+- [Require identity verification for resource access](policy-require-identity-verification.md#configure-a-resource-access-policy) for resource policy design, supported issuance testing, and failure handling.
+- [Protect onboarding and recovery](policy-require-identity-verification.md#configure-an-onboarding-and-recovery-policy) for bootstrap policy boundaries.
+- [Configure risk policies](../../id-protection/howto-identity-protection-configure-risk-policies.md) for the separate risk scenario.
+
+Use onboarding and recovery user-action targeting to protect bootstrap separately from ordinary resource access. Confirm the target and exclusion options available in your tenant. Preserve emergency access, and keep exclusions scoped and approved rather than removing ordinary resource protection.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> **Terms of use** and **Require authentication strength** aren't supported for the onboarding and recovery user action. Most other Microsoft Entra-specific controls also aren't supported for this action. Review the [onboarding and recovery control limitations](policy-require-identity-verification.md#review-control-limitations) before combining controls. This limitation doesn't apply to ordinary resource-access policies.
+
+**Require risk remediation** remains a distinct control with the behavior described above. The identity verification requirement isn't a rename or an automatic change to that control.
+
+Report-only evaluation isn't enforcement and doesn't prove that verification completed. Report-only guidance excludes user-action policies from evaluation; don't rely on it for onboarding and recovery without confirming support for that action.
+
+
 ## Multiple grant controls
 
 When multiple grant controls apply to a user, understand that Conditional Access policies follow a specific validation order by design. For example, if a user has two policies requiring multifactor authentication (MFA) and Terms of Use (ToU), Conditional Access validates the user's MFA claim first, then the ToU.

 # Require remediation for risky users
 
+
 ## Overview
 
 Organizations with Microsoft Entra ID P2 licenses can create Conditional Access policies incorporating [Microsoft Entra ID Protection user risk detections](~/id-protection/concept-identity-protection-risks.md). This policy enables end users to self-remediate and unblock themselves, increasing their productivity while reducing incidents sent to your help desk or security operations teams.  
@@ -23,6 +29,18 @@ This risk remediation policy covers both password-based and passwordless users.
 
 [!INCLUDE [conditional-access-policy-user-risk](../../includes/conditional-access-policy-user-risk.md)]
 
+## Remediate risk with identity verification
+
+Identity verification provides a separate risk-remediation path. Before configuring the policy, [create an identity verification profile](../authentication/concept-authentication-verified-id.md#create-and-manage-identity-verification-profiles) with **Profile purpose** set to **All** or **Verification** and a provider and credential type that support your risk scenario. For tenant-issued credentials, select **Verification**. Use [Configure risk policies](../../id-protection/howto-identity-protection-configure-risk-policies.md) to configure the policy, test the user journey, and check the remediation outcome.
+
+Review [Identity verification licensing](../../fundamentals/licensing.md#identity-verification) for the requirements that apply to this remediation path. Don't assume that the user-risk policy license requirement above covers every identity verification capability.
+
+Don't substitute the **Require risk remediation** steps above for identity verification configuration. That control covers password-based and passwordless users and doesn't automatically use identity verification.
+
+Use the risk conditions supported for identity verification in your tenant. Resource-access verification and risk remediation are different outcomes: check both the verification result and the applicable risk outcome in your pilot. Don't assume that every successful identity verification clears every risk state.
+
+Preserve emergency access and approved user exclusions when configuring identity verification for risk remediation. Report-only mode evaluates which policies could apply without triggering identity verification. Don't interpret report-only results as actual identity verification or cleared risk. Conduct enforcement and remediation tests separately with approved pilot users before expanding scope.
+
